title: Nebulized interferon-β1a (SNG001) in COVID-19 patients: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to determine the efficacy of nebulised interferon-β1a (SNG001) in patients with Coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19). METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and clinicaltrials.gov, without language restrictions. Studies were searched up to November 2025. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on treatment of COVID-19 with SNG001, compared with placebo or standard of care, were reviewed. Data were analysed using the RevMan Version 5.1 (The Cochrane Collaboration). Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for dichotomous outcomes. RESULTS: Four RCTs (enrolling 1055 participants) met the inclusion criteria. The proportion of patients with hospitalisations (data extracted from two RCTs) (RR 0.16, 95% CI 0.03 to 0.88), and serious adverse events (RR 0.65, 95% CI 0.47 to 0.90) were significantly fewer in SNG001 groups. There was no statistically significant difference in all-cause mortality (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.37 to 1.39), patients non-recovery at day 28 (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65 to 1.17), and adverse event (RR 0.97, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.04) between the two groups. CONCLUSIONS: Nebulised SNG001 was safe and associated with a reduction in COVID-19-related hospital admission. SNG001 shows a potential benefit for outpatients with COVID-19, but it requires larger clinical trials for future validations, particularly in vaccinated and previously infected populations.

title: Retrospective analysis of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron strains (2023 to 2024) from Pakistan reveals differential phylogenetic diversity across genomes compared with other countries
abstract: BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants continued to emerge globally in 2023 and 2024 however, genomic epidemiology from Pakistan has been limited. We compared Omicron variants in Pakistan by studying phylogenetic diversity and entropy across genomes compared with isolates from Western countries USA, UK and France, as well as neighbouring India. METHODS: We studied SARS-CoV-2 genomes collected between January 2023 and September 2024. For Pakistan, we also focused on RT-PCR positive samples from Aga Khan University Hospital. Statistical analyses identified P value < 0.05 as considered significant. Genome-based lineages were assigned using Pangolin v4.4 pangoLEARN with clade assignment using Nextclade v3.5.0. Sequences were aligned using MAFFT v7.505 and a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree was constructed with IQ-TREE v2.2.0. Substitution rates and Shannon genomic entropy was determined. RESULTS: In Pakistan, XBB.1 and its subvariants were predominant in 2023 and JN.1 and its subvariants persisted through 2024. Whilst, variants KP.2, LB.1, and LA.1 emerging by mid-2024, JN.1 remained dominant. In contrast, SARS-CoV-2 in US, UK and France showed XBB.1.5 transition​ed to JN.1 and KP.3.3 by September 2024. Notably, JN.1 strains persisted in India until 2024. Genomic substitution rates in Pakistan at 0.467E-04 (95CI: 3.29E-04-6.04E-04) were similar compared with those from USA, UK and France, but higher than those from India. SARS-CoV-2 mean positional entropy in Pakistan at 0.0324 was higher (other countries 0.01-0.013). CONCLUSIONS: We describe Omicron diversity in Pakistan with persistence of XBB and JN.1 lineage strains into 2024. These finding provide insights into SARS-CoV-2 genomic evolution. ​The relatively small genomic sequences available limits the comparison with substitution rates between global strains. Expanded surveillance is required to understand local transmission of pandemic strains.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a retrospective analysis of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron strains in Pakistan from 2023 to 2024, comparing their phylogenetic diversity and genomic entropy with those from the USA, UK, France and India. The research identified XBB.1 and JN.1 as predominant in Pakistan, with JN.1 remaining dominant through 2024. In contrast, the USA, UK and France showed a transition from XBB.1.5 to JN.1 and KP.3.3 by September 2024, while JN.1 persisted in India until 2024. Genomic substitution rates in Pakistan were similar to those in Western countries but higher than in India. The mean positional entropy in Pakistan was also higher than in other countries. The study highlights the need for expanded surveillance to understand local transmission dynamics of pandemic strains. However, the relatively small number of genomic sequences limits the strength of the comparison with global strains.

title_zh: 对巴基斯坦 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Omicron 菌株(2023 年至 2024 年)的回顾性分析揭示了 基因组 与其他国家相比存在差异的系统发育多样性
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants continued to emerge globally in 2023 and 2024 however, genomic epidemiology from Pakistan has been limited. We compared Omicron variants in Pakistan by studying phylogenetic diversity and entropy across genomes compared with isolates from Western countries USA, UK and France, as well as neighbouring India. METHODS: We studied SARS-CoV-2 genomes collected between January 2023 and September 2024. For Pakistan, we also focused on RT-PCR positive samples from Aga Khan University Hospital. Statistical analyses identified P value < 0.05 as considered significant. Genome-based lineages were assigned using Pangolin v4.4 pangoLEARN with clade assignment using Nextclade v3.5.0. Sequences were aligned using MAFFT v7.505 and a maximum-likelihood phylogenetic tree was constructed with IQ-TREE v2.2.0. Substitution rates and Shannon genomic entropy was determined. RESULTS: In Pakistan, XBB.1 and its subvariants were predominant in 2023 and JN.1 and its subvariants persisted through 2024. Whilst, variants KP.2, LB.1, and LA.1 emerging by mid-2024, JN.1 remained dominant. In contrast, SARS-CoV-2 in US, UK and France showed XBB.1.5 transition​ed to JN.1 and KP.3.3 by September 2024. Notably, JN.1 strains persisted in India until 2024. Genomic substitution rates in Pakistan at 0.467E-04 (95CI: 3.29E-04-6.04E-04) were similar compared with those from USA, UK and France, but higher than those from India. SARS-CoV-2 mean positional entropy in Pakistan at 0.0324 was higher (other countries 0.01-0.013). CONCLUSIONS: We describe Omicron diversity in Pakistan with persistence of XBB and JN.1 lineage strains into 2024. These finding provide insights into SARS-CoV-2 genomic evolution. ​The relatively small genomic sequences available limits the comparison with substitution rates between global strains. Expanded surveillance is required to understand local transmission of pandemic strains.

title: Structural and functional analysis of VYD222: A broadly neutralizing antibody against SARS-CoV-2 variants.
abstract: Extensive mutations in SARS-CoV-2 spike protein have rendered most therapeutic monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) ineffective. However, here we describe how VYD222 (pemivibart), a human mAb re-engineered from ADG20 (adintrevimab) exhibits substantially improved neutralization potency and breadth against SARS-CoV-2 variants despite substantial virus evolution. VYD222 received FDA Emergency Use Authorization for pre-exposure prophylaxis of COVID-19 in certain immunocompromised adults and adolescents. Here we show potent neutralization of this antibody against a broad range of emerging variants, including the recently dominant XFG. X-ray crystal structures of VYD222 in complex with the receptor-binding domains of prototype SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron BA.5 demonstrate the molecular basis of how VYD222 accommodates the mutations in SARS-CoV-2 variants that escape other previous FDA-approved antibodies. Notably, many of the mutations between ADG20 and VYD222 occur in the second shell outside the paratope contact residues. Deep mutational scanning indicates that SARS-CoV-2's ability to escape VYD222 is constrained by structural compatibility and the need to maintain receptor binding. These findings provide crucial insights into the escape-resistant neutralization of VYD222 against a broad panel of clinically relevant SARS-CoV-2 variants and offer valuable guidance for risk assessment of emergent variants.

title: Echoes of infection: viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes in long COVID: a systematic review
abstract: Long COVID, or post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC), affects an estimated 10–20% of individuals following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Despite its substantial global burden, the pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize available evidence on viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes across multiple organ systems, drawing from studies of individuals with Long COVID as well as broader post-acute cohorts, autopsy investigations, and case-based reports relevant to Long COVID pathophysiology. Following PRISMA guidelines and holding a PROSPERO registration (CRD420261403869), a systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible reports were stratified as (A) symptom-defined Long COVID assessed at or after 12 weeks, (B) post-acute or mixed populations without a consistently confirmed Long COVID definition or timing, (C) autopsy studies, and (D) isolated case/fetal reports. Findings were synthesized narratively by specimen, assay target, and unit of analysis. JBI checklists were used for item-level appraisal, not as certainty-of-evidence ratings. Forty-five reports were included: 16 in stratum A, 23 in stratum B, three autopsy studies, and three isolated case/fetal reports. SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA, viral proteins, and markers compatible with recent viral activity were reported in selected tissue and blood compartments, but detection varied with population selection, timing, specimen, and assay. No included study established replication competence by recovery of infectious virus. Histopathological abnormalities included inflammatory infiltrates, fibrosis, and vascular injury; however, causal attribution to Long COVID was limited by acute disease severity, biopsy indication, comorbidity, and incomplete comparator data. A single participant total was not reported because of overlapping cohorts, repeated sampling, and outcome-specific denominators. The review supports biological heterogeneity after SARS-CoV-2 infection, including residual viral material, immune dysregulation, vascular injury, and maladaptive tissue repair. Organ-specific prevalence, a hierarchy of tissue tropism, replication-competent reservoirs, and superiority of antiviral or immunomodulatory treatment remain undefined. Standardized Long COVID definitions, representative cohorts, validated assays, appropriate comparators, and longitudinal studies linking biological markers to clinical outcomes are required.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review explores the pathophysiological mechanisms of Long COVID, focusing on viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes. It synthesizes evidence from 45 studies, including symptom-defined Long COVID cohorts, post-acute populations, autopsy investigations, and case-based reports. The review highlights biological heterogeneity, such as residual viral material, immune dysregulation, vascular injury, and maladaptive tissue repair. However, it notes limitations, including the absence of studies establishing replication competence, incomplete comparator data, and the lack of standardized definitions. The findings emphasize the need for further research on organ-specific prevalence, tissue tropism, and the effectiveness of antiviral or immunomodulatory treatments. Additionally, the review calls for improved methodologies, including validated assays and longitudinal studies, to better understand Long COVID's biological underpinnings and clinical outcomes.

title_zh: 感染回声:长新冠 中的病毒持久性、免疫激活和组织病理学变化:系统评价
source_body_en: Long COVID, or post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC), affects an estimated 10–20% of individuals following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Despite its substantial global burden, the pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This systematic review aimed to synthesize available evidence on viral persistence, immune activation, and histopathological changes across multiple organ systems, drawing from studies of individuals with Long COVID as well as broader post-acute cohorts, autopsy investigations, and case-based reports relevant to Long COVID pathophysiology. Following PRISMA guidelines and holding a PROSPERO registration (CRD420261403869), a systematic literature search was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, EMBASE, and Cochrane CENTRAL. Eligible reports were stratified as (A) symptom-defined Long COVID assessed at or after 12 weeks, (B) post-acute or mixed populations without a consistently confirmed Long COVID definition or timing, (C) autopsy studies, and (D) isolated case/fetal reports. Findings were synthesized narratively by specimen, assay target, and unit of analysis. JBI checklists were used for item-level appraisal, not as certainty-of-evidence ratings. Forty-five reports were included: 16 in stratum A, 23 in stratum B, three autopsy studies, and three isolated case/fetal reports. SARS-CoV-2 genomic RNA, viral proteins, and markers compatible with recent viral activity were reported in selected tissue and blood compartments, but detection varied with population selection, timing, specimen, and assay. No included study established replication competence by recovery of infectious virus. Histopathological abnormalities included inflammatory infiltrates, fibrosis, and vascular injury; however, causal attribution to Long COVID was limited by acute disease severity, biopsy indication, comorbidity, and incomplete comparator data. A single participant total was not reported because of overlapping cohorts, repeated sampling, and outcome-specific denominators. The review supports biological heterogeneity after SARS-CoV-2 infection, including residual viral material, immune dysregulation, vascular injury, and maladaptive tissue repair. Organ-specific prevalence, a hierarchy of tissue tropism, replication-competent reservoirs, and superiority of antiviral or immunomodulatory treatment remain undefined. Standardized Long COVID definitions, representative cohorts, validated assays, appropriate comparators, and longitudinal studies linking biological markers to clinical outcomes are required.

title: [Dynamics of behavioral factors and attitudes toward vaccination in moscow during the COVID-19 pandemic: from the acute phase to adaptation].
abstract: BACKGROUND: The transition of the COVID-19 pandemic from the acute phase to adaptation was accompanied by changes in preventive behavior, institutional trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination. OBJECTIVE: To analyze the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents in 2021 compared with 2020. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. CATI was conducted using a stratified dual-frame sample. The article analyzes the 4th and 5th survey waves: February 2021 (n = 1038) and July-August 2021 (n = 998). RESULTS: By the 5th wave, adherence to most preventive measures decreased, especially social distancing, limiting contacts and using hand sanitizers. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized. CONCLUSIONS: Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups and horizontal trust.

title_zh: [Dynamics of behavioral factors and attitudes toward vaccination in moscow during the COVID-19 pandemic: from the acute phase to adaptation].

OBJECTIVE: To analyze the dynamics of awareness, preventive behavior, trust, emotional state and attitudes toward vaccination among Moscow residents in 2021 compared with 2020. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The survey tool was developed by the WHO Regional Office for Europe with support from the University of Erfurt and adapted to the Moscow context. The proportion not wearing gloves increased sharply after the requirement was lifted. The mean self-assessment of emotional state decreased to 3.47 points; institutional assessments declined and vaccination attitudes became more polarized. CONCLUSIONS: Public health strategies should combine consistent scientific communication, targeted work with vaccine-hesitant groups and horizontal trust.

title: Modelling severe COVID-19 by adaptation of SARS-CoV-2 in Syrian hamsters.
abstract: While most patients infected with recent Omicron subvariants develop milder disease than those infected with preceding SARS-CoV-2 strains, some patients remain susceptible to developing severe disease and/or long-term complications. The pathogenesis of and optimal countermeasures for severe COVID-19 remain incompletely understood. Readily available small animal models closely mimicking severe COVID-19 are lacking. We have previously established a Syrian hamster model for COVID-19 that mimics mild-to-moderate disease in humans. In this study, we established a new Syrian hamster model resembling severe COVID-19 using a hamster-adapted SARS-CoV-2 (SARS-CoV-2HA) obtained through serial passage. Compared to the ancestral virus strain P0, SARS-CoV-2HA P16 causes more severe disease with significantly higher clinical scores, higher viral burden, more weight loss, prominent cytokine storm, and significant pulmonary injury. Age and sex are key factors influencing disease severity in this model. Comparing SARS-CoV-2HA P16 and P0, N_S194L was identified as a key adaptive mutation that enhances the antagonistic effect of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein and viral replication. Using this new SARS-CoV-2HA P16 model, we showed that nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir were effective in improving the clinical and virological parameters of hamsters with severe COVID-19. This new model serves as a robust platform for investigating the pathogenesis of and countermeasures for severe COVID-19.

We have previously established a Syrian hamster model for COVID-19 that mimics mild-to-moderate disease in humans. In this study, we established a new Syrian hamster model resembling severe COVID-19 using a hamster-adapted SARS-CoV-2 (SARS-CoV-2HA) obtained through serial passage. Compared to the ancestral virus strain P0, SARS-CoV-2HA P16 causes more severe disease with significantly higher clinical scores, higher viral burden, more weight loss, prominent cytokine storm, and significant pulmonary injury. Age and sex are key factors influencing disease severity in this model. Comparing SARS-CoV-2HA P16 and P0, N_S194L was identified as a key adaptive mutation that enhances the antagonistic effect of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein and viral replication. Using this new SARS-CoV-2HA P16 model, we showed that nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir were effective in improving the clinical and virological parameters of hamsters with severe COVID-19. This new model serves as a robust platform for investigating the pathogenesis of and countermeasures for severe COVID-19.

title: A dose of reality: autodisable syringe supply challenges in the COVID-19 immunization response.
abstract: Autodisable (AD) syringes are vital for safe immunization, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, as they prevent reuse and reduce the risk of disease transmission. Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, global supply was stable and met routine immunization needs. The pandemic, however, highlighted coordination challenges in aligning vaccine and injection device supply chains. The rapid rollout of COVID-19 vaccines led to a surge in demand for AD syringes, including those with nonstandard dose volumes, which required new product development and matching of syringes to specific vaccines-a synchronization that is typically not needed. Limited early information on COVID-19 vaccine dose volume specifications, long lead times, and lack of coordination between vaccine and syringe stakeholders created forecasting difficulties. Procurement agencies faced increased costs and logistical constraints and had to quickly adapt contracts and supply strategies. Although manufacturing capacity expanded, syringe shortages still emerged, increasing the risk of dosing errors and placing additional strain on health systems. As demand later declined, oversupply and market instability followed, prompting contract adjustments. This paper incorporates lessons learned from the COVID-19 response and emphasizes that syringes must not be an afterthought in immunization planning for both future outbreak preparedness and routine immunization efforts. It also outlines key strategies for strengthening syringe market resilience.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the challenges of supplying autodisable (AD) syringes during the COVID-19 immunization response. It highlights the critical role of AD syringes in preventing reuse and reducing disease transmission, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. The review notes that prior to the pandemic, global supply of AD syringes was stable and met routine immunization needs. However, the rapid rollout of vaccines created a surge in demand for AD syringes with nonstandard dose volumes, requiring new product development and synchronization between vaccines and syringes. Despite expanded manufacturing capacity, syringe shortages emerged, increasing the risk of dosing errors and straining health systems. The review also discusses the difficulties in forecasting due to limited early information on vaccine dose specifications and lack of coordination between stakeholders. It concludes that syringes must be a central consideration in immunization planning, both for outbreak preparedness and routine efforts, and outlines strategies to strengthen syringe market resilience.

title_zh: A dose of reality: autodisable syringe supply challenges in the COVID-19 immunization response.
source_body_en: Autodisable (AD) syringes are vital for safe immunization, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, as they prevent reuse and reduce the risk of disease transmission. Prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, global supply was stable and met routine immunization needs. The pandemic, however, highlighted coordination challenges in aligning vaccine and injection device supply chains. The rapid rollout of COVID-19 vaccines led to a surge in demand for AD syringes, including those with nonstandard dose volumes, which required new product development and matching of syringes to specific vaccines-a synchronization that is typically not needed. Limited early information on COVID-19 vaccine dose volume specifications, long lead times, and lack of coordination between vaccine and syringe stakeholders created forecasting difficulties. Procurement agencies faced increased costs and logistical constraints and had to quickly adapt contracts and supply strategies. Although manufacturing capacity expanded, syringe shortages still emerged, increasing the risk of dosing errors and placing additional strain on health systems. As demand later declined, oversupply and market instability followed, prompting contract adjustments. This paper incorporates lessons learned from the COVID-19 response and emphasizes that syringes must not be an afterthought in immunization planning for both future outbreak preparedness and routine immunization efforts. It also outlines key strategies for strengthening syringe market resilience.

title: Time-Dependent Activity of SARS-CoV-2 Mpro Inhibitors.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic led to the rapid development of vaccines and antiviral drugs to prevent severe disease and death. Several drugs that inhibit the essential main viral protease Mpro are in clinical use (Voget R, Gutschow M. Early Kinetic Characterization of SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease Inhibitors: A Review and Guidance for Biochemical Assessments. 2026;65:860-81.) and additional Mpro inhibitors are being developed to address drug-resistance and novel emergent coronaviruses. Early drug discovery and development has primarily used non-cell-based biochemical assays to characterize the pharmacokinetic properties of drug candidates (Tonge PJ. Drug-target kinetics in drug discovery. Because drugs that remain bound to the target may have prolonged activity following drug elimination enabling dose frequency to be reduced, we evaluated the relationship between target residence time and antiviral activity of four Mpro inhibitors with different mechanisms of action. This included the irreversible inhibitor N3, the noncovalent inhibitor ensitrelvir, which had a residence time of 2.4 min, and the reversible covalent inhibitors 13b and nirmatrelvir, which had residence times of 19 and 23.3 min, respectively. To correlate the in vitro residence times with time-dependent antiviral activity, we performed washout experiments with Vero-E6 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2. While all the compounds inhibited viral RNA production, ensitrelvir with the shortest residence time was significantly less active than the other compounds following washout. The intracellular washout experiments confirmed that ensitrelvir exhibited a shorter residence time in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells, falling below the functional lifespan of nascent viral replicase/transcriptase complexes.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on SARS-CoV-2 and evaluates the relationship between the target residence time of four Mpro inhibitors and their antiviral activity. The central question is whether the duration of drug-target binding influences the effectiveness of these inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of the pharmacokinetic properties of Mpro inhibitors. It includes in vitro washout experiments with Vero-E6 cells infected with SARS-CoV-2 to correlate residence time with antiviral activity. The evidence is derived from biochemical assays and experimental data on drug-target interactions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study concludes that the residence time of Mpro inhibitors in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells is associated with their antiviral activity. Specifically, compounds with longer residence times, such as nirmatrelvir, showed greater antiviral efficacy compared to ensitrelvir, which had the shortest residence time and was less active post-washout.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The evidence highlights a potential limitation in early drug discovery methods, which primarily used non-cell-based assays. This may have led to an incomplete understanding of in vivo drug behavior. Additionally, the study does not address the long-term effects of these inhibitors or their performance against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest that future drug development should prioritize compounds with longer target residence times to enhance antiviral efficacy. There is also a need for more comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies to evaluate the effectiveness of Mpro inhibitors against new SARS-CoV-2 variants and to refine dosing strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the relationship between the target residence time of four SARS-CoV-2 Mpro inhibitors and their antiviral activity. The study uses in vitro washout experiments with Vero-E6 cells to demonstrate that compounds with longer residence times, such as nirmatrelvir, exhibit greater antiviral efficacy compared to ensitrelvir, which had the shortest residence time and was less active post-washout. The evidence underscores the importance of residence time in determining drug effectiveness and highlights the need for more in vivo studies to assess performance against emerging variants. The findings suggest that future drug development should focus on improving residence time to optimize antiviral activity and dosing strategies.

title: SARS-CoV-2 antibody landscape following multiple vaccinations and infections during Omicron period
abstract: Background: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination effects on the immunogenicity, breadth, and durability of antibody responses across antigenically distinct SARS-CoV-2 variants remain incompletely understood. Method: Participants receiving >= five COVID-19 vaccine doses 2020-2025 were selected from a prospective cohort in Michigan. Serum IgG, IgM, and ACE2 percent inhibition were measured using multiplex assays. Baseline-adjusted immunogenicity, cross-reactivity, and formulation-specific antibody durability were evaluated using regression models. Result: Twenty-one participants were included (median: seven vaccine doses). For every two-fold increase in pre-vaccination IgG concentration, post-vaccination fold-rise was 34% (95% CI: 16%-48%), 43% (95% CI: 15%-62%), and 55% (95% CI: 21%-75%) lower following monovalent, bivalent, and 2023-24 vaccination, while baseline-adjusted immunogenicity showed no significant trends across successive vaccines. Antibody landscapes demonstrated broad cross-reactivity against ancestral and Omicron variants, with similar strain-specific IgG changes across ancestral, vaccine-matched, and antigenically distant strains, but greater heterogeneity in ACE2 inhibition. Formulation-specific waning models showed significant IgG declines following monovalent and bivalent vaccination (beta = -1.03, 95% CI: -1.51 to -0.55; P<0.001 and -1.00 , 95% CI: -1.71 to -0.30; P=0.007, respectively) and ACE2 inhibition declines following monovalent vaccination, while other formulations showed less consistent changes. Despite waning, antibody levels generally remained relatively high across variants up to 300 days post-vaccination, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Conclusion: Repeated COVID-19 vaccination maintained baseline-adjusted immunogenicity and broad cross-reactive antibody responses, with formulation-specific differences in durability. Higher baseline immunity was associated with smaller post-vaccination increases, suggesting repeated boosting continues to reinforce humoral immunity despite increasingly complex immune histories.

title: Misperceived norms and willingness to get a COVID-19 vaccine: a whole-population study of adults in rural Uganda.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perceptions about others' willingness to get vaccinated for COVID-19 are understudied in HIV-endemic settings. Perceived social norms influence engagement in other protective behaviors. Information about COVID-19 vaccine norms could inform future HIV vaccination efforts. METHODS: All adults across 8 villages in Uganda completed a survey in 2021-2022. Participants reported personal willingness to take a COVID-19 vaccine (definitely yes vs any hesitance) and estimated how many village adults would take a COVID-19 vaccine ("all or almost all," "more than half," "less than half," "very few or no one," "do not know"). Participants also reported COVID-19 related beliefs, whether they knew someone who had COVID-19, personal HIV status, and sociodemographic characteristics. A multivariable Poisson regression model estimated associations between perceptions about others' willingness to get a vaccine and personal willingness to get a vaccine. RESULTS: Among 1561 participants (>90% response rate), 1163 (75%) were willing to get a COVID-19 vaccine. One in three vaccine-hesitant participants and 1 in 10 vaccine-willing participants incorrectly thought most adults in their village would not get vaccinated. Compared to participants who thought more than half of villagers were willing to get vaccinated, those who mistakenly thought fewer than half (adjusted relative risk [aRR] = 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.70-0.94) or few to none (aRR = 0.65; 95% CI: 0.50-0.85) were willing were less likely to report willingness themselves. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, one-fifth of adults mistakenly thought most other villagers were unwilling to get vaccinated. Adults with this misperception were less willing to get a COVID-19 vaccine themselves. Strategies that provide information about vaccine effectiveness and communicate that most adults are willing to get vaccinated may increase uptake. Changing perceived norms about vaccine uptake may also foster conversations about accessing vaccines and reduce vaccine-related stigma, important considerations with an HIV vaccine on the horizon.

Participants also reported COVID-19 related beliefs, whether they knew someone who had COVID-19, personal HIV status, and sociodemographic characteristics. A multivariable Poisson regression model estimated associations between perceptions about others' willingness to get a vaccine and personal willingness to get a vaccine. RESULTS: Among 1561 participants (>90% response rate), 1163 (75%) were willing to get a COVID-19 vaccine. One in three vaccine-hesitant participants and 1 in 10 vaccine-willing participants incorrectly thought most adults in their village would not get vaccinated. Compared to participants who thought more than half of villagers were willing to get vaccinated, those who mistakenly thought fewer than half (adjusted relative risk [aRR] = 0.81; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.70-0.94) or few to none (aRR = 0.65; 95% CI: 0.50-0.85) were willing were less likely to report willingness themselves. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, one-fifth of adults mistakenly thought most other villagers were unwilling to get vaccinated. Adults with this misperception were less willing to get a COVID-19 vaccine themselves. Strategies that provide information about vaccine effectiveness and communicate that most adults are willing to get vaccinated may increase uptake. Changing perceived norms about vaccine uptake may also foster conversations about accessing vaccines and reduce vaccine-related stigma, important considerations with an HIV vaccine on the horizon.

title: A decoupled ensemble framework for real-time nowcasting of COVID-19 case numbers and transmission dynamics.
abstract: Timely monitoring of epidemics such as SARS-CoV-2 transmission is essential for guiding public health and social measures, yet real-time estimation of the time-varying effective reproductive number ( R t ) from case data suffers from right-censoring bias, systematically underestimating recent R t values and requiring 7-14 days of additional data to stabilize. To address this limitation, we developed and evaluated a three-step framework that decouples case forecasting from R t estimation. Daily PCR-confirmed case counts are first forecast up to 14 days ahead using an ensemble of 10 statistical, machine learning and deep learning models. Forecasted cases are then deconvolved to reconstruct infection timelines, from which R t is estimated for up to 7 days ahead. This approach mitigates right-censoring artefacts by generating R t estimates from projected rather than truncated case data. We applied this framework to Hong Kong's Omicron outbreaks (February to December 2022), incorporating 15 epidemiological, meteorological, air pollution and policy-related predictors. An unweighted ensemble of top-performing models substantially improved forecast accuracy, reducing the root mean square error and the mean absolute percentage error by 10 and 9% for case numbers and by 38 and 34% for R t . By separating predictive modelling from epidemiological inference, this framework enables accurate real-time monitoring of epidemic burden and transmission dynamics to support timely public health decision-making.

Daily PCR-confirmed case counts are first forecast up to 14 days ahead using an ensemble of 10 statistical, machine learning and deep learning models. Forecasted cases are then deconvolved to reconstruct infection timelines, from which R t is estimated for up to 7 days ahead. This approach mitigates right-censoring artefacts by generating R t estimates from projected rather than truncated case data. We applied this framework to Hong Kong's Omicron outbreaks (February to December 2022), incorporating 15 epidemiological, meteorological, air pollution and policy-related predictors. An unweighted ensemble of top-performing models substantially improved forecast accuracy, reducing the root mean square error and the mean absolute percentage error by 10 and 9% for case numbers and by 38 and 34% for R t . By separating predictive modelling from epidemiological inference, this framework enables accurate real-time monitoring of epidemic burden and transmission dynamics to support timely public health decision-making.

title: Spatiotemporal analysis of COVID-19 in Japan: The twelve epidemic waves from 2020 to 2025
abstract: Since the first confirmed case of COVID-19 in Japan in January 2020, multiple epidemic waves have emerged under changing legal classifications and public health measures. Although nationwide surveillance data have been continuously available, integrated analyses of temporal and geographic patterns remain limited. This study described the spatiotemporal evolution of COVID-19 in Japan in relation to the timing of major policy, vaccination, variant, and surveillance changes. Weekly prefecture-level case counts from 2020 to 2025 were analyzed using official data from the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, and the epidemic period was divided into early epidemic, expansion, and plateau phases. Three-dimensional log-transformed visualizations were generated to illustrate nationwide temporal and regional trends. We identified twelve epidemic waves. Early outbreaks were localized in densely populated urban areas with low synchrony. During the expansion phase, large nationwide waves occurred in the period when a highly transmissible variant emerged, and peak timing was most closely aligned across prefectures in the 5th and 7th waves. In the plateau phase, following the transition to “Category 5 infectious disease,” reported waves were lower and more prolonged, with smaller differences among prefectures; because these values are based on sentinel reports, they are not directly comparable with earlier phases. Overall, COVID-19 in Japan evolved from localized clusters to synchronized nationwide waves with reduced regional differences across prefectures, suggesting the value of integrated spatiotemporal surveillance frameworks for future pandemic preparedness.

title: Identification of small-molecule inhibitors of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD–ACE2 interaction by structure- and affinity-based screening
abstract: Abstract The receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein mediates viral entry through its interaction with angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2), making it an attractive target for antiviral intervention. However, the broad and relatively shallow ACE2-binding interface presents a challenge for small-molecule inhibitor discovery. In the present study, we explored conserved regions outside the ACE2-binding interface as potential druggable sites for small-molecule inhibitors targeting the SARS-CoV-2 RBD. Structure-based virtual screening was performed using the structure of the SARS-CoV-1 RBD as a structural surrogate, and selected compounds were evaluated using a newly established affinity-based assay on diazirine-modified amorphous carbon plates. Evaluation of 175 virtual hits identified eight RBD-binding compounds. Among them, only RABI-1 inhibited RBD–ACE2 interaction in a Calu-3 cell-based binding assay without affecting ACE2 expression or cell viability. Evaluation of structural analogs of RABI-1 led to the identification of RABI-3, which showed stronger inhibitory activity compared with RABI-1. In addition, RABI-3 inhibited the interaction between ACE2 and RBDs derived from multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants in an AlphaLISA immunoassay and suppressed pseudovirus infection in Calu-3 cells. These findings support the feasibility of targeting regions of the RBD outside the ACE2-binding interface as a strategy for identifying small-molecule inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 entry.

abstract_zh: 摘要 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2) 刺突蛋白 的受体结合域 (RBD) 通过与血管紧张素转换酶 2 (ACE2) 相互作用介导病毒进入,使其成为 抗病毒药物 干预的有吸引力的靶点。然而,广泛且相对浅的 ACE2 结合界面对小分子抑制剂的发现提出了挑战。在本研究中,我们探索了 ACE2 结合界面之外的保守区域,作为针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RBD 的小分子抑制剂的潜在药物位点。使用 SARS-CoV-1 RBD 的结构作为结构替代物进行基于结构的虚拟筛选,并使用新建立的基于亲和力的测定法在二氮丙啶修饰的无定形碳板上评估选定的化合物。对 175 个虚拟命中的评估确定了 8 种 RBD 结合化合物。其中,在基于 Calu-3 细胞的结合测定中,只有 RABI-1 抑制 RBD-ACE2 相互作用,而不影响 ACE2 表达或细胞活力。对 RABI-1 结构类似物的评估导致了 RABI-3 的鉴定,与 RABI-1 相比,RABI-3 显示出更强的抑制活性。此外,RABI-3 在 AlphaLISA 免疫测定中抑制了 ACE2 和源自多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的 RBD 之间的相互作用,并抑制了 Calu-3 细胞中的假病毒感染。这些发现支持以 ACE2 结合界面之外的 RBD 区域为目标的可行性,作为识别 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 进入的小分子抑制剂的策略。

title: Predictors and prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19: a prospective observational study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Dysfunctional breathing is increasingly recognised among individuals with post-COVID-19 condition (PCC), yet data on long-term prevalence and predictors are scarce. This study assessed the prevalence of symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing, as indicated by elevated Nijmegen questionnaire (NQ) scores, four years after COVID-19 illness in adults with PCC and identified associated factors and baseline predictors by comparing individuals with and without elevated NQ scores. METHOD: In this prospective observational study, adults with PCC, both previously hospitalised and non-hospitalised for COVID-19, were recruited from a specialised post-COVID outpatient clinic. Baseline assessments (2020-2022) were analysed together with data from a digital follow-up survey in 2024. Symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing was defined as a NQ score ≥ 23 at follow-up. Between group differences were examined, and multivariable logistic regression models were used to identify associated factors and baseline predictors. RESULTS: Among 288 participants (median follow-up 50 months), 143 (50%) had symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing. These individuals were younger, often female, and more frequently non-hospitalised during acute COVID-19. Baseline predictors included non-hospitalisation, higher dyspnoea severity, lower FEV1, and younger age. At four years, elevated NQ scores (≥ 23) were independently associated with higher dyspnoea severity, greater PCC-symptom burden, depressive symptoms and postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome. Individuals with symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing performed worse in the six-minute walk test, one-minute sit to stand test, and maximal inspiratory pressure test at baseline, whereas lung function did not differ. Patient-reported outcomes were consistently worse compared with those with NQ scores < 23 and improved less over time. CONCLUSION: Half of the individuals with PCC in this cohort reported symptoms suggestive of dysfunctional breathing four years after COVID-19, as indicated by a NQ score ≥ 23. Elevated NQ scores were associated with greater PCC-symptom burden and poorer health outcomes, highlighting their potential clinical relevance in long-term PCC. Future studies should combine patient-reported measures with objective assessment of breathing pattern and ventilatory function.

title: Evolution of the clinical profile and cardiac outcomes of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across three COVID-19 waves in Central Kerala: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical profile, laboratory findings, cardiac manifestations, treatment patterns and outcomes of children diagnosed with multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) across the Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves of the COVID-19 pandemic. DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study. SETTING: A tertiary care teaching hospital in Central Kerala, India. PARTICIPANTS: 95 children fulfilling established diagnostic criteria for MIS-C admitted between November 2020 and December 2022 were included. Patients were categorised into three groups according to the predominant SARS-CoV-2 variant wave: Alpha (wave 1), Delta (wave 2) and Omicron (wave 3). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Clinical characteristics, laboratory parameters, echocardiographic findings, treatment modalities and markers of disease severity, including duration of hospitalisation, intensive care stay, oxygen requirement, inotropic support and ventilator support. RESULTS: Gastrointestinal symptoms remained the predominant presentation across all three waves, whereas respiratory symptoms increased during the later waves. Mucocutaneous manifestations varied significantly across waves (p=0.02). The duration of hospital stay (p=0.004), duration of fever (p=0.009) and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels (p=0.003) decreased significantly over successive waves, suggesting reduced overall disease severity. Pericardial effusion also decreased significantly (p=0.002), while the prevalence of left ventricular dysfunction showed a declining trend. In contrast, coronary artery dilatation increased significantly during the Omicron wave (p<0.0001). Oxygen requirement declined significantly in the third wave (p=0.02), whereas intensive care stay, inotropic support and ventilator support did not differ significantly between waves. CONCLUSIONS: The clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across successive COVID-19 waves, with evidence of decreasing systemic disease severity but persistent changes in cardiac involvement. The marked increase in coronary artery dilatation during the Omicron wave highlights the importance of continued echocardiographic surveillance and long-term cardiac follow-up, even during clinically milder phases of the pandemic.

The study included 95 children diagnosed with MIS-C between November 2020 and December 2022, categorised by the predominant SARS-CoV-2 variant: Alpha, Delta, and Omicron. Key findings showed that gastrointestinal symptoms remained the most common presentation, while respiratory symptoms increased in later waves. The study observed a significant decrease in disease severity markers such as hospital stay duration, fever duration, and pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels over time. However, coronary artery dilatation increased significantly during the Omicron wave, indicating persistent cardiac involvement. elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: The clinical phenotype of MIS-C evolved across successive COVID-19 waves, with evidence of decreasing systemic disease severity but persistent changes in cardiac involvement.

title: Social support networks of older adults before, during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Societies are considerably challenged by population aging, especially when it comes to providing services and support for older adults. Although formal services such as home care and volunteering address some of these needs, the informal social support given by relatives, friends and neighbours is just as vital. In Slovenia, the share of older adults reporting they have no informal social support rose from around 1% in 2002 to 7.8% in 2020, coinciding with the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic. The article examines the prevalence and characteristics of social support network types relied on by older adults in Slovenia between 2002 and 2025, with a special focus on the post-pandemic recovery. To that end, a cross-sectional survey collected ego-centred network data of older adults (65+) in Slovenia in 2002, 2020 and 2025. The samples are representative of both gender and region. The data were analysed using clustering for symbolic data and correspondence analysis. Distinct network types were identified based on the number and characteristics of the support providers, including relationship type, spatial proximity, and frequency of contact across emotional, instrumental and socialising dimensions. The identified types of social support networks are: family dependent, private restricted, local self-contained, locally integrated, and wider community network type, along with the cluster of egos that did not list any alter called “no-listed alters”. Trends regarding the prevalence of these network types suggest that while some were more strongly affected by the COVID-19 pandemic (no-listed alters, local self-contained, wider community), other network types (family dependent, private restricted, locally integrated) appear to reflect longer-term demographic changes. The partial recovery of informal social support is shown by the share of older adults with no social support having dropped to 4.4% by 2025. Nevertheless, persistent inequalities remain, with men in particular revealed to have greater chances of being socially isolated, pointing to the need for social services to provide proactive support targeting these groups.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the social support networks of older adults in Slovenia before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. It examines the prevalence and characteristics of different types of social support networks, including informal support from relatives, friends, and neighbors, and how these networks have evolved over time, particularly in response to the pandemic.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study is a cross-sectional survey conducted in Slovenia in 2002, 2020, and 2025, collecting ego-centred network data from older adults (65+). The data were analyzed using clustering for symbolic data and correspondence analysis. The samples are representative of both gender and region.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identifies five distinct types of social support networks: family dependent, private restricted, local self-contained, locally integrated, and wider community network. It also notes the emergence of a group called 'no-listed alters' who reported no informal social support. The prevalence of these network types suggests that some were more affected by the pandemic, while others reflect longer-term demographic changes. By 2025, the share of older adults with no social support had dropped to 4.4%, indicating partial recovery.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Persistent inequalities in social support are observed, with men being more likely to experience social isolation. The review highlights the need for targeted social services to address these disparities. However, the evidence does not provide detailed mechanisms or explanations for these inequalities, nor does it explore the impact of specific SARS-CoV-2 variants on social support networks.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest that social services should focus on proactive support for socially isolated older adults, particularly men. Further research is needed to understand the underlying reasons for persistent inequalities and to explore how different SARS-CoV-2 variants may influence social support dynamics.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the social support networks of older adults in Slovenia from 2002 to 2025, with a focus on changes during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. It identifies five distinct network types and highlights the emergence of a group with no listed social support. While some network types were significantly impacted by the pandemic, others reflect long-term demographic shifts. By 2025, the proportion of older adults with no social support decreased to 4.4%, indicating partial recovery. However, persistent inequalities, particularly among men, suggest the need for targeted interventions. The review underscores the importance of understanding how social support networks evolve in response to public health crises and calls for further research to address disparities and explore the influence of SARS-CoV-2 variants on these networks.

title: Misinformation-based preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar: A cross-sectional study
abstract: Widespread misinformation influenced public understanding of disease risk and preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in low-resource and conflict-affected settings such as Myanmar. Although preventive behaviors were generally protective, some actions driven by misinformation may have been ineffective or harmful. Evidence on determinants of misinformation-based preventive behaviors remained limited. This study aimed to examine associations between misinformation-based preventive behaviors (MPB) and sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media use, and health belief factors in Myanmar. A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among adults residing in Myanmar, with data collected between March and May 2024. Participants were asked to retrospectively report their preventive behaviors during the COVID-19 pandemic period (2020–2022). Data were collected using a structured questionnaire adapted from previous COVID-19 studies. The outcome variable was misinformation-based preventive behaviors, categorized as low (0–2 behaviors) and high (3–4 behaviors) engagement. Independent variables included sociodemographic characteristics, information sources, social media platform use, and selected health belief variables based on the Health Belief Model (HBM). A total of 434 respondents were included in the analysis, of whom 106 (24.4%) reported high engagement in MPB. Use of social media platforms other than Facebook was associated with higher engagement (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 2.30, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.22–4.35). Participants reporting ≤3 hours and 4–6 hours of daily social media use had lower odds of MPB engagement compared with those reporting >6 hours (AOR = 0.46, 95% CI: 0.25–0.86; AOR = 0.48, 95% CI: 0.24–0.95, respectively). Higher self-efficacy was independently associated with greater engagement in MPB (AOR = 1.70, 95% CI: 1.03–2.82). MPB were more strongly associated with information environments and specific health beliefs than with sociodemographic characteristics alone. These findings underscore the importance of addressing misinformation and improving access to reliable health information to reduce engagement in non–evidence-based practices.

abstract: The epidemiology of influenza has shifted in recent years due to COVID-19 social restrictions.However, it remains unclear whether these findings apply to China, where a strict Zero-COVID policy was implemented.We evaluated influenza trends in Zhejiang Province, China from 2010-2023before, during, and after the strict policy.Specifically, using weekly surveillance data (2010-2023), we applied changepoint detection to identify structural shifts and interrupted time-series models to quantify policy impacts by comparing predicted (P) and observed (O) influenza cases based on differences (O -P) and ratios (P/O).Individual-level data (2017-2023; N=24,165 cases) were also analyzed for lineage and demographic shifts.A total of 4,295,302 influenza diagnoses occurred during the study period.During the policy, observed cases dropped by 248,781 cases in 2020 (P/O: 2.40; 95% prediction interval, 2.28 to 2.52), 204,619 in 2021 (1.72; 1.63 to 1.81), and 199,773 in 2022 (1.66; 1.58 to 1.76).Following policy relaxation in 2023, influenza cases exceeded expectations by 148,662 (0.8; 0.76 to 0.84); however, cases in children under 5 still declined by 22,388 (1.08; 1.04 to 1.12).B/Victoria lineage dominated early in the pandemic (>99% of cases in 2021), while influenza A/H3 (55%) and A/H1 (41%) emerged as the most prevalent strains by 2023.China's Zero-COVID policy was associated with changes in influenza transmission dynamics, with explosive outbreaks after relaxation except among young children.Changes in lineage predominance among lineages intensified during and after restrictions, with uncertain long-term implications.

analysis.summary_en: This observational study from Zhejiang, China, examines how the Zero-COVID policy impacted influenza trends between 2010 and 2023. The researchers used weekly surveillance data and individual-level case data to analyze changes in influenza cases and lineage predominance. They found that during the policy, observed cases dropped significantly in 2020, 2021, and 2022, but increased after relaxation in 2023, with declines in children under 5 persisting. The B/Victoria lineage dominated early in the pandemic, while A/H3 and A/H1 strains became more prevalent by 2023. The study suggests that the Zero-COVID policy altered influenza transmission dynamics, with potential long-term implications. However, the evidence is moderate due to reliance on observational data and possible confounding factors.

title: Gender differences regarding body image-related aspects in the general population during the COVID-19 pandemic: a systematic review
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted daily routines, physical activity, eating behaviors, and social interactions, all of which may have influenced body image. Previous research suggests that body image concerns differ by gender and may be particularly pronounced among sexual and gender minority (SGM) individuals, who face unique challenges due to internalized appearance ideals and societal stigma. This systematic review examined gender differences in body image-related concerns in the general adult population during the pandemic. Supported by: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (01KX2121). Methods This systematic review was preregistered (PROSPERO CRD42023421727) and conducted according to PRESS, PRISMA guidelines. Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, PsycINFO were searched for original studies published January 2019-July 2024. Studies were eligible if they 1) examined body image-related outcomes during the COVID-19 pandemic and reported gender-specific analyses in non-clinical adult populations. Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. Studies were narratively summarized according to body image-related constructs assessed and the reported gender-specific findings. Results Sixteen studies comprising 9,813 participants were included. Across most studies, women reported greater body dissatisfaction, weight and shape concerns, body shame and guilt, and dysmorphic concerns than men. Men generally reported lower body dissatisfaction and higher body satisfaction and were more likely to perceive their bodies as slimmer or more athletic. However, three studies found no significant gender differences, and one study reported higher body dissatisfaction among men. Longitudinal evidence suggested increases in body dissatisfaction among men over the course of the pandemic, whereas weight concerns decreased among women over time. One study found higher levels of weight- and body-related shame and guilt among gender minority participants compared with cisgender men, while another study reported no association between sexual orientation and body appreciation. Conclusions Women generally reported greater body image-related concerns than men during the COVID-19 pandemic, although findings were not entirely consistent across studies. Evidence regarding SGM individuals remains limited due to their underrepresentation in the literature. Additional longitudinal and gender diverse research is needed to better understand body image changes during public health crises and to inform targeted prevention and intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examined gender differences in body‐image concerns among adults during the COVID‐19 pandemic. Sixteen studies (9,813 participants) were identified through comprehensive database searches and assessed for quality. The prevailing evidence shows that women experienced greater body dissatisfaction, weight‐shape concerns, and related shame than men, while men reported higher body satisfaction and a slimmer self‐perception. However, a minority of studies reported no gender effect or even higher dissatisfaction in men, and data on sexual and gender minority groups are limited. Longitudinal insights are scarce, with only one report of rising dissatisfaction in men over time. The authors recommend additional longitudinal, gender‐inclusive investigations to better inform prevention and intervention efforts in future public‐health emergencies.

title: Investigation of anti-SARS-CoV-2 multimeric bicyclic peptide inhibitors in a range of preclinical therapeutic settings
abstract: ABSTRACT The spread of respiratory viruses, such as influenza and SARS-CoV-2, has presented significant challenges over the last 30 years, with few effective therapeutic options available to this day. Bicyclic peptides represent a unique, modular modality in the antiviral armamentarium against future pandemics. This study utilizes tool molecules to provide a deeper evaluation of multivalent bicyclic (Bicycle) molecule efficacy in several preclinical SARS-CoV-2 challenge settings. We explore both pre-exposure prophylaxis and post-exposure therapeutic settings via subcutaneous and intranasal routes of administration. We contextualize this further in bespoke scenarios where the immune system is compromised, as well as viral transmission. Promisingly, in all studies, we observe efficacy, significantly reducing infectious viral burden at each study endpoint. These data further support the candidacy of Bicycle molecules as a differentiated antiviral therapeutic class in the context of pandemic preparedness. IMPORTANCE The COVID-19 pandemic triggered a rapid wave of innovation, accelerating the delivery of new vaccine technology and antiviral treatments. In our first paper, we described the discovery and molecular optimization of Bicycle molecules as a novel drug class for the potential treatment of SARS-CoV-2. Here, we have performed deeper characterization of these tool molecules in established animal models to evaluate scenarios for deployment, simulating SARS-CoV-2 transmission, testing more convenient delivery routes, such as intranasal, as well as looking at immunocompromised animals. The Bicycle molecules demonstrated positive outcomes in each of these studies and suggest that Bicycle molecules, as convenient and effective antiviral treatments, could be an important addition to help future preparedness against new viral pandemics.

title: From Viral Detection to Disease Measurement: Lessons from COVID-19.
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic demonstrated a fundamental distinction between detecting an infectious stimulus and measuring the disease produced by that stimulus. SARS-CoV-2 establishes infection, whereas COVID-19 reflects the interaction among viral replication, host immunity, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, coagulation and tissue injury. These processes are related but are not interchangeable measurements. A positive molecular test establishes evidence of viral genetic material; it does not, by itself, quantify tissue injury, systemic thromboinflammation or disease severity. Similarly, individual biomarkers measure components of a biological response rather than necessarily defining the complete disease state. Clinical outcomes, including hospitalization and death, provide important measures of consequence but do not necessarily identify the mechanisms that produced them. COVID-19 therefore provides a case study in measurement fidelity: the quantity measured must be distinguished from the biological process that the investigator seeks to understand. title: Host-Directed p53 and NRF2 Co-Activation Reverses Acute COVID-19 and Long COVID Pathology by Restoring the miR-29 and miR-145 Epigenetic Axis
abstract: Abstract Despite over 524,592 COVID-19 papers indexed in PubMed as documented in our synthesis compilation and widespread vaccine deployment over the past six years, COVID-19 has caused more than 7.11 million officially reported deaths globally—with WHO excess mortality estimates reaching 14.83 million for 2020–2021 alone and cumulative excess death estimates spanning 18.5 to 35.2 million [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]—while leaving an estimated 400 million individuals worldwide with Long COVID (post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2, or PASC) at an approximate $1 trillion annual economic cost [1, 5]. To address the absence of a phase-independent mechanistic therapy, we propose and computationally evaluate a unified host-directed therapeutic framework centered on co-activating the cellular stress-response regulators p53 and NRF2 [1]. Across acute and post-acute phases, SARS-CoV-2 suppresses p53 and NRF2 signaling, depleting miR-29 (which harbors 11 conserved binding sites on the SARS-CoV-2 genome and directly targets IFNG) and miR-145 (which restrains Tissue Factor F3, Semaphorin-3A Sema3a, Granzyme K GZMK, and MYC) while hyperactivating NF-κB [1, 7, 8, 9, 10]. This upstream collapse drives persistent elevations in IFN-γ, Tissue Factor (TF), Sema3a, and Granzyme K (GzmK), promoting myocarditis, thromboembolism, myocardial dysfunction, and age-related tissue remodeling independently of age-associated immune dysfunction [1, 11, 12, 13]. Stiff ordinary differential equation (ODE) simulations (solve_ivp/BDF) parameterized from published turnover kinetics demonstrate that simulated p53/NRF2 co-activation induces a sharp bifurcation switch near an agonist threshold of Uth = 0.4–0.6 under persistent antigenic stimulation, producing a 13.75-fold recovery of miR-29 and a 54.39-fold recovery of miR-145 while suppressing NF-κB by 94.0% and reducing IFN-γ, TF, Sema3a, and GzmK by 98.3% to 99.1% in locked PASC steady states [14]. In an aggressive acute infection simulation (rv = 0.12 h-1), therapy initiated at 24 h lowers 168 h viral load by 46.2% and suppresses the four terminal effectors by 92.0% to 95.1% [14]. Because these quantitative dynamics derive from in silico modeling and cross-study synthesis, key evidentiary caveats remain—including incomplete extraction of individual duplex coordinates for all 11 miR-29 viral sites, cross-species differences in miR-145 validation for GZMK and Sema3a, compartment-specific p53 paradoxes, and the absence of prospective randomized trials testing combined p53/NRF2 agonism in PASC [1, 10, 15].

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of phase-independent mechanistic therapies for COVID-19 and Long COVID by proposing a host-directed therapeutic framework targeting p53 and NRF2 co-activation.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research involved in silico modeling and cross-study synthesis to evaluate the therapeutic potential of co-activating p53 and NRF2 across both acute and post-acute phases of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.methods: The study used stiff ordinary differential equation (ODE) simulations (solve_ivp/BDF) parameterized from published turnover kinetics to model the effects of p53/NRF2 co-activation on miR-29 and miR-145 dynamics and their downstream effectors.
analysis.main_results: Simulations showed that p53/NRF2 co-activation induced a sharp bifurcation switch near an agonist threshold of Uth = 0.4–0.6, resulting in a 13.75-fold recovery of miR-29, a 54.39-fold recovery of miR-145, and a 94.0% suppression of NF-κB, with reductions in IFN-γ, TF, Sema3a, and GzmK by 98.3% to 99.1% in locked PASC steady states.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that co-activating p53 and NRF2 can reverse the pathological effects of SARS-CoV-2 by restoring the miR-29 and miR-145 epigenetic axis, offering a novel therapeutic strategy for both acute and post-acute phases of infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest a potential new approach for treating both acute and long-term sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection, which could inform future research and therapeutic development for COVID-19 and related conditions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on in silico modeling and cross-study synthesis, with key caveats including incomplete extraction of miR-29 viral sites, cross-species differences in miR-145 validation, and the absence of prospective randomized trials, resulting in moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the lack of phase-independent mechanistic therapies for COVID-19 and Long COVID by proposing a host-directed therapeutic framework centered on co-activating p53 and NRF2. Using in silico modeling and cross-study synthesis, the authors demonstrate that co-activating these stress-response regulators can restore the miR-29 and miR-145 epigenetic axis, reversing the pathological effects of SARS-CoV-2. The simulations show significant recovery of miR-29 and miR-145 and suppression of key inflammatory effectors in locked PASC steady states. However, the study's reliance on computational models and absence of prospective randomized trials limit the confidence in its findings, resulting in a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

title: Intranasal azelastine for the treatment and prevention of SARS-CoV-2: A systematic review and exploratory meta-analysis of randomized trials
abstract: BACKGROUND Azelastine, a widely used H1-antihistamine with demonstrated antiviral and antiinflammatory activity against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) in preclinical and early clinical studies, has emerged as a potential repurposed therapy for early infection.This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intranasal azelastine for the treatment of established SARS-CoV-2 infection and the prevention of incident SARS-CoV-2 infection.AIM To systematically evaluate the randomized evidence on intranasal azelastine for the treatment of established SARS-CoV-2 infection and the prevention of incident SARS-CoV-2 infection, with particular emphasis on virological outcomes, prevention efficacy, and safety.METHODS PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library, together with trial registries and preprint servers, were searched through January 16, 2026.Randomized controlled trials evaluating intranasal azelastine vs placebo were identified through January 2026.Treatment efficacy was assessed using changes in SARS-CoV-2 viral load at predefined follow-up time points, while prevention efficacy was assessed using incident polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection.Safety outcomes were synthesized separately.Risk of bias was assessed using RoB-2 and certainty using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.Randomeffects meta-analysis was used where quantitative pooling was appropriate. RESULTS / 45Three randomized controlled trials involving 754 participants were included.Two treatment trials contributed to the viral-load analyses, while one prevention trial evaluated incident SARS-CoV-2 infection.Among the two treatment trials, moderatecertainty evidence suggested a greater reduction in SARS-CoV-2 viral load at day 3 [mean difference (MD): -0.18, 95% confidence interval (CI): -0.25 to -0.12; I2 = 0%].The difference was smaller at day 5/6 (MD: -0.11, 95%CI: -0.18 to -0.05; I2 = 0%) and was not statistically significant at day 11 (MD: -0.09, 95%CI: -0.26 to 0.07; I2 = 4%).In the prevention trial, PCR-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection occurred in 5/227 participants (2.2%) receiving azelastine vs 15/223 (6.7%) receiving placebo [risk ratio (RR): 0.33, 95%CI: 0.12-0.89].Treatment-only all-adverse event pooling showed RR 0.85 (95%CI: 0.56-1.27;I2 = 61%), whereas the prevention trial showed RR 2.25 (95%CI: 1.64-3.09). CONCLUSIONModerate-certainty evidence suggested an early virological difference with intranasal azelastine in established SARS-CoV-2 infection, particularly at day 3, although the clinical relevance of this surrogate outcome remains uncertain.Evidence for prevention was based on a single randomized trial, while safety findings differed between treatment and prevention populations.Overall, the available evidence is exploratory and insufficient to establish clinical benefit on patient-important outcomes.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examined the efficacy and safety of intranasal azelastine for treating established SARS‐CoV‐2 infection and preventing incident infection, focusing on virological outcomes, prevention efficacy, and safety in randomized trials.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library through January 16, 2026 identified randomized controlled trials comparing intranasal azelastine to placebo; risk of bias was assessed with RoB‐2 and certainty with GRADE, and random‐effects meta‐analysis was employed where appropriate.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Moderate‐certainty evidence indicated a greater reduction in SARS‐CoV‐2 viral load at day 3 with intranasal azelastine in established infection, though the clinical relevance of this surrogate outcome remains uncertain.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence for prevention was limited to a single randomized trial, and safety findings varied between treatment and prevention populations, underscoring the exploratory nature of the data.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The current evidence is insufficient to confirm clinical benefit on patient‐important outcomes, highlighting the need for larger, well‐designed trials to clarify efficacy and safety.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and exploratory meta‐analysis evaluated intranasal azelastine for treating and preventing SARS‐CoV‐2 infection. Searches of major databases up to January 2026 yielded three randomized controlled trials (754 participants). Meta‐analysis showed a modest, statistically significant reduction in viral load at day 3 in treatment trials, but the effect waned by day 5/6 and was not significant by day 11. A single prevention trial suggested a 67 % relative risk reduction in PCR‐confirmed infection, yet safety outcomes differed between treatment and prevention groups. Overall, moderate‐certainty evidence points to an early virological benefit, yet the clinical relevance is unclear, and the limited number of trials and heterogeneous safety data preclude definitive conclusions. Further large, rigorously designed studies are required to determine whether intranasal azelastine offers meaningful patient‐important benefits.

title: A monoclonal antibody panel to track antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 JN.1 subvariants
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 continues to evolve, generating successive variants with enhanced resistance to antibody-mediated neutralization. However, many existing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) were derived from ancestral or early Omicron strains and have lost activity against recent variants, limiting their ability to resolve the antigenic effects of mutations arising in emerging lineages. Here, we generated a mAb panel by immunizing naive, unimprinted VelocImmune mice with the KP.3.1.1 spike, and isolated and characterized 11 human neutralizing antibodies targeting diverse epitopes of evolved variants. We then integrated these antibodies with characterized mAbs to establish a toolbox for profiling antigenic evolution among emerging variants. Application of this panel to emerging variants provided mechanistic insight into recent antigenic evolution, highlighting the potential role of altered receptor-binding domain conformation. Our data also revealed clear differences in antibody-evasion profiles between JN.1-derived lineages and BA.3.2 lineages. Together, our findings establish an updated mAb panel for monitoring antigenic evolution of JN.1 subvariants.

title: Methods to Account for Competing Events With Unknown Duration in Health Policy Evaluations: The Case of COVID-19.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare methods for estimating policy effects in the presence of competing events such as COVID-19. STUDY SETTING AND DESIGN: We created a simulation study to evaluate how single interrupted time series (ITS) and comparative interrupted time series (CITS) estimators performed when policy implementation occurred near a competing event (COVID-19). The onset of the competing event was known (March 2020) but the duration was unknown. ITS approaches included assuming different COVID-19 durations (ITS-Assume) or searching for the COVID-19 duration that provided the best fit to the data (ITS-Grid Search). Outcomes included percent bias, power, and Type 1 error. DATA SOURCES AND ANALYTIC SAMPLE: We varied the duration of COVID-19 effects, the time between the policy implementation and COVID-19 onset, and the magnitude and sign of the policy effects relative to COVID-19 (2080 scenarios). Each simulated time series had 99 monthly observations (October 2015-December 2023). PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: CITS had the lowest bias and Type 1 error and had high power across scenarios, except for intercept changes and when assumptions about shared COVID-19 effects between treatment and control groups were violated. ITS-Grid Search had lower bias and Type 1 error than ITS-Assume, which produced biased parameter estimates when the assumptions were incorrect. Estimates were more accurate when the policy was implemented prior to the competing event. CONCLUSIONS: Using estimation approaches that leverage control groups, such as CITS, can mitigate the potential bias of competing events in ITS frameworks, but these approaches are biased when competing event effects differ between treatment and control groups. Searching for the best-fitting competing event duration does not require a control group and outperforms methods that assume the duration of competing event effects a priori. More generally, researchers should be cautious about bias, specification error, and low power when using ITS methods with competing events.
