analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare methods for estimating policy effects in the presence of competing events such as COVID-19. The background highlights the need for robust analytical approaches to account for competing events with unknown durations in health policy evaluations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A simulation study was conducted to evaluate the performance of single interrupted time series (ITS) and comparative interrupted time series (CITS) estimators when policy implementation occurred near a competing event, specifically COVID-19. The study included 2080 scenarios with varying durations of COVID-19 effects, time between policy implementation and COVID-19 onset, and magnitudes of policy effects.
analysis.methods: The methods involved creating simulated time series with 99 monthly observations from October 2015 to December 2023. Two ITS approaches were tested: one assuming different durations of COVID-19 effects (ITS-Assume) and another using grid search to find the best-fitting duration (ITS-Grid Search). Outcomes measured were percent bias, power, and Type 1 error.
analysis.main_results: CITS had the lowest bias and Type 1 error and maintained high power across scenarios, except for intercept changes and when assumptions about shared COVID-19 effects between treatment and control groups were violated. ITS-Grid Search showed lower bias and Type 1 error than ITS-Assume, which produced biased estimates when assumptions were incorrect.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that estimation approaches leveraging control groups, like CITS, can reduce bias from competing events in ITS frameworks. They noted that ITS-Grid Search outperforms methods assuming a priori durations without requiring a control group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the cautious use of ITS methods in health policy evaluations involving competing events like COVID-19, emphasizing the importance of control groups and adaptive duration estimation to improve accuracy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on simulated data and the assumption that policy effects and competing events can be quantified. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a simulation study without real-world validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates methods for estimating policy effects in the presence of competing events like COVID-19, focusing on interrupted time series (ITS) and comparative ITS (CITS) approaches. It highlights that CITS reduces bias and Type 1 error, while ITS-Grid Search outperforms ITS-Assume in duration estimation. The results suggest that ITS methods should be used cautiously, especially when competing events have unknown durations. The study's findings have implications for improving the accuracy of health policy evaluations during pandemics. However, the reliance on simulated data and assumptions about policy effects limits the strength of the evidence.

title: Comparison of methodological approaches in COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness estimation using observational data
abstract: Abstract Background: Target trial emulation (TTE) is a framework to systematically address potential design-related biases in causal inference when using observational data. We estimated vaccine effectiveness (VE) of the Omicron XBB.1.5 booster vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 infection between 2 October 2023 and 2 April 2024 using four TTE approaches. Methods: A hypothetical target trial was designed where eligible participants would be randomly assigned to receive booster vaccination or not. Four approaches were used to emulate this hypothetical trial using data of an ongoing prospective cohort study in the Netherlands. The first and second approach defined time zero as the start of the booster vaccination rollout and considered vaccination as a time-varying variable. The first approach adjusted for confounders by regression adjustment, while the second used inverse probability weighting. The third and fourth approach used multiple time zeros. In the third approach, all persons who received a booster vaccination on a specific day were matched 1:1 to persons who were not (yet) vaccinated on that day. In the fourth approach, confounders were adjusted for using inverse probability weighting. Results: Overall VE was 30% (95%CI:26-34), 28% (24-32), 25% (18-30) and 27% (24-31) in the first, second, third and fourth approach, respectively. VE decreased as time since vaccination increased. Conclusions: Estimated VE was similar across the four approaches. The choice of approach should be based on the model assumptions, estimand of interest, and feasibility.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used observational data from an ongoing prospective cohort study in the Netherlands, estimating VE of the Omicron XBB.1.5 booster vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 infection between 2 October 2023 and 2 April 2024.
analysis.methods: A hypothetical target trial was designed where participants were randomly assigned to receive booster vaccination or not, and four approaches were used to emulate this trial using the cohort data.
analysis.main_results: Overall VE was 30% (95%CI:26-34), 28% (24-32), 25% (18-30) and 27% (24-31) in the first, second, third and fourth approach, respectively. VE decreased as time since vaccination increased.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the estimated VE was similar across the four approaches, highlighting the importance of selecting an approach based on model assumptions, estimand of interest, and feasibility.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the choice of methodological approaches for estimating vaccine effectiveness in observational studies, which is critical for public health decision-making and vaccine policy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-only evidence, and the estimated VE values are based on hypothetical trial emulation, which may not fully capture real-world complexities. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares four methodological approaches for estimating vaccine effectiveness (VE) of the Omicron XBB.1.5 booster against SARS-CoV-2 infection using observational data from a Dutch cohort. The approaches included regression adjustment, inverse probability weighting, and varying definitions of time zero. Overall VE estimates ranged from 25% to 30%, with a decline over time since vaccination. The authors concluded that VE estimates were similar across methods, emphasizing the need to select approaches based on model assumptions and feasibility. The study's findings have implications for improving VE estimation in observational studies, which is important for public health decision-making. However, the evidence is based solely on abstract data, limiting the confidence in the results to a moderate level.

abstract_zh: 摘要背景:目标试验仿真(TTE)是一个框架,用于系统地解决使用观察数据时因果推理中潜在的设计相关偏差。我们使用四种 TTE 方法估计了 2023 年 10 月 2 日至 2024 年 4 月 2 日期间 Omicron XBB.1.5 加强剂 疫苗接种 对抗 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的 疫苗 有效性 (VE)。方法:设计了一项假设的目标试验,其中合格的参与者将被随机分配接受或不接受加强 疫苗接种。使用荷兰正在进行的前瞻性 队列研究 研究的数据,使用四种方法来模拟这一假设试验。第一种和第二种方法将零时间定义为增强器 疫苗接种 推出的开始,并将 疫苗接种 视为随时间变化的变量。第一种方法通过回归调整来调整混杂因素,而第二种方法则使用逆概率加权。第三种和第四种方法使用多个时间零。在第三种方法中,所有在特定日期接受加强疫苗 疫苗接种 的人都与当天(尚未)接种疫苗的人进行 1:1 匹配。在第四种方法中,使用逆概率加权调整混杂因素。结果:第一种、第二种、第三种和第四种方法的总体 VE 分别为 30% (95%CI:26-34)、28% (24-32)、25% (18-30) 和 27% (24-31)。VE 随着 疫苗接种 时间的增加而减少。结论:四种方法的估计 VE 相似。方法的选择应基于模型假设、兴趣估计和可行性。

title: Glycoform Distributions and Heparan Sulfate Binding of Intact SARS-CoV-2 Spike Variants by DIA-ECCR Native Mass Spectrometry
abstract: Glycosylation influences the structure, immunogenicity, and evolutionary selection of the SARS CoV 2 spike protein (S), but its extensive heterogeneity has hindered characterization of intact glycoform distributions. Here, we illustrate a data-independent analysis - electron capture charge reduction (DIA-ECCR) native mass spectrometry workflow for direct analysis of intact spike glycoforms across multiple variants. DIA-ECCR resolves variant-dependent differences in glycoform distributions and higher mass subpopulations. Monte Carlo simulations based on published site-specific bottom-up glycoproteomic data reproduce the central mass of the D614G experimental distribution and support a connection between intact and bottom-up measurements, while the broader experimental distributions and a second Gamma subpopulation indicate heterogeneity not captured by the simulations Mass photometry and charge detection mass spectrometry provide orthogonal measurements consistent with the DIA-ECCR results. DIA-ECCR also resolves mass shifts associated with binding of truncated heparan sulfate, demonstrating analysis of a heterogeneous protein:ligand complex. Together, these results outline a practical workflow that combines DIA-ECCR with native mass spectrometry (nMS) for characterizing intact glycoform distributions and ligand binding in highly heterogeneous glycoprotein assemblies, with potential applications in antigen characterization, vaccine design, and biopharmaceutical quality control.

The study also demonstrates the analysis of a heterogeneous protein:ligand complex formed with truncated heparan sulfate. These findings outline a practical workflow for characterizing glycoform distributions and ligand binding, with potential applications in vaccine design and biopharmaceutical quality control. The study notes that Monte Carlo simulations may not fully capture the observed heterogeneity, highlighting the need for further validation with additional methods.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决表征 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 中糖型分布的广泛异质性的挑战,这阻碍了对其结构、免疫原性和进化选择的理解。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究引入了数据独立分析 - 电子捕获电荷还原 (DIA-ECCR) 原生质谱工作流程,可直接分析多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的完整刺突糖型。
analysis_zh.methods: 该研究利用 DIA-ECCR 天然质谱法来解决糖型分布和较高质量亚群中变异依赖性的差异,并使用基于位点特异性自下而上糖蛋白质组数据的蒙特卡罗模拟来支持研究结果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 蒙特卡洛模拟再现了 D614G 实验分布的中心质量,并支持完整测量和自下而上测量之间的联系,而更广泛的实验分布和第二个伽马亚群表明模拟未捕获的异质性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果证明了 DIA-ECCR 在分析异质蛋白:配体复合物(例如用截短的硫酸乙酰肝素形成的复合物)方面的实用性,并概述了表征糖型分布和配体结合的实用工作流程。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现在抗原表征、疫苗 设计和生物制药质量控制方面具有潜在应用,为了解 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 的结构和功能多样性提供了见解。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究承认蒙特卡罗模拟可能无法完全捕捉到实验分布中观察到的异质性,这表明需要使用其他方法进一步验证以加强证据。

title: Rising Tuberculosis Presentations in Ontario, Canada Are Not Explained by Community SARS-CoV-2 Activity: A Population-Based Time-Series Study
abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) notifications have increased in several high-income countries since 2020. Proposed explanations include pandemic related disruption of treatment for latent tuberculosis, changes in population composition, and immune dysfunction following SARS CoV 2 infection. We assessed whether TB presentations increased during the pandemic era and then tested whether community SARS CoV 2 activity was followed by increased mycobacterial disease. Methods: We conducted a population-based ecological time-series study of first TB- and nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM)-coded hospital, emergency-department and ambulatory clinic presentations in the Greater Toronto/Hamilton Area Plus (GTHA+), Ontario (2024 population approximately 11.2 million), from April 2011 through March 2024. NTM served as a comparator because it shares diagnostic pathways with TB but differs epidemiologically. Negative binomial projection and full-series models estimated pandemic-era changes under three alternative trend assumptions. Distributed lag non linear models estimated cumulative rate ratios for standardized community viral activity over 0 to 12 weeks; sensitivity analyses extended the maximum lag to 26 and 52 weeks. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were prespecified comparators; data for five additional viral exposures were obtained after the primary analysis was completed and analysed as exploratory comparisons. Results: We identified 3,985 first TB-coded and 5,214 first NTM-coded acute-care presentations. Across six models, estimated pandemic-era TB increases ranged from 3% to 22%. No model suggested an increased in NTM. SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with TB (cumulative rate ratio per 1-SD increase over 0 to 12 weeks 0.909, 95% CI 0.822 to 1.006) or NTM (0.953, 0.868 to 1.047). No positive associations were identified in subgroup analyses or with maximum lags of 26 or 52 weeks. Influenza was not associated with either outcome. RSV was associated with TB and NTM; only the RSV/NTM association met the Bonferroni threshold among the prespecified comparisons, and no exploratory associations met the experiment wide threshold. Conclusions: We identified a modest pandemic era increase in TB-coded acute-care presentations in Ontario, Canada, although its estimated size depended on assumptions about underlying trends. NTM-coded presentations did not increase. Community SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with subsequent TB or NTM presentations at lags of up to one year and did not provide a temporal explanation for the population-level TB increase. Individual-level effects cannot be excluded.

title: Application of a Human Nasal Mucosa Ex Vivo Culture System to Model Inflammatory Responses
abstract: Introduction The nasal cavity is the entry point of the upper respiratory tract and the primary site of inflammatory responses to inhaled pathogens. Methods Human nasal mucosa (HNM) tissues were obtained from patients undergoing endoscopic nasal surgery. Six HNM specimens from patients with house dust mite (HDM)-allergic rhinitis were used for paired Der p 1 challenge experiments, and 8 chronic rhinosinusitis–derived HNM specimens were used for paired SARS-CoV-2 infection experiments. Histology, Reverse Transcription Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction, Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and bulk RNA sequencing were performed at the indicated time points. Results Cultured HNM maintained structural and functional integrity during short-term ex vivo culture. HDM stimulation enhanced secretory activity and induced IL-4 and IL-5 expression at day 3. Both SARS-CoV-2 variants (HU-1 and Omicron BA.2) produced detectable viral RNA and viral N-protein signals in HNM expressing Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 and Transmembrane Protease Serine 2. Viral inoculation induced an interferon-associated antiviral response, which was most pronounced following HU-1 exposure, although between-variant differences in the measured antiviral markers were not significant. At 3 days postinfection under standardized infection conditions, HU-1 showed higher viral RNA burden and more marked epithelial injury than BA.2 at day 3. Discussion The ex vivo HNM model preserved key structural and cellular features of native nasal mucosa, including an intact epithelial barrier, stromal immune cells, and glandular components, supporting its use as a tissue-level platform that complements conventional 2-dimensional cultures. HDM-sensitized HNM showed Der p 1-associated type 2 responses, whereas the viral arm revealed an antiviral response and exploratory variant-associated differences in epithelial injury. Conclusions Short-term ex vivo HNM may provide a practical tissue-level platform for investigating upper-airway responses to allergen exposure and SARS-CoV-2 infection. It preserves multicellular tissue architecture, while further validation in larger, better-stratified cohorts and extended culture optimization will support broader mechanistic and translational application.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to model inflammatory responses in the nasal cavity to inhaled pathogens, focusing on the role of the nasal mucosa as the primary site of such responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used six human nasal mucosa specimens from patients with house dust mite (HDM)-allergic rhinitis and eight chronic rhinosinusitis-derived specimens for SARS-CoV-2 infection experiments.
analysis.methods: Histology, Reverse Transcription Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction, Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay, and bulk RNA sequencing were performed at the indicated time points to assess tissue responses.
analysis.main_results: Cultured HNM maintained structural and functional integrity during short-term ex vivo culture. At 3 days postinfection, HU-1 showed higher viral RNA burden and more marked epithelial injury than BA.2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The ex vivo HNM model preserved key structural and cellular features of native nasal mucosa, supporting its use as a tissue-level platform for studying upper-airway responses to allergens and SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that this ex vivo model could be valuable for understanding and developing strategies to combat upper-airway inflammation caused by SARS-CoV-2 and allergens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's results are based on a small sample size and short-term culture, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong given the direct observation of viral RNA and antiviral responses in HNM.

analysis.summary_en: This study applied an ex vivo human nasal mucosa culture system to model inflammatory responses to inhaled pathogens, specifically allergens and SARS-CoV-2. The research aimed to investigate how nasal tissues respond to allergen exposure and viral infection, with a focus on preserving tissue architecture and function. Six HNM specimens from patients with allergic rhinitis were used for Der p 1 challenge experiments, while eight from chronic rhinosinusitis patients were used for SARS-CoV-2 infection experiments. The methods included histology, RT-qPCR, ELISA, and bulk RNA sequencing. Results showed that cultured HNM maintained structural and functional integrity, and SARS-CoV-2 variants HU-1 and BA.2 induced detectable viral RNA and N-protein signals. HU-1 caused higher viral RNA burden and more epithelial injury than BA.2. The authors interpreted these findings as supporting the use of the HNM model for studying upper-airway responses, highlighting its preservation of key features like the epithelial barrier and immune cells. The study's significance lies in its potential to inform surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment strategies for SARS-CoV-2 and allergen-related inflammation. However, the small sample size and short-term culture limit the generalizability of the results, though the evidence is considered strong due to direct observations.

abstract_zh: 简介 鼻腔是上呼吸道的入口点,也是吸入病原体炎症反应的主要部位。方法从接受内窥镜鼻手术的患者身上获取人鼻粘膜(HNM)组织。来自房尘螨 (HDM) 过敏性鼻炎患者的 6 个 HNM 标本用于配对 Der p 1 攻击实验,8 个慢性鼻窦炎衍生的 HNM 标本用于配对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染实验。在指定时间点进行组织学、逆转录定量聚合酶链反应、酶联免疫吸附测定和批量 RNA 测序。结果培养的 HNM 在短期离体培养过程中保持了结构和功能的完整性。HDM 刺激增强了分泌活性,并在第 3 天诱导了 IL-4 和 IL-5 表达。两种 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体(HU-1 和 Omicron BA.2)在表达血管紧张素转换酶 2 和跨膜蛋白酶丝氨酸 2 的 HNM 中产生了可检测到的病毒 RNA 和病毒 N 蛋白信号。病毒接种诱导了干扰素相关的 抗病毒药物 反应,该反应在以下情况下最为明显HU-1 暴露,尽管测量的 抗病毒药物 标记的变体间差异并不显着。在标准化感染条件下感染后 3 天,HU-1 在第 3 天表现出比 BA.2 更高的病毒 RNA 负荷和更明显的上皮损伤。讨论离体 HNM 模型保留了天然鼻粘膜的关键结构和细胞特征,包括完整的上皮屏障、基质免疫细胞和腺体成分,支持其用作补充传统二维培养物的组织水平平台。HDM 致敏的 HNM 显示出与 Der p 1 相关的 2 型反应,而病毒臂则显示出 抗病毒药物 反应以及探索性变异相关的上皮损伤差异。结论 短期离体 HNM 可能为研究上呼吸道对过敏原暴露和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的反应提供实用的组织水平平台。它保留了多细胞组织结构,同时在更大、更好分层的 队列研究 和扩展培养优化中进一步验证将支持更广泛的机械和转化应用。

title: Post-COVID-19 Emergence and Spread of Hypertransmissible Cryptosporidium hominis gp60 Subtype IfA12G1R5, Spain.
abstract: COVID-19 pandemic containment measures in 2020 selectively altered established Cryptosporidium hominis anthroponotic transmission in Spain. Rapid emergence and expansion of hypertransmissible human-adapted gp60 subtypes such as IfA12G1R5 and, less markedly, IbA13G3 followed. Conversely, transmission of the largely zoonotic C. parvum remained comparatively stable, yielding a dual epidemiologic scenario in this country.

title: Persistent Fungal Mortality in the United States Following the COVID-19 Pandemic Peak, 2022-2025.
abstract: Objectives: Fungal infection–associated deaths increased in the United States during the COVID-19 pandemic, but mortality patterns after the pandemic peak are not well-characterized. We analyzed national mortality data to assess whether fungal mortality remained elevated during 2022-2025 and to describe demographic, geographic, pathogen-specific, and underlying cause-of-death patterns after the COVID-19 pandemic peak. Methods: We analyzed National Vital Statistics System multiple-cause-of-death data for 2022-2025. We defined fungal deaths as deaths with a fungal pathogen listed as an underlying or contributing cause of death and summarized deaths by year, month, pathogen, COVID-19 association, underlying cause of death, demographic characteristics, and US Census division. We used 2018-2019 (prepandemic) and 2021 (peak) as reference periods for selected comparisons. Results: During 2022-2025, a total of 30 225 fungal deaths occurred (annual average = 7556). The annual age-adjusted mortality rate per 100 000 population increased from 1.2 in 2018-2019 to 1.5 in 2020 and 1.9 in 2021, and remained between 1.8 and 1.9 during 2022-2025. COVID-19–associated fungal deaths declined after early 2022, but overall fungal mortality remained stable. During 2022-2025, the most common underlying causes of death among fungal deaths were malignant neoplasms, HIV disease, and diseases of the heart; the most commonly specified pathogens were Candida and Aspergillus . Mortality rates varied by age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region. Conclusions: Fungal mortality remained elevated after the COVID-19 pandemic peak despite declines in COVID-19–associated fungal deaths. Continued efforts to monitor fungal disease–related mortality are important to inform efforts to enhance diagnostic capacity and surveillance to better characterize and ultimately reduce the impact of fungal diseases.

title: Genomic surveillance reveals age-structured SARS-CoV-2 transmission across settings.
abstract: Understanding respiratory virus transmission requires integrating pathogen genomic data with detailed epidemiological context. We analyzed >85,000 SARS-CoV-2 genomes linked to epidemiological data collected in Massachusetts from November 2021 to January 2023. Collected in 666 settings, including schools, colleges, and skilled nursing facilities, this dataset enabled direct comparison of within-setting transmission to community-wide risk. Elevated transmission was concentrated in specific age-defined subpopulations-older adolescents in schools, undergraduates in colleges, and residents in nursing facilities-with little additional risk among other groups, notably including staff. Young adults, particularly in colleges, played a disproportionate role in spread, and new viral lineages consistently expanded first within this group. Viral spread followed reproducible urban-to-rural gradients, and vaccination was associated with reduced onward transmission. We further estimated sequencing thresholds required for timely detection of emerging variants. Together, these findings reveal consistent demographic and spatial structure in SARS-CoV-2 transmission that can inform viral respiratory pathogen genomic surveillance.

title_zh: 基因组监测 揭示了跨设置的年龄结构 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 传播。
source_body_en: Understanding respiratory virus transmission requires integrating pathogen genomic data with detailed epidemiological context. We analyzed >85,000 SARS-CoV-2 genomes linked to epidemiological data collected in Massachusetts from November 2021 to January 2023. Collected in 666 settings, including schools, colleges, and skilled nursing facilities, this dataset enabled direct comparison of within-setting transmission to community-wide risk. Elevated transmission was concentrated in specific age-defined subpopulations-older adolescents in schools, undergraduates in colleges, and residents in nursing facilities-with little additional risk among other groups, notably including staff. Young adults, particularly in colleges, played a disproportionate role in spread, and new viral lineages consistently expanded first within this group. Viral spread followed reproducible urban-to-rural gradients, and vaccination was associated with reduced onward transmission. We further estimated sequencing thresholds required for timely detection of emerging variants. Together, these findings reveal consistent demographic and spatial structure in SARS-CoV-2 transmission that can inform viral respiratory pathogen genomic surveillance.

title: Neurological manifestations in pediatric COVID-19: a comparative single-center study.
abstract: Objective To compare clinical characteristics, investigations, management, and outcomes of hospitalized children with SARS-CoV-2 infection with and without neurological involvement, and to determine whether neurological disease reflects systemic severity or a distinct clinical pattern. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study of children aged 1 month-16 years with laboratory-confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection admitted to a tertiary pediatric center between June 2022 and June 2023. Patients were divided into those with neurological manifestations (ND group, n = 24) and those without neurological involvement (non-ND group, n = 23). Demographic features, clinical presentation, laboratory and neuroimaging findings, treatment, and outcomes were compared. Results Children with neurological involvement were significantly older (median 5.75 vs. 3.00 years, p = 0.022) and less likely to present with fever or systemic inflammatory features. They demonstrated lower inflammatory markers and significantly less cardiac involvement, including dilated cardiomyopathy. Common neurological presentations included encephalopathy (50%), headache (45.8%), and seizures (20.8%). 37% met MIS-C criteria. Neuroimaging revealed lacunar infarctions, demyelinating white matter lesions, longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis, and cauda equina nerve root enhancement. Despite similar mortality rates, children with neurological involvement had a significantly higher rate of incomplete recovery, with more than a quarter experiencing persistent neurological sequelae (29.2% vs. Conclusion Neurological manifestations of pediatric COVID-19 represent a clinically distinct pattern characterized by limited systemic inflammation but an increased risk of persistent neurological sequelae. Early neurological evaluation, appropriate neuroimaging, and structured long-term follow-up are warranted even in the absence of severe systemic illness.

elements_zh.main_results: 患有神经系统受累的儿童年龄明显较大(中位数为 5.75 岁与 3.00 岁,p = 0.022),并且不太可能出现发烧或全身炎症特征。他们表现出较低的炎症标志物和显着较少的心脏受累,包括扩张型心肌病。神经影像显示腔隙性梗死、脱髓鞘性白质病变、纵向广泛的横贯性脊髓炎和马尾神经根增强。尽管 死亡率 发生率相似,但神经系统受累儿童的不完全恢复率显着较高,超过四分之一的儿童出现持续性神经系统后遗症(29.2% vs. 29.2%)。

title: Disparities During the COVID-19 Pandemic in SARS-CoV-2 Testing Increased After a Federal Government's At-Home Testing Distribution Program Compared with Before in a U.S. Urban Setting.
abstract: Diagnostic testing is essential for controlling the transmission of infectious diseases. During the COVID-19 pandemic, testing became widely available in the United States. However, the association between a federal at-home COVID-19 rapid antigen test distribution program and sociodemographics and COVID-19 testing remains unknown. This secondary analysis aims to (1) assess the association between the federal at-home testing program and testing uptake and (2) examine associations, including interactions with the testing program, between sociodemographic characteristics, testing experience, and COVID-19 testing. We analyzed baseline data collected from February 2021 to November 2022 in a randomized comparative effectiveness parent trial conducted in a mid-Atlantic U.S. Logistic regression models with robust standard errors were used. Overall, 79.9% (1486) of participants reported receiving a COVID-19 test. Exposure to the federal testing program (odds ratio [OR] = 2.25; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.61, 3.13), higher education (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 1.02, 1.80), private health insurance (OR = 2.03; 95% CI: 1.41, 2.92), higher household income (OR = 1.49; 95% CI: 1.06, 2.09), and ease of testing access (OR = 1.40; 95% CI: 1.04, 1.87) were significantly associated with testing. After adjustment, private insurance (adjusted OR [aOR] = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.12, 2.31) and higher income (aOR = 1.50; 95% CI: 1.12, 2.02) remained associated with testing. The adjusted odds of COVID-19 testing were 2-fold higher (aOR = 2.21; 95% CI: 1.21, 4.04) for high-income (vs. low-income) households during the federal at-home COVID-19 rapid antigen testing program than before its implementation. Disparities in COVID-19 testing by socioeconomic status increased during the federal testing program compared with the period before its implementation. Ensuring equitable access to diagnostic testing remains critical for an effective public health response.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines how a federal at-home SARS-CoV-2 rapid antigen test distribution program affected disparities in testing during the COVID-19 pandemic in a U.S. urban setting. title_zh: Disparities During the COVID-19 Pandemic in SARS-CoV-2 Testing Increased After a Federal Government's At-Home Testing Distribution Program Compared with Before in a U.S. Urban Setting.
source_body_en: Diagnostic testing is essential for controlling the transmission of infectious diseases. During the COVID-19 pandemic, testing became widely available in the United States. However, the association between a federal at-home COVID-19 rapid antigen test distribution program and sociodemographics and COVID-19 testing remains unknown. This secondary analysis aims to (1) assess the association between the federal at-home testing program and testing uptake and (2) examine associations, including interactions with the testing program, between sociodemographic characteristics, testing experience, and COVID-19 testing. We analyzed baseline data collected from February 2021 to November 2022 in a randomized comparative effectiveness parent trial conducted in a mid-Atlantic U.S. Logistic regression models with robust standard errors were used. Overall, 79.9% (1486) of participants reported receiving a COVID-19 test. Exposure to the federal testing program (odds ratio [OR] = 2.25; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.61, 3.13), higher education (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 1.02, 1.80), private health insurance (OR = 2.03; 95% CI: 1.41, 2.92), higher household income (OR = 1.49; 95% CI: 1.06, 2.09), and ease of testing access (OR = 1.40; 95% CI: 1.04, 1.87) were significantly associated with testing. After adjustment, private insurance (adjusted OR [aOR] = 1.61; 95% CI: 1.12, 2.31) and higher income (aOR = 1.50; 95% CI: 1.12, 2.02) remained associated with testing. The adjusted odds of COVID-19 testing were 2-fold higher (aOR = 2.21; 95% CI: 1.21, 4.04) for high-income (vs. low-income) households during the federal at-home COVID-19 rapid antigen testing program than before its implementation. Disparities in COVID-19 testing by socioeconomic status increased during the federal testing program compared with the period before its implementation. Ensuring equitable access to diagnostic testing remains critical for an effective public health response.

title: First-hand Alcohol-Related Harms in Hong Kong University Dormitories: A Serial Cross-sectional Study Comparing the Normative, Social Unrest, and COVID-19 Pandemic Periods.
abstract: Between September 2018 and June 2021, we conducted serial cross-sectional surveys of university dormitory residents in Hong Kong (n = 2659). Drinking behaviors and first-hand harms were examined across a normative period, time of protests, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Drinking levels remained steady between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic, and the proportions reporting drinking-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5%, respectively. Binge drinking was associated with high first-hand harms across 3 periods (adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 3.46-5.76). Having a drinking roommate was also correlated with harms during the normative period (AOR = 1.66). During the protests, underage drinking history and university location were associated with high first-hand harms (AOR: 1.69 and 1.82). During the COVID-19 pandemic, weekend dormitory residence and low alcohol-related knowledge were significant factors (AOR: 2.78 and 2.85). The findings indicate the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study examines first-hand alcohol-related harms among university dormitory residents in Hong Kong during three distinct periods: the normative period, the time of social unrest (protests), and the COVID-19 pandemic. The central question is whether alcohol-related behaviors and their associated harms differ across these periods.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study is a serial cross-sectional survey conducted between September 2018 and June 2021, involving 2659 participants. It compares drinking behaviors and first-hand harms across three time periods: normative, social unrest, and the pandemic. The methodology includes statistical analysis of associations using adjusted odds ratios.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that drinking levels remained stable between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic. The proportions of participants reporting alcohol-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5% for the normative, protest, and pandemic periods, respectively. Binge drinking was consistently associated with higher first-hand harms across all three periods.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study does not provide detailed information on the mechanisms linking alcohol consumption to first-hand harms or on the effectiveness of interventions. It also does not explore the role of cultural or policy factors in shaping drinking behaviors during these periods.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories, particularly during periods of social and health crises like the pandemic.

analysis.summary_en: This serial cross-sectional study conducted between September 2018 and June 2021 analyzed alcohol-related harms among university dormitory residents in Hong Kong during three distinct periods: the normative period, the time of social unrest (protests), and the COVID-19 pandemic. The study found that drinking levels remained stable between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic. The proportions of participants reporting alcohol-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5% for the normative, protest, and pandemic periods, respectively. Binge drinking was consistently associated with higher first-hand harms across all three periods. The study highlights the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories, especially during health and social crises. However, it does not explore the underlying mechanisms or the effectiveness of interventions.

The central question is whether alcohol-related behaviors and their associated harms differ across these periods.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study is a serial cross-sectional survey conducted between September 2018 and June 2021, involving 2659 participants. It compares drinking behaviors and first-hand harms across three time periods: normative, social unrest, and the pandemic. The methodology includes statistical analysis of associations using adjusted odds ratios.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The study found that drinking levels remained stable between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic. The proportions of participants reporting alcohol-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5% for the normative, protest, and pandemic periods, respectively. Binge drinking was consistently associated with higher first-hand harms across all three periods.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study does not provide detailed information on the mechanisms linking alcohol consumption to first-hand harms or on the effectiveness of interventions. It also does not explore the role of cultural or policy factors in shaping drinking behaviors during these periods.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories, particularly during periods of social and health crises like the pandemic.

title_zh: First-hand Alcohol-Related Harms in Hong Kong University Dormitories: A Serial Cross-sectional Study Comparing the Normative, Social Unrest, and COVID-19 Pandemic Periods.
source_body_en: Between September 2018 and June 2021, we conducted serial cross-sectional surveys of university dormitory residents in Hong Kong (n = 2659). Drinking behaviors and first-hand harms were examined across a normative period, time of protests, and the COVID-19 pandemic. Drinking levels remained steady between the normative and protest periods but increased during the pandemic, and the proportions reporting drinking-related harms were 57.1%, 53.9%, and 62.5%, respectively. Binge drinking was associated with high first-hand harms across 3 periods (adjusted odds ratio [AOR]: 3.46-5.76). Having a drinking roommate was also correlated with harms during the normative period (AOR = 1.66). During the protests, underage drinking history and university location were associated with high first-hand harms (AOR: 1.69 and 1.82). During the COVID-19 pandemic, weekend dormitory residence and low alcohol-related knowledge were significant factors (AOR: 2.78 and 2.85). The findings indicate the need for context-specific alcohol harm reduction strategies in East Asian university dormitories.

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该研究是2018年9月至2021年6月期间进行的系列横断面调查,涉及2659名参与者。它比较了三个时期的饮酒行为和第一手伤害:正常时期、社会动荡时期和大流行时期。该方法包括使用调整后的比值比对关联进行统计分析。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究发现,饮酒水平在正常时期和抗议时期保持稳定,但在大流行期间有所增加。在正常时期、抗议时期和大流行时期,报告与酒精有关的伤害的参与者比例分别为 57.1%、53.9% 和 62.5%。在这三个时期,酗酒始终与较高的第一手伤害相关。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究没有提供有关饮酒与第一手伤害之间联系的机制或干预措施有效性的详细信息。它还没有探讨文化或政策因素在这些时期塑造饮酒行为的作用。

title: Real-World Effectiveness of Nirmatrelvir-Ritonavir in Preventing COVID-19-Associated Hospitalization: A Population-Based Cohort Study in the Province of Québec, Canada.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The nirmatrelvir-ritonavir has shown to reduce coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) hospitalization and death before the Omicron era, but updated real-world evidence studies are needed. The current study aimed to assess whether nirmatrelvir-ritonavir reduces the risk of COVID-19-associated hospitalization among high-risk outpatients. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2-infected outpatients between 15 March and 15 October 2022, using data from the Québec clinico-administrative databases. Propensity score matching was used to compare infected outpatients treated with nirmatrelvir-ritonavir with those not receiving nirmatrelvir-ritonavir. The relative risk (RR) of COVID-19-associated hospitalization occurring within 30 days following the index date was assessed using a Poisson regression. RESULTS: A total of 14 756 treated outpatients were matched to controls. Regardless of vaccination status, nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment was associated with a 74% reduced RR of hospitalization (RR, 0.26 [95% confidence interval [CI], .23-.29]; number needed to treat [NNT, 15). The effect was more pronounced in outpatients with an incomplete primary vaccination course (RR, 0.13 [95% CI, .08-.20]; NNT, 9). Benefit was also found in those with a complete primary vaccination course (RR, 0.28 [95% CI, .25-.32]; NNT, 17) regardless of age and the delay since the last vaccination. Subgroups analysis among high-risk outpatients with a primary vaccination course showed that nirmatrelvir-ritonavir treatment was associated with a significant decrease in the RR of hospitalization in severely immunocompromised outpatients (RR, 0.28 [95% CI, .21-.36]; NNT, 7), regardless of the delay since the last vaccination. CONCLUSIONS: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir reduces the risk of COVID-19-associated hospitalization among incompletely and completely vaccinated high-risk outpatients, as well as immunocompromised individuals, regardless of age and the delay since the last vaccination.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America

title: Letter to the Editor: Coronavirus disease 2019, multisystem inflammatory syndrome, and children’s hearts: Finding answers with cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
abstract: The article refers to “Persistent long-term subclinical myocardial changes in multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children revealed by cardiac magnetic resonance and galectin-3” by OV et al published in the World Journal of Clinical Pediatrics , multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) associated with coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and its cardiovascular complications. MIS-C frequently causes cardiovascular complications, including coronary artery dilatation, low left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction, diastolic dysfunction, myocarditis, and pericardial effusion, decreases over time, usually resolving within 6-9 months after the disease onset. Echocardiographic evaluations reveal mild to moderate LV dysfunction, resolving within two weeks. Severe dysfunction normalizes after approximately 1.5 months. Global longitudinal strain proves valuable for detecting subclinical myocardial damage. Long-term effects based on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMRI) data indicate the persistent myocardial edema and/or fibrosisupto12 months after the initialevent. Signs of interstitial fibrosis were found in 7.7% of patients during a one-year follow-up period. CMRI is an important additional method in the assessment of children who have experienced multisystem inflammatory syndrome in COVID-19, especially in patients with persistent symptoms or abnormal data from other cardiac findings.

title: Bevacizumab and thrombosis risk in cancer patients with COVID-19: A national retrospective cohort study (TIC-TAC)
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cancer patients treated with bevacizumab are at increased risk of thromboembolic events. COVID-19 is also associated with thromboembolism, but its impact on thromboembolic risk in cancer patients receiving bevacizumab remains unclear. The TIC-TAC study aimed to assess whether COVID-19 diagnosis is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) within 30 days or arterial (ATE) thromboembolic events within 90 days in this population. METHODS: A retrospective nationwide cohort study was conducted using the French national health data system. Cancer patients treated with bevacizumab between January 2019 and December 2021 were included. Bevacizumab exposures were used as statistical unit, and defined to 5 half-lives (100 days) after its administration. COVID-19 diagnosis was defined by ICD-10 codes or positive virological tests. The primary outcome was the occurrence of VTE or ATE during hospitalization. Cox models with time-dependent exposure and Fine and Gray competing-risk models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HR) and subdistribution hazard ratios (SHR), with death considered as a competing risk. RESULTS: Among 58,855 patients (median age 67 years, 79.9% with metastatic disease), 5,589 VTE and 1,926 ATE were recorded over 46,750 and 46,915 person-years, respectively. COVID-19 diagnosis was associated with a higher risk of VTE within 30 days after diagnosis in crude (HR 1.89, 95% CI 1.55-2.29) and adjusted Cox models (aHR 1.99 [1.64-2.43]), as well as in the Fine and Gray model (aSHR 1.70 [1.40-2.07]). However, the unadjusted absolute risk increase was modest: one additional VTE per 64.6 person-months of COVID-19 exposure. A significant interaction between COVID-19 diagnosis and anticoagulant therapy was observed in the VTE Cox model (p = 0.007), but not in the Fine and Gray model. No significant association was found between COVID-19 diagnosis and ATE risk. CONCLUSION: The study showed that 30 days period after a COVID-19 diagnosis could be associated with an increased risk of VTE in cancer patients treated with bevacizumab. However, the absolute risk difference, although unadjusted and therefore uncertain, appeared modest. Causality cannot be established in this retrospective design. No significant association was observed for ATE.

title: Investigation of a Novel Lipopeptide-Based Mucosal Vaccine for SARS-CoV-2, its Variants, and Other Heterologous Coronaviruses
abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the causative agent of COVID-19, has infected >700 million people and caused >7 million deaths worldwide. The development of the first COVID-19 vaccines helped mitigate severe disease outcomes, hospitalizations, and mortality associated with COVID-19. However, the emergence of highly pathogenic and infectious variants (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron) has continuously challenged the efficacy of current spike-based, intramuscular vaccines. The short-lived, variant-specific immunity induced by these vaccines has required periodic updates to vaccine constructs and repeated administration of booster doses, ultimately leading to vaccine fatigue among the global population. Moreover, the limited induction of mucosal immune responses at the site of infection has hampered the ability to prevent breakthrough infections and reduce viral transmission. Collectively, these challenges highlight the need to develop a next-generation vaccine that induces durable, long-lasting immunity against current and emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants, prevents infections, and enhances mucosal immune responses. In this study, we examined a novel lipopeptide-based vaccine platform integrating three key design principles: intranasal immunization; targeting conserved viral epitopes; and incorporating SARS-CoV-2 structural proteins beyond spike (S), including nucleocapsid (N) and membrane (M) proteins. Implementing these approaches led to the development of our lipopeptide-based formulation, LPMix, which induced long-lasting systemic IgM and IgG responses, as well as mucosal IgA responses, against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Alpha, Beta, Delta, and Omicron, while also demonstrating neutralizing capacity. Splenocytes and bone marrow cells derived from LPMix-immunized mice demonstrated robust proliferative responses against vaccine antigens, which were maintained up to 2 and 7 months after immunization, respectively. Moreover, memory T- and B-cell responses were long-lived and maintained up to 7 months post-immunization in the lungs, spleen, and bone marrow. Notably, the addition of the adjuvant HKCC enhanced proliferative and antibody responses and increased the longevity of T- and B-cell memory responses. In the hamster efficacy study, the LPMix vaccine significantly improved lung pathology, reduced viral loads in nasal and oral swabs, and protected against severe disease outcomes. These findings address major limitations of current COVID-19 vaccines, including limited protection against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants, insufficient stimulation of mucosal immunity at the site of viral entry, waning cellular and humoral immunity over time, and the need for frequent booster doses. More broadly, our work establishes a novel framework for designing and developing future vaccines against respiratory pathogens through the selection of conserved viral epitopes across multiple viral proteins, the use of the intranasal route of administration, and optimization of vaccine constructs and adjuvant combinations to induce effective, long-lasting immunity. These design principles can be further applied to other respiratory pathogens, including influenza, RSV, tuberculosis, and emerging coronaviruses, advancing mucosal vaccinology and pandemic preparedness.

title: Progerin Expression in Alveolar Epithelial Cells Exacerbates Inflammatory Responses to SARS-CoV-2 Infection
abstract: Abstract Age is a major determinant of severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), yet the cell-intrinsic consequences of ageing for SARS-CoV-2 infection remain difficult to examine in human experimental systems. Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived tissues provide accessible models of infection but generally lack hallmarks of ageing. Here, we employed an iPSC line containing an inducible progerin cassette and differentiated these cells towards an alveolar type II-like epithelial fate. Progerin induction in differentiated cells increased DNA-damage-associated γH2AX staining and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, reduced the heterochromatin-associated mark H3K9me3, and induced transcriptional programs associated with extracellular matrix remodeling, fibrosis and inflammation. Following infection with authentic SARS-CoV-2, progerin-expressing cultures exhibited a greater perturbation of the host transcriptome, including increased interferon-associated and inflammatory gene signatures. Transcriptomic analysis support higher viral RNA abundance in the aged model, and this was further confirmed by functional assays that showed increased infectious activity from condition media. Together, these data establish a temporally controlled model of selected ageing-associated phenotypes in human alveolar epithelial-like cells and suggest that progerin-induced cellular stress can amplify epithelial responses to SARS-CoV-2. More broadly, these findings distinguish epithelial-intrinsic inflammatory priming from the multicellular pathology of severe COVID-19.

title: COVID-19 e acidente vascular cerebral: mecanismos fisiopatológicos COVID-19 and stroke: pathophysiological mechanisms COVID-19 y accidente cerebrovascular: mecanismos fisiopatológicos
abstract: Objective: To analyze the scientific evidence available on the pathophysiological mechanisms involved in the association between SARS-CoV-2 infection and stroke, integrating the main biological processes described in the literature. Methods: This is an integrative literature review, conducted according to the method proposed by Whittemore and Knafl, with searches performed in the PubMed/MEDLINE, BVS, and CAPES Periodicals Portal databases, using the descriptors COVID-19, Stroke, and Pathophysiology, combined with the AND operator, covering publications from January 2021 to June 2026. Results: Of the 711 studies identified, 14 composed the final sample, revealing seven recurring pathophysiological axes: renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system dysregulation, cerebral endotheliopathy, immunothrombosis, blood-brain barrier degradation, neuroinvasion and mitochondrial dysfunction, systemic hypoxia with cardioembolism, and persistent endothelial dysfunction in long COVID, revealing COVID-19 as a multisystemic vascular disease associated with increased cerebrovascular risk. Final considerations: This study reinforces the central role of thromboinflammation and endothelial injury in the pathophysiology of COVID-19-associated stroke, although gaps remain regarding the contribution of direct viral neuroinvasion and the duration of post-infection vascular alterations.

Methods: This is an integrative literature review, conducted according to the method proposed by Whittemore and Knafl, with searches performed in the PubMed/MEDLINE, BVS, and CAPES Periodicals Portal databases, using the descriptors COVID-19, Stroke, and Pathophysiology, combined with the AND operator, covering publications from January 2021 to June 2026. Results: Of the 711 studies identified, 14 composed the final sample, revealing seven recurring pathophysiological axes: renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system dysregulation, cerebral endotheliopathy, immunothrombosis, blood-brain barrier degradation, neuroinvasion and mitochondrial dysfunction, systemic hypoxia with cardioembolism, and persistent endothelial dysfunction in long COVID, revealing COVID-19 as a multisystemic vascular disease associated with increased cerebrovascular risk. Final considerations: This study reinforces the central role of thromboinflammation and endothelial injury in the pathophysiology of COVID-19-associated stroke, although gaps remain regarding the contribution of direct viral neuroinvasion and the duration of post-infection vascular alterations.

title: Impactos da pandemia da COVID-19 no rastreamento e diagnóstico precoce do câncer de mama no Brasil Impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on breast cancer screening and early diagnosis in Brazil Impactos de la pandemia de COVID-19 en el rastreo y diagnóstico precoz del cáncer de mama en Brasil
abstract: Objective: To analyze the scientific evidence regarding the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on breast cancer screening and early diagnosis in Brazil. Methods: This is an integrative literature review conducted in the Virtual Health Library and PubMed databases, including primary studies published between 2020 and 2025 in Portuguese and English. After applying the eligibility criteria, 12 studies composed the final sample. Results: A significant reduction in mammography screening during the pandemic period was identified, as well as diagnostic delays, decreased detection of cases at early stages, and a proportional increase in advanced-stage diagnoses. In addition, important impacts on oncological care and increased regional inequalities in access to health services were observed. Difficulties related to the temporary suspension of elective services, overload of the healthcare system, and the population’s fear of seeking in-person care were also identified. Final considerations: It can be considered that the pandemic negatively impacted breast cancer screening and early diagnosis in Brazil, reinforcing the need for resilient strategies, reorganization of health services, and strengthening of public policies to ensure continuity of care during health crisis scenarios.

title: Long-Term Cardiopulmonary Sequelae and Rehabilitation After MERS-CoV and COVID-19: A Narrative Review from a Saudi Perspective
abstract: Saudi Arabia has carried the largest global burden of Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and a substantial burden of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the cause of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). This narrative review, written from the perspectives of clinical immunology and cardiopulmonary rehabilitation, synthesises evidence on long-term sequelae (persisting for at least 3 months) and rehabilitation after MERS-CoV infection and COVID-19, with implications for Saudi Arabia. MERS-CoV survivors show reduced diffusing capacity for at least 12 months, radiographic lung fibrosis in about one-third of recovering patients at short-term follow-up, and high rates of chronic fatigue, depression and post-traumatic stress. A dedicated search of six databases and registries (355 records) found no study of a rehabilitation intervention after MERS-CoV infection. Because most MERS-CoV survivors with sequelae were critically ill, evidence on post-intensive care syndrome and acute respiratory distress syndrome is the closest basis for extrapolation; it shows persistent disability but uncertain benefit from generic post-discharge programmes. After COVID-19, randomised trials show that rehabilitation improves functional capacity, dyspnoea and quality of life, while post-exertional malaise, autonomic dysfunction and myocardial involvement require screening and symptom-titrated or cardiology-guided care. We propose a phenotype-directed rehabilitation pathway with explicit screening criteria, adapted to Saudi factors that include Vision 2030 reforms and virtual care, high metabolic comorbidity, a hot climate, women’s access to physical activity and occupational groups at risk of MERS-CoV, and a research agenda that includes MERS-CoV survivor registries and rehabilitation trials.

title: Structural insights into subunit exchange inhibition and ligand-induced dimerization of SARS-CoV-2 main protease.
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro ) is an essential homodimeric cysteine protease that mediates viral polyprotein processing and represents a primary therapeutic target for COVID-19 treatment. While peptidomimetic inhibitors such as nirmatrelvir have demonstrated clinical efficacy, their effects on M pro quaternary structure dynamics remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests these compounds may paradoxically promote dimerization, a phenomenon termed ligand-induced dimerization (LID), which could enhance catalytic activity at low inhibitor concentrations. Here, we employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform combining metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors. We demonstrate that apo-M pro exists in a dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium characterized by rapid subunit exchange. Remarkably, peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro . Region-resolved HDX-MS revealed that inhibitor binding induces widespread conformational stabilization extending beyond the active site to the N-finger (residues 1-17) and dimer interface (residues 291-302). A notable transition of exchange mode from bimodal (EX1) to unimodal (EX2) in the N-finger region provided a sensitive structural marker of ligand-induced dimerization. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that the observed stabilization arises primarily from dimer formation rather than direct ligand contacts. These findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor-stabilized dimerization, identify the N-finger as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, and demonstrate the power of integrated mass spectrometry for dissecting complex protein assembly dynamics with therapeutic implications for antiviral drug development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the structural dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro) and its response to peptidomimetic inhibitors, which are critical for understanding their therapeutic effects on viral polyprotein processing.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform to analyze the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors, focusing on SARS-CoV-2 and its variants.
analysis.methods: The researchers used metabolic 15 N labeling, native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to examine the structural changes and dimerization dynamics of M pro in response to inhibitors.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that apo-M pro exists in a dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium with rapid subunit exchange, and that peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor-stabilized dimerization and highlight the N-finger region as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, offering new insights into the structural modulation of M pro by therapeutic agents.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide critical structural insights that can inform the development of more effective antiviral drugs targeting SARS-CoV-2 main protease, with potential implications for improving therapeutic strategies against COVID-19.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro analyses using mass spectrometry and simulations, and the evidence is based on abstract-level reporting, which may not fully capture in vivo dynamics. The evidence strength is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the structural dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro) and its response to peptidomimetic inhibitors. The research highlights the dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium of apo-M pro and demonstrates that inhibitors like nirmatrelvir can trap the dimeric state, stabilizing it and suppressing subunit exchange. The findings reveal that inhibitor binding induces conformational stabilization beyond the active site, affecting the N-finger and dimer interface. These results offer a mechanistic understanding of how inhibitors modulate M pro dimerization, which has implications for the development of more effective antiviral therapies. However, the study is limited to in vitro analyses and abstract-level reporting, which may not fully reflect in vivo conditions, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究采用集成质谱平台来分析 M pro 二聚化的动态性质及其拟肽抑制剂的调节,重点关注 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 及其变体。

title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 主蛋白酶亚基交换抑制和配体诱导二聚化的结构见解。
source_body_en: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro ) is an essential homodimeric cysteine protease that mediates viral polyprotein processing and represents a primary therapeutic target for COVID-19 treatment. While peptidomimetic inhibitors such as nirmatrelvir have demonstrated clinical efficacy, their effects on M pro quaternary structure dynamics remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests these compounds may paradoxically promote dimerization, a phenomenon termed ligand-induced dimerization (LID), which could enhance catalytic activity at low inhibitor concentrations. Here, we employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform combining metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors. We demonstrate that apo-M pro exists in a dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium characterized by rapid subunit exchange. Remarkably, peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro . Region-resolved HDX-MS revealed that inhibitor binding induces widespread conformational stabilization extending beyond the active site to the N-finger (residues 1-17) and dimer interface (residues 291-302). A notable transition of exchange mode from bimodal (EX1) to unimodal (EX2) in the N-finger region provided a sensitive structural marker of ligand-induced dimerization. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that the observed stabilization arises primarily from dimer formation rather than direct ligand contacts. These findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor-stabilized dimerization, identify the N-finger as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, and demonstrate the power of integrated mass spectrometry for dissecting complex protein assembly dynamics with therapeutic implications for antiviral drug development.

title: Biosafety level-3 cryo-electron tomography of active severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 virions.
abstract: Understanding the structural properties of pathogenic viruses in their native, infectious state is critical for rational vaccine and drug development. However, conducting cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) under biosafety level 3 (BSL-3) containment presents significant challenges. Here, we established and validated a high-end cryo-EM workflow within a BSL-3 facility, comprehensively integrating facility design, containment measures, sample handling, cryo-transfer systems, and decontamination protocols. To demonstrate the utility and reproducibility of this workflow, we applied cryo-electron tomography to investigate severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in its native, active state. Our observations confirm that unfixed viral particles display pleomorphic features comparable to those previously reported in fixed or inactivated preparations, validating that these structural characteristics represent native features rather than artifacts of chemical fixation. Furthermore, spatial redistribution of surface spikes was observed. The establishment of this robust BSL-3 cryo-EM workflow provides a practical blueprint for the structural characterization of emerging high-consequence pathogens, supporting pandemic preparedness, vaccine development, and antiviral discovery.

title_zh: 活动性严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 病毒体的生物安全 3 级冷冻电子断层扫描。
source_body_en: Understanding the structural properties of pathogenic viruses in their native, infectious state is critical for rational vaccine and drug development. However, conducting cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) under biosafety level 3 (BSL-3) containment presents significant challenges. Here, we established and validated a high-end cryo-EM workflow within a BSL-3 facility, comprehensively integrating facility design, containment measures, sample handling, cryo-transfer systems, and decontamination protocols. To demonstrate the utility and reproducibility of this workflow, we applied cryo-electron tomography to investigate severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in its native, active state. Our observations confirm that unfixed viral particles display pleomorphic features comparable to those previously reported in fixed or inactivated preparations, validating that these structural characteristics represent native features rather than artifacts of chemical fixation. Furthermore, spatial redistribution of surface spikes was observed. The establishment of this robust BSL-3 cryo-EM workflow provides a practical blueprint for the structural characterization of emerging high-consequence pathogens, supporting pandemic preparedness, vaccine development, and antiviral discovery.

title: Predicting engagement in care before and during the COVID-19 pandemic among people with HIV.
abstract: BACKGROUND Engagement in care is poor in the US for people with HIV (PWH) and may have been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS This retrospective, longitudinal study analyzed data from the IQVIA PharMetrics® Plus Claims database to assess engagement in care among PWH in the US 12 months before and during the COVID-19 pandemic (pre- and post-March 1, 2020). Eligible PWH had ≥ 2 medical claims with a HIV-1 diagnosis and continuous health plan enrollment. Three definitions of engagement in care were used: HIV-related healthcare visits, CD4 count/HIV viral load tests, and treatment adherence. Logistic regression compared pre- and during-pandemic engagement in care and identified factors associated with disengagement. RESULTS In 19,782 PWH analyzed, the likelihood of engaging with care decreased significantly (p < 0.001) during the pandemic for HIV-related healthcare visits (odds ratio [OR] 0.65), laboratory testing (OR 0.55), and treatment adherence (OR 0.90). Strong predictors of disengagement included younger age, being female, insurance type, HIV treatment type, and having a pre-pandemic HIV-related emergency room visit. CONCLUSIONS Engagement in care for PWH declined during the pandemic, with a variety of characteristics predictive of disengagement. These findings may help to inform interventions and initiatives throughout the HIV care continuum.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding access to sexual and reproductive health and gender-based violence services in Brazil since the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic: A multi-stakeholder qualitative analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Understanding how disruptions to essential sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and gender based violence (GBV) services because of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-COV-2;COVID-19) pandemic were experienced across different population groups is critical to health system responses. The objective of this study was to explore how the pandemic influenced knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to access to SRH and GBV services in Brazil. METHOD: A qualitative study was conducted in five healthcare facilities in Brazil between November 2022 and May 2023. Purposive sampling included pregnant and non-pregnant women, partners, and healthcare professionals. Pregnant women were interviewed at two time points. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using inductive thematic content analysis guided by Bronfenbrenner's ecological systems theory. RESULTS: A total of 99 participants contributed to 120 interviews. Political-institutional mistrust, conflicting public messaging, and health system reorganization affected access to SRH and GBV services. Although healthcare professionals reported continuity of essential services, women described reduced availability of gynecological care and contraceptive services. Socioeconomic barriers, transportation difficulties, and poor coordination further limited access, particularly for vulnerable groups. The COVID-19 pandemic intensified GBV by increasing household stressors such as unemployment and alcohol abuse while weakening safety nets. Victim blaming and financial dependence hinder reporting. Over time, pregnant women's perceptions shifted from fear of COVID-19-related fetal outcomes to concerns about vaccination and newborn care. CONCLUSION: The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on SRH and GBV service access in Brazil was not solely due to service disruption but resulted from dynamic interactions across political, institutional, interpersonal, and temporal levels.

title: Development and preliminary analytical characterisation of an in-house indirect ELISA for relative measurement of IgG binding to SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD (Omicron BA.1)
abstract: We developed an in-house indirect ELISA for relative measurement of IgG binding to the SARS-CoV-2 Spike receptor-binding domain (RBD; Omicron BA.1). Four antigen coating concentrations and three serum dilutions were evaluated using an internal convalescent-serum calibrator assigned arbitrary units (AU/mL). title: Hereditary angioedema attacks with COVID-19 vaccination: a Canadian cross sectional analysis
abstract: Background Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is a rare disease characterized by recurrent attacks of severe swelling, driven by dysregulation of the kallikrein-kinin system. Known attack triggers include infection, stress and immune activation, raising concern that COVID-19 infection and vaccination may provoke HAE attacks. No Canadian data on this relationship is currently available. Objective To describe the relationship between COVID-19 vaccination and HAE attack frequency/severity, and to characterize patient-reported disease control through the pandemic in a Canadian HAE cohort. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional survey was distributed (March 2020–December 2023) to members of the Hereditary Angioedema Canada and Angio-oedeme Hereditaire Quebec. Participants reported demographics, vaccination history, HAE attack frequency/severity/timing, prophylaxis use, and Hereditary Angioedema Activity Score (HAE-AS) for 6-month periods pre-pandemic and post-vaccination. Results Of 400 patients invited, 51 completed surveys were analyzed (12.5% response rate). Most respondents were female (78%), diagnosed > 5 years (78%), and on long-term prophylaxis (84%), primarily lanadelumab. HAE-AS scores remained stable across vaccination periods. Nine patients (mostly on prophylaxis) reported an HAE attack within 72 h of vaccination (mostly mRNA), generally mild-to-moderate, with no urgent care visits or treatment changes. Five patients declined vaccination, three citing fear of triggering an attack. Conclusion Canadian patients with HAE reported stable disease activity and low rates of severe vaccine-related attacks throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, alongside low vaccine hesitancy, though high baseline prophylaxis use may limit generalizability. Clinical Implication COVID-19 vaccination, including mRNA formulations, appears generally safe for HAE patients, particularly those on long-term prophylaxis. This observation supports continued adherence to routine vaccine recommendations while highlighting the need for patient counseling to address attack-related vaccine hesitancy.

title: A scoping review of COVID-19 modelling and analytical studies relevant to the epidemic context in Belgium, 2020–2024
abstract: The COVID-19 p​andemic required timely quantitative evidence for epidemic monitoring and public health decision-making. Here, we conduct a scoping review of quantitative COVID-19 studies relevant to the Belgian epidemic context. The literature showed strengths in genomic surveillance, social contact analysis, and forecasting, but gaps remained: limited sub-national analyses, weak integration of individual-level datasets, delayed estimation of variant-specific transmission parameters, insufficient characterisation of superspreading, and limited evaluation of digital contact tracing. These findings highlight the need for improved data governance, faster access to linked datasets, and integrated epidemic intelligence systems to support evidence-based decision-making during public-health crises.

title: Inflammatory protein trajectories and severe respiratory failure in COVID-19: a secondary analysis of the SAVE-MORE randomised trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND Severe COVID-19 is characterised by maladaptive host inflammation. In the SAVE-MORE trial (EudraCT no. 2020-005828-11; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04680949), suPAR-guided anakinra treatment reduced mortality and progression to severe respiratory failure (SRF), but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. METHODS We performed longitudinal proteomic profiling (Olink Inflammation panel, 67 proteins) in 587 SAVE-MORE participants (400 treated with anakinra and 187 with placebo), of whom 453 had samples at all three time points (baseline, Day 4, and Day 7). Analyses aimed to (i) identify baseline predictors of SRF, (ii) define inflammatory trajectories using mixed-effects models, and (iii) characterise proteomic changes at SRF onset. Cox models identified prognostic markers, validated in an independent anakinra-treated cohort from the SAVE trial (n = 153). FINDINGS Multivariate Cox regression models adjusted for sex, age, BMI, and dexamethasone treatment showed that baseline IL-6 concentrations predicted SRF across both treatment arms (placebo HR = 1·99, CI: 1·31-3·02; anakinra HR = 2·12, CI: 1·56-2·87), while PD-L1 predicted SRF only in the placebo group (HR = 2·75, CI: 1·79-4·24). Anakinra allocation was associated with changes in inflammatory trajectories related to SRF progression. Patients developing SRF showed sustained activation marked by elevated concentrations of IL-6, MCP-1/3, EN-RAGE, and PD-L1, whereas SRF-free patients had higher levels of proteins linked to regulatory and adaptive immunity, including CD6, CD244, TRAIL, TNF-B, and FLT3L. Event-aligned analyses showed an acute inflammatory surge at SRF onset involving IL-6, CXCL5, OSM, and VEGFA, which was significantly attenuated by anakinra. Results were further confirmed in the SAVE cohort. INTERPRETATION Progression to SRF was associated with an inflammatory amplification programme involving cytokine, chemokine, tissue-injury, and immune-checkpoint pathways. Anakinra allocation was associated with smaller changes in proteins associated with inflammatory amplification and acute inflammatory changes accompanying respiratory deterioration. These findings provide biological context for the clinical benefit observed in the SAVE-MORE trial. FUNDING Hellenic Institute for the Study of Sepsis (sponsor) and Swedish Orphan Biovitrum (funder).

title: Gut microbiota in non-hospitalised SARS-CoV-2 infection is compositionally distinct from IBS despite comparable dysbiosis prevalence: a prospective cohort study from acute infection to six months
abstract: Background Gut dysbiosis has been documented after COVID-19, but whether it occurs and persists after mild to moderate non-hospitalised infection, and how it compares with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), remains unclear. Methods We prospectively followed 31 non-hospitalised patients with mild-to-moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection at acute infection, four weeks and six months using the GA-map® Dysbiosis Test, with healthy controls (n = 36) and patients with moderate-to-severe IBS (n = 58) as cross-sectional reference groups. Composition was compared by PERMANOVA on Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, individual taxa by Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with false discovery rate (FDR) correction, and within-patient change by linear mixed-effects models. Gastrointestinal symptoms, fatigue and cognitive symptoms were related to the microbiota by Spearman correlation. Results Overall composition differed across groups (p = 0.001). SARS-CoV-2 patients differed from healthy controls (adjusted p = 0.048, 0.005 and 0.007) and from IBS (adjusted p = 0.011, 0.004 and 0.004) at all three time points, whereas composition within the SARS-CoV-2 cohort did not change over follow-up and IBS did not differ from healthy controls. Alpha diversity did not differ across groups. Five taxa were altered at every time point against both reference groups, with Eubacterium rectale , Bacteroides stercoris , Ruminococcus gnavus and Proteobacteria depleted and Shigella spp. Actinobacteria and Bifidobacterium spp. increased within patients by four weeks (both FDR = 0.002) and exceeded IBS levels at six months (both FDR < 0.001). Dysbiosis was as prevalent as in IBS (8/28, 3/29 and 7/26 versus 15/58) and more prevalent than in healthy controls (2/36) at baseline and six months, but individual trajectories were bidirectional and no patient was dysbiotic throughout. Gastrointestinal symptoms largely resolved, whereas mental fatigue remained at the IBS level and cognitive symptoms were present in 13/26 patients at six months versus 6/35 healthy controls. Neither individual taxa nor the Dysbiosis Index was associated with symptom severity in the SARS-CoV-2 cohort. Conclusions Gut microbiota alterations after mild-to-moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection persisted through six months without resembling the microbiota seen in IBS, and were not associated with persistent fatigue or cognitive symptoms.
