source_records.abstract: Background Gut dysbiosis has been documented after COVID-19, but whether it occurs and persists after mild to moderate non-hospitalised infection, and how it compares with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), remains unclear. Methods We prospectively followed 31 non-hospitalised patients with mild-to-moderate SARS-CoV-2 infection at acute infection, four weeks and six months using the GA-map® Dysbiosis Test, with healthy controls (n = 36) and patients with moderate-to-severe IBS (n = 58) as cross-sectional reference groups. Composition was compared by PERMANOVA on Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, individual taxa by Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with false discovery rate (FDR) correction, and within-patient change by linear mixed-effects models. Gastrointestinal symptoms, fatigue and cognitive symptoms were related to the microbiota by Spearman correlation. Results Overall composition differed across groups (p = 0.001). SARS-CoV-2 patients differed from healthy controls (adjusted p = 0.048, 0.005 and 0.007) and from IBS (adjusted p = 0.011, 0.004 and 0.004) at all three time points, whereas composition within the SARS-CoV-2 cohort did not change over follow-up and IBS did not differ from healthy controls. Alpha diversity did not differ across groups. Five taxa were altered at every time point against both reference groups, with Eubacterium rectale , Bacteroides stercoris , Ruminococcus gnavus and Proteobacteria depleted and Shigella spp. Actinobacteria and Bifidobacterium spp. increased within patients by four weeks (both FDR = 0.002) and exceeded IBS levels at six months (both FDR < 0.001). Dysbiosis was as prevalent as in IBS (8/28, 3/29 and 7/26 versus 15/58) and more prevalent than in healthy controls (2/36) at baseline and six months, but individual trajectories were bidirectional and no patient was dysbiotic throughout. Gastrointestinal symptoms largely resolved, whereas mental fatigue remained at the IBS level and cognitive symptoms were present in 13/26 patients at six months versus 6/35 healthy controls. Neither individual taxa nor the Dysbiosis Index was associated with symptom severity in the SARS-CoV-2 cohort. title: Association of Fungal Isolates with In-Hospital Mortality in Patients with COVID-19: A Retrospective Cohort Study
abstract: Fungal co-infections are increasingly reported in hospitalized COVID-19 patients; but their clinical significance remains uncertain. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 3373 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 to evaluate the association between fungal isolates and in-hospital mortality. Fungal isolates were identified in 197 (5.8%) patients, predominantly from respiratory specimens, with non-albicans Candida species accounting for most isolates. Patients with fungal isolates were older, had longer hospital stays, and exhibited higher rates of comorbidities, intensive care use, and exposure to broad-spectrum antibiotics, corticosteroids, and tocilizumab. In-hospital mortality was higher among patients with fungal isolates (18.8% vs. However, in multivariable logistic regression analysis, fungal isolates were not independently associated with mortality (adjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 0.97-2.29). Mortality was independently associated with age, chronic kidney disease, immunosuppression, and treatment-related factors. These findings suggest that fungal isolates are more likely markers of disease severity and treatment exposure rather than direct contributors to mortality.

title: Immunogenicity and protection against omicron subvariants induced by XBB.1.5 Spike DNA vaccine
abstract: Updating SARS-CoV-2 vaccines has become a recommendation to enhance immunity induced by vaccination or prior infection, given the continued circulation of variants/subvariants of concern. The waning effectiveness of vaccines and the immune evasion of circulating variants/subvariants require continuous improvements to new vaccine compositions based on multiple platforms. We developed and evaluated monovalent vaccines based on a plasmid DNA platform (pCTV), encoding the Spike protein of the SARS-CoV-2 Wuhan strain (pCTV-Wuhan), the Omicron variant (pCTV-Omicron), and the XBB.1.5 subvariant (pCTV-XBB). Immunogenicity and protective efficacy against the Omicron variant, as well as the XBB.1.5 and JN.1 subvariants, were evaluated in preclinical models using K18-hACE2 mice and Syrian hamsters. Immunizing mice with pCTV-Wuhan and pCTV-Omicron using homologous and heterologous prime-boost schedules showed that only the homologous pCTV-Omicron protocol induced significantly higher neutralizing antibody titers, along with reduced viral RNA levels in the lungs and nasal wash after Omicron variant challenge. Based on these findings and the subsequent emergence of XBB-derived subvariants, we developed a DNA vaccine encoding the XBB.1.5 Spike protein. Immunization with pCTV-XBB elicited robust immune responses, including high antibodies levels and neutralizing activity against XBB.1.5. After XBB.1.5 challenge, vaccinated animals showed reduced viral RNA in the lungs, milder inflammation, improved lung pathology, and protection against disease in both mice and hamsters. Immunization with pCTV-XBB also elicited a cellular immune response, resulting in significant IFN-γ production by CD4 + and CD8 + T cells. However, B-cell-deficient K18-hACE2 (K18-hACE/BKO) mice, immunized with pCTV-XBB and subsequently challenged with XBB.1.5, succumbed to the infection, demonstrating that the protective mechanism relies primarily on the humoral response. T-cell depletion reduced protection in animals infected with the XBB.1.5 subvariant, suggesting that the cellular response also contributes to protective immunity. The pCTV-XBB vaccine also demonstrated cross-protection against the JN.1 subvariant, as evidenced by a significant reduction in viral RNA, particularly in the lungs of challenged animals. Overall, pCTV-XBB conferred protection against the XBB.1.5 and JN.1 subvariants, mediated primarily by a humoral and T-cell response, respectively. These results support continued evaluation of updated DNA vaccines to address the ongoing evolution of SARS-CoV-2.

title: Widespread SARS-CoV-2 brain infection after intranasal challenge leads to innate and anti-viral immune response and interference with neuronal function in K18-hACE2 mice
abstract: Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the causative agent of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, often spreads to the brain in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice after intranasal challenge, leading to widespread neuronal infection. Despite frequent reports of this phenomenon, the effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection on neurons have not yet been fully investigated. Therefore, using the K18-hACE2 mouse model, we performed an in-depth in situ characterisation of brain changes associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, with a specific focus on infected neurons and glial cells. We challenged mice intranasally with the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant at a low dose of 100 PFU/mouse and investigated the brains 6 or 7 days later with a combination of morphologic (light microscopy, transmission electron microscopy), virologic (RT-qPCR), and bulk multi-omics (transcriptome, proteome, metabolome, lipidome) approaches. In our model, SARS-CoV-2 infected only neurons, where it replicated, as confirmed by ultrastructural analysis and supported by multi-omics results. Despite high viral burden, productive SARS-CoV-2 infection of neurons elicited only minimal degenerative changes and rare cell death; however, the transcriptome suggested possible functional alterations. Besides the previously reported mild inflammatory response, neuronal infection initiated an innate immune and antiviral response as well as a mild glial response. In conclusion, the K18-hACE2 model of intranasal SARS-CoV-2 Delta infection allows to study the pathomechanisms associated with viral neuronal infection without overt cell death, contrasting with other neurotropic viruses.

title: Early COVID-19 Public Health Emergency Disruption and Non-COVID Infection-Related Hospitalizations in Home Health Care.
abstract: Using linked national Medicare data from 2019-2020, we examined non-COVID infection-related hospitalizations across 7,956,006 home health care (HHC) episodes before and immediately after COVID-19 public health emergency onset. In adjusted models, the early public health emergency (PHE) period was not associated with hospitalization among White patients; Black patients experienced a significant increase, narrowing the pre-PHE Black-White difference. Findings highlight the need for resilient HHC infection monitoring and escalation pathways during public health disruptions.

In adjusted models, the early public health emergency (PHE) period was not associated with hospitalization among White patients; Black patients experienced a significant increase, narrowing the pre-PHE Black-White difference. Findings highlight the need for resilient HHC infection monitoring and escalation pathways during public health disruptions.

title: Allograft function in kidney transplant recipients following COVID-19
abstract: This multicenter cohort study assessed the impact of COVID-19 on kidney function in kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) at 12 months after SARS-CoV-2 infection. The final analytic cohort comprised 1,145 KTRs diagnosed with COVID-19 between March-2020 and December-2021, after exclusion of patients who died or experienced graft loss within 90 days of diagnosis. Kidney function at one year was evaluated, as were variables associated with graft loss or a decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥30% from baseline. eGFR trajectories were analyzed using a multi-step missing-data approach. At the time of COVID-19 diagnosis, the median time from transplantation was 5.9 years (IQR 2.5-10.4), and the median eGFR was 52 mL/min/1.73m2 (IQR 38-68). The cumulative incidence of acute rejection at 12 months was 1.0%; 3.1% of patients died and 3.3% experienced graft loss. Mean eGFR declined by 3.77 mL/min/1.73m2 (95%CI, -4.70 to -2.83) in the imputed dataset. In multivariable analysis, diabetes (OR 1.56; 95%CI 1.05-2.33;p = 0.029), hospitalization during COVID-19 (OR 1.79; 95%CI 1.19-2.69;p = 0.005), and acute rejection (OR 16.67; 95%CI 4.59-60.57;p < 0.001) were independently associated with the composite outcome of graft loss or ≥30% decline in eGFR, whereas higher baseline eGFR was protective (OR 0.89 per 10 mL/min/1.73m2 increase; 95%CI 0.82-0.97;p = 0.007). In conclusion, although acute rejection and graft loss were uncommon, COVID-19 was associated with a statistically significant reduction in eGFR over 12 months that exceeded the trajectory previously reported for stable KT cohorts, raising concerns about long-term graft outcomes.

title: Neonatal exposure to SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in mice is associated with localized changes in cerebral cortex cell proliferation
abstract: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can cause acute and persistent neurological manifestations, and evidence suggests these effects may be at least partly explained by direct effects of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein, which includes neuroinflammation, cognitive dysfunction, and persistent pain. Because the developing brain undergoes finely regulated processes of cellular proliferation, differentiation, and cerebrovascular maturation, exposure to SARS-CoV-2 or its components during this critical period may interfere with neurodevelopment. We therefore investigated whether neonatal exposure to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein affects processes underlying brain development. To this end, we used a mouse model previously developed by our group, where Swiss mice received an injection (s.c.) of spike protein from the ancestral viral strain or vehicle at postnatal day 1 (P1). Body weight, body length, and the righting reflex were evaluated until postnatal day 20 (P20). At P10, mouse brains were analyzed for cell proliferation, neural cell populations, and cerebrovascular organization, while blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability was assessed at P20 using Evans Blue. Neonatal spike protein exposure did not affect body weight, body length, or postural righting reflex. At P10, cell proliferation in spike-exposed animals was comparable to control groups, whereas region-specific alterations in SOX2-positive cells and TBR1-positive neurons were observed. Spike protein exposure did not broadly alter cerebrovascular architecture or BBB permeability, although increased IB4 fluorescence was detected in the lateral dentate gyrus (DG). Our findings provide evidence that exposure to the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein during postnatal development can influence specific aspects of neural development, highlighting the importance of understanding how viral components may affect the developing brain during critical windows of vulnerability. Keywords: spike protein, brain development, coronavirus, COVID-19, SARS-CoV-2, cerebrovasculature.

title: Contrasting COVID-19-Related Beliefs and Dietary Behavior Among University Students During the Pandemic and Post-Pandemic Periods
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic led to widespread physical, social, and academic disruptions among university students across the U.S. The aim of this study is to compare COVID-19-related beliefs and self-reported fruit and vegetable consumption among two independent samples of undergraduate students across two time periods: pandemic (August 2022–March 2023) and post-pandemic (August 2025–March 2026). A cross-sectional survey was administered to a total convenience sample of 535 male and female undergraduate students from diverse ethnic backgrounds and majors at a New Jersey state university. Frequency of COVID-19 prevention behaviors (e.g., indoor masking, handwashing), and consumption of fruit and vegetables (dark green and orange) over the previous week were measured. Health beliefs stemming from the Health Belief Model (HBM) were assessed (e.g., perceived susceptibility to COVID-19, severity, benefits, barriers and self-efficacy). Statistical distributions were computed for the entire sample and independent sample t-tests were computed to assess differences in the mean values for behaviors and beliefs. Univariate analysis of variance was conducted for COVID-19 prevention behaviors and the HBM variables as separate dependent variables, with time period, biological sex, and academic major as fixed factors. The sample mean of the pandemic sample was 21.7 years with 73% females, and 46% identified as White, non-Hispanic. The mean age of the post-pandemic sample was 21.7 with 60% females and 46% White. Results indicated less adoption of COVID-19 prevention behaviors (p < 0.001), weaker perceptions of susceptibility (p < 0.001), lower perceptions of benefits (p < 0.01), and lower cues to action (p < 0.01) in the post-pandemic sample than their counterparts. Mean scores for perceived severity, barriers, and self-efficacy remained relatively unchanged in the two samples. For the post-pandemic sample, the average daily vegetable (dark green and orange) and fruit intake was 0.62 cup and 0.87 cup, respectively. There were no statistically significant differences in the mean daily fruit and vegetable intake between the two samples. Time period exerted a partial eta squared value of 0.049 for COVID-19 prevention behaviors (p < 0.001). Study findings demonstrate notable differences in university students’ COVID-19 preventive measures, perceptions of susceptibility and benefits in the subsequent years after the pandemic. Health educators and nutrition professionals should examine factors contributing to potentially low fruit and vegetable intake among young adults.

title: Activity-based fluorescence screening uncovers host enzymatic responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection
abstract: Transcriptomic and proteomic studies have characterized host responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection, yet changes in endogenous enzymatic activities remain poorly understood. Here, we screened 89 enzyme-activatable fluorescence probes in living SARS-CoV-2-infected Calu-3 cells and identified 18 probes showing enhanced fluorescence, with some exhibiting multiplicity-of-infection-dependent responses. Neither SARS-CoV-2 Mpro nor PLpro activated the tested probes, and several did not exhibit comparable fluorescence enhancements in influenza-virus-infected cells. Target identification and biochemical validation implicated calpain-1 (CAPN1) and puromycin-sensitive aminopeptidase (PSA) as major contributors to probe activation. A PSA-reactive fluorescence probe confirmed that SARS-CoV-2-infected living cells showed enhanced PSA activity, which was suppressed by puromycin. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed a strong positive correlation between PSA and SARS-CoV-2 spike protein signals. Notably, neither CAPN1 nor PSA was included among differentially expressed genes or proteins previously identified in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells. These findings highlight activity-based fluorescence screening as a complementary strategy to expression-based analyses for discovering infection-induced biomarker enzymes.

source_records.abstract: Transcriptomic and proteomic studies have characterized host responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection, yet changes in endogenous enzymatic activities remain poorly understood. Here, we screened 89 enzyme-activatable fluorescence probes in living SARS-CoV-2-infected Calu-3 cells and identified 18 probes showing enhanced fluorescence, with some exhibiting multiplicity-of-infection-dependent responses. Neither SARS-CoV-2 Mpro nor PLpro activated the tested probes, and several did not exhibit comparable fluorescence enhancements in influenza-virus-infected cells. Target identification and biochemical validation implicated calpain-1 (CAPN1) and puromycin-sensitive aminopeptidase (PSA) as major contributors to probe activation. A PSA-reactive fluorescence probe confirmed that SARS-CoV-2-infected living cells showed enhanced PSA activity, which was suppressed by puromycin. Immunofluorescence analysis revealed a strong positive correlation between PSA and SARS-CoV-2 spike protein signals. Notably, neither CAPN1 nor PSA was included among differentially expressed genes or proteins previously identified in SARS-CoV-2-infected cells. These findings highlight activity-based fluorescence screening as a complementary strategy to expression-based analyses for discovering infection-induced biomarker enzymes.

title: The global burden of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias: New public health intervention targets driven by the long-term impact of COVID-19 and sex and age differences
abstract: Introduction This study focuses on the impact and future trends of COVID-19 on the burden of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD), analyzing multidimensional differences in the burden of disease for ADRD in 204 countries between 1990 and 2021. Methods Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data (1990–2021), we analyzed Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD) prevalence and burden across 204 countries, stratified by sex and age. Joinpoint regression identified temporal inflection points in incidence, mortality, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and years of life lost (YLL), while age-standardized rates and estimated annual percentage changes assessed global burden trends. We further evaluated ADRD-associated risk factors, quantified COVID-19’s impact through excess burden attribution models, and projected incidence trajectories to 2050 via Bayesian Age-Period-Cohort analysis. Results Global Burden of Disease analyses (1990–2021) show 2021 ADRD incidence of 119.76/100,000, with 450.98 DALYs and 309.03 YLL/100,000. Post-2019 COVID-19 onset, all SDI regions except high-SDI exhibited significant ADRD incidence increases (P < 0.05). Women ≥55 years had the highest burden, with behavioral risks contributing most to DALYs (2021). China showed the steepest ADRD incidence rise (1990–2021), accelerating post-COVID-19, contrasting declines in Denmark and Australia. COVID-19 ASIR (2020) and ADRD ASPR (2020) had a standardized path coefficient of 0.237 (P < 0.05); COVID-19 ASIR (2020) and ADRD ASPR (2021) covariance reached 0.275 (P < 0.05). Projections suggest declining ASIR for ages 40–79 but rising ASIR for ≥80 by 2050. Conclusion To effectively mitigate the ongoing rise in ADRD, particularly among older women and middle-high SDI populations, targeted prevention and control strategies must be developed, with careful consideration of socioeconomic factors and the long-term impacts of COVID-19.

title: Immunometabolic Reversal of Long COVID and Inflammatory Memory via Host-Directed Antiviral and Metabolic Shielding
abstract: Abstract Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection provokes an intense acute inflammatory response (1, 16). However, in hundreds of millions of individuals surviving the acute phase, clinical presentation frequently diverges into persistent post-acute sequelae known as Long COVID, or Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 (PASC) (1, 16). With global epidemiological estimates now surpassing 400 million affected patients worldwide, Long COVID has emerged as one of the most debilitating public health crises of the modern era (1, 16). Characterized by intractable chronic fatigue, post-exertional malaise (PEM), neuro-psychiatric cognitive impairment ("brain fog"), autonomic dysregulation, and accelerated biological aging (inflammaging) in the absence of active viral replication, the syndrome imposes an immense socioeconomic and healthcare burden (1, 16). Current clinical management remains severely bottlenecked by palliative symptom management, largely because existing therapeutic models fail to address the core drivers of disease persistence (1, 16). Here, we uncover the precise molecular circuitry coupling viral persistence and metabolic stress to chronic post-viral fatigue: the SARS-CoV-2 ORF7b-c-Myc-MALAT1/NEAT1-miR-22-3p-NLRP3 axis, integrated with the SIRT6-SIRT3-LCAD/SLC25A13-mitochondrial dysfunction-associated senescence (MIDAS) axis and the p53-FBXO22-NSP5 / RIG-I / MAVS feedforward antiviral loop (1, 9, 10, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21). Utilizing an expanded deterministic eight-variable non-linear ordinary differential equation (ODE) kinetic model and phase-space separatrix analysis, we establish a critical therapeutic separatrix threshold (S_"ImmunoShield" ≥2.85" a.u." ) and demonstrate how a host-directed p53/NRF2-metformin-taurine immunometabolic shield successfully dismantles pathological attractors, clears oxidized mitochondrial DNA, restores sirtuin-mediated deacetylation, and terminates inflammatory memory.

title: ‘The vaccine is not a gris-gris, it does not come from the darkness’: a qualitative study of perceptions of COVID-19 vaccination among people living in a prison of Madagascar
abstract: Background People living in prisons represent some of the most marginalised members of society, with incarceration further exacerbating existing health inequities. Substantial evidence shows that inmates experience disproportionately worse access to healthcare than the general population, as reflected for instance by the limited availability of immunisation services for them in some settings. Despite the World Health Organization's endorsement of prioritising COVID-19 vaccinations for inmates, the prison population of Madagascar was neglected during the pandemic. This study sought to explore the perceptions of the COVID-19 vaccine among people living in the adult, mixed-sex Marofoto prison in north-western Madagascar. Methods In April 2023, this qualitative study conducted individual interviews and focus group discussions guided by a semi-structured topic guide as methods for qualitative data generation. Purposive sampling was used to invite 12 female and 12 male inmates willing to provide informed consent for their participation. Data analysis were guided by a constructivist grounded theory approach to qualitative health research. Triangulation sessions were held with community spokespersons, inmates, prison staff, and health care professionals to ensure the study's trustworthiness. Results Key motivating factors for COVID-19 vaccine acceptance and uptake among participants in this study were: acute awareness of the need for COVID-19 vaccination to prevent severe COVID-19, particularly given the inmates' living conditions (e.g., closed and shared living quarters); inmates' active engagement in prison leadership roles; vaccination endorsement by prison officers; and the provision of food and official vaccination cards during the campaign. Participants did not perceive the vaccination process as a coercive measure but rather as a matter of individual choice. Conclusion The findings reported in this study show that people living in a prison in Madagascar were receptive towards COVID-19 vaccination campaigns. The commitment and engagement of various authorities and stakeholders, including inmates with a leadership role, to improve inmates' health, rather than merely increasing financial support, may have a far greater impact on strengthening meaningful disease prevention approaches and, ultimately, on ensuring their right to health as a fundamental human right.

title: Co-administration of DTaP with COVID-19 mRNA vaccine in mice alters immune responses and induces increased protection from Bordetella pertussis challenge
abstract: ABSTRACT During the COVID-19 pandemic, children received COVID-19 mRNA vaccines alongside other regularly scheduled immunizations, such as the acellular Bordetella pertussis vaccine DTaP. It is known that mRNA vaccines are pro-inflammatory in nature, leading to protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2 infection. The goal of this study was to investigate the potential adjuvanticity of co-administration of a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine alongside DTaP. Mice were immunized with DTaP alone or with a co-administration of DTaP plus COVID-19 mRNA vaccine. To understand the impact of co-administration, we evaluated protection against B. pertussis aerosol challenge in mice and potential correlates of protection, including cytokine responses to vaccination, antibody responses, and single-cell transcriptomic analysis of the draining lymph node. Three decreasing doses of each vaccine were used to simulate waning immunity. Overall, compared to mice immunized with DTaP, co-administration of DTaP + COVID-19 mRNA vaccines elicited higher pro-inflammatory cytokine responses, higher IgG2b antibody responses, and mice were afforded increased protection against aerosol challenge of B. Single-cell transcriptomics studies on the lymph node of vaccinated mice at 1 day post-boost further characterized how co-administration of COVID-19 mRNA vaccine alongside DTaP vaccine shapes immunity. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that co-administration of DTaP and COVID-19 mRNA vaccine generated populations of B and T cells with upregulated expression of interferon-stimulated genes, which were absent when vaccinating with DTaP alone. Altogether, these data suggest that administering DTaP alongside COVID-19 mRNA vaccine alters immune responses and provides increased protection from an aerosol challenge of B. pertussis compared to DTaP alone in mice.

title: Identification and Characterization of Surfactant Binding Sites on the SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein and Its Variants by Microseconds-Long Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
abstract: While airborne coronavirus virions penetrate respiratory airways, lung surfactants (LS) adsorb on spike proteins and may hinder their binding to cell receptors. In this work, we utilize microsecond-long unbiased and adaptive sampling molecular dynamics simulations performed on the Anton 2 supercomputer to elucidate the molecular mechanisms and dynamics of the adsorption of lung surfactant lipids and cholesterol onto the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and its Delta and Omicron variants. From unbiased simulations of spontaneous multisurfactant binding, we show that surfactants tend to destabilize the protein and induce enhanced structural fluctuations that can influence the receptor-binding interface. We identify four surfactant-binding sites (SBS) that are conserved across the variants, one of which corresponds to the experimentally identified fatty acid binding site (FABS). By developing an approximate model, we analyze the energetics of multisurfactant binding and show that the binding of multiple surfactants at a site weakens individual surfactant-protein interactions, leading to potentially more dynamic binding behavior. Using adaptive sampling with the Tempered Binding approach, we demonstrate unbinding and rebinding of surfactants from selected binding sites, elucidating the structural dynamics and the binding enthalpy profiles. Identification and quantitative characterization of the binding sites' affinity and stability provide a better understanding of the specifics of lung surfactant-spike protein interactions and may support future investigations into the potential role of these interactions in surfactant-based therapeutic strategies.
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B

title: Shortest IZ motif-driven assembly of SARS-CoV-2 HR1 peptides yields a potent fusion inhibitor.
abstract: The continuous evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and the emergence of immune-evasive variants underscore the urgent need for antiviral agents with novel mechanisms of action. Our group recently demonstrated that chimeric peptides constructed by fusing a trimerization tool motif to HR1-derived sequences can mimic the natural HR1 coiled-coil conformation of type I enveloped viruses, thereby enabling the design of novel virus inhibitors independent of strict sequence homology. Building on this principle, herein we engineered a series of chimeric N-peptides by fusing a minimal residue isoleucine zipper motif to SARS-CoV-2 HR1-derived sequences of varying lengths. Among these, IZ11N42 emerged as the most potent inhibitor against SARS-CoV-2 XDV-type virus with an IC50 of 0.492 μM, representing a 37-fold improvement over the native HR1P peptide (IC50 = 18.43 μM), with no significant cytotoxicity (CC50 > 100 μM). Drying-wetting experiments on structural characterization reveal that IZ11N42 predominantly forms trimers, providing the structural basis for target engagement. Mechanism investigation confirmed that IZ11N42 assembles with HR2-derived peptide into a stable heterologous 6-HB complex with enhanced thermal stability and high-binding affinity. Importantly, in hACE2 transgenic mice challenged with SARS-CoV-2 pseudovirus, IZ11N42 significantly reduced viral loads in the nasal turbinates, lungs, and brain, and mitigated weight loss compared to the model control. Collectively, these findings establish IZ11N42 as a promising N-peptide fusion inhibitor and validate the tool peptide-chimeric strategy for constructing HR1-mimetic coiled-coil as a versatile approach for designing antiviral peptides against emerging coronaviruses.

title: Growing US Rural-Urban Mortality Gap During the COVID-19 Pandemic, 2018-2023.
abstract: To assess whether the rural mortality penalty widened after COVID-19 pandemic onset and remained elevated through 2023 in the United States. We used Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research data to compare age-adjusted underlying cause mortality between rural and urban US counties from 2018 to 2023. Using difference-in-differences, we estimated changes after pandemic onset relative to prepandemic trends and assessed cause-specific and geographic subgroups. After pandemic onset, the rural-urban mortality gap increased by 2.99 deaths per 100 000 in monthly analyses and 39.40 in annual analyses; the mean monthly gap was 16.37 per 100 000 in 2020 to 2023. Differences increased for circulatory disease, neoplasms, and respiratory disease. COVID-19 mortality was nearly 10 deaths per 100 000 higher in rural counties. Gaps widened in all regions, with the greatest disparities in the Southern United States. State-level changes varied widely. The long-standing rural mortality gap widened after pandemic onset, likely driven by structural disparities and pandemic-related disruptions. Public Health Implications. Narrowing the rural mortality gap will require sustained investment in rural health and targeted public health interventions. ( Am J Public Health . Published online ahead of print November 19, 2026:e1-e11. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308843).

title: Structure-Based Identification and Functional Characterization of SARS-CoV-2 RBD–hACE2 Interface Inhibitory Peptides Displayed on the RAD Scaffold
abstract: The interaction between the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein and human angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (hACE2) is a key molecular event in viral entry and an attractive target for the identification of antiviral compounds, including inhibitory peptides. Here, we identified peptide motifs derived from the RBD–hACE2 interface using a structure-based method and examined their functional activity when presented within the Pyrococcus furiosus RAD scaffold (RAD-display). Candidate peptides derived from both RBD and hACE2 were selected initially by computational analyses of the crystallographic complex, cloned and expressed as RAD-display constructs. Functional activities were evaluated by ELISA, LumitTM luminescence assay, pseudovirus entry inhibition, and cytopathic-effect-based infection neutralization assays with the parental SARS-CoV-2 lineage. Peptides derived from RBD showed superior performance compared with peptides derived from hACE2. In particular, the RAD_R19 construct consistently showed RBD–hACE2 inhibitory effects reducing pseudoviruses and virus-mediated cytopathic effects. Together, these findings identify R19 as a promising native RBD-derived inhibitory motif whose functional activity was demonstrated when presented within the RAD scaffold. In the context of previous studies showing limited inhibitory activity of closely related native linear RBM peptides, our results further suggest that the molecular context of peptide presentation is an important determinant of inhibitory behavior.

title: Author Correction: SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines sensitize tumours to immune checkpoint blockade.
abstract: In the version of this article initially published, in Fig. 2d, the red triangle depicting vaccine administration at day 17 originally appeared at day 20; in Fig. 5o, the colours of the red and blue traces in the plot were interchanged; in Extended Data Fig. 3h,i, the red and blue colour keys (currently, blue for vaccine, red for no vaccine) were interchanged. 3b legend, in the text now reading “vaccine days 3, 6, 21,” 21 replaces the original “17,” and in the Fig. 3k legend, now reading “vaccine days 3, 6, 20,” 20 replaces the original “21.” In the first sentence of the Methods “Cox proportional hazards regression” section, in the text now reading “For Cox proportional hazards regression, exposures defined relative to an index date...,” “exposures defined relative to an index date” replaces the original “time-dependent variables were defined.” In the first paragraph of the Methods and in the Reporting Summary, data collection timelines have been updated to say “The data-collection cut-off was 1 September 2024 for the NSCLC and melanoma datasets and 1 January 2025 for the tissue agnostic dataset.” Finally, the Acknowledgements have been amended to include the statement that G.A. were supported by the CPRIT Research Training Award CPRIT Training Program (RP210028). The changes have been made in the HTML and PDF versions of the article.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for correcting errors in the original publication regarding the timing of vaccine administration and color coding in figures, as these issues could affect the interpretation of results.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a correction of data presentation errors in the original article, which was published in Nature and focused on SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines and their impact on immune checkpoint blockade in cancer patients.
analysis.methods: The correction included updating the text and figures to accurately reflect the timing of vaccine administration and the color coding of traces in plots, as well as amending the acknowledgments section to include funding information.
analysis.main_results: The main results of the correction were the revised timing of vaccine administration (day 21 instead of day 17) and the corrected color coding of the red and blue traces in the plot, with the red trace now representing the no-vaccine group and the blue trace representing the vaccine group.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the corrections as necessary to ensure the accuracy and clarity of the data presentation, and the novelty lies in the updated reporting of the study's findings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have implications for the accurate interpretation of vaccine-related data in clinical studies, which is crucial for understanding the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade in cancer treatment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to the correction of errors in the original publication, and the confidence in the corrected data is high as the changes were made to ensure accuracy.

The correction updates the text and figures to accurately reflect the vaccine administration schedule and the color coding of traces in plots. title: Sensitive electrochemical competitive detection of SARS-CoV-2 antigen on a 2D MoWSe 2 bioelectrode: a new screening strategy for water contamination and clinical diagnostics
abstract: Although the spread of SARS-CoV-2 has been largely controlled, recurring infections continue to necessitate reliable monitoring and surveillance. The global COVID-19 pandemic has, in turn, accelerated the demand for advanced biosensors capable of precise and efficient detection of viruses across diverse matrices. This work unveils a novel competitive electrochemical immunosensor based on a new two-dimensional bimetallic molybdenum tungsten diselenide (2D MoWSe 2 ) for the sensitive detection of SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) antigen, marking its first application in tap water and human serum samples. The sensor platform ingeniously utilizes 2D MoWSe 2 coated on a screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCE), leveraging its good electrochemical reactivity and biomolecule immobilization capacity. Thionine (TH) is adsorbed onto the modified SPCE, serving as both a potent redox indicator and signal amplifier. Nanotags, prepared by attaching anti-RBD antibodies onto poly(ethyleneimine)-coated gold nanoparticles (PEI-AuNPs), play a pivotal role in amplification via electron-transfer restriction for the designated competitive immunoassay. In the presence of the target SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD protein, it competitively binds to the nanotags in solution, consequently reducing the number of free nanotags available to attach to the sensing surface. Since bound nanotags inherently hinder the TH redox response, a higher concentration of target protein results in fewer nanotags binding to the electrode, thereby reducing hindrance and commensurately increasing the current response. The fabricated immunosensor exhibits outstanding analytical performance, with high selectivity, robust stability, and acceptable reproducibility across complex matrices. It offers a wide linear detection range for SARS-CoV-2 spike RBD antigen from 0.50 to 50 ng mL -1 , with limits of detection of 0.304 and 0.462 ng mL -1 in PB and human serum, respectively. This reliable immunosensor provides a compelling alternative for proactive monitoring of SARS-CoV-2 contamination and rapid clinical diagnostics, thereby making a significant contribution to global pandemic control efforts.

title: COVID-19 Mortality and Vaccination Coverage Among Older Adults in Tunisia, 2020–2022: A National Descriptive and Ecological Study
abstract: Background: Older adults experienced a disproportionate burden of COVID-19 mortality, but national evidence is limited. We described COVID-19 mortality among adults aged ≥65 years (March 2020–December 2022) and vaccination coverage among the campaign-eligible population aged ≥60 years (March 2021–December 2022). Methods: We conducted a retrospective national descriptive and ecological study using mortality surveillance data from the National Observatory of New and Emerging Diseases (ONMNE) and aggregated data from the national COVID-19 vaccination platform (EVAX). We calculated mortality, age-standardized, and proportional mortality rates; vaccination coverage; dropout proportions; and no-show rates. Results: Of 29,306 COVID-19 deaths, 20,467 (69.8%) occurred among adults aged ≥65 years; 8,725 (42.6%) were aged ≥80 years and 11,463 (56.0%) were male. Cumulative mortality was 1,809.9 per 100,000, with the highest period-specific rate during Delta predominance (750.1 per 100,000). In a sensitivity analysis restricted to adults aged ≥75 years, the only band fully covered by both data sources, mortality was 3,306.4 per 100,000. Coverage among adults aged ≥60 years was 95.4% for at least one dose, 88.3% for a complete schedule, and 38.4% for a third dose; cumulative uptake was 215.1 doses per 100. Coverage varied by governorate, and no-show rates increased in 2022. Governorate-level correlations between coverage and mortality were weak and not statistically significant (age-standardized mortality, Spearman ρ = −0.06, p = 0.77; governorate-specific mortality, ρ = −0.28, p = 0.18). Conclusions: Mortality was concentrated among the oldest-old and during Delta predominance. Coverage was high nationally but uneven geographically, and booster uptake and attendance declined. Targeted outreach and equitable access remain priorities.

title: After the COVID-19 Pandemic, Cinema Attendance in China Was Higher in Provinces With Tighter Norms.
abstract: In this paper, we showed that post-COVID cinema attendance was positively predicted by cultural tightness, across 31 mainland China provinces. This result suggests that cultural tightness accompanies a societal tendency of recovering from a disruption of social routines.

title: Investigating the impact of the Covid-19 epidemic on mortality and fertility indicators in Qom province and comparing it with national indicators from 2019 to 2023
abstract: Objective (s): Communicable and non-communicable diseases are always associated with many impacts on fertility rates, mortality, and disease burden. The present study aimed to investigate the impact of COVID-19 on fertility and mortality indicators. Methods: The present study was a mixed-method study that was conducted in two phases: a descriptive cross-sectional study and a review study. In the descriptive phase, statistical data were reviewed during 3 time periods before the COVID epidemic (March 2017 to March 2020), during the epidemic (March 2020 to March 2021), and after the epidemic (March 2021 to March 2023) for 24 months. In the second phase, a review study was conducted on the impact of the COVID-19 epidemic on mortality and fertility indicators, as well as maternal-fetal outcomes in Iran over the past years, which was searched through the electronic databases PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Persian Database (SID) for articles up to 2023. The source of the study of outcomes and complications related to the mother and newborn was obtained through a review study. Data analysis was performed using descriptive statistics in SPSS software and expressed using numbers, percentages, and graphs. Results: The general fertility rate in the pre-epidemic period was estimated at about 3.5%, which decreased to 1.3% during and after the epidemic . The stillbirth rate in the pre-epidemic period was reported to be approximately 4.6%, which decreased to 3.8% in the post-epidemic period. The crude birth rate in the pre-epidemic and post-epidemic periods was also 1.4% and 1.05%, respectively. In terms of maternal outcomes during and after the COVID-19 epidemic , most pregnant mothers faced the risk of cesarean section, premature birth, and prolonged hospital stay. In terms of neonatal outcomes, fetal heart rate abnormalities, hospitalization in the neonatal intensive care unit, and the need for resuscitation in the first minute were the most reported outcomes. Vaccination coverage decreased during and after the epidemic . Conclusion: The study findings showed that fertility and crude birth rates have decreased during and after the epidemic . Also, during the Covid-19 period, maternal and fetal complications such as respiratory complications, preterm labor, premature rupture of membranes, preeclampsia, coagulation disorders, and cardiopulmonary disorders of pregnant mothers and newborns increased. Therefore, awareness raising to prevent any type of infection during pregnancy that can affect the occurrence of pathological consequences in the mother and newborn, as well as improving and continuing prenatal care, seems necessary.

source_records.title: Investigating the impact of the Covid-19 epidemic on mortality and fertility indicators in Qom province and comparing it with national indicators from 2019 to 2023
source_records.abstract: Objective (s): Communicable and non-communicable diseases are always associated with many impacts on fertility rates, mortality, and disease burden. The present study aimed to investigate the impact of COVID-19 on fertility and mortality indicators. Methods: The present study was a mixed-method study that was conducted in two phases: a descriptive cross-sectional study and a review study. In the descriptive phase, statistical data were reviewed during 3 time periods before the COVID epidemic (March 2017 to March 2020), during the epidemic (March 2020 to March 2021), and after the epidemic (March 2021 to March 2023) for 24 months. In the second phase, a review study was conducted on the impact of the COVID-19 epidemic on mortality and fertility indicators, as well as maternal-fetal outcomes in Iran over the past years, which was searched through the electronic databases PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Persian Database (SID) for articles up to 2023. The source of the study of outcomes and complications related to the mother and newborn was obtained through a review study. Data analysis was performed using descriptive statistics in SPSS software and expressed using numbers, percentages, and graphs. Results: The general fertility rate in the pre-epidemic period was estimated at about 3.5%, which decreased to 1.3% during and after the epidemic . The stillbirth rate in the pre-epidemic period was reported to be approximately 4.6%, which decreased to 3.8% in the post-epidemic period. The crude birth rate in the pre-epidemic and post-epidemic periods was also 1.4% and 1.05%, respectively. In terms of maternal outcomes during and after the COVID-19 epidemic , most pregnant mothers faced the risk of cesarean section, premature birth, and prolonged hospital stay. In terms of neonatal outcomes, fetal heart rate abnormalities, hospitalization in the neonatal intensive care unit, and the need for resuscitation in the first minute were the most reported outcomes. Vaccination coverage decreased during and after the epidemic . Conclusion: The study findings showed that fertility and crude birth rates have decreased during and after the epidemic . Also, during the Covid-19 period, maternal and fetal complications such as respiratory complications, preterm labor, premature rupture of membranes, preeclampsia, coagulation disorders, and cardiopulmonary disorders of pregnant mothers and newborns increased. title: TORNADO study: what impact did the COVID-19 pandemic have on psychotropic drug user profiles? Application of a multichannel sequence analysis based on the French healthcare database.
abstract: Since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, an increase in the delivery of psychotropic drugs has been observed. However, there are no more precise data to date on the profile of people affected by these changes in consumption. The aim of this study was therefore to assess its impact on the profile of psychotropic drug users. Two historical cohorts, a "COVID cohort" (2020-2021) and a "pre-COVID cohort" (2018-2019), were constituted from the National Health Data System (SNDS) database. Within each of these two cohorts, three distinct subpopulations were defined according to the presence of reimbursements for psychotropic drugs during year n-1 (no previous use population, low previous use population, high previous use population). Then we analyzed reimbursements for psychotropic drugs using a multichannel sequence analysis and performed clustering analysis of sequences. The clusters identified in the three sub-populations of the COVID cohort were broadly similar to the clusters identified in the three sub-populations of the pre-COVID cohort with equivalent proportions. However, the COVID cohort differs in some aspects from the pre-COVID cohort: (1) the loss of a cluster of hypnotic users in the low previous use population, (2) earlier and longer consumption of certain psychotropic drugs (antidepressants, anxiolytics) in some clusters of the no previous use and low previous use populations, (3) a higher proportion of individuals affiliated to a specific insurance plan for low-income patients in some clusters corresponding to psychiatric profiles thought to be more severe in the three sub-populations and (4) a change in the sex ratio in some clusters of the no previous use and low previous use populations. In addition to providing answers to the specific question of the impact of the Covid-19 health crisis on the profile of psychotropic drug users, this study highlights the interest and feasibility of the multichannel sequence analysis method in pharmaco-epidemiology.

title: Self-reported neuropathic symptoms following COVID-19 vaccination: An exploratory cross-sectional survey in Egypt.
abstract: Peripheral neurological manifestations have been reported following Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) infection, whereas neuropathic symptoms after COVID-19 vaccination remain less well characterized. To evaluate self-reported neuropathic symptoms following COVID-19 vaccination and identify factors associated with postvaccination symptom reporting, while accounting for previous confirmed COVID-19 infection. This cross-sectional survey included adults recruited from university-affiliated settings. Data were collected using a structured English/Arabic questionnaire covering COVID-19 infection, vaccination history, comorbidities, medication use, and neuropathic symptoms, including tingling, numbness, burning sensation, and electric shock-like sensations. Participants who reported symptoms were invited for neurological clinical assessment. The primary outcome was self-reported neuropathic symptoms potentially suggestive of peripheral neuropathy following COVID-19 vaccination. Previous confirmed COVID-19 infection was treated as a potential confounder in multivariable analysis. A total of 1201 individuals were screened, of whom 1166 were included in the final analysis. Postvaccination self-reported neuropathic symptoms were reported by 472 of 1090 vaccinated participants (43.3%). Following the first vaccine dose, symptom reporting differed significantly by vaccine type (P < .001), with the highest proportions observed among recipients of Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine (190/316 [60.1%]) and Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine (37/92 [40.2%]). In multivariable analysis, older age, use of medications with reported or potential associations with peripheral neuropathy, and receipt of ChAdOx1-S, Gam-COVID-Vac, or Sinovac-CoronaVac were associated with increased post-vaccination symptom reporting (P < .05), whereas previous confirmed COVID-19 infection was not independently associated with the outcome. In exploratory booster-dose analysis, homologous booster vaccination was associated with lower odds of symptom reporting than heterologous boosting (adjusted odds ratio 0.38, P < .001). Self-reported neuropathic symptoms were frequently reported following COVID-19 vaccination and varied according to vaccine type. Older age, selected vaccine types, and heterologous booster schedules were associated with symptom reporting. These findings are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted cautiously because they reflect self-reported symptoms rather than confirmed peripheral neuropathy diagnoses and were not routinely confirmed by objective neurological investigations.

title: Childhood and adolescent cancer diagnosis, treatment, and hospitalizations during the COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec, Canada, a population-based study
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare delivery globally. In Quebec, Canada, measures were introduced to prioritize pediatric oncology care. Using administrative data, we estimated pandemic-related changes in cancer diagnoses, treatments, and length of hospital stay among individuals aged 0-19 in Quebec (2015-2023). Interrupted time series analyses using autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models assessed immediate and sustained changes in monthly age-standardized rates of diagnoses, treatments (chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy-related encounters), positron emission tomography scans, and hospital admissions. Separate ARIMA models fitted to pre-pandemic monthly counts generated counterfactual forecasts to estimate the cumulative differences between observed and expected diagnoses and treatments over 3, 12, and 46 months of the pandemic. Generalized linear mixed models assessed changes in length of stay between the pre- and post-pandemic periods and whether these changes differed by patient characteristics. We identified 2,570 patients: 1,475 diagnosed through February 2020 and 1,095 from March 2020 onward. We found no evidence of immediate or sustained changes in monthly incidence rates. Cumulative diagnoses and treatments remained within expected levels across periods, although estimates were imprecise. For diagnoses, the 3-, 12-, and 46-month cumulative differences were -1 (95% uncertainty interval [UI] -17 to 15), 24 (95% UI, -9 to 57), and 2 (95% UI, -94 to 96), respectively. Changes in length of hospital stay varied across subgroups, although their clinical significance remains uncertain. Pediatric cancer diagnosis and treatment activity was largely maintained across Quebec throughout the pandemic, consistent with the objectives of provincial and institutional measures to preserve pediatric oncology services.

title: COVID-19 and Alzheimer’s disease in the ADNI cohort
abstract: Abstract INTRODUCTION: There is growing evidence that COVID-19 infection in older adults increases the risk of diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease and accelerates cognitive decline. We hypothesized that participants reporting COVID-19 infection would have greater cognitive and functional decline and greater occurrence of neuropsychiatric symptoms after COVID-19 infection in comparison to uninfected matched controls. METHODS This secondary data analysis from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) cohort examined participants with and without self-reported history of COVID-19 infection comparing visits before and after infection. RESULTS The 16 participants included in the COVID-19 cohort and the 32 controls, had similar changes in cognitive, functionality and behavioral measures between study visits. CONCLUSIONS While there is evidence that COVID-19 infection increases the risk for depression, cognitive changes and conversion to dementia, this examination of a well characterized cohort of at risk and cognitive impaired individuals did not find evidence for the impact of COVID-19 after infection.

title: Allosteric Control and Glycan Shielding Adaptations in the SARS-CoV-2 Spike from Early to Peak Virulence
abstract: Abstract The SARS-CoV-2 Spike glycoprotein is central to viral infectivity and immune evasion, making it a key target for vaccine and therapeutic design. This trimeric peplomer undergoes dynamic conformational changes, particularly in its Receptor Binding Domain (RBD), which transitions between closed (down) and ACE2-accessible (up) states relative to the rest of the protein, to facilitate host cell entry. Structural understanding of such critical interdomain motions, as well as epitope exposure quantification, is essential for obtaining an effective biochemical handle over this protein and, in turn, exploiting it toward improved immunogen development. Focusing on the early circulating D614G form and the later emerging Delta (B.1.617.2) variant with higher virulence, we performed large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of the soluble form of the Spike in both “down” and “up” conformations of the RBD. Guided by differences in domain-scale fluctuations, we constructed targeted reaction coordinates capturing NTD and RBD rotations and tilting motions, enabling variant-specific structural distinctions to be quantitatively extracted. Conformational landscape mapping and principal component analysis (PCA) reveal a previously uncharacterized dynamic coupling between the NTD and RBD, wherein tilting motions of the NTD are coupled to RBD gating on the neighboring protomer. While several elements of this interdomain coupling are conserved, the Delta variant exhibits a more constrained and functionally optimized RBD-up conformation that favors ACE2 engagement. Concurrently, Delta-specific mutations restructure NTD-local glycans to enhance shielding of the immunogenic supersite, diminishing neutralizing antibody accessibility. Finally, the D950N substitution at the heptad repeat HR1 helix reshapes long-range interactions and alters bending/twisting dynamics of the Spike stalk, likely contributing to both fusion efficiency and immune evasion. Together, these simulations uncover chemically encoded strategies of variant adaptation─through long-range allostery, glycan repositioning, and conformational bias─that shape Spike structure and function. These biochemical and structural insights offer valuable guidance for rational vaccine and therapeutic design against SARS-CoV-2 and emerging variants.
journal: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Longitudinal changes in symptom burden and health-related quality of life after hospitalization for COVID-19
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Persistent symptoms after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) are common after hospitalization, but longitudinal changes in symptom burden and their relationship with health-related quality of life (HRQoL) remain incompletely understood. METHODS: In this prospective single-center observational study, hospitalized adults with PCR-confirmed COVID-19 were assessed during the acute phase and at 3-month follow-up. Symptom burden was operationally defined as the count of 16 predefined binary symptoms. Changes were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank and McNemar tests with false discovery rate correction. Associations between within-patient changes in symptom burden and changes in SF-36 domains were assessed using Spearman correlations with false discovery rate correction. RESULTS: Among 49 patients with complete symptom data, median symptom burden decreased from 4 (IQR 5) at baseline to 2 (IQR 3) at follow-up (Z = -3.863, p < 0.001). Symptom burden decreased in 35 patients (71.4%) and increased in 8 (16.3%). Loss of appetite, diarrhea/vomiting, dizziness, sleep disturbances, headache, and fever decreased significantly, whereas hair loss increased at follow-up. Among 48 patients with complete paired data, changes in symptom burden correlated inversely with changes in seven SF-36 domains, most strongly for vitality (ρ = -0.343), social functioning (ρ = -0.318), and emotional well-being (ρ = -0.289), but none remained significant after FDR correction. CONCLUSIONS: Symptom burden decreased within three months after COVID-19 hospitalization. Although higher symptom burden was associated with poorer HRQoL at follow-up, associations between changes in symptom burden and changes in HRQoL were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons.

title: Natural Killer Cell Decrease at Admission Is Associated With Severe Outcomes in Hospitalized Influenza and COVID-19: An 8-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background Natural killer (NK) cells are central effector cells in early innate antiviral immunity, but the clinical significance of NK cells at admission in hospitalized respiratory viral infection remains insufficiently defined. Methods We conducted a retrospective cohort study of hospitalized patients with influenza (n=366) from December 2016 to June 2024, with a COVID-19 validation cohort (n=1,072) from December 2021 to June 2024. NK cell counts were measured in peripheral blood within 48 hours of admission and NK cell decrease was defined as below the hospital laboratory lower reference limit of 136 cells/μL. The associations between NK cells and clinical outcomes were assessed using logistic regression and restricted cubic splines (RCS). Results NK cell decrease occurred in 48.6% (178/366) of the influenza cohort and 51.0% (547/1,072) of the COVID-19 cohort. After adjustment for age, sex, and comorbidities, NK cell decrease was associated with prolonged hospitalization (influenza: aOR 2.3 [1.5-3.5], P Conclusions Decreased NK cell at admission was independently associated with severe clinical outcomes in hospitalized viral infections. NK cell counts may help identify patients who warrant closer clinical monitoring.

title: Fraudulent COVID-19 prevention and treatment claims online: A content analysis of FDA warning letters, 2020-2023.
abstract: Background The digital age has brought about a major change in how health-related information is created and disseminated, particularly through the internet and social media platforms. During the COVID-19 pandemic, social media amplified unverified or misleading claims and misinformation that could have resulted in serious public health consequences. The FDA issued warning letters to companies marketing products with fraudulent COVID-19 prevention or treatment claims. Objectives Using a content-analysis approach, the purpose of the study was to review FDA issued warning letters between March 2020-December 2023 for products with fraudulent claims regarding COVID-19 prevention, treatment, or cure. Methods Full-text copies of all warning letters are available on the FDA website. A data abstraction form was developed based on past literature on the relevant topic, and pilot tested on warning letters issued in March 2020. Information collected in the form included product name, company name, product details, type of media, number of violations, target audience for promotional claims, corrective action taken, and current product status. Two researchers reviewed the warning letters issued March 2020-December 2023 using this form. Data were analyzed using SAS. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and Firth's penalized logistic regression were used to evaluate trends. Results A total of 218 WLs were analyzed, with most issued in 2020 (61.9%). Drugs (64.2%) and medical devices (23.9%) were most frequently cited. Websites combined with social media were the predominant channels (45.0%), with Facebook, X (formerly known as Twitter), and Instagram most implicated. Consumers were the primary target (96.8%). Corrective actions were documented in 63.1% of cases, yet 36.9% remained non-compliant. Clinical outcome claims comprised 79.7% of violations. Firth's penalized logistic regression revealed significantly higher odds of non-compliance among dietary supplements (OR=11.5) and medical devices (OR=3.6) relative to drugs. Conclusion This study revealed COVID-19 related fraudulent and unproven claims included in the warning letters issued by the FDA. Protecting consumers from products with such claims is crucial to promote consumer safety during COVID-19.

title: Cellular Composition, Not Transcriptional Reprogramming, Drives the COVID-19 Brain Aging Signature in Postmortem Frontal Cortex
abstract: Severe COVID-19 produces a frontal cortex transcriptome that resembles brain aging. What remains unresolved is the regulatory architecture behind that signature, and whether the bulk RNA-seq signal reflects cell-intrinsic transcriptional reprogramming or shifts in cellular composition. We addressed both questions in a single integrated analysis of GSE188847 (n = 54 postmortem frontal cortex samples; 22 COVID-19, 23 age- and sex-matched controls, 9 ICU/ventilated non-COVID controls). DESeq2 differential expression with apeglm shrinkage identified 7,079 differentially expressed genes between COVID-19 and control samples (4,086 up, 2,993 down). Gene set enrichment analysis recovered 1,708 GO Biological Process terms, with humoral and innate immune programs activated and synaptic transmission, axonal development and oxidative phosphorylation suppressed. VIPER master regulator analysis using DoRothEA confidence A/B/C regulons identified 31 transcription factors with significantly altered activity. NF-κB (RELA, NFKB1) and IFN/JAK-STAT (STAT1, STAT2, STAT3, IRF2) emerged as dominant activated regulators. REST, the canonical neuronal-aging longevity factor, reached significance (NES = +3.29, padj = 0.016) and showed coordinated suppression of 8 of 11 neuronal-identity targets including BDNF, VGF and TUBB3. BRETIGEA cell-type deconvolution revealed neuronal depletion alongside astrocyte, microglia, oligodendrocyte progenitor and endothelial expansion, a five-cell-type neurovascular response. Composition-corrected DESeq2 collapsed 98.3% of the original differential expression signal: of 6,603 symbol-mapped DEGs, only 110 (1.7%) survived adjustment for neuronal and astrocyte composition. The COVID-19 frontal cortex transcriptome is therefore dominantly compositional rather than cell-intrinsic, with implications for therapeutic prioritization in post-acute neurological sequelae.

title: Upper respiratory microbiome and host immune signatures associated with SARS-CoV-2 susceptibility and illness in a human challenge model
abstract: The upper respiratory tract (URT) microbiome modulates the local mucosal immune environment, with potential implications for respiratory viral infection susceptibility and outcomes. We leveraged a first–in–human SARS–CoV–2 challenge study in 34 healthy young adults, 18 of whom became infected, to characterize host gene expression and microbiome composition and dynamics in nasal and throat samples collected before viral inoculation and over the subsequent 14 days. Compared with participants who remained uninfected, participants who became infected had elevated baseline nasal expression of gene modules related to interferon, innate inflammatory, and neutrophil responses, as well as a delayed transcriptional response to viral challenge. Baseline nasal microbiome composition differed modestly by subsequent infection status, with lower relative abundances of Corynebacterium accolens and higher abundances of Dolosigranulum pigrum and Staphylococcus aureus among participants who became infected. Integrated analyses of microbiome and host gene expression data identified coordinated networks of microbiome features and host immune modules that distinguished infected from uninfected participants, including prior to inoculation. Notably, immune modules associated with infection susceptibility were positively correlated with S. aureus abundance and negatively correlated with the abundances of common nasal commensals, Corynebacterium spp. and Staphylococcus epidermidis , linking altered nasal microbiome community structure with the heightened inflammatory state associated with infection susceptibility. Symptom burden and viral load were similarly linked to distinct networks of microbiome and host gene expression features within nasal samples. Taken together, these findings highlight potential microbiome–host interactions within the nasal mucosa that may contribute to differences in respiratory viral infection outcomes.

title: Reactogenicity, persistent symptom clusters, causal attribution, and interference with daily activities after COVID-19 vaccination in Bangladesh
abstract: Abstract Concern about post-vaccination symptoms influences vaccine confidence, yet safety studies seldom examine how symptoms co-occur or how recipients interpret them. This study aimed to examine whether acute reactions, persistent symptom clusters, and attribution of symptoms to vaccination were associated with interference with daily activities. In a retrospective cross-sectional study, 450 vaccinated people in Tangail District, Bangladesh, were selected by purposive sampling with quotas and interviewed face-to-face between May and August 2026 using a pretested, structured Bangla questionnaire. Participants recalled first-week symptoms after dose one, problems lasting over one month, whether they attributed symptoms to vaccination, and any interference with daily activities. Associations were estimated by structural equation modelling for categorical data. Stronger acute reactions were associated with a greater persistent somatic–cognitive and allergic-type burden (β = 0.624 and 0.558), whereas sociodemographic and vaccine characteristics explained 8.0% of the variance in acute reactions. Both clusters were associated with stronger attribution, and attribution was associated with interference (β = 0.497), accounting statistically for 42–45% of each cluster’s association with interference. Alternative orderings fitted equally well, so the direction of these associations remains unresolved. Prospective studies with validated measures and a comparison group are needed before appraisal-focused interventions are considered.

title: Characteristics and Factors Associated with SARS-CoV-2 Positivity Among Hospitalized Pregnant and Postpartum Women with Acute Respiratory Febrile Illness in Suzhou, China, 2020–2024
abstract: Background/Objectives: To describe SARS-CoV-2 positivity, temporal patterns, and associated factors among pregnant and postpartum women hospitalized with acute respiratory infection or febrile illness (ARFI) in Suzhou, China. Methods: Women who met the ARFI case definition between 2020 and 2024 were included and tested for SARS-CoV-2. Epidemiological and clinical characteristics, disease severity, and outcomes were compared between SARS-CoV-2-positive and non-SARS-CoV-2 ARFI cases. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with SARS-CoV-2 positivity. Results: Among 4219 pregnant and postpartum women hospitalized with ARFI and enrolled in surveillance, 512 (12.1%) tested positive for SARS-CoV-2. After excluding six women with influenza coinfection, the analytic cohort included 512 women who tested positive and 3701 who tested negative. SARS-CoV-2 positivity peaked in December 2022, May–June 2023, and July–August 2024. Among women admitted from December 2022 through December 2024, gestational diabetes mellitus was associated with higher odds of SARS-CoV-2 positivity after adjustment for admission year, vaccination status before admission, and other covariates (aOR 2.21, 95% CI 1.57–3.10). Conclusions: Among pregnant and postpartum women hospitalized with ARFI, gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) was associated with higher odds of SARS-CoV-2 positivity. These findings support continued active surveillance for respiratory viral infections in this population during the post-emergency phase, with particular attention to women with GDM.

title: Themes, Temporal Dynamics, and Public Engagement in COVID-19 Vaccination Disclosures on Twitter: Computational Content Analysis.
abstract: Background Social media has become a primary infrastructure for vaccine communication. Personal vaccination disclosures, or first-person announcements of vaccination decisions shared publicly online, represent an underexamined channel through which peer influence may shape vaccine attitudes and behavior. Understanding what individuals disclose when they announce vaccination, and how those disclosures evolve over time, offers actionable insights for designing peer-based communication strategies in future health emergencies. Objective This study aimed to identify the themes present in COVID-19 vaccination disclosures on Twitter (rebranded as X in 2023), examine how those themes changed across 4 phases of the US vaccine rollout, and determine which themes were associated with greater public engagement. Methods Guided by the disclosure decision model (DDM), we analyzed 207,647 vaccination disclosure posts on Twitter from December 14, 2020, to January 1, 2022. Posts were identified using a robustly optimized BERT pretraining approach (RoBERTa) binary classifier ( F 1 -score=0.85) trained on 6348 human-coded posts. A mixed deductive-inductive coding approach, grounded in the DDM's motivational goals, yielded 11 disclosure themes (Krippendorff α =0.72-0.93). Eleven additional RoBERTa classifiers were trained to label themes across the full dataset. Network analysis examined co-occurrence of themes within each rollout phase. Negative binomial regression assessed the association between disclosure themes and an engagement metric (sum of likes, reposts, quotes, and replies), controlling for follower count, media presence, word count, sentiment, and other post-level factors. Results Eleven distinct disclosure themes were identified, including community identity (n=31,847, 15.34%), encouraging others (n=29,619, 14.26%), and gratitude (n=29,511, 14.21%). Themes shifted meaningfully across rollout phases: gratitude dominated phase 1, community identity rose in phases 2 and 4, and encouraging vaccination became prominent in phase 3. Gratitude was associated with a 25% increase in engagement (incidence rate ratio [IRR]=1.25; 95% CI 1.23-1.28; P P P P P P P Conclusions Vaccination disclosures on Twitter were thematically patterned, theoretically interpretable via the DDM, and responsive to changing public health contexts. Identity-based and emotionally resonant disclosures, particularly gratitude and community identity, were among the themes most strongly associated with public engagement. These findings provide an empirically grounded framework for designing peer-based vaccine communication strategies that leverage voluntary self-disclosure in future immunization campaigns.

title: Impacto da COVID-19 na vacinação infantil contra poliomielite no Brasil entre 2020 e 2023: uma revisão sistemática
abstract: Introduction: Poliomyelitis, also known as Infantile Paralysis, is an acute infectious disease caused by the poliovirus, which inhabits the intestine and can infect both children and adults. In severe cases, it can cause paralysis of the lower limbs. Transmission occurs through direct contact with feces or secretions expelled from the mouths of infected individuals, and vaccination is the only form of prevention, as recommended by the Brazilian Ministry of Health. Objective: This systematic review aimed to analyze, between 2020 and 2023, how COVID-19 influenced the decline in vaccination coverage and the possible reemergence of poliomyelitis. Methodology: This is a systematic review without meta-analysis, conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. The following databases were used: PubMed, Virtual Health Library (BVS), and Google Scholar, for the search of studies and reviews published in English and Portuguese during the aforementioned period. Articles were selected based on the following inclusion criteria: original research, published between 2020 and 2023, written in Portuguese or English, and articles addressing relevant historical aspects of poliomyelitis. The exclusion criteria included: duplicate articles, studies not addressing poliomyelitis vaccination, articles not discussing the impact of the pandemic on childhood immunization, publications outside the 2020–2023 period, opinion pieces, and doctoral theses. Results: A relationship was observed between the decline in vaccination rates and the reemergence of poliomyelitis in Brazil; however, this decline had already been noted prior to the pandemic. The studies identified several factors contributing to vaccine hesitancy, such as misinformation, fear of exposure to the virus at vaccination sites, and difficulties accessing healthcare services. Nevertheless, it is important to note that vaccination coverage was already below the nationally recommended threshold even before the pandemic. Conclusion: Although the number of administered vaccines decreased due to the influence of the COVID-19 pandemic, data from the Ministry of Health show that, up to the year 2023, there have been no new cases of poliomyelitis in Brazil. Therefore, it cannot be stated that there is a reemergence of the disease in the country.

title: Condiciones laborales y salud mental del personal de Enfermería en México durante la pandemia Covid-19 Working conditions and mental health of nursing workers in Mexico during the covid-19 pandemic
abstract: Nursing staff faced working conditions that impacted their mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic. Objective: To analyze the relationship between working conditions and mental health—burnout, anxiety, and depression—among nursing staff in Mexico during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methodology: A descriptive cross-sectional study using online surveys to assess working conditions and mental health. Results: 81.1% reported an emotional disturbance. Anxiety was the most common (60%), followed by burnout (40%) and depression (30%). 8.8% reported all three conditions simultaneously, and 94.8% reported job satisfaction. The models (logistic regression and Random Forest) highlighted that exposure to environmental risks, physical exertion, and a lack of material resources exacerbated symptoms. Conclusion: The evidence points to the need for structural interventions; institutional policies are required to improve working conditions and implement psychosocial support, especially for young staff and those in critical areas.
