title: Detection of SARS-CoV-2 in Semen Months After COVID-19: Potential Evidence of Low-Level Replicative Persistence.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Viral persistence is considered one of the key mechanisms driving long COVID symptoms. The male genital tract (MGT), particularly the testis, is an immune-privileged site that may serve as a viral reservoir for SARS-CoV-2. However, the presence of SARS-CoV-2 in semen and its long-term infectiousness remains controversial. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to investigate the long-term presence and potential replicative activity of SARS-CoV-2 in semen, evaluating whether the virus can persist and maintain low-level culture signals in the MGT well beyond the acute phase of infection. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This observational, prospective, cross-sectional study included 38 men treated at Mater Dei Hospital, Brazil, between October 2020 and October 2021, who had recovered from mild to moderate COVID-19 and consented to participate. Semen samples were collected from mildly symptomatic participants at approximately 1 month (15- 45 days), 3 months, and 6 months after symptom onset. The moderately symptomatic group provided a single sample approximately 6 months post-infection. Semen analysis and SARS-CoV-2 detection were performed using RT-qPCR, followed by viral isolation in Vero CCL-81 cells. Potential viral persistence and replication signals were evaluated through immunofluorescence and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). RESULTS: SARS-CoV-2 was detected by RT-qPCR in 21 of 38 patients (55%), with high cycle threshold (Ct 38-39) values observed for more than 6 months post-infection. Following inoculation into Vero cell cultures, a low-level in vitro expansion of viral copies was identified in a subset of samples from mild and moderate patients. title: A Beta-to-Alpha seasonal coronavirus antibody signature identifies high and low responders to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination
abstract: Pre-existing immunity to endemic seasonal human coronaviruses may shape subsequent responses to SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. We longitudinally profiled 775 healthcare workers using a systems immunology machine learning framework and found that a recursive feature elimination cross-validation model classified individuals in the top and bottom quartiles of SARS-CoV-2 Spike IgG responses (AUC=0.72, empirical P<0.001). This predictive signature was prominently driven by a baseline bias toward Beta-coronavirus relative to Alpha-coronavirus Spike reactivity.

title: Resilient outputs, disrupted inputs: Internalised intermediation and the decoupling of university spin-off pipelines during COVID-19
abstract: Abstract Entrepreneurial ecosystem research usually judges resilience by whether venture outputs continue. This paper argues that in staged knowledge-commercialisation systems such judgements can mislead, because inputs, outputs and the intermediaries that connect them can respond differently to the same shock. Using a validated panel of 93 UK universities’ invention disclosures, spin-out formation and pre-pandemic commercialisation arrangements (2014/15–2024/25), linked to a register of 2,560 university spin-outs, I examine how university spin-off pipelines responded to COVID-19. Because restriction intensity barely differed across the four UK nations, identification relies on comparisons across pipeline stages within each university and year, and on differences in how universities organised commercialisation before the pandemic. Invention disclosures fell by about 19% at the trough, yet spin-out formation did not decline: spin-outs relative to disclosures rose by about 40% during the shock years, partly continuing a pre-pandemic upward trend. Universities that lost more disclosures formed fewer spin-outs over the following years. Contrary to the view that partner-based, relationally embedded intermediation confers adaptability, conversion rose less where spin-off support was delivered with external partners and more where it was provided in-house, while pre-pandemic ties with industry buffered neither disclosures nor spin-outs. I conceptualise these patterns as stage-specific resilience and propose that under correlated shocks, internalised conversion capacity matters more than access to partners. The findings caution against output-based resilience metrics and inform how universities and policymakers configure technology transfer for future disruptions. JEL classification: I23; L26; M13; O32; O33; O38

title: Malaria burden and care in hard-to-reach indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon during the COVID-19 pandemic: A mixed-methods study.
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with reported disruptions to healthcare delivery and malaria control activities in remote, malaria-endemic indigenous communities with limited access to healthcare. Such communities in the Peruvian Amazon may have been especially vulnerable due to interruptions in malaria surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment. We investigated malaria burden, healthcare access, and community perceptions during the COVID-19 pandemic in hard-to-reach indigenous communities in the Amazonas region of Peru. Methods A convergent parallel mixed-methods study was conducted in 2021 and 2022 across four indigenous communities in the Río Santiago district, Amazonas region, Peru. Quantitative data were collected through cross-sectional malaria surveys, and qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with inhabitants, community health workers, and local health personnel. Malaria was detected by microscopy and confirmed by PCR. Factors associated with PCR-confirmed malaria were analyzed using a generalized estimating equation (GEE) to account for repeated observations within participants across study years. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically, and both components were integrated using the Pillar Integration Process framework. Results A total of 514 participants were included. PCR-based malaria prevalence was 17.6% in 2021 and 26.09% in 2022. falciparum prevalence was particularly high in the Alianza Progreso community (2021: 24.19%, 2022: 16.16%) compared to the other studied communities. Previous malaria and chills were associated with PCR-confirmed malaria. Qualitative findings indicated that COVID-19-related disruptions affected malaria control activities by interrupting diagnosis and treatment availability, reducing community follow-up, and prioritizing COVID-19 response activities over malaria control. Participants also described fear of COVID-19, temporary migration to farm areas, and reliance on herbal medicine during the pandemic. Conclusions The COVID-19 pandemic may have contributed to exacerbated pre-existing challenges to malaria control in remote indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon. Our findings document a substantial malaria burden, alongside participant-reported disruptions to malaria surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment. Strengthening malaria surveillance, ensuring continuity of diagnosis and treatment, and improving healthcare access in geographically isolated communities will be critical priorities for supporting malaria elimination efforts in Peru.

title: Employment and Coping Strategies of Young Intellectuals in Vietnam During the Covid-19 Pandemic
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic brought about significant disruptions to Vietnam’s labour market, affecting the employment and incomes of various groups of workers, including young intellectuals. Drawing on an analysis of data from the 2019 and 2020 Labour Force Surveys conducted by the General Statistics Office of Vietnam, complemented by a review of relevant studies, this article examines the employment situation, income, and coping strategies of young intellectuals in Vietnam during the pandemic. The findings indicate that, in addition to job losses, temporary work suspensions, and declining incomes, some young intellectuals chose to wait for work until they were able to resume their employment. This pattern was more pronounced among younger individuals and those who were unmarried. Other coping strategies included seeking alternative employment, transitioning to remote work, and undertaking training to acquire or upgrade skills. However, their capacity to adapt was also shaped by employment conditions, employers’ orientations, and access to training opportunities. These findings contribute to a better understanding of the challenges faced by young intellectuals and the strategies they adopted in response to labour market disruptions during the COVID-19 pandemic.
journal: Journal of Social Science and Human Research Studies

title: Innate immune single-cell profiling after SARS-CoV-2 BA.1 infection unveils remodeling of monocytes and antigen-presenting cells modulated across viral variants
abstract: Continuous genetic diversification of SARS-CoV-2 has generated viral variants with distinct transmissibility and immune-evasion properties. While adaptive immune escape was extensively investigated, how epidemiologically successive variants interact with circulating innate immune cells and modulate antiviral, inflammatory and antigen-presenting functions remains incompletely understood. By applying an integrated experimental approach combining high-dimensional immunophenotyping, secretome profiling, functional and virological assays, innate immune reprogramming induced by ancestral D614G strain, Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Omicron BA.1, and recombinant Omicron XBB.1 variants was assessed using a human peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC)–based in vitro model. Single-cell multi-omic profiling upon Omicron BA.1 exposure revealed profound remodeling of the innate immune landscape, with a particularly marked dampening on monocyte differentiation and functional maturation. Viral RNA mapping and dsRNA+ cell detection demonstrated preferential viral accumulation within monocyte compartment, associated with transcriptomic reprogramming. Omicron emergence leads to a more balanced inflammatory profile with preserved antiviral type I interferon (IFN) responses and moderated chemokine induction, indicating a progressively regulated virus–host equilibrium and reduced innate immune-mediated tissue damage. Post-Omicron recombinant XBB.1 subvariant robustly re-engaged antiviral pathways, inducing high IFN release and uniquely promoting IL-12p70 production, driving expansion of antiviral and mature PD-L1+CD80+ plasmacytoid dendritic cell (DC) and BDCA3+ conventional DC subsets, supporting CD8+ T-cell priming. These findings identify monocytes as major cell targets for SARS-CoV-2-induced innate immune remodeling and demonstrate that circulation of epidemiologically successive viral variants elicit distinct innate immune profiles, providing a framework to investigate how variant-intrinsic properties influence antiviral defense, inflammation and antigen-presenting cell differentiation.

title: Prolonged SARS-CoV-2 viral shedding in a patient with lymphoma and systemic lupus erythematosus treated with B cell targeted therapy: a case report
abstract: Vaccination and the emergence of antiviral drugs have led to a reduction in the COVID-19 fatality rate. However, prolonged SARS-CoV-2 shedding remains a concern, especially among patients receiving chemotherapy or immunosuppressive therapy, and many aspects of the virological characteristics of prolonged shedding remain unknown. A 61-year-old Japanese woman with a history of lymphoma and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) was infected with the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.2 variant in April 2022 while undergoing treatment with rituximab and belimumab, which targets B cells. Treatment with sotrovimab resulted in clinical improvement, but on day 32 her respiratory status worsened and she was readmitted to a hospital. Although her respiratory symptoms and pneumonia improved after treatment with remdesivir, corticosteroids, and tocilizumab, she remained SARS-CoV-2 RNA positive until day 134 and was eventually confirmed to be negative on day 163. Virological analysis revealed the presence of the SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) E340K mutation, which has been reported to be associated with sotrovimab treatment, on day 39. The mutation was followed by the S: E340D mutation on days 56 and 63, with subsequent reversion to S: E340K on day 70. This is the first report of prolonged COVID-19 case for an extended period in patients with a history of belimumab administration. The virus remained positive for a long period of time, but after being transferred to our hospital, appropriate treatment was performed and no recurrence of symptoms was observed. Even in immunosuppressed patients, it is important to provide appropriate anti-inflammatory therapy during acute pneumonia and worsening respiratory conditions. In addition, early tapering of immunosuppressants, such as corticosteroids and additional administration of antiviral drugs, might be considered.

title: Uneven Home-to-Work Geographies during COVID-19: Evidence from U.S. LODES
abstract: Abstract Changes in aggregate employment counts do not fully describe the geography of linked home and workplace locations during COVID-19. Census Bureau Longitudinal Employer--Household Dynamics Origin--Destination Employment Statistics (LODES) for 2019--2021 to compare employment-linkage volume and distance dispersion across illustrative states and industry categories. Block-level records are aggregated to a 1-km grid and reciprocal directions are combined. Grid cells are organized into ten ordinal linkage-intensity groups, and job-weighted distance dispersion is calculated for each group pair. Across five illustrative states, linked-job counts fell by 1.2\%--9.5\% in 2020 relative to 2019. Arizona was 0.6\% above its 2019 level in 2021, whereas Alabama, Colorado, Connecticut, and New York remained 1.3\%--9.5\% below their pre-pandemic levels. Occupied-cell counts changed much less than linked-job totals. The normalized dispersion matrices also differed: Connecticut and New Jersey retained higher displayed values toward high-intensity group pairs, while Montana and Oklahoma showed different arrangements across the group indices. Iowa's three broad industry categories exhibited distinct group-pair dispersion configurations. These descriptive comparisons show why employment volume, spatial coverage, and distance dispersion should be examined separately. The framework makes sector and geographical differences visible while distinguishing administrative employment linkages from observed daily commuting trips.

title: Unnecessary spending by health care entities on unproven COVID-19 treatments in the United States from January 2020 to December 2022.
abstract: Background During the COVID 19 pandemic, inaccurate and false information regarding treatments was disseminated via numerous internet based, mainstream media, and social media outlets. Hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine, and ivermectin received substantial public attention despite limited evidence supporting their use for COVID-19. Medications used without evidence of benefit may carry unknown risks, contribute to adverse effects, or delay appropriate care. Objective To evaluate whether changes in institutional purchasing expenditures for selected COVID-19-related therapies were temporally associated with public announcements, media coverage, and social media dissemination during the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods Monthly U.S. institutional health care expenditures for hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine, and ivermectin from January 2020 through December 2022 were analyzed using IQVIA's National Sales Perspective database. These therapies were selected for promotion despite limited evidence, and subsequent recommendations against their use by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA). Graphical analyses and interrupted time-series analyses using Prais-Winsten regression models were conducted to assess temporal associations between expenditures and periods of heightened media attention. Results Expenditures for hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine peaked sharply in early 2020 before returning to baseline levels. In contrast, ivermectin expenditures fluctuated substantially and peaked in 2021, without clear alignment with evidence-based clinical recommendations. Conclusion Institutional spending increases appeared to be temporally associated with media and social media dissemination rather than with established clinical evidence, highlighting the potential impact of misinformation on medication purchasing during public health emergencies.

title: Stakeholders' collaboration towards strengthening health systems for effective response to the COVID-19 pandemic in the African region: a multi-method qualitative study.
abstract: Introduction Weak health systems across WHO Regional Office for Africa (WHO AFRO) Member States before the COVID-19 pandemic were a major driver of the need for coordinated multi-stakeholder support. This study aimed to analyse how WHO AFRO and other stakeholders collaborated to strengthen the six health system building blocks during the COVID-19 response, to identify the mechanisms that worked well and the tensions, gaps and unresolved challenges that limited collaboration and to inform future pandemic preparedness. Methods We conducted a multi-method qualitative study combining document review (n=191), key informant interviews (n=164) across 18 purposively selected countries, 10 focus group discussions (n=75 participants) and an online survey (n=215 respondents) with WHO, ministries of health, non-governmental organisations and civil society organisations between 2020 and 2022. Data were thematically analysed and triangulated across sources and organised against the six health system building blocks. Results Respondents described WHO AFRO's collaborative role in maintaining essential health services, training and protecting the health workforce, strengthening health information systems, securing and distributing medicines, mobilising funding and coordinating leadership structures such as incident management teams. However, respondents and documentary evidence also identified substantial challenges, including workforce repurposing and burnout, weak data analytics capacity, delayed and inequitable vaccine access through COVAX, insufficient stockpile financing and uneven government commitment to early containment measures. Conclusions Multi-stakeholder collaboration, in which WHO AFRO played a coordinating role, contributed to health system gains during the COVID-19 response, but these gains were uneven across the six health system pillars and constrained by unresolved structural weaknesses, including vaccine access inequity and limited direct engagement of some key regional actors. Addressing these gaps alongside the successes identified is essential for strengthening future pandemic preparedness in the WHO AFRO region.

title: Search Interest in Alleged COVID-19 Treatments During the Pandemic and the Impact of Mass News Media Coverage Based on Google Trends and Media Cloud Data: Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: Background During a public health emergency, interest in unsafe or illegitimate medications can delay appropriate treatment and foster medical mistrust. Objective The aim of this study is to assess the relationship between search interest and media coverage of 3 purported COVID-19 treatments: hydroxychloroquine, ivermectin, and remdesivir. Methods The authors obtained daily US-based Google Trends and Media Cloud data from 2019 through 2022, conducted national-level anomaly detection, and assessed the state-level association of treatment-specific search interest and media coverage by regressing search interest against daily media coverage, and vice versa, for each treatment using a 2-stage process. This allowed us to explicitly model the questions: (1) does a state have any of the outcomes (search interest or media coverage), and (2) given a nonzero outcome, how much is it impacted by the exposure? Results Search interest and media coverage of all 3 treatments were significantly elevated during the study period. Anomaly detection identified several periods of higher-than-expected activity; anomalies in search interest and media coverage showed similar temporal patterns within treatments. There were distinct patterns of media source bias across treatments: while the plurality of top sources for all treatments were rated "Left" or "Left Leaning," ivermectin was covered by the highest number of "Right"-biased sources, and remdesivir had the highest coverage by "Center" or unbiased sources. Significant associations between media coverage and search interest were observed for all 3 treatments. Media coverage had the strongest impact on same-day search interest for hydroxychloroquine (21.3% increase, 95% CI 20.1%-22.5%) and ivermectin (18.3% increase, 95% CI 16.8%-19.7%), and a more modest impact for remdesivir (12.8% increase, 95% CI 11.8%-13.8%). For hydroxychloroquine and remdesivir, this same-day effect was more transient, while interest in ivermectin remained elevated at a comparable level 1 and 2 days after media coverage. When evaluating the separate impact of search interest on media coverage, the associations were much weaker for all 3 treatments and all lagged conditions. Conclusions During a public health emergency, the information accessed by populations can directly influence health-seeking behaviors, potentially resulting in life-threatening consequences. Given the observed associations between treatment-related news media coverage and public interest in those treatments, our results suggest that news media serve as a powerful mechanism for experts to inform the landscape of public opinion and to reach audiences during future public health emergencies.

title: Maladaptive personality trait change during the first eight months of the COVID-19 pandemic in the German general population
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic provides a context for examining whether maladaptive personality traits—dispositions that can lead to distress and impaired functioning—respond to a lasting change in the shared environment. Using data from the GESIS Panel (N = 4,742), a probability-based sample of the German adult population, we examined maladaptive personality traits based on the Alternative Model for Personality Disorders in DSM-5. Traits were assessed four months before and eight months after the outbreak of the pandemic in Germany. Mean levels increased in antagonism (d = 0.20), the general factor of personality disorder (0.13), detachment (0.11), psychoticism (0.11), and disinhibition (0.10), but not in negative affectivity (−0.01). These changes are small but exceed the near-zero mean-level change expected over one year under normal conditions. Under assumptions we make explicit, we interpret them as a nonspecific effect of the pandemic. Increases were larger among younger and middle-aged adults than among older adults, for whom they were close to zero except in antagonism. Pre-pandemic trait levels predicted adverse life circumstances and negative perceptions of one’s life. In exploratory analyses, romantic relationship conflict, psychopathological symptoms, and mistrust in public institutions were associated with small individual shifts toward higher trait levels.

title: Astrocytes as a Convergence Point for Neuroprotection and Drug Repurposing in Long COVID Comorbidities.
abstract: Astrocytes are central regulators of metabolic homeostasis, redox balance, and neuroimmune signaling within the central nervous system, and accumulating evidence implicates these cells as key mediators of the neurological sequelae associated with long COVID. SARS-CoV-2 has been shown to infect neural cells, inducing substantial alterations in these regulatory parameters and promoting a sustained reactive astrocyte phenotype that compromises synaptic plasticity, blood-brain barrier integrity, and metabolic support, thereby contributing to neurometabolic and neuropsychiatric dysfunction. Despite the convergence of these findings, no review has addressed the interplay between astrocyte biology, systemic metabolic and psychiatric comorbidities, and the potential for drug repurposing within a gliopharmacological context in long COVID. In this review, we propose an astrocyte-centered model in which long COVID arises from the convergence of direct viral injury and pre-existing disorders. We then critically examine the repurposing potential of three pharmacological categories, each selected on the basis of their documented actions on astrocytic metabolic, redox, or inflammatory pathways: systemic medications already in wide clinical use for metabolic and cardiovascular indications, including metformin, angiotensin II receptor blockers, calcium-channel blockers, and statins; centrally acting agents with established or emerging use in psychiatry, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors and ketamine; and the glioprotective polyphenol resveratrol. Accordingly, we delineate a translational rationale for repurposing existing therapeutics to target astrocyte-mediated pathways in long COVID. This manuscript, therefore, reinforces astrocytes as central mediators of neuroprotection and supports gliopharmacological approaches as a rational strategy to mitigate neurological dysfunction in long COVID associated with neurometabolic and neuropsychiatric comorbidities.

title: TMPRSS2 reduces antibody recognition of SARS-CoV-2 spike
abstract: The serine protease TMPRSS2 acts as a cofactor for SARS-CoV-2 entry by cleaving the viral spike (S) to initiate fusion. Whether TMPRSS2 has an impact on humoral immune response against S remains poorly characterized. Here, we show that TMPRSS2 impairs antibody binding to S. In S-expressing and infected cells, TMPRSS2 decreases monoclonal antibody (mAb) and immune serum binding, as well as antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) induction. Using a panel of 39 mAbs targeting various S regions, we observe that those binding to the S2 subunit are the most affected by TMPRSS2. TMPRSS2 promotes a partial shedding of S1 and changes S2 conformation. This processing reduces Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 (ACE2) binding while increasing cell-cell fusion. We further observe that the capacity of TMPRSS2 to decrease antibody recognition is conserved across coronaviruses and shared with other TMPRSS proteins. However, TMPRSS2 expression in infected cells does not impact significantly virions' infectivity or the antibody recognition, as measured by flow virometry. Collectively, our findings suggest that TMPRSS2 processing of S favors a conformation which is less sensitive to antibody recognition.

title: Decomposition of age-specific income-related health inequalities: mobility around the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in Germany
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic caused major societal disruptions that may have altered existing health inequalities. This study examines how income-related inequalities in physical and mental health in Germany changed between 2018 and 2020, and whether these changes were driven by income-related health changes or by health-related income changes. Methods Data from the 2018 and 2020 waves of the German Socio-Economic Panel were used to analyze physical and mental health outcomes derived from the SF-12 questionnaire. Age-specific mean levels were estimated, and a varying concentration index was applied to estimate smoothed, age-specific measures of income-related health inequality for men and women and for households with and without children. Changes in inequality were separated into income-related health changes and health-related income changes using a mobility decomposition. Results Physical health declined significantly for working-age and older men, while remaining largely stable for women. Mental health decreased across most groups. The physical health advantage of higher-income individuals grew, while their mental health advantage shrank and disappeared among women in their 30s. Both shifts were driven by income-related health changes, while health-related income changes contributed significantly only to mental health inequality among women in their mid-30s. Conclusions The pandemic period did not uniformly exacerbate income-related health inequality but shifted its social distribution. In a crisis that affected both health and income, individuals in poorer health largely kept their income position, at least in the short term, whereas lower-income individuals experienced comparatively larger declines in physical health.

title: Understanding the Support Needs of People With Long COVID: A Qualitative Study in Aotearoa New Zealand.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Long COVID is a multi-system condition that affects an increasing number of individuals. Little is known about the support needs of people living with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences and healthcare access challenges of people with long COVID to better inform service design. METHODS: Co-design methodology was used, informed by the Stanford Design Thinking process and knowledge mobilisation approaches. Participants were recruited via snowballing, through professional networks and support groups. People with lived experience of long COVID were invited to participate in a 2-h workshop, facilitated by researchers, conducted between March and September 2024. Participants were asked to create a depiction of their experience of long COVID and describe their creation to the group; descriptions were audio-recorded, transcribed and thematically analysed. The inclusion of people with lived experience of long COVID as co-investigators ensured that the study was designed and conducted to forefront their knowledge and experience. RESULTS: Eight workshops were conducted, including 30 participants, between March and August 2024. Of these, 25 (83%) were female; of the 25 who provided their age, most were aged 45 to 64 years (n = 18, 72%), four (16%) were aged 25 to 44 years and three (12%) aged 65 years or older. Five key themes emerged: (i) lack of assistance; (ii) systemic barriers; (iii) absence of long COVID clinics; (iv) financial strain; and (v) low quality of care. A sixth theme identified personal coping strategies. CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand face major barriers to care, including inadequate services, financial hardship, and fragmented healthcare pathways. Findings support improved pathways and primary health care education in long COVID. A person-centred, coordinated, and accessible model of care is needed. LIVED EXPERIENCE OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was designed with two people with lived experience of long COVID included as co-investigators, and a further one on the Advisory Board. All participants had lived experience of long COVID.

title_zh: 了解 长新冠 患者的支持需求:新西兰奥特罗亚的定性研究。
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Long COVID is a multi-system condition that affects an increasing number of individuals. Little is known about the support needs of people living with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand. This study aimed to explore the lived experiences and healthcare access challenges of people with long COVID to better inform service design. METHODS: Co-design methodology was used, informed by the Stanford Design Thinking process and knowledge mobilisation approaches. Participants were recruited via snowballing, through professional networks and support groups. People with lived experience of long COVID were invited to participate in a 2-h workshop, facilitated by researchers, conducted between March and September 2024. Participants were asked to create a depiction of their experience of long COVID and describe their creation to the group; descriptions were audio-recorded, transcribed and thematically analysed. The inclusion of people with lived experience of long COVID as co-investigators ensured that the study was designed and conducted to forefront their knowledge and experience. RESULTS: Eight workshops were conducted, including 30 participants, between March and August 2024. Of these, 25 (83%) were female; of the 25 who provided their age, most were aged 45 to 64 years (n = 18, 72%), four (16%) were aged 25 to 44 years and three (12%) aged 65 years or older. Five key themes emerged: (i) lack of assistance; (ii) systemic barriers; (iii) absence of long COVID clinics; (iv) financial strain; and (v) low quality of care. A sixth theme identified personal coping strategies. CONCLUSIONS: Individuals with long COVID in Aotearoa New Zealand face major barriers to care, including inadequate services, financial hardship, and fragmented healthcare pathways. Findings support improved pathways and primary health care education in long COVID. A person-centred, coordinated, and accessible model of care is needed. LIVED EXPERIENCE OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was designed with two people with lived experience of long COVID included as co-investigators, and a further one on the Advisory Board. All participants had lived experience of long COVID.

title: Trial design and methods of home-based exercise tele-rehabilitation in high-risk veterans: Impact of COVID-19 exposure and socioeconomic factors.
abstract: Background Successful rehabilitation strategies for Veterans during and post Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) is a high clinical research priority. Long-term effects of COVID-19 on cardiopulmonary and physical function are uncertain, and rehabilitation should be feasible for Veterans. The objectives of this clinical trial are to investigate the effect of home-based supervised exercise via tele-rehabilitation on cardiopulmonary and physical function outcomes, its' impact on recovery defined by World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) components, and its effect on self-efficacy, inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers in adults who have had SARS-CoV-2 infection. Methods In the Home-Based Exercise Tele-Rehabilitation in High-Risk Veterans: Impact of COVID-19 Exposure and Socioeconomic Factors (BOOST) trial (NCT05425264), 80 middle-aged and older adults (>50 years) will be enrolled with documented COVID-19 > 90 days prior to enrollment and diagnosed with ≥2 conditions: hypertension, diabetes and/or pre-diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, dyslipidemia or 1 condition and BMI > 30 kg/m 2 . Veterans will participate from home in the 12-week exercise intervention that will consist of virtual supervised group exercise classes. Procedures before and after the intervention will include cardiopulmonary exercise testing, pulmonary function tests, assessments of physical function, and questionnaires targeting exercise self-efficacy. Discussion This novel 12-week exercise intervention program, which was designed to promote health in Veterans who have a history of SARS-CoV-2 infection, will provide critical information on the benefits of exercise on cardiopulmonary and physical function in this heterogenous population.

title: Ten-Year Surveillance of Occupational Blood and Body Fluid Exposures Across COVID-19 Pandemic Phases: A Profession- and Experience-Stratified Analysis at a Tertiary Care Hospital.
abstract: Background Blood and body fluid exposures (BBFEs) remain persistent occupational hazards for healthcare workers. Long-term profession- and experience-specific trends across pandemic phases remain poorly characterized. Methods We analyzed a 10-year BBFE surveillance dataset (2016-2025) from a tertiary hospital. Exposure rates per 1,000 healthcare workers were stratified by profession (nurses and physicians) and clinical experience (first-year, 2-3 years, ≥4 years) across four pandemic phases: pre-pandemic, early-pandemic, pandemic-stabilization, and post-pandemic transition. Results First-year nurses experienced a marked early-pandemic exposure surge (90.9 per 1,000 healthcare workers) compared with pre-pandemic baseline (33.9 per 1,000; Rate Ratio [RR] = 2.68, p = 0.0075), followed by post-pandemic normalization (30.4 per 1,000; RR = 0.33, p = 0.0034). Experienced nurses showed no significant early-pandemic increase. Physicians maintained stable exposure patterns across all experience strata, with rate variability reflecting small cohort size. Conclusions Early-pandemic workforce redistribution and reduced supervisory availability temporally coincided with increased BBFE rates among first-year nurses, whereas physician exposure patterns remained stable. Staffing restoration during the post-pandemic period aligned with novice nurse rate normalization. Accessible supervisory support and structured procedural guidance may help safeguard early-career personnel during operational disruptions.

title: Recognising Need: Social Assistance, Gender and Food Ethics in Albania during COVID-19
abstract: Abstract During the COVID−19 pandemic, many governments protected access to food by expanding existing cash social-assistance schemes rather than distributing food. Ethical assessments of such assistance have focused mainly on targeting methods, and much less on how schemes define need in the first place, particularly the needs of women carrying unpaid care. This article addresses that gap. It argues that crisis responses inherit the definitions of need built into the schemes they extend, a dynamic termed inherited recognition, so that the fairness of emergency food assistance is largely settled before the emergency. To examine this, the article develops a Recognition-to-Access framework with four stages: recognition of need, translation into eligibility rules, practical access, and ethical assessment. Through a qualitative documentary analysis of 24 coded records, comprising provisions of Albania’s 2019 social assistance law, implementing decisions and 2020 crisis measures, and findings from institutional assessments, the framework is applied to Albania’s economic assistance scheme. Albania doubled payments quickly and paid them to women, yet extra support reached almost only families already in the scheme. The law sanctions families whose working-age members do not register as jobseekers and allows no exception for unpaid care, which fell largely on women during lockdown, while food in kind was left mostly to charity. Drawing on care ethics and the right to adequate food, I contend that this rule cannot be justified without a care exemption. The article contributes a concept, a transferable analytical framework and stage-specific reforms for future crisis assistance.

title: The relationship between SARS-CoV-2 infection history and persistent symptoms in a rural Wisconsin community cohort
abstract: Some individuals experience persistent symptoms after COVID-19 (“Long COVID”). We assessed persistent symptoms consistent with Long COVID by SARS-CoV-2 infection history. Participants of a longitudinal, community-based cohort completed a survey about new persistent symptoms starting on/after January 2022. Cox models assessed relative hazards of symptoms among those with Omicron-only infection, or Omicron plus pre-Omicron infection, versus no infection. Models controlled for age group (18–49 versus ≥ 50 years), sex, and chronic health conditions as time-fixed effects and vaccination status as time-varying. Of 646 respondents, 61% were female; 66% were ≥ 50 years old. The presence of ≥ 1 new persistent symptom was 37% (107/287), 41% (124/303), and 43% (24/56) among individuals with no infection, Omicron-only infection, and Omicron plus pre-Omicron infection, respectively. Individuals with Omicron-only infection had increased, non-significant hazards of new persistent symptoms (aHR: 1.23, 95% CI: 0.94–1.61) compared to individuals with no infection. Individuals with Omicron plus pre-Omicron infection had increased, statistically significant hazards of new persistent symptoms (aHR: 1.94, 95% CI: 1.33–2.83) compared to no infection. During the Omicron variant period, SARS-CoV-2 reinfection was associated with new persistent symptoms in adults. Primary infection was not statistically significantly associated with new persistent symptoms compared to those not infected.

title: Epidemiología del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica: transmisión, carga viral salival y bioseguridad Epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 in dental practice: transmission, salivary viral load and biosafety
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre la transmisión del SARS-CoV-2 en la práctica odontológica, la carga viral salival y las medidas de bioseguridad. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la saliva y los aerosoles de los procedimientos odontológicos son vías relevantes de transmisión. La detección molecular del virus en saliva respalda su papel como reservorio y como muestra diagnóstica. Los colutorios antisépticos reducen el virus in vitro, pero su efecto clínico sobre la carga viral salival es limitado. El triaje, la protección personal, el control de aerosoles y la teleodontología fueron las medidas centrales. Conclusión: la bioseguridad debe mantenerse como norma permanente.

title: Coronavirus infection COVID-19, sarcopenia and obesity
abstract: Coronavirus infection COVID-19 is an infectious disease that can occur in acute, subacute and long-term forms. Long-term coronavirus infection (Long-COVID, post-COVID-19 syndrome) can bring delayed consequences for the patient’s body from various organs and systems. Neurological, psychoemotional, cardiovascular complications of COVID-19 are known. The pathological effect of coronavirus infection on the musculoskeletal system, including skeletal muscles, is of interest. In addition, obesity may develop, including in combination with sarcopenia - sarcopenic obesity. The destructive effect of the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus on muscle and adipose tissue is complex and multifactorial, and can occur both in the acute and subacute period of COVID-19, and against the background of Long-COVID. The pathological continuum involves hyperproduction of cytokines (called a “cytokine storm” in the acute period of severe coronavirus infection), neuromuscular transmission disorders, increased catabolism, forced physical inactivity, the consequences of self-isolation, and a number of other factors. The relationship between various pathogenic mechanisms of COVID-19 and their impact on muscle and adipose tissue is discussed in this literature review.

title: Pediatric forensic cases during the COVID 19 lockdown and reopening periods: a retrospective cohort study from a tertiary care pediatric emergency department.
abstract: The COVID‐19 lockdown disrupted daily life, altering children's exposure to risks and reshaping emergency department utilisation. Understanding how these changes influenced pediatric forensic epidemiology is essential for prevention and policy development. All forensic cases involving children aged 1 month-18 years were included. Two periods were analysed: the COVID-19 lockdown period (March 2020-June 2021) and the post-lockdown period (June 2021-March 2024). Data on demographics, causes, outcomes and costs were extracted from medical and forensic records. During the COVID‐19 lockdown period, the incidence of forensic cases was 25.8 per 1000 PED visits per month, whereas during the reopening period this rate decreased to 12.7 per 1000 PED visits per month (p < 0.001). Exposure to chemical substances and assault were more frequent during the lockdown period (p = 0.01 and p = 0.001, respectively), whereas food poisoning was more common during the reopening period (p = 0.004). Forensic cases were predominant among female adolescents (p = 0.004). Male sex was associated with a significantly higher likelihood of forensic cases (OR = 1.25, 95% CI: 1.05-1.49, p = 0.011). Furthermore, the COVID-19 lockdown period was independently associated with an increased odds of forensic cases (OR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.65-2.56, p < 0.001). The median outpatient and total bills per PED visit were lower in forensic cases (48.7 vs. 68.1 TRY, p < 0.001 and 57.8 vs. 90.2 TRY, p < 0.001, respectively). Different COVID‐19 periods were associated with significant differences in the incidence, causes, and patterns of pediatric forensic cases. Male sex and the lockdown period were identified as independent risk factors for forensic presentations, highlighting the complex interaction between demographic and temporal factors in forensic epidemiology.

title: What hospitals do, not how their revenue is composed: service content and the uneven depth of the COVID-19 shock in Zhejiang, China
abstract: Abstract Background When hospital revenue falls during a shock, the headline decline conflates two problems that require different responses: patients receiving fewer services, and each service earning less. The COVID-19 shock hit hospital finances unevenly, and why some hospitals lost far more than others is usually sought in their baseline revenue structure. Methods Using monthly monitoring reports from public hospitals in Zhejiang Province, China (2016–2022; 30,571 hospital-months), we separate each hospital's revenue change into volume and unit-service-revenue components, and then ask which baseline characteristics predict shock depth. Results Revenue fell to an index of 75.56 in February–April 2020 (2019 same month = 100). Almost all of the decline (134.4%) came from fewer services, while revenue per service rose and buffered the fall; in the recovery, positive growth came mainly from revenue per service (80.7%). Baseline revenue structure explains almost none of the cross-hospital variation in shock depth: the mechanical channel through which structure could act accounts for 0.1% of variance, and structural shares add no explanatory power (ΔR2 = 0.001). What separates hospitals is what they do. Those whose work is largely deferrable care, notably dental, ophthalmic and rehabilitation services, lost far more than those centered on emergency and chronic-disease care. Conclusions Resilience monitoring should therefore report the volume and revenue-per-service channels separately, alongside service content: three indicators built from routine reports identify which hospitals are exposed before the next shock arrives, and distinguish a care-backlog problem from a revenue-per-service problem. Reporting only how much revenue fell misses this choice.

title: Prevalence and excess risk of long COVID symptoms examining controlled studies of adult populations: systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Evidence of pooled excess risk estimates of long COVID disease (COVID) symptoms based on comparisons between individuals with confirmed severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infections and negative controls remains scarce. A dedicated meta-analytic investigation focusing on adult populations has not yet been undertaken. Methods The methodology developed for this review was pre-registered with PROSPERO (CRD42022352752). A systematic literature search was conducted in the PubMed, PsycINFO, and PSYNDEX databases to identify studies assessing symptom prevalence among adult COVID-19 survivors compared with negative controls. We extracted data on outcomes reported at least 1 month after infection. Meta-analytic calculations yielded log-odds ratios and pooled prevalence estimates based on random-effects models. Furthermore, exploratory subgroup analyses were conducted. Results A total of 48 studies were included ( n = 672,168 participants). More than 200 symptom denominators were compared across studies. Meta-analytic prevalence comparisons were possible for 53 symptoms. Thirty of the 53 symptoms showed a significantly higher prevalence after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Large effect sizes were observed only for the symptoms “loss of smell” and “loss of taste.” Subgroup analyses tended to show larger effect sizes in smaller studies and in studies of lower methodological quality. Conclusion The majority of the investigated symptoms showed statistically significant differences, with higher prevalence estimates in the SARS-CoV-2 group. The symptoms “loss of smell” and “loss of taste” appear to be particularly enhanced prevalent among individuals after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Further research is needed to determine symptom prevalence rates in relation to other post-acute infection syndromes. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42022352752 , identifier CRD42022352752.

source_records.title: Prevalence and excess risk of long COVID symptoms examining controlled studies of adult populations: systematic review and meta-analysis
source_records.abstract: Background Evidence of pooled excess risk estimates of long COVID disease (COVID) symptoms based on comparisons between individuals with confirmed severe acute respiratory syndrome-coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infections and negative controls remains scarce. A dedicated meta-analytic investigation focusing on adult populations has not yet been undertaken. Methods The methodology developed for this review was pre-registered with PROSPERO (CRD42022352752). A systematic literature search was conducted in the PubMed, PsycINFO, and PSYNDEX databases to identify studies assessing symptom prevalence among adult COVID-19 survivors compared with negative controls. We extracted data on outcomes reported at least 1 month after infection. Meta-analytic calculations yielded log-odds ratios and pooled prevalence estimates based on random-effects models. Furthermore, exploratory subgroup analyses were conducted. Results A total of 48 studies were included ( n = 672,168 participants). More than 200 symptom denominators were compared across studies. Meta-analytic prevalence comparisons were possible for 53 symptoms. Thirty of the 53 symptoms showed a significantly higher prevalence after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Large effect sizes were observed only for the symptoms “loss of smell” and “loss of taste.” Subgroup analyses tended to show larger effect sizes in smaller studies and in studies of lower methodological quality. Conclusion The majority of the investigated symptoms showed statistically significant differences, with higher prevalence estimates in the SARS-CoV-2 group. The symptoms “loss of smell” and “loss of taste” appear to be particularly enhanced prevalent among individuals after SARS-CoV-2 infection. Further research is needed to determine symptom prevalence rates in relation to other post-acute infection syndromes. title: COVID-19 vaccine mRNA and Spike induce cell signaling pathways favoring the growth of tumor cells.
abstract: Copyright: © 2026 Federico. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. Billions of doses of the mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccines have been dispensed worldwide. Vaccine mRNA molecules enter cells due to their complexing with synthetic lipids. Afterwards, the synthetic mRNA translates into a full-length, biologically active, and stabilized form of the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein. Both mRNA and Spike molecules possess intrinsic signaling properties. Vaccine mRNA induces cell responses similar to those elicited by microbial RNA, including the release of downstream soluble factors like IFNα, IFNγ, and IL-6. Spike activates cell signaling pathways, such as those driven by NF-κB, ERK, and AKT, by binding to the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE)-2 cell receptor, cell membrane integrins, and other signaling molecules, both intracellularly and extracellularly. This research perspective offers a detailed analysis of the effects on cell signaling induced by both the vaccine mRNA and the Spike protein. A bulk of experimental data supports the idea that these effects, alone and in combination, can switch molecular mechanisms that both directly and indirectly contribute to the neoformation and growth of cancer cells. This possibility calls for additional investigations, considering that, in any case, favoring the growth of tumor cells does not necessarily imply the development of clinically evident tumors, which require additional, still largely unknown conditions.

title: Pathology of Iran’s Criminal Policy during the COVID-19 Pandemic (Challenges and Solutions)
abstract: The outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic confronted legal systems and criminal policy frameworks worldwide with profound challenges concerning the protection of public health, the preservation of social order, and the determination of the reciprocal responsibilities between the state and citizens. In the Islamic Republic of Iran, responses to this crisis were primarily implemented through a set of fragmented regulations, traditional criminalization approaches, and emergency executive measures that lacked legislative coherence and a unified theoretical foundation. The present study, employing a descriptive–analytical method based on documentary and library sources, provides a comprehensive examination of Iran’s criminal policy toward threats arising from epidemic diseases, with particular emphasis on COVID-19. The findings indicate that despite the existence of considerable jurisprudential, legal, and institutional capacities, Iran’s criminal policy in this field has faced multiple challenges, including ambiguity in the legal foundations for restricting individual freedoms, difficulties in proving causation in the transmission of contagious diseases, weaknesses in establishing criminal intent (mens rea), disproportionality of sanctions, overlapping institutional jurisdictions, and the absence of a comprehensive epidemic diseases law. At the same time, the experience of the COVID-19 crisis demonstrates a gradual shift in Iran’s criminal policy away from excessive criminalization toward the adoption of hybrid preventive mechanisms, participatory governance policies, non-custodial sanctions, and compensatory state responsibility. The study concludes that enhancing the effectiveness of criminal policy in confronting biosecurity threats requires a fundamental reconsideration of legislative approaches, the enactment of a comprehensive communicable diseases law grounded in the principles of necessity and proportionality, strengthened inter-institutional coordination, the development of rule-based executive policies, increased social participation, the establishment of coherent judicial practice, and the protection of fundamental rights alongside the safeguarding of public health.

title: Strategi Kampanye Komunikasi Publik Satgas Covid-19 Nasional dalam Penanganan Covid-19
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia generated significant impacts on public health and the national economy, reflected in rising confirmed cases, economic contraction, and increasing unemployment resulting from physical distancing policies. These conditions required society to adapt to new behavioral norms through structured and effective public communication. This study aims to analyze the public communication campaign strategy implemented by the National COVID-19 Task Force in managing the pandemic and to identify the supporting and inhibiting factors influencing its implementation. The research employed a qualitative approach within a constructivist paradigm using a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with the public communication division and community members and were analyzed interpretatively. The findings indicate that the campaign strategy was systematically designed with informative and persuasive objectives to enhance public awareness and encourage behavioral change. Messages were science-based and delivered by credible communicators with authentic voices. Furthermore, stakeholder mapping was conducted to strengthen collaborative support, contributing to the development of active and sustainable public participation in pandemic management.

title: Transcriptional responses of white-tailed deer to SARS-CoV-2 challenge
abstract: Abstract White-tailed deer are susceptible hosts for SARS-CoV-2, exhibiting robust viral replication, active shedding, efficient deer-to-deer transmission, and widespread natural infection across the United States. However, the molecular level host responses remain poorly defined. In this study, we describe whole blood transcriptomes from experimentally infected deer and compare their responses with other previously published wildlife hosts such as elk and bison, to better understand the molecular mechanisms underlying infection. Over time, deer exhibited a regulated antiviral response, with rapid activation of innate immune pathways and Coronavirus Pathogenesis signaling as early as day 2 post infection (pi), followed by prevalent transcriptomic remodeling and inhibition of cytokine storm associated pathways at day 5 pi, and a reduction in differential expression by day 7 pi. Ingenuity Pathway Analysis highlighted early induction of interferon associated networks and hypercytokinemia related signaling. Comparative analysis with elk and bison revealed 22 conserved upregulated genes at day 2 pi, including antiviral regulators such as ADAR and STAT1 . At day 5 pi, a mere five downregulated genes and 20 upregulated genes remained conserved between the species, highlighting a lack of shared molecular responses across species, in line with divergent infection susceptibilities. Together, these findings define the temporal architecture of the deer immune response and identify conserved host defense mechanisms serving as molecular markers of SARS-CoV-2 infection in wildlife.

title: Antibody profiling in quantity and avidity across SARS-CoV-2 variants identifies distinct long Covid endotypes
abstract: Introduction Post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection or long Covid is now estimated to affect 400 million globally, but there is no diagnostic test. The patient antibody response to 15 variants of SARS-CoV-2 for both quantity and avidity was measured to test the hypothesis that antibody response signatures can define mechanistic long Covid endotypes. Methods A retrospective cohort analysis was performed on three cohorts: the UK control cohort (n = 46), the UK long Covid cohort (n = 113), and the US long Covid cohort (n = 90). Three measures were derived for each variant: total antibody concentration, high-quality antibody concentration, and percentage of high-quality antibody. The three parameter distributions for each variant were control median-normalised, and a top-and-tail receiver operator characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to derive long Covid thresholds for both lower and upper extremes of the distributions. Results A patient was classified as having long Covid if they were above or below the extreme thresholds in one or more variants for antibody concentration, antibody quality, or percentage quality. UK long Covid analysis gave a sensitivity of 92%, a specificity of 59%, an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.72, and a diagnostic accuracy of 81%. The ROC analysis applied to the US cohort gave a sensitivity of 90%, a specificity of 72%, an AUC of 0.88, and an accuracy of 84%. Conclusion The classification of patients with long Covid is 70% hypo-immune or immunocompromised, suggesting latent persistent virus; 10% are hyper-immune or autoimmune, 15% have normal antibody spectra, and 5% are hypo-immune for some variants and hyper-immune for others.

title: Spatiotemporal contact network modelling for retrospective detection of nosocomial SARS-CoV-2 outbreaks: a comparative study with traditional epidemiological investigations
abstract: Nosocomial SARS-CoV-2 transmission posed a critical challenge during the COVID-19 pandemic. Traditional epidemiological investigation methods may underestimate true outbreak frequency. We compared traditional outbreak investigation with a spatiotemporal contact network modelling approach to detect nosocomial SARS-CoV-2 outbreaks and characterise transmission dynamics. An observational analytical longitudinal study was conducted at Hospital Universitario Ramón y Cajal (Madrid, Spain) from August 2020 to December 2022. Of 703 patients with a SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis ≥ 48 h after admission, 613 (87.2%) were confirmed as nosocomial after exhaustive case-by-case clinical record review, exclusion of symptoms at admission, exclusion of recent infection (< 3 months), and elimination of cases with documented household or community exposure. Two parallel approaches were applied: traditional epidemiological investigation using clinical and spatiotemporal criteria, and a contact network modelling pipeline employing a novel room nomenclature-based proximity metric ( s(i , j) = 1/n). Traditional investigation identified 48 outbreaks (226/613 cases, 36.9%); network-based modelling detected 71 outbreaks (207/613, 33.8%), representing a 48% higher count of network-derived outbreaks and a partly overlapping case set (κ = 0.704, 95% CI 0.645–0.763; 175 cases classified as outbreak-associated by both methods, 51 only by the traditional method and 32 only by the network method). Mean outbreak size was 4.83 (SD 2.77; median 4, IQR 3–6) for the traditional method and 2.92 (SD 2.20; median 2, IQR 2–3) for the network-based method. Mean outbreak duration was substantially shorter with the network-based method (8.9 vs. 30.7 days; permutation test p < 0.001). The estimated secondary transmission rate was 0.7 (95% CI: 0.59–0.79). Over 95% of transmission events occurred within the same hospital unit. In-hospital mortality was 11.6% and 38.6% of the cases were asymptomatic at the time of diagnosis. Spatiotemporal contact network modelling complements traditional nosocomial outbreak investigation, yielding a partly overlapping but structurally different cluster classification. Coupled with rigorous case definition and clinical record review, the hybrid approach combines the contextual depth of conventional epidemiology with the pattern-recognition capacity of contact network analysis, offering a scalable, genomics-independent surveillance tool.

Of 703 patients with a SARS-CoV-2 diagnosis ≥ 48 h after admission, 613 (87.2%) were confirmed as nosocomial after exhaustive case-by-case clinical record review, exclusion of symptoms at admission, exclusion of recent infection (< 3 months), and elimination of cases with documented household or community exposure. Two parallel approaches were applied: traditional epidemiological investigation using clinical and spatiotemporal criteria, and a contact network modelling pipeline employing a novel room nomenclature-based proximity metric ( s(i , j) = 1/n). Traditional investigation identified 48 outbreaks (226/613 cases, 36.9%); network-based modelling detected 71 outbreaks (207/613, 33.8%), representing a 48% higher count of network-derived outbreaks and a partly overlapping case set (κ = 0.704, 95% CI 0.645–0.763; 175 cases classified as outbreak-associated by both methods, 51 only by the traditional method and 32 only by the network method). Mean outbreak size was 4.83 (SD 2.77; median 4, IQR 3–6) for the traditional method and 2.92 (SD 2.20; median 2, IQR 2–3) for the network-based method. Mean outbreak duration was substantially shorter with the network-based method (8.9 vs. 30.7 days; permutation test p < 0.001). The estimated secondary transmission rate was 0.7 (95% CI: 0.59–0.79). Over 95% of transmission events occurred within the same hospital unit. In-hospital mortality was 11.6% and 38.6% of the cases were asymptomatic at the time of diagnosis. Spatiotemporal contact network modelling complements traditional nosocomial outbreak investigation, yielding a partly overlapping but structurally different cluster classification. Coupled with rigorous case definition and clinical record review, the hybrid approach combines the contextual depth of conventional epidemiology with the pattern-recognition capacity of contact network analysis, offering a scalable, genomics-independent surveillance tool.

title: Smartphone use patterns and physical and behavioral health outcomes in undergraduates during the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: Objective: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted routines and mental health among college students. We analyzed College Experience Study data combining passive smartphone sensing and weekly Ecological Momentary Assessments to examine behavioral and mental health changes during Winter and Spring 2020 relative to prior years and associations with phone use. Methods: Analyses included 184 participants categorized as low (≤2 hrs/day), moderate (>2-4 hrs/day), or high (>4 hrs/day) users. Results: The initial pandemic period was marked by reduced walking and increased sleep. Phone-use groups differed significantly in walking and sleep: moderate users walked more than low users, while lower-use participants slept more than moderate- and high-use participants. Groups did not differ in PHQ-4 scores, stress, or social activity. Greater phone use was associated with shorter sleep and, exploratorily, lower social activity. Conclusions: These findings suggest that phone use may reflect meaningful differences in students' daily behavioral patterns rather than broad differences in distress during the pandemic.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on maternal and perinatal outcomes: a global systematic review
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare delivery worldwide. Beyond the direct effects of SARS-CoV-2 infection, changes in maternity service organization and access may have affected maternal and perinatal outcomes. To synthesize evidence on the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic period on births, delivery mode and intrapartum interventions, maternal and neonatal outcomes, and maternal mortality. We conducted a systematic review following Cochrane methods and PRISMA reporting. Searches were performed in PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL, LILACS/BVS, Scopus, and Web of Science (last search: September 30, 2025) without language restrictions. Observational studies comparing pandemic versus pre-pandemic periods (or counterfactual trajectories) among pregnant women were included. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E. Due to heterogeneity, meta-analysis was not feasible; findings were synthesized narratively and complemented by effect-direction plots. Vote counting based on effect direction (excluding non-significant results) and exact two-sided sign tests were applied when appropriate, consolidating studies using overlapping national databases to avoid double counting. Eighty-seven studies across 27 countries were included. Most studies were judged to have high or very high risk of bias, mainly due to confounding and post-exposure system changes. Births/deliveries most often decreased; vote counting showed decreases were significantly more frequent than increases (p < 0.001). Cesarean section rates more frequently increased than decreased (p < 0.001), while induction of labor and instrumental delivery showed heterogeneous and mostly non-significant changes. Evidence on preterm birth and stillbirth was mixed across settings, with no consistent predominance of direction. Maternal length of stay generally decreased. Antenatal care indicators more often declined than improved, but the evidence base was limited. Maternal mortality showed a predominant increase across settings after consolidating overlapping national datasets (p = 0.022). During the COVID-19 pandemic period, maternity care outcomes showed substantial heterogeneity across countries and study designs. Nevertheless, the overall evidence suggests reductions in births/deliveries, more frequent increases in cesarean section rates, shorter maternal hospital stays, and a predominant rise in maternal mortality. These findings underscore the importance of resilient maternity systems that maintain antenatal care continuity and timely access to emergency obstetric services during public health crises. PROSPERO CRD42024541301.

title: Neuroinflammation as a Mechanism in Long COVID
abstract: Long COVID is recognized as a chronic post-viral condition characterized by fatigue, cognitive impairment, mood changes, and other neuropsychiatric symptoms that go beyond the acute phase of COVID-19. More research is now suggesting that neuroinflammation processes, involving microglial reactivity, altered cytokine signaling, and increased permeability of the blood-brain barrier, may contribute to the persistence of these symptoms. This paper provides a critical review of four recent empirical studies that directly examined neuroinflammatory mechanisms in individuals with long COVID using functional neuroimaging, biomarker analysis, and structural MRI measures. Across studies, converging evidence shows persistent central and peripheral immune activation linked to deficits in memory, attention, and mood regulation. Despite promising findings, the literature is limited by small sample sizes, inconsistent diagnostic criteria, and primarily cross-sectional designs, which limit conclusions about causality. Differences in imaging techniques and biomarker measurement approaches hinder direct comparison and synthesis of results. Future research should prioritize longitudinal, multimodal designs that integrate neuroimaging with immune and behavioral markers to clarify the trajectory and clinical relevance of neuroinflammation in long COVID. Overall, the evidence suggests that neuroinflammation plays a significant role in long COVID related cognitive and mood disturbances and emphasizes the need for biologically guided and consistent clinical approaches.
journal: Journal of Clinical Psychology and Neurology

title: Comparative analysis of the development of oral language as a cognitive process constitutive of learning in child cohorts exposed to COVID-19 lockdown
abstract: This study analyzes oral language development as a constitutive cognitive process of learning in child cohorts exposed to COVID-19 confinement. A mixed-method, comparative, and correlational approach is proposed with a sample of 60 children distributed across three cohorts: pre-, during-, and post-pandemic. Exposure to the pandemic context is examined through questionnaires and interviews with parents and caregivers, while language development is assessed through PLON-R, systematic observation, and pedagogical records. The theoretical review and available contextual evidence suggest variations in morphosyntactic, semantic, and pragmatic performance associated with reduced social interaction, disrupted routines, and lower communicative stimulation. The study provides an analytical basis for understanding the relationship among confinement, language, and learning, and for supporting educational and psychopedagogical interventions in post-pandemic contexts.
journal: Journal of Systems and Educational Management

title: Neurodevelopmental Outcomes of 3-Year-Old Children Exposed to Maternal Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) Infection in Utero
abstract: doi: 10.1097/AOG.0000000000006112) Maternal infections during pregnancy have long been associated with an increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in children, prompting researchers to investigate whether COVID-19 infection during pregnancy produces similar effects. In this retrospective cohort study, investigators evaluated whether prenatal exposure to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection increased the likelihood of neurodevelopmental diagnoses by age three.

title: IMPACTOS DA INFECÇÃO POR SARS-COV-2 NA SÍNTESE DE MATERIAL GENÉTICO (RNA/DNA) EM CÉLULAS HUMANAS E SUAS MANIFESTAÇÕES CLÍNICAS: UMA REVISÃO DE ESTUDOS PUBLICADOS ENTRE 2020-2024
abstract: A emergência do SARS-CoV-2 impôs desafios sem precedentes aos sistemas de saúde globais, resultando no desenvolvimento acelerado de vacinas baseadas em diferentes plataformas tecnológicas (mRNA, vetores virais e proteínas recombinantes) direcionadas à proteína viral Spike (glicoproteína da espícula de coronavírus, ou proteína S). Apesar da eficácia demonstrada na redução de casos graves e mortalidade, emergiram preocupações crescentes quanto às sequelas pós-infecção, caracterizadas pela síndrome pós-COVID ou COVID longa. Por se tratar de um vírus de RNA, o SARS-CoV-2 apresenta mutações significativas durante a replicação, originando variantes com fenótipos distintos de transmissibilidade e escape imunológico cada vez mais eficaz, além de reforçar os sintomas e as sequelas. As sequelas documentadas abrangem múltiplos sistemas orgânicos, predominando manifestações neurológicas (disfunção cognitiva, cefaleia, anosmia/ageusia), cardíacas (miocardite, arritmias, trombopenias), respiratórias e psiquiátricas, com persistência sintomatológica por meses ou anos após a fase aguda, podendo desenvolver-se para condições crônicas. Evidências demonstram que o SARS-CoV-2 induz alterações epigenéticas no infectado, particularmente modificações nos padrões de metilação, sem a capacidade de alterar a sequência nucleotídica. Pacientes graves apresentam hipometilação em loci específicos, resultando em hiperativação de genes pró-inflamatórios e metilação diferencial nos promotores da enzima ECA2 e na atuação do gene TMPRSS2. A persistência circulante da glicoproteína de espícula (spike) sustenta o estado pró-inflamatório crônico e a ativação desses componentes, perpetuando modificações epigenéticas que podem afetar a gravidade da infecção e o desenvolvimento de sequelas tardias. A incidência e a severidade dessas manifestações são moduladas por características individuais pré-existentes, estabelecendo-se grupos de risco definidos por variáveis demográficas, clínicas e comorbidades que influenciam significativamente o prognóstico a longo prazo.

Por se tratar de um vírus de RNA, o SARS-CoV-2 apresenta mutações significativas durante a replicação, originando variantes com fenótipos distintos de transmissibilidade e escape imunológico cada vez mais eficaz, além de reforçar os sintomas e as sequelas. As sequelas documentadas abrangem múltiplos sistemas orgânicos, predominando manifestações neurológicas (disfunção cognitiva, cefaleia, anosmia/ageusia), cardíacas (miocardite, arritmias, trombopenias), respiratórias e psiquiátricas, com persistência sintomatológica por meses ou anos após a fase aguda, podendo desenvolver-se para condições crônicas. Evidências demonstram que o SARS-CoV-2 induz alterações epigenéticas no infectado, particularmente modificações nos padrões de metilação, sem a capacidade de alterar a sequência nucleotídica. Pacientes graves apresentam hipometilação em loci específicos, resultando em hiperativação de genes pró-inflamatórios e metilação diferencial nos promotores da enzima ECA2 e na atuação do gene TMPRSS2. A persistência circulante da glicoproteína de espícula (spike) sustenta o estado pró-inflamatório crônico e a ativação desses componentes, perpetuando modificações epigenéticas que podem afetar a gravidade da infecção e o desenvolvimento de sequelas tardias. A incidência e a severidade dessas manifestações são moduladas por características individuais pré-existentes, estabelecendo-se grupos de risco definidos por variáveis demográficas, clínicas e comorbidades que influenciam significativamente o prognóstico a longo prazo.

title: Regular exercise had protective and rehabilitation effectiveness in cardiovascular impairments caused by long-term covid-19 infections: a systematic review and bioinformatics analysis
abstract: This study aimed to assess cardiovascular impairments associated with long-term COVID-19 infections and to evaluate rehabilitation strategies. We searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science for both randomized and non-randomized intervention studies published between 2019 and 2025, last updated on 31 December 2025, that evaluated exercise‐based rehabilitation (aerobic, resistance, qigong, or combined training) in patients with cardiovascular impairments or long COVID–related cardiopulmonary symptoms. Eight studies (pooled sample size of 578 participants) evaluated combined interval training on an ergometer bike/resistance, aerobic–resistance training, and qigong cardiopulmonary rehabilitation protocols in post‐COVID or long‐COVID populations with cardiovascular and respiratory involvement. Supervised exercise programmed improved functional capacity and cardiorespiratory fitness, with 6‐minute walk test distances increasing by approximately 70–120 m and peak oxygen consumption rising by 10–18%; in one 8‐week cardiopulmonary rehabilitation trial, VO2peak improved by + 2.7 mL kg−1 min−1 (95%CI 1.6–3.8) in the rehabilitation group versus + 0.3 mL kg−1 min−1 (95%CI − 0.8 to 1.3) in controls. Ventilatory efficiency/symptom burden improved, multiple studies reported clinically meaningful reductions in fatigue and dyspnoea scores, improved health‐related quality of life, supporting beneficial role exercise‐based rehabilitation. Clinicians could prescribe supervised, symptom-limited, multicomponent exercise-based therapy for post-COVID-19-conditions with cardiovascular or pulmonary involvement, rather than simply encouraging physical activity. For clinically stable adults without major contraindications, exercise begins with individualized, symptom-limited aerobic training at a low-to-moderate initial intensity, with heart-rate reserve used only as an approximate starting guide and interpreted alongside rating of perceived exertion, dyspnea, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, and heart-rate recovery. Because cardiovascular drift and autonomic abnormalities may occur during prolonged exercise, heart-rate targets should not be treated as fixed intensities or universal safety ceilings.
