title: Longitudinal SARS-CoV-2 wastewater genomic surveillance in Surat, India: comparison with clinical genomes and detection of recurrent environmental mutations
abstract: Background Environmental genomic surveillance is a vital One Health tool for tracking pathogen circulation and preparing for emerging infectious diseases. While the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated wastewater genomic surveillance globally, its broader role as an early-warning framework for new pathogens remains only partly understood. Methods We conducted a longitudinal wastewater genomic surveillance study in Surat, India, under INSACOG. Between March 2023 and January 2024, 945 samples were screened, yielding 51 wastewater consensus sequences meeting predefined quality criteria, compared with 1,814 regional human genomes. Analyses assessed lineage dynamics, mutation sharing, lead times, persistence, and cryptic genomic signatures. Results Comparative analysis identified 953 mutations shared between wastewater and clinical genomes and 205 mutations not observed in the selected clinical dataset. Fifteen mutations were detected in wastewater before their first observation in the analyzed clinical sequence dataset, with apparent lead times ranging from 21 to 187 days. The spike mutation S:I670V preceded first observation in the clinical dataset by 187 days. Longitudinal analysis further identified nine recurrently co-detected mutations that remained detectable for approximately 147 days across multiple independent wastewater genomes; genomic linkage among these mutations has not yet been established from consensus sequence data alone. Conclusions Our findings show that integrated environmental and clinical genomic surveillance identified mutation signals earlier in wastewater than in the available local clinical sequence collection, and revealed recurrently co-detected mutations underrepresented in clinical samples. Although demonstrated using SARS-CoV-2 only, this approach may be adaptable to other pathogens with further validation, and environmental genomic surveillance could serve as one component of a broader One Health preparedness strategy.

title: 'Things aren't going to be settled...each one [pandemic] will be different': learning about inclusive pandemic preparedness from people with HIV's stories of HIV and COVID-19.
abstract: This paper examines what we can learn for inclusive pandemic preparation from people with HIV's narratives of living with HIV and COVID-19. The paper treats 'inclusion' as entwined with exclusion, and as a technology of social justice. It reports on findings from twelve semi-structured interviews with people with HIV in 2019, repeated by telephone during 2020. Half the participants were gay or bisexual men, half were of majority-world origin, and almost all were over 40. Interviews explored how having access to resources or being excluded from them affected people's lives in both pandemics. Thematic narrative analysis showed stories of exclusion intensified in the COVID-19-era interviews, across health but especially in the socio-economic and psychosocial fields. Narratives of inclusion technologies drew powerfully on HIV histories but were limited, particularly during COVID-19, and for participants with precarious socio-economic, health and residency statuses. Inclusion technologies also shifted during COVID-19, developing new coalitions, commons, and 'weak links' or associations. Findings highlight the importance of mobilising pandemic histories for inclusive pandemic preparation; paying attention to intersectional patterns of exclusion; analysing which inclusion technologies work for specific groups; and framing 'inclusion' as a social and planetary justice issue.

title: Probable Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder and Coping Mechanisms Among Quarantined and Isolated University Students During the COVID-19 Pandemic in South Africa
abstract: Quarantine and isolation during the COVID-19 pandemic raised concerns about the psychological well-being of university students. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of probable post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and coping strategies among students who underwent quarantine or isolation at a university in South Africa. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted using a self-administered online questionnaire. Systematic sampling was used to select participants from the university’s COVID-19 register. Probable PTSD was assessed using the five-item Primary Care PTSD Screen for DSM-5 (PC-PTSD-5), while coping strategies were assessed using the 32-item Billings and Moos Coping Scale. A total of 167 students were included in the analysis, of whom 66.5% screened positive for probable PTSD. Undergraduate students had higher odds of screening positive than postgraduate students (AOR = 5.41, 95% CI: 1.17–25.00; p = 0.031), while students who presented with COVID-19-related symptoms had higher odds than those who had contact with a confirmed case (AOR = 3.84, 95% CI: 1.54–9.57; p = 0.004). Participants reported using cognitive, behavioural, and avoidance coping strategies. Avoidance coping was associated with higher odds of screening positive for probable PTSD (OR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.07–1.47; p = 0.006), whereas active cognitive and active behavioural coping were not statistically significantly associated with screening status. The high proportion of positive screens highlights the importance of considering students’ psychological support needs during public health emergencies.

title: Viral lineage features can enhance the detection of COVID-19 surges via machine learning
abstract: Accurately detecting infectious disease surges is essential for timely public health response. We asked whether incorporating SARS-CoV-2 viral lineage information improves machine learning–based detection of COVID-19 surges. We obtained COVID-19 clinical case counts and wastewater collected from 17 wastewater treatment plants’ catchment areas and viral lineage data from March 2022 to February 2023 in Minnesota. We developed a two-step framework in which surge periods were first defined, followed by training a supervised classification model to identify surge weeks. Model performance was evaluated using nested leave-one-group-out cross-validation (LOGOCV), holding out wastewater treatment plants to assess generalization to unseen locations within the study period. A model using wastewater viral load measures alone achieved a recall of 0.57, precision of 0.27, F1-score of 0.33, area under the precision-recall curve (PR-AUC) of 0.38, and accuracy of 0.65. Adding a lineage-derived feature increased recall to 0.72 (0.15 improvement, 95% CI 0.05 – 0.25), precision to 0.41 (0.14 improvement, 95% CI 0.07 – 0.22), F1-score to 0.48 (0.15 improvement, 95% CI 0.07 – 0.23), PR-AUC to 0.71 (0.33 improvement, 95% CI 0.22 – 0.44), and accuracy to 0.76 (0.11 improvement, 95% CI 0.06 – 0.17). These findings demonstrate that integrating genomic surveillance with wastewater data can meaningfully enhance infectious disease surge detection. The proposed framework may be generalizable and could potentially be applied to future pathogens.

title: Wavelet-derived indices of cardiac vagal and vasomotor oscillations as a new tool to better understand autonomic imbalance in post-COVID-19 dysautonomia
abstract: Background When aiming to quantify autonomic imbalance, conventional heart rate variability (HRV) analysis generally reduces each posture to a single spectral value derived from interbeat intervals (IBI) alone. This analysis based only in IBI obscures transient events during blood pressure changes. We propose two wavelet-derived indices that quantify cardiac vagal and vasomotor sympathetic oscillations separately and over time. Since autonomic imbalance is directly related to baroreflex sensitivity (BRS), we evaluated them against an estimate of baroreflex sensitivity in post-COVID-19 patients. Methods In this study, 121 participants (32 healthy controls and 89 patients with persistent post-COVID-19 autonomic symptoms) underwent an active standing test with continuous finger blood pressure. The continuous wavelet transform with generalized Morse wavelets yielded time-varying high-frequency power of IBI and low-frequency power of systolic blood pressure (SBP). Two new indices were proposed: Index I combined the magnitude and variability of HF IBI power (aimed to quantify parasympathetic activity), and the index J combined LF SBP power with the rate of its transient elevations (bursts), which aims to quantify sympathetic vasomotor activity; J/I was their ratio. Indices were computed for supine and orthostatic periods and compared with conventional HRV and BRS measurements. Results Index I correlated strongly with HF power of IBI and was lower in all patient subgroups than in controls, Index J had only a weak relation with LF power of IBI. On standing, J increased most in the subgroups with the worst baroreflex function. Orthostatic J/I was higher than in controls amongst patients, while LF/HF showed no differences. J/I was inversely correlated with BRS, most strongly when standing, and more strongly than LF/HF also. Adding J to I raised the cross-validated variance explained in orthostatic BRS substantially. In one example patient, a window during symptoms showed vasomotor oscillations that were hidden in the posture average. Conclusions Wavelet-derived indices from routine beat-to-beat recordings separate cardiac vagal modulation from sympathetic vasomotor oscillations and their transients. J/I correlates with BRS impairment more closely than LF/HF, providing a potential alternative estimate of autonomic balance, and its time-resolved visual output allows analysis of clinically relevant windows within a posture. The new proposed variables allowed an evaluation of autonomic imbalance that could be applied to different pathologies.

title: DISSEMINATED, FATAL TRICHOSPORON ASAHII FUNGAEMIA IN A CRITICALLY ILL COVID-19 PATIENT: A CASE REPORT AND REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE
abstract: The usage of immunomodulators and immunosuppressants in critically ill COVID-19 patients increase the risk for opportunistic infections such as fungaemia. Trichosporon asahii is a yeast-like basidiomycete normally found in soil, plants, and birds that could cause rare, invasive trichosporonosis in immunocompromised patients. A 74-year-old man with comorbid dyslipidaemia and hypertension who completed two doses of COVID-19 vaccination was initially admitted for ascending cholangitis. He was infected with COVID-19 on the sixth day of admission and deteriorated, which required intubation with intensive care, and started on high-dose steroids as well as immunomodulators. However, he developed a multidrug-resistant nosocomial infection with T. Antifungals fluconazole and voriconazole were started, while the steroid was tapered down. The patient succumbed to multiple organ dysfunction and acute respiratory distress syndrome despite aggressive management in the ICU. asahii is a threat to critically ill COVID-19 patients despite treatment with antifungal agents proven to be effective, which warrants further research for more refined management guidelines and to identify alternative therapies to improve patients’ survival.
journal: Journal of Defence Science Engineering & Technology

title: Boron-Nitride-Doped Graphene Oxide FETs for COVID-19 Detection: A Comparative Review Against Existing Market Solutions
abstract: COVID-19 point-of-care tests return results faster than centralized RT-PCR, but none combines high sensitivity, speed, low cost, and ease of use. This review compares a boron-nitride-doped graphene oxide (BN-GO) FET biosensor with commercial diagnostics and other graphene-based FET biosensors using LOD, PPA/NPA, detection time, cost, shelf life, and ease of use. Because the BN-GO platform is at technology readiness level 4 and has been tested only in buffer, the market comparison is treated as a gap analysis. The BN-GO FET biosensor showed promising early-stage analytical performance, responding rapidly to N-protein in buffer at its lowest tested concentration, below the detection limits of the other graphene FETs compared. However, the lowest-concentration response was obtained from an initial set of device tests. Future studies will assess the repeatability, reproducibility, clinical performance, and manufacturing scalability of the device. They will also focus on extending its shelf life, because the current estimate falls short of the WHO target product profile and would complicate stockpiling and distribution. The estimated cost per test is approximately the same as that of rapid antigen tests. These findings position the BN-GO FET biosensor as a promising next-generation candidate for point-of-care COVID-19 diagnostics if the remaining cost and shelf-life challenges are addressed.

title: COVID-19 Burden, Vaccination Uptake, and Hospital Capacity in a Brazilian Regional Hub City, 2020-2025: A Population-Based Ecological Study of Uberlândia, Minas Gerais
abstract: Introduction Five years after the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, municipal-level descriptions of how its burden evolved through the vaccination era and into the post-emergency period remain scarce for medium-sized Brazilian cities. We described COVID-19 hospitalizations, deaths, vaccination uptake, and hospital capacity in Uberlândia, a regional hub city in Minas Gerais, Brazil, from 2020 to 2025, and situated its mortality relative to other municipalities. Methods We conducted a population-based ecological study using routinely collected national data: severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) surveillance (SIVEP-Gripe), the Mortality Information System (SIM), individual-level vaccination records (National Immunization Program Information System (SI-PNI)), the hospital bed registry (National Registry of Health Establishments (CNES)), federal transfers, and municipal accounts, with 2022 census denominators. The study period was divided into pre-vaccine (March 2020-January 2021), vaccine rollout with Gamma/Delta circulation (February-December 2021), Omicron (2022), and endemic (2023-2025) periods. We estimated age-standardized rates, adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for in-hospital death, and all-cause excess mortality, and used funnel plots to compare Uberlândia with all 853 municipalities of Minas Gerais and the 97 Brazilian regional capitals defined by the national urban hierarchy. Results Age-standardized COVID-19 mortality fell from 30.2 deaths per 100,000 per month during the 2021 rollout period to 0.67 per 100,000 per month in the endemic period (2023-2024; 97.8% lower; crude reduction 97.9%). In-hospital mortality among patients hospitalized with COVID-19 SARI was higher in 2021 than in the pre-vaccine period (aOR 1.77; 95% CI 1.61-1.95) and lower in the Omicron (aOR 0.64; 0.55-0.75) and endemic (aOR 0.69; 0.56-0.85) periods. As primary-series coverage among adults aged ≥80 years increased, the share of COVID-19 deaths in this age group decreased (odds ratio 0.88 per 10 percentage points; 95% CI 0.85-0.91). In 2021, Uberlândia had the highest age-standardized COVID-19 mortality among the 34 municipalities of Minas Gerais with ≥100,000 inhabitants and an all-cause excess of 58% above expected, exceeding the 99.8% funnel-plot control limit. Federal COVID-19 funding per capita was close to the median of comparable cities and was not correlated with excess mortality. In the endemic period, hospitalized COVID-19 patients were older than those with influenza (median 72 vs. 14 years) and had higher adjusted in-hospital mortality (aOR 2.14; 1.32-3.47), while the proportion of residents aged ≥60 years vaccinated within each calendar year declined from 98% (2021) to 37% (2024) and 16% (2025). Conclusions In this descriptive ecological analysis, COVID-19 mortality in Uberlândia declined by approximately 98% after 2021, in temporal association with high vaccine coverage, while residual hospital mortality remained concentrated in older adults with declining annual vaccine uptake. The city's unusually high 2021 mortality was not accompanied by lower federal funding than in comparable cities. These findings are hypothesis-generating and cannot establish causal effects of vaccination, funding, or local health-system responses.

title: RECURRENT OPTIC NEURITIS IN A CHILD FOLLOWING SARS COV 2 INFECTION: LONG TERM EVOLUTION INTO PEDIATRIC MOGAD
abstract: Background: SARS-CoV-2 infection has been increasingly associated with post-infectious or immune-mediated neurological complications in children. Among these, optic neuritis is rare but clinically significant, as it can represent an isolated inflammatory event or the heralding episode of an underlying demyelinating disorder such as myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody–associated disease (MOGAD). COVID-19–related immune dysregulation may act as a trigger for autoimmune CNS disease through mechanisms of molecular mimicry, cytokine activation, or altered immune tolerance. Case Presentation Summary: A 7-year-old previously healthy girl presented with acute, progressive bilateral visual loss over four days, two months after an asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection. She had received a single COVID-19 vaccine dose before infection. Ophthalmologic assessment revealed bilateral optic disc swelling, severe reduction in visual acuity (1/10 OU), and impaired color perception. Brain MRI was normal; serum and CSF immunologic studies were negative. Visual evoked potentials were abnormal in the right optic nerve. High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (IVMP) led to full recovery. Eighteen months later, following another SARS-CoV-2 infection, she developed a second episode of subacute bilateral visual decline. Visual acuity was 7/10 + 1 OD and 5/10 + 1 OS. MRI showed nonspecific demyelinating lesions in the occipital horn of the right lateral ventricle, while bilateral visual evoked responses were again abnormal. No autoimmune antibodies were detected. IVMP therapy resulted in complete visual recovery. Over four years of follow-up, imaging remained stable, and no new relapses occurred. At puberty, serum anti-MOG IgG antibodies became positive, confirming the diagnosis of MOG-antibody associated disease (MOGAD) . Learning Points Discussion Post-infectious immune activation by SARS-CoV-2 can precipitate CNS autoimmunity in children, including MOGAD, NMOSD, and autoimmune encephalitis. Optic neuritis following COVID-19 —especially when recurrent or bilateral—should prompt investigations for MOG and AQP4 antibodies, even if initial immunologic and imaging studies are normal. MOGAD accounts for nearly one-third of pediatric acquired demyelinating syndromes and often presents with optic neuritis in older children. Long-term monitoring with MRI and antibody testing is essential, as seroconversion may occur years after the first demyelinating event. The case reinforces accumulating evidence that COVID-19 may act as a trigger for autoimmune diseases in children, potentially unmasking latent immune susceptibilities affecting the CNS. Awareness of this temporal association is crucial for early recognition and management. High-dose corticosteroids remain first-line therapy for acute episodes, with favorable visual and neurological outcomes in most pediatric cases.

MOGAD accounts for nearly one-third of pediatric acquired demyelinating syndromes and often presents with optic neuritis in older children. Long-term monitoring with MRI and antibody testing is essential, as seroconversion may occur years after the first demyelinating event. source_records.abstract: Background: SARS-CoV-2 infection has been increasingly associated with post-infectious or immune-mediated neurological complications in children. Among these, optic neuritis is rare but clinically significant, as it can represent an isolated inflammatory event or the heralding episode of an underlying demyelinating disorder such as myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody–associated disease (MOGAD). title: Differences in Drinking Status and Associated Factors Among Japanese University Students During the Late and Post-COVID-19 Periods.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study examined differences in drinking status and associated factors among Japanese undergraduate and graduate students across three time points: 2022 (late COVID-19 pandemic), 2023 (first post-pandemic year), and 2024 (second post-pandemic year). METHODS: Self-administered web-based questionnaires were used during health examinations at the University of Tsukuba (analytic sample: sizes 6288 in 2022, 5716 in 2023, and 5730 in 2024). Drinking status was classified as non-drinker, ex-drinker, low-risk drinker, or high-risk drinker using Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test scores and drinking history. Multinomial logistic regression included sex, age, student status (undergraduate or graduate), depressive symptoms, smoking habits, and exercise habits, with low-risk drinking as the reference category. Mean predicted probabilities were estimated from a model including interactions between student status and survey year. RESULTS: Significant interactions between student status and survey year were observed for non-drinking and ex-drinking, but not for high-risk drinking. Mean predicted probabilities of non-drinking among undergraduates were 13% in 2022, 34% in 2023, and 37% in 2024. Among graduate students, differences between survey years were small for all drinking status categories. Mean predicted probabilities of high-risk drinking differed little across the three survey years in either student group. Compared with low-risk drinking, high-risk drinking was associated with depressive symptoms (OR = 2.06, 95% CI: 1.81-2.36) and smoking habits (OR = 5.09, 95% CI: 4.36-5.93) after adjustment for sex, survey year, and other covariates. CONCLUSIONS: Drinking status differed by student status and survey year, with a higher proportion of non-drinkers among undergraduates in the post-pandemic years than in the late-pandemic year, while high-risk drinking differed little across years in either student group. High-risk drinking was associated with depressive symptoms and smoking habits. These findings suggest that interventions for high-risk drinkers should continue to incorporate the assessment and support of depressive symptoms and smoking habits even after the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: The impact of demographic variables and personality characteristics on nurse compassion fatigue: A cross-sectional analysis during and following the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract: Compassion fatigue can undermine nurses' work efficiency, care quality, and well-being, and its correlates among nurses warrant further investigation. To examine compassion fatigue among nurses during and after the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, identify its demographic and personality correlates, and provide evidence to inform mitigation strategies. This study was conducted using a survey that included a basic information questionnaire and two validated instruments: the Chinese Compassion Fatigue Short Scale and the brief version of the Chinese Neuroticism Extraversion Openness Five-Factor Inventory. The sampling frame for this study consisted of nurses working at a tertiary hospital between 2022 and 2024, and a convenience sampling approach was used for data collection and analysis. Independent cross-sectional samples were surveyed at two time points (during and following the coronavirus disease 2019 [COVID-19] pandemic). For each round, 360 questionnaires were issued, resulting in 335 valid returns (93.1% valid response rate) in the first survey and 332 valid returns (92.2% valid response rate) in the second survey, yielding an overall valid response rate of 92.6%. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, independent samples t tests, one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation analysis, and hierarchical regression. The average compassion fatigue score was 54.87 ± 23.81. Age, working years, professional title, income, and department influence compassion fatigue. The COVID-19 pandemic also significantly impacts it. Nurses reported a higher compassion fatigue score during the COVID-19 pandemic than following it (P .05), openness(β=-.045, P > .05), agreeableness(β=-.293, P .05) and neuroticism(β=-.014, P < .01). After adjusting for demographic variables, only Neuroticism and Agreeableness were significantly associated with compassion fatigue among nurses, with the personality traits collectively accounting for an additional 50.6% of variance (ΔR2 = .506; total R2 = .553). Specifically, higher neuroticism increased the risk, whereas higher agreeableness appeared to be a protective factor. Based on these demographic and personality findings, nursing managers can implement tailored interventions to alleviate compassion fatigue.

title: Beyond Single-Split Performance: A Rigorous Assessment of Statistical Reliability and Generalisability in Deep Learning-Based SARS-CoV-2 Computed Tomography Classification
abstract: Chest computed tomography (CT) has driven extensive deep-learning research on COVID-19 screening, and the public SARS-CoV-2 CT-scan dataset has become a widely used benchmark on which reported accuracies routinely approach 99%. These results are typically obtained from a single train-test split of one cohort at the slice level, leaving open how far they extend to new seeds, new patients and new sites. This paper assembles three checks that are rarely applied together on this benchmark: pairwise McNemar testing across five random seeds, subject-disjoint splitting, and zero-shot validation on independent cohorts. All three are applied to prototype-based and attention-based models, namely a reproduced explainable deep neural network (xDNN) baseline, the Vision Transformer (ViT), the Swin Transformer, ConvNeXt and a soft-voting ensemble. Prototype explanations are contrasted with saliency from gradient-weighted class activation mapping and attention rollout. In-domain the models are strong, reaching 96.6-99.0% accuracy with an AUC of 99.7-99.95%, and each check adds information a single split leaves out: repeated seeds show ConvNeXt and the ensemble consistently ahead of Swin in point accuracy, while no pairwise difference among the deep models reaches significance in more than one of five seeds; subject-disjoint splitting isolates patient-level generalization, a gap of 6-8 F1 points; and zero-shot evaluation on two independent cohorts measures how much of that performance is cohort-specific, placing accuracy at the majority-class baseline. The protocol adds four retraining runs to a standard experiment, needs no training for the cross-dataset step, and is released in full; the authors argue it should accompany any accuracy claim on this benchmark.
journal: IJACI : International Journal of Advanced Computing and Informatics

title: “Que cringe ter covid agora!”: Produção de sentidos acerca da covid-19 no contexto de flexibilização sanitária “How cringe to have covid now!”: Production of meanings about covid-19 in the context of health flexibility “¡Qué cringe tener covid ahora!”: Producción de significados sobre el covid-19 en el contexto de la flexibilización sanitaria
abstract: Este artigo resulta de uma pesquisa que teve como objetivo compreender os sentidos atribuídos por pessoas diagnosticadas com covid-19 acerca de seu processo de adoecimento e vivência da pandemia no contexto de flexibilização sanitária. Trata-se de um recorte de uma pesquisa qualitativa, sob perspectiva da Análise Institucional. Evidencia-se que o fim da pandemia, nas experiências concretas das pessoas, não ocorreu quando a Organização Mundial da Saúde declarou o fim da emergência sanitária, mas como resultado gradativo de um conjunto de mudanças psicossociais.

title: Studying in higher education without barriers during COVID-19? Perceptions of subjective wellbeing in the daily study routine of students with disabilities
abstract: This study examined positive and negative activation among higher education students in Vienna during COVID-19-related distance learning compared with their retrospective ratings of their study routine before the transition to distance learning. Data were collected in a cross-sectional online survey in which participants rated their positive and negative activation for both reference periods. The analyses compared students with disabilities with a manuscript-coded comparison group and included paired comparisons as well as Group × reference-period interaction analyses. Students in both groups reported significantly lower positive activation and significantly higher negative activation for the distance-learning period compared with the retrospectively rated pre-transition period. However, the Group × reference-period interactions were not statistically significant for either positive or negative activation, providing insufficient evidence to conclude that the magnitude of the differences between reference periods varied by disability group. These findings suggest less favorable affective experiences during the distance-learning period across both groups. The nonsignificant interactions should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between groups. Given the cross-sectional and retrospective design, the observed differences should not be interpreted as evidence of changes caused by the transition to distance learning.

title: Scarcity in crises: access disparities to COVID-19 vaccines among natives, migrants, and refugees in Germany
abstract: This paper investigates disparities in the timing of COVID-19 vaccination uptake among natives, migrants, and refugees in Germany. Using data from the representative, nationwide RKI-SOEP-2 survey and employing Kaplan–Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazard models, and an Oaxaca–Blinder decomposition, the study reveals a significant temporal gap and associated factors. Natives received their vaccination earlier than migrants, and those in turn earlier than refugees. While accounting for differences in eligibility and individual vaccination intentions, the paper examines the role of potential access barriers. In line with fundamental cause theory, key flexible resources such as income, language skills, social networks, and access to transportation are found to be significantly associated with vaccination timing. Differences in these flexible resources account for a substantial share of the observed gap in vaccination timing between natives, migrants, and refugees. The paper highlights how structural disadvantages can have direct public health implications. The results stress that—beyond the health crisis of the COVID-19 pandemic—ensuring fair access to scarce resources is essential to prevent existing social inequalities from translating into health disparities during crises.

title: Concerns about multiple crises and COVID-19-related stress symptoms in Tyrolean children (Austria) during and after the pandemic
abstract: The multiple systemic crises of recent years have the potential to impact child and adolescent mental health. There is extensive evidence on short-term mental health declines during the COVID-19 crisis. However, research on post-pandemic consequences and the relevance of other crises is limited. Here, we combined parent and child perspectives to analyse COVID-19-related stress over time and its association with concerns about other crises. We used repeated cross-sectional surveys of parents in Tyrol, Austria, regarding their children’s (3–13 years) COVID-19-related stress symptoms (CATS-2) between 2020 and 2025 (N = 5,056 measurements). Children (7–13 years) participated in cross-sectional surveys about their symptoms (CRIES-13, N = 575) and concerns about different crises (N = 259) in 2025. Based on parent information, we identified a peak in children’s COVID-19-related stress symptom prevalence during the pandemic winters of 2020/21 and 2021/22. In 2025, parents reported no symptoms for 99% (95% CI [95.3, 99.7]) of preschool children. However, approximately 10% (95% CI [7.3, 13.5]) of then school-aged children had COVID-19-related stress symptoms according to parents. The post-pandemic survey of children corroborated prevalence rates identified in parent reports. Additionally, children reported concerns about different crises. Concerns about all crises were particularly prevalent in children with COVID-19-related stress symptoms. The findings point to the long-term significance of temporary crises for children. Children are concerned about themselves and others and may struggle to navigate the threat of multiple crises.

Children (7–13 years) participated in cross-sectional surveys about their symptoms (CRIES-13, N = 575) and concerns about different crises (N = 259) in 2025. Based on parent information, we identified a peak in children’s COVID-19-related stress symptom prevalence during the pandemic winters of 2020/21 and 2021/22. In 2025, parents reported no symptoms for 99% (95% CI [95.3, 99.7]) of preschool children. However, approximately 10% (95% CI [7.3, 13.5]) of then school-aged children had COVID-19-related stress symptoms according to parents. The post-pandemic survey of children corroborated prevalence rates identified in parent reports. Additionally, children reported concerns about different crises. Concerns about all crises were particularly prevalent in children with COVID-19-related stress symptoms. The findings point to the long-term significance of temporary crises for children. Children are concerned about themselves and others and may struggle to navigate the threat of multiple crises.

title: Variant escape site mapping and characterization of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid rapid antigen test antibodies
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid antigen tests (RATs) were a critical tool for diagnosing severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection during the height of the pandemic, but their performance depends on antibodies that remain robust to viral evolution. Since most commercial RATs target the viral nucleocapsid protein, mutations in this domain can compromise binding and test performance. To systematically define this risk, we used deep mutational scanning (DMS) to map escape mutations for 82 antibodies across 43 commercially available tests, generating the most comprehensive escape database of SARS-CoV-2 viral mutations to date. Most antibodies target conformational epitopes, with 47 (57%) mapping to the RNA-binding domain and 23 (28%) to the dimerization domain. Principal component analysis and clustering revealed escape phenotypes, including shared features outside of predicted epitopes. As the pandemic proceeded, we noted a change in industry preference from IgG to IgM-type antibodies, which was associated with changes to epitope sub-class prevalence. Analysis of paired capture-detection antibodies revealed a preference for targeting the same structural domain (20/33 or 61%), indicating a slight preference for test antibodies to hit orthogonal yet proximal sites. Together, the results establish a comprehensive resource for understanding how SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein mutations affect antibody binding and the phenotypes that underlie RAT antibody selection. This resource and approach can help prioritize antibodies for follow-up performance testing and support the design of more mutation-resilient diagnostics. IMPORTANCE It is critical during a pandemic for diagnostic tests to be accurate and for the false negative rate to be kept low. The rapidly changing nature of SARS-CoV-2 exposed a weakness with using rapid antigen tests to diagnose infection, as mutations to the viral nucleocapsid protein can cause the virus to evade detection. In this work, we systematically tested the robustness of 82 antibodies from 43 separate commercially available tests by deliberately mutating the nucleocapsid protein and investigating which changes caused weakened binding to the test antibodies. In addition to determining which specific tests were at risk from certain mutations, we collated our datasets into a meta-analysis, allowing us to identify some best practices for designing robust tests. We, therefore, expect that this resource will support the design of more mutation-resilient diagnostics, whether for future variants of SARS-CoV-2 or in applying these principles to other respiratory viruses, such as influenza virus.

title: A tecnologia como estratégia de cuidado durante a internação por Covid-19 TECHNOLOGY AS A CARE STRATEGY DURING HOSPITALIZATION FOR COVID-19
abstract: Neste artigo busco analisar como a tecnologia transformou em uma importante estratégia de cuidado durante a pandemia. Ao longo de 2020 pessoas com Covid-19 ao serem admitidas nos hospitais viram a comunicação com suas famílias suspensas, graças à interrupção das visitas e dos acompanhamentos. Nesse contexto, muitos/as internado/as viram-se privados do cuidado familiar. Como contrapartida algumas famílias utilizaram a tecnologia, em especial, o aparelho celular e as mídias disponíveis, como forma de conseguirem oferecer um cuidado ainda que à distância. Para tanto trabalhei com o termo “estratégias de cuidado”, enquanto um mecanismo utilizado pelos/as familiares para recuperar parte da sua capacidade cuidadora
journal: ACENO - Revista de Antropologia do Centro-Oeste

title: Prognostic Value of the Stress Hyperglycemia Ratio for In-Hospital Mortality in Critically Ill Patients With COVID-19
abstract: Objective: Hyperglycemia is associated with adverse outcomes in patients with COVID-19. However, the prognostic significance of chronic glycemic status, reflected by glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and relative hyperglycemia, assessed by the stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR), remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association of HbA1c and SHR with in-hospital mortality in critically ill patients with COVID-19. Methods: In this retrospective observational study, 324 adult patients with confirmed COVID-19 admitted to the intensive care unit were evaluated. Admission blood glucose and HbA1c levels were obtained from laboratory records. The SHR was calculated to assess relative hyperglycemia. Factors associated with in-hospital mortality were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Results: Of the 324 patients included in the study, 125 (38.6%) died during hospitalization. Non-survivors had a significantly higher SHR compared with survivors (median [IQR], 1.30 [0.65] vs 1.15 [0.43]; P = .003). Admission glucose levels were also higher in non-survivors (178 versus 147 mg/dL; P = .01), as was the glycemic gap (34.3 and 20.2 mg/dL, respectively; P = .008). In contrast, HbA1c levels were similar between non-survivors and survivors (median [IQR], 5.9% [2.2%] vs 5.8% [2.5%]; P = .589). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, SHR remained independently associated with mortality across all adjusted models. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis showed that SHR had the highest predictive performance for the outcome (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.611) compared with glycemic gap, admission glucose, and HbA1c. Conclusions: Relative hyperglycemia assessed by the SHR may be a more informative prognostic marker of mortality in critically ill patients with COVID-19 than chronic glycemic status reflected by HbA1c.

title: Associação entre higiene das mãos e infecção pelo SARS-CoV-2 em profissionais de saúde: estudo transversal Association between hand hygiene and SARS-CoV-2 infection among healthcare professionals: a cross-sectional study Asociación entre la higiene de manos y la infección por SARS-CoV-2 en profesionales de la salud: estudio transversal
abstract: Objective: To analyze the association between adherence to hand hygiene, knowledge of the five moments, and SARS-CoV-2 infection among healthcare professionals. Method: A cross-sectional study conducted with 364 healthcare professionals with symptoms suggestive of COVID-19. Sampling was non-probabilistic. Individual interviews were conducted, and samples were collected via nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs. Multiple logistic regression was used to analyze the associations between adherence to hand hygiene, knowledge of the five moments, and SARS-CoV-2 positivity. Results: Participants had a mean age of 37.1 years, with 73.6% being female. Nursing technicians (33.8%) made up the largest share of participants, followed by nurses (17.0%). The prevalence of SARS-CoV-2 infection was 33.8%. Adherence to hand hygiene was 90.1%, and knowledge of the five moments reached 74.5%. Lack of adherence and lack of knowledge regarding the five moments of hand hygiene increased the odds of SARS-CoV-2 infection by 111% (Odds ratio: 2.11) and 72% (Odds ratio: 1.72), respectively. Conclusion: It was found that non-adherence to hand hygiene and the lack of knowledge about the five moments increase the odds of SARS-CoV-2 infection by 2.11 and 1.72 times, respectively.

title: COVID 19 vaccination gaps and sociospatial predictors among healthcare students in Northern Nigeria
abstract: Background Healthcare students face high occupational exposure during clinical training and serve as crucial frontline advocates for community immunization. While their clinical role is vital, their vaccine compliance remains a significant, unquantified gap in institutional biosecurity frameworks within sub-Saharan Africa. This study evaluates coverage not as an emergency response, but as a baseline indicator of institutional readiness for endemic respiratory pathogens. This study assessed vaccination coverage, motivators, barriers, and predictors of uptake among health science students at Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among healthcare students at Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto, between 19 July and 9 September 2025. Of 427 students selected, 410 (96.0%) completed the questionnaire; 408 (95.6% of those selected) constituted the final analytical sample. Data were collected using a pretested, structured, self-administered questionnaire distributed via social media platforms. The primary outcome was receipt of at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. Bivariate associations were examined using chi-square tests, and independent predictors of vaccination uptake were identified through binary logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results Vaccination coverage was critically deficient; only 16.4% ( n = 67) of the participants had received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine. Personal health protection was the principal driver among vaccinated individuals (71.2%). Conversely, systemic bottlenecks like lack of access (29.0%) and cognitive barriers like vaccine distrust (21.3%) limited compliance. In the adjusted model, lower odds of vaccination were independently predicted by religion (Christianity vs. Islam; aOR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.12–0.85, p = 0.023) and residential type (living with family vs. campus hostel; aOR = 0.26, 95% CI: 0.09–0.79, p = 0.017). Conclusions Vaccine coverage within this cohort is severely suboptimal, transforming a priority training group into an active vector for nosocomial transmission to vulnerable patient populations. To rectify this blind spot, institutional policy must pivot from passive information dissemination to structural interventions, including decentralized on-campus deployment frameworks and enforced clinical-posting vaccination prerequisites.

title: Human coronavirus population genetics and phenotypic consequences
abstract: First identified in the 1960s, human coronaviruses cause a significant global health burden. Seasonal human coronaviruses HCoV-229E, HCoV-OC43, HCoV-NL63 and HCoV-HKU1 cause ‘common cold’-like symptoms in immunocompetent individuals and account for approximately 5-30% of respiratory infections globally. Several severe human coronaviruses have emerged over the past two decades, causing localised outbreaks with high case fatality rates, including SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV. However, the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 in 2019 grew into a pandemic impacting global economies and societies, resulting in a public health emergency. During the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, global sequencing efforts facilitated real-time mass genomic surveillance of genomic variation and subsequent lineage divergence, aiding the pandemic response. This thesis investigated human coronavirus evolutionary patterns by sequencing clinical samples to elucidate intra-host genomic changes. Total-RNA and ARTIC-amplicon sequencing of longitudinal SARS-CoV-2 isolates identified the P323L substitution in NSP12 which rapidly evolved in hospitalised patients in the containment phase in the UK (early 2020). This rapid selection was also observed in a non-human primate model for COVID-19. The P323L substitution emerged concurrently with the D614G substitution in Spike in early 2020 and was one of the first identified divergent genomic changes compared to the reference sequence. The maintenance of P323L in the global viral population throughout the pandemic was demonstrated, although its functionality was never characterised. To investigate the genotype to phenotype consequences of P323L, transcriptomic and proteomic analyses were conducted using an in vitro lung cell culture model. The P323L substitution was associated with increased autophagy and phosphorylation pathways, suggesting that L323 interacts with the host cell through the phosphoproteome and impacts cellular responses during infection compared to P323. To investigate viral genomic change in human populations, longitudinal nasopharyngeal swab samples were collected from a cohort of ‘healthy’ immunocompetent participants during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection. Samples were NimaGen-Illumina sequenced to characterise viral evolution. Intra- and inter-participant differences in the dominant and minor genomic variation were reported, with SARS-CoV-2 from several participants showing dynamic changes in the lineages identified over time. This underscores the fact that viral diversity generation is also a dynamic process during SARS-CoV-2 infection of ‘healthy’ individuals, not just immunocompromised individuals. To explore the future trajectory of SARS-CoV-2 evolution, a biobank of 1127 seasonal HCoV samples collected between 2012-2022 were amplicon-Illumina sequenced and compared to SARS-CoV-2. Phylogenetic analysis showed that there was a high sequence diversity both intra- and inter-HCoV. These were similar evolutionary patterns to SARS-CoV-2, as determined by minor and dominant level single nucleotide polymorphisms and insertion/deletion frequencies over time. This suggested that SARS-CoV-2 will continue to evolve and diversify in the future through increased genomic change. In conclusion, this thesis describes a detailed analysis of human coronavirus evolution, drawing upon longitudinal samples of both SARS-CoV-2 and the seasonal HCoVs. This data was used to drive genotype to phenotype studies to provide functional analysis of evolutionary pressures.

title: Trends in the Causes and Severity of Household Burns during the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Longitudinal Study
abstract: Background: Burn injuries remain a global public health challenge with significant morbidity, mortality, and socioeconomic burden. The COVID-19 pandemic, through nationwide lockdowns and lifestyle alterations, influenced patterns of domestic accidents, including burns. While earlier studies examined short-term effects of lockdowns, limited literature exists on longitudinal outcomes in a metropolitan burn centre. Objective: To assess the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on burn epidemiology, clinical severity, and outcomes, and to compare findings across pre-COVID, COVID, and post-COVID periods Methods: A retrospective observational study was conducted at a major burn centre in Bengaluru from September 2018 to December 2022. The study period was divided into three 17-month intervals: pre-COVID (Sept 2018–Jan 2020), COVID (Feb 2020–Jun 2021), and post-COVID (Jul 2021–Dec 2022). Demographic data, type and etiology of burns, severity (total body surface area, TBSA), management, hospital stay, COVID-19 positivity, and mortality were analysed. Results: A 30% reduction in burn admissions occurred during the COVID period. A reversal in gender distribution was observed, with females outnumbering males. Age distribution showed reduced incidence in extremes and increased incidence among middle-aged adults. Thermal burns significantly increased, while scald, electrical, chemical, and cracker-related burns decreased. Severity of burns, measured by TBSA, increased during the pandemic. Accidental burns predominated, whereas suicidal and homicidal burns declined. Mortality rates increased substantially, particularly among COVID-positive burn patients who also experienced longer hospital stays. Elective burn surgeries decreased during the pandemic due to restricted healthcare capacity. Conclusion: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered the epidemiology of burns in metropolitan India. Fewer admissions masked higher burn severity and mortality, underscoring gaps in access to timely burn care. Preventive measures, community education, and resilient burn management protocols are critical for safeguarding vulnerable populations during future crises.
journal: Clinical Journal of Plastic & Reconstructive Surgery

title: How Did COVID-19 Affect Urban Slums?
abstract: Abstract During the COVID-19 pandemic, slum settlements received significant attention for their vulnerabilities. To mitigate risks of disease transmission and containment measures, experts called for community-driven solutions. But such approaches frequently neglect pre-existing structures of local leadership in these settlements. How did India’s slum leaders respond to the pandemic? What factors shape their success in helping residents? To answer these questions, we conducted a phone survey of 321 slum leaders in two north Indian cities during India’s stringent 2020 national lockdown. Our survey reveals striking continuities with pre-pandemic politics. Slum leaders persist in their problem-solving roles but tilt efforts toward pandemic response activities. Their effectiveness in doing so remains informed by the same factors that shape efficacy during “normal times,” notably their education and degree of embeddedness in party networks. Finally, pre-pandemic disparities in slum-level infrastructural development shape how much residents must depart from social distancing guidelines to secure essential services.

title: ‘Reaching and Teaching’: Understanding the Supercomplexity of Primary Teachers’ Work in an Area of High Social Deprivation During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract This chapter explores the supercomplexity of primary teachers’ work in four northern English schools serving communities of high social deprivation during the COVID-19 pandemic. Based on a multiple case study, it shows how teachers’ safeguarding, pastoral and welfare roles expanded during the pandemic, requiring sustained family engagement amid overlapping social, economic and digital disadvantage and in response to shifting policy guidance. Framed by Barnett’s (2000a) notion of supercomplexity, the analysis identifies five overlapping themes: evolving definitions of vulnerability, mediating learning through homes, the emotional labour of care, rapid pedagogical and organisational adaptation and re-evaluation of educational aims beyond high-stakes accountability. While teachers demonstrated remarkable adaptability; developing hybrid provision, restructuring Early Years pedagogy and prioritising wellbeing, the moral weight of this labour remained largely unrecognised in policy. This chapter argues for teacher education and system design that centre adaptability, relational care and professional judgement, positioning teachers as co-constructors of educational meaning and essential agents in building resilience for future crises.
journal: Schools and Families on the Frontline

title: Widening the Gap? The Impact of COVID-19 Restrictions on Education for Students With Special Educational Needs and Disabilities in an English Special School
abstract: Abstract This study explores how COVID-19 restrictions impacted on the provision of education for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), from the point of view of four parents and the headteacher at a special school in the North of England. Thematic analysis of the data through Bronfenbrenner’s bioecological theory and Biesta’s domains of education contextualised the effects of school closures and policies on the people and systems that students engage with, as well as how they both interact with one another. While existing research has largely examined the impact of school closures and remote learning, this case study highlights the critical role of specialist provision in supporting families and maintaining student wellbeing. Findings reveal how the pandemic exacerbated existing inequalities and exposed the marginalisation of SEND learners within policy and practice. The study calls for a radical reframing of education through a social model of disability, advocating for inclusive environments and pedagogies. Although focused on only one special school, insights offer valuable lessons for mainstream and specialist settings alike. Wellbeing must be embedded in educational policy and practice to better support all learners moving forward.

title: Reimagining Secondary Schools as a Result of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Qualitative Study
abstract: Abstract This chapter reports the findings of a qualitative study that set out to examine the experiences and priorities of English state-funded secondary schools during the COVID-19 pandemic. It considers how historical and contemporary policy eras have shaped the capacities of schools to respond to the challenges posed by the pandemic. Research took place within three schools with different types of governance: an inner-city new build that is part of a multi-academy trust, a Faith School and a Maintained School. It purposively recruited staff across a range of roles (senior leader, teaching and non-teaching support) to gain a complete picture of school approaches. Findings were as follows: going into the pandemic, each school identified challenges around staff recruitment, budgetary pressures, social deprivation and an increasing special educational needs and disabilities register. In the early days of school closure, schools utilised their existing pastoral structures to support children and families with varying degrees of success. As the pandemic evolved, all staff found themselves taking on new activities outside of their remit, which enabled a better understanding of the families and communities that they served. The authors conclude that in taking almost total responsibility for the welfare of pupils and their families during the pandemic, participating schools – whatever their governance – continued to resist neoliberal-driven educational policy that focuses purely on the classroom and excellent teaching. Learning from the pandemic suggests that there is a strong case to re-imagine schools as integral to communities and furthermore, that there is an appetite to achieve this.
journal: Schools and Families on the Frontline

title: Sex-specific age prioritization of epidemic interventions under alternative equality objectives: a case study of COVID-19
abstract: Resource scarcity necessitates prioritization during epidemics, and equity is often used as a main guiding principle. However, alternative operational definitions of equity may yield different priorities. We developed a framework to investigate how equality objectives translate age- and sex-specific COVID-19 infection fatality ratio (IFR) estimates into prioritization strategies. IFR estimates were combined with demographic data from the UK to derive sex-specific age thresholds under Individual Risk Equality, Benefit Equality, Mortality Equality, and Life-year Equality. Male IFR at a given age approximated female IFR 7 years older. The four objectives produced different age thresholds, with differences ranging from a few years to several decades. In addition, we evaluated these objectives in a counterfactual reconstruction of the UK vaccination campaign, incorporating detailed empirical data but varying prioritization. In the reconstruction, prioritization based on Benefit, Mortality, and Life-year Equality yielded vaccination age thresholds that were 3.49/3.12, 4.92/3.75, and 6.62/4.47 years lower for males compared with females for first/second doses. Relative to sex-neutral allocation, total deaths changed by − 0.20%, + 0.48%, and + 2.61%, respectively, despite reductions in male mortality. These findings demonstrate that allocation outcomes depend on operational definition of equity and that achieving parity does not necessarily minimize total mortality.

title: EBV REACTIVATION AND MIS-C AFTER COVID-19 IN AN ADOLESCENT
abstract: Background: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) is a post-infectious complication of SARS-CoV-2 characterized by systemic hyperinflammation and multiorgan involvement. Emerging evidence suggests that the immune dysregulation associated with MIS-C may facilitate reactivation of latent viruses, including Epstein–Barr virus (EBV). We describe an adolescent with MIS-C and concomitant EBV DNAemia, raising the possibility of EBV reactivation during the hyperinflammatory response. Case Presentation: A 15-year-old girl presented with a 3-day history of persistent high-grade fever (maximum temperature, 39°C) accompanied by rigors, facial and periorbital edema, generalized abdominal pain, and decreased urine output. On admission, she was moderately unwell but hemodynamically stable (blood pressure, 102/78 mmHg; heart rate, 120 beats/min). Clinical examination revealed pharyngeal erythema, generalized abdominal tenderness, hepatosplenomegaly, pallor, and facial edema. Initial laboratory investigations demonstrated leukopenia, neutropenia, and thrombocytopenia (white blood cell count, 2,800/μL; absolute neutrophil count, 1,140/μL; platelet count, 74,000/μL; hemoglobin, 12.4 g/dL). Respiratory multiplex PCR was positive for rhinovirus/enterovirus, while EBV DNA was detected in peripheral blood and EBV IgG was positive. Electrocardiography revealed repolarization abnormalities, although echocardiography was normal. Empirical cefuroxime and intravenous fluids were initiated. On the second day of hospitalization, her clinical condition deteriorated, with persistent high-grade fever and worsening cytopenias (white blood cell count, 2,500/μL; platelet count, 65,000/μL; hemoglobin, 11.6 g/dL). SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid-specific IgM antibodies were positive. Peripheral blood immunophenotyping and serum immunoglobulin levels were normal for age. Macrophage activation syndrome was initially considered, and intravenous immunoglobulin (1 g/kg/day for 2 consecutive days) was administered. The combination of persistent fever, gastrointestinal manifestations, hematological abnormalities, evidence of previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, and electrocardiographic changes supported the diagnosis of MIS-C. Methylprednisolone and aspirin were subsequently added to the therapeutic regimen. Learning Points: The final diagnosis was MIS-C associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, accompanied by EBV DNAemia in the presence of positive EBV IgG, suggesting possible reactivation of a previous EBV infection. Emerging evidence indicates that MIS-C-associated immune dysregulation may facilitate EBV reactivation through impaired antiviral T-cell responses, potentially contributing to the hyperinflammatory milieu. However, EBV reactivation cannot be definitively established from EBV PCR positivity and IgG seropositivity alone, and a causal role for EBV in MIS-C cannot be inferred. This case highlights the potential interaction between latent viral infections and the dysregulated immune response of MIS-C and emphasizes the importance of considering concomitant viral reactivation in children with atypical or severe hyperinflammatory presentations.

title: COVID-19 in the Village
abstract: Abstract This chapter examines why frontline health workers played such uneven roles in India’s rural COVID-19 response. Focusing on Accredited Social Health Activists, Anganwadi workers, and Auxiliary Nurse Midwives, it conceptualizes frontline workers as hybrid actors positioned between local communities and the state. Drawing on interviews with workers and officials, a multistate survey, and grassroots video documentation, the chapter shows that pandemic responses rose or fell with hybrid actors’ social standing and institutional support. Many frontline health workers were doubly constrained—by weak backing from state agencies and by entrenched inequalities of caste, class, and gender—leaving them exposed, overburdened, and unable to deliver reliable care or welfare. Others were doubly empowered, combining bureaucratic authority with community trust, and so were able to mobilize resources, enforce public health measures, and extend assistance more equitably. The chapter argues that inequalities affecting frontline workers are a central but overlooked feature of crisis response and identifies the conditions under which local intermediaries might reduce, rather than reproduce, social exclusion.

title: Indirect pathways linking psychological flexibility with paranoia worries through social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking, and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions among late adolescents.
abstract: Background This cross-sectional study examines the association between psychological flexibility and paranoia worries, through indirect pathways of social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking, and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions. This cross-sectional study aimed to examine the direct and indirect pathways linking psychological flexibility and paranoia worries among late adolescents aged 18-20 years. Methods Data were collected from 967 late adolescents aged 18-20 years in eastern China, including sociodemographic characteristics, psychological flexibility, paranoia worries, COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions, social-media-related social anxiety, antisocial rule-breaking, and social-emotional expertise. Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to analyze the direct and indirect pathways linking psychological flexibility with paranoia worries through social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions. Results Significant indirect associations between psychological flexibility and paranoia worries were observed through social-media-related social anxiety (β = -0.089, p = 0.001). Psychological flexibility was indirectly associated with paranoia worries through COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions (β = 0.023, p = 0.001). Significant indirect associations between psychological flexibility and paranoia worries were observed through a sequential indirect pathway of social-media-related social anxiety and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions (β = -0.021, p = 0.001). These findings highlight indirect pathways linking psychological flexibility with paranoia worries through social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions. Conclusions These findings highlight indirect associations linking psychological flexibility with paranoia worries through social-media-related social anxiety, social-emotional expertise, antisocial rule-breaking, and COVID-19-specific catastrophic cognitions among late adolescents. The findings may provide useful insights for research involving comparable late-adolescent and university student populations. Broader applicability to other sociocultural and upper-and middle-income countries (UMICs) contexts requires further cross-cultural replication.

title: Differentiation of COVID-19 from other viral pneumonias on chest CT: radiologist and AI perspectives
abstract: To evaluate the chest CT features of COVID-19 pneumonia and non-COVID viral pneumonias and assess the diagnostic efficacy of radiologists and an AI-based system in distinguishing between the two. This retrospective study included 181 patients (101 COVID-19 and 80 non-COVID). Chest CT images were independently assessed by two radiologists blinded to clinical and PCR data. CT examinations were also analyzed by a deep-learning AI algorithm. CT features were compared between groups using univariate and multivariate logistic regression. Agreement between the two observers and between the AI and COVID-19 RT-PCR test results was calculated using kappa statistics. Age and sex showed no statistically significant differences between groups. Peripheral distribution, nodular ground-glass opacities and a crazy-paving pattern were significantly more prevalent in COVID-19 cases ( p 20% of lung volume. The AI algorithm achieved a sensitivity of 60% and specificity of 83.8% (κ = 0.414). Interobserver agreement between radiologists was almost perfect (κ = 0.834), and both radiologists exhibited substantial agreement with the PCR results (κ = 0.777 and 0.700). Presence of peripheral distribution, nodular GGO and crazy-paving pattern as well as a lack of lobar consolidation, bronchial wall thickening, upper lobe predominance, and tree-in-bud nodules may favor COVID-19 pneumonia with a sensitivity of 91% and specificity of 88%. Several odds ratios in the multivariable analysis had wide confidence intervals, reflecting limited precision due to the modest sample size. Indicative CT characteristics, including peripheral distribution, nodular ground-glass opacities, and crazy paving, may assist in differentiating COVID-19 from non-COVID viral pneumonias. While AI demonstrated potential as a supportive triage tool, the radiologists achieved higher diagnostic accuracy and consistency. These findings support the integration of AI as a complementary decision-support system rather than a standalone diagnostic tool in future pandemic preparedness efforts. All performance estimates derive from internal, single-center validation and should be regarded as exploratory pending external validation.

title: Was It Worth It? A Mature Reappraisal of Anti-CD20 Maintenance for Follicular Lymphoma During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Background: Anti-CD20 maintenance prolongs progression-free survival (PFS) in follicular lymphoma (FL) but sustains B-cell depletion and blunts vaccine responses. Methods: we conducted a retrospective study comparing two Italian centres that, during the COVID-19 pandemic, adopted opposite policies: Centre A continued maintenance; Centre B discouraged it. Results: Among 62 consecutive patients completing first- or second-line induction in 2019–2022, maintenance was started in 47 (95% and 41% by centre; 92% and 27% among patients aged ≥70 years); patients not receiving it were older (79 vs. 66 years, p < 0.001). After a median follow-up of 70 months, crude 5-year PFS favoured maintenance (59% vs. 27%; hazard ratio [HR] 0.39), but the advantage shrank after adjustment for age (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.30–1.72) or overlap propensity weighting (HR 0.60, 0.27–1.31); overall survival did not differ. The strong association between more than four cycles and survival (HR 0.22) faded at a 12-month landmark (HR 0.61, 0.19–1.95), consistent with immortal-time bias. All five COVID-19 deaths (10.6%) occurred in maintained patients, 2.0–3.7 months after the last dose and mostly without seroconversion, and none among the older patients without maintenance. Censoring these deaths brought the PFS benefit back within the range of randomised trials (weighted HR 0.41, 0.17–0.96). Conclusions: In this small real-world cohort, COVID-19 mortality appears to have offset much of the expected gain from maintenance during the pandemic.

title: The implementation of vaccination campaigns for COVID-19 in primary healthcare centres in Bamako, Mali
abstract: Despite the unprecedented speed of COVID-19 vaccine development, vaccination coverage in Mali remained low. Research has primarily focused on individual vaccine hesitancy, overlooking systemic issues in implementing vaccination in health facilities. This article analyses the implementation of Mali’s national vaccination strategy in 2021 and 2022 to understand the challenges associated with COVID-19 vaccination coverage and the lessons learned. The study employed a qualitative approach. Data collection comprised field observations ( n = 20 days) and semi-structured interviews ( n = 57) conducted at two Primary Health Centres ( Centres de Sante Communautaire , or CSComs) in Bamako, Mali. The analysis utilised a conceptual quality implementation framework to identify factors that influenced the campaign’s successes or limitations. Vaccination campaigns intensified gradually between 2021 and 2023. Implementation followed a top-down approach, largely controlled by the Health District staff. The limited involvement of CSComs in key vaccination activities (planning, capacity building, supervision) prompted them to develop adaptation strategies to meet their assigned objectives. The analyses showed that the intensity of implementing the national vaccination strategy varied across the quality phases of implementation. The CSComs conducted very few evaluation activities. We cannot fully understand vaccine coverage without a thorough analysis of implementation mechanisms. This study highlights the importance of building local capacity, tailoring strategies to community realities, and improving documentation of field practices for future public health interventions.

title: Enhancing respiratory viruses surveillance in Belgium: a validation of the wastewater-based surveillance of influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 in the 2024/2025 winter season
abstract: During the 2024/2025 respiratory virus season, Belgium recorded the highest incidence of general practitioner visits for influenza-like illness since the COVID-19 pandemic. The pressure on healthcare systems was driven by epidemics of influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), while SARS-CoV-2 activity remained at low levels. This exceptional situation was observed through conventional surveillance as well as via a novel wastewater-based surveillance program integrating influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 measurements. The innovative program monitors over 4.5 million inhabitants, representing 38% of the Belgian population, on a weekly basis by analysing samples from 30 wastewater treatment plants. The present study aims to validate wastewater data on influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 by comparing it with conventional surveillances. Wastewater-based epidemiological thresholds were computed using a quartile method. Throughout the entire season, high levels of correlation were observed between wastewater data and cases confirmed by sentinel laboratories. Wastewater-based thresholds effectively monitored viruses circulation. Wastewater-based data was assessed to provide information of added value for monitoring SARS-CoV-2 through wastewater compared to conventional surveillance, offering a large and general population coverage, a short and constant reporting time, and a feature for pandemic preparedness. Several perspectives are proposed in this work to increase the quality of RSV and influenza wastewater monitoring.

title: COVID-19 in the States
abstract: Abstract This chapter analyzes how the COVID-19 pandemic tested democratic capabilities at the subnational level. It argues that the crisis exposed not only core dimensions of state capacity but also the relational forms of power needed to secure public cooperation in highly unequal societies. It shows that national-level analyses overlook these dynamics by focusing narrowly on formal democracy and fixed bureaucratic resources, whereas the subnational level better captures how state agencies interact with civil society to coordinate high-touch health and welfare responses. It explains why state governments in India became the central actors during the pandemic and how political competition, state–society relations, and local institutions shaped state performance in health and welfare responses. These factors were key in mobilizing resources, inducing compliance, and mitigating inequalities. In doing so, the chapter demonstrates that subnational democratic capabilities are critical both for crisis response and for strengthening equitable state action more broadly.

title: Shifting landscapes of infectious diseases: lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: How the COVID-19 pandemic changed our understanding of immunity and respiratory infections The COVID-19 pandemic changed how infectious diseases spread and how the immune system responds to infections and vaccines. This thesis explores two consequences of the pandemic: vaccine responses in people with Down syndrome and the return of Mycoplasma pneumoniae, a bacterium that can cause respiratory infections. The immune system of people with Down syndrome functions differently, making them more vulnerable to infections. This was especially visible during the COVID-19 pandemic. This thesis showed that adults with Down syndrome generally produced lower concentrations of antibodies after COVID-19 vaccination than people without Down syndrome. These antibodies also became less effective with increasing age. Additional booster vaccinations increased antibody levels, but the overall responses remained lower. In contrast, the T-cell response, another important part of the immune system, was largely comparable to that of people without Down syndrome. These findings highlight the importance of tailored vaccination strategies and better protection for vulnerable groups. The thesis also described the reemergence of M. pneumoniae after the COVID-19 pandemic. Following several years of low circulation, infections increased sharply in Europe in 2023 and 2024. Although most infections were mild, within this research specialists reported substantial numbers of hospital admissions among children, including admissions to pediatric intensive care units. Severe lung disease and complications affecting other parts of the body were also observed. Together, the findings of this thesis demonstrate that pandemics have consequences beyond the immediate crisis. They can expose weaknesses in our immune responses and change the patterns of other infectious diseases. Better surveillance, continued research and collaboration between healthcare professionals and scientists are essential to protect vulnerable populations and prepare for future outbreaks.

title: The Implications of COVID-19 Policy Responses in Canada for Food Systems and Vulnerable Populations
abstract: Various federal and provincial measures were introduced in Canada during the COVID-19 pandemic to contain the spread of the virus and mitigate its socioeconomic and food security impacts. The chapter provides a systematic review of the pandemic’s impacts on Canada’s food supply chains and policy responses. It shows that Canada’s food system experienced far-reaching disruptions, such as labour shortages in agriculture and outbreaks in food processing. Food retail and food services were hit particularly hard, with long-term changes such as the surge in online food ordering. As a result of these disruptions, both physical and economic access to food were affected, particularly in the early stages of the pandemic, leading to a surge in food bank visits and reduced access to culturally appropriate foods, with rising food prices creating lasting consequences. Although government assistance programmes such as the Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB) temporarily alleviated food insecurity, the exclusion of the poorest groups reinforced existing inequities. The phasing out of these supports in 2022 coincided with renewed increases in food insecurity. The chapter therefore calls for more inclusive income supports, strengthened labour protections for migrant workers, and the integration of equity considerations into food security policies to enhance long-term resilience.

The phasing out of these supports in 2022 coincided with renewed increases in food insecurity. The chapter therefore calls for more inclusive income supports, strengthened labour protections for migrant workers, and the integration of equity considerations into food security policies to enhance long-term resilience.

title: Maternal lived experiences during COVID-19 pandemic: Inferences from GaRBH cohort, Bikaner, India
abstract: Introduction : The COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2021) severely disrupted maternal care services, especially for pregnant women from low- and middle-income countries. Rural and semi-urban areas of Rajasthan were under increased healthcare stress. This paper examines the lived experiences and threats to pregnant women during the pandemic, with emphasis on care disruptions and ensuing physical, emotional, and social impacts. Materials and Methods : This phenomenological sub-study was conducted in Rajasthan's Bikaner district under the larger GaRBH birth cohort. Twenty-four pregnant women were purposively selected for in-depth interviews during and after the pandemic. Thematic analysis was conducted using Colaizzi’s seven-step method, and the emerging themes were categorized through a socio-ecological framework. Results : Participants reported a fear of COVID-19 transmission, which led to missed antenatal check-ups and vaccinations. Access to healthcare was disrupted by lockdowns, economic pressure, and overwhelmed medical systems, forcing many into unsafe home-based care. Increased household responsibilities, social isolation, and stressful family relationships further increased stress. A few women described encounters of intimate partner violence and social stigma, particularly following testing COVID-positive. Conclusion : This research illustrates the multifaceted impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on maternal healthcare in Rajasthan's Bikaner. For any future health crises, resilient, sustainable, and inclusive maternal health systems are required to protect the health of pregnant women and their infants
