source_records.abstract: This study aimed to model the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on economic growth and stability in Nigeria using Vector Autoregressive (VAR) Model and Autoregressive Distributive Lag (ARDL) Model, integrating four variables encompassing Nigerian COVID-19 daily confirmed cases data (CC) along with other economic metrices including the Nigerian Stock Exchange All Shares Index (ASI), Daily Nigerian Naira/United States Dollar Exchange Rate (NGNUSD), and Nigerian Crude Oil Price (OP), to discern the pandemic's trends and implications on the Nigerian Economy amid post-pandemic. Covering daily time series data for the variables from May 26, 2020, to May 25, 2022, a total of 501 days. The VAR model estimation revealed insights into short-term dynamics among key economic variables, supported by stable outcomes consistent with previous studies, emphasizing significant causal relationships among economic indicators during crises like the COVID-19 pandemic. The VAR(8) model was selected as the most appropriate model using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). The VAR Residual Normality Test indicates that multivariate residuals are normal, as evidenced by the Chi-square test statistics and their associated p-values being less than 0.05. Moreover, the VAR Residual Heteroscedasticity Test shows no evidence of heteroscedasticity, as the Chi-square test statistic value of 1400.368 with a corresponding probability value of 0.51341 suggests. In examining the short-term impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on Nigeria's economic growth and stability, the variance decomposition analysis conducted on the VAR(8) model offers valuable insight on significant impact of COVID-19 on economic growth and stability over a short period of time. Meanwhile, the ARDL model estimation, employing various model specifications such as ARDL(4,0,2,2), ARDL(3,1,1,0), ARDL(2,3,0,0), and ARDL(4,3,0,0) for CC, ASI, NGNUSD, and OP as dependent variables, respectively, underscored the significance of autocorrelation effects in fluctuating economic variables, providing detailed insights into only short-run impacts which corresponded to the result of VAR model and emphasizing the interconnectedness of economic indicators, particularly with oil prices. The study's findings underscore the dynamic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on economic growth in Nigeria, revealing a short-run relationship among key variables. There were no long run effects of the pandemic on the economic stability as both VAR and ARDL suggested. ARDL emerged as the preferred model for analyzing these relationships, offering insights into both short-term fluctuations and also investigating for a long-term trends among interacting macroeconomic indicators while VAR could only account for short-run relationship only. This highlights the nuanced nature of the pandemic's effects on Nigeria's economy, emphasising the importance of adaptable analytical frameworks like ARDL for comprehensively assessing the evolving economic landscape amidst this post pandemic era.

title: The Association Between Maternal Anxiety Levels and Adherence to Basic Immunization in Toddlers During the COVID-19 Pandemic at Kuta Alam Primary Health Care
abstract: Introduction: Basic immunization is an essential preventive health intervention aimed at protecting toddlers from vaccine-preventable diseases. During the COVID-19 pandemic, immunization services were substantially disrupted, particularly between January and April 2020. Concerns regarding COVID-19 transmission increased maternal anxiety and reduced utilization of primary health care services, potentially affecting adherence to routine immunization schedules. This study aimed to examine the association between maternal anxiety levels and adherence to basic immunization in toddlers during the COVID-19 pandemic at Kuta Alam Primary Health Care.Methods: This observational analytic study employed a cross-sectional design. A total of 71 mothers of toddlers residing in the working area of Kuta Alam Primary Health Care, Banda Aceh, were recruited using proportional sampling, with the required sample size determined using the Slovin formula. Maternal anxiety levels were assessed using the validated Indonesian version of the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) questionnaire, while adherence to basic immunization was determined based on immunization records documented in the Maternal and Child Health (MCH/KIA) handbook. The association between maternal anxiety and immunization adherence was evaluated using the Chi-square test for trend and binary logistic regression, with adjustment for maternal education and age.Results: The findings showed that 45.1% of mothers experienced moderate levels of anxiety, while 60.6% of toddlers were non-adherent to the basic immunization schedule during the COVID-19 pandemic. A significant dose-response relationship was observed between anxiety level and non-adherence (χ2 = 35.03, df = 3, p < 0.001; Cochran-Armitage trend test Z = 5.75, p < 0.001). After adjusting for maternal education and age, each one-point increase in GAD-7 score was associated with a 54% higher odds of immunization non-adherence (adjusted OR 1.54, 95% CI: 1.26-1.88, p < 0.001), while maternal education and age were not significantly associated with adherence.Conclusion: Maternal anxiety levels were significantly and independently associated with adherence to basic immunization in toddlers during the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings highlight the importance of addressing maternal psychological well-being to support immunization adherence and sustain immunization coverage at the primary health care level during public health emergencies.

title: Clinical practice during the COVID-19 pandemic: perspectives of Ontario social workers
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic ushered in a period of global economic, financial, medical, social and emotional upheaval. The public health crisis necessitated that mental health care to pivot to online delivery in accordance with social distancing and lockdown protocols. Social workers, accustomed to working largely in-person, found themselves delivering therapeutic interventions online. This study examined how social workers (N = 28) in Ontario, Canada, adapted their practice to online formats and how they maintained their personal wellness during the pandemic. Social workers participated in a one-hour qualitative interview to share their experiences, while data analysis used Reflexive Thematic Analysis. The findings revealed two overarching themes: Adapting Social Work Practice and Social Worker Wellness Practices. Implications for social work practice and education are offered in light of the findings.

title: Burnout Experiences of Nurses Working in COVID-19 and Palliative Care Units: A Comparative Qualitative Study
abstract: This study aimed to compare the burnout experiences of the same nurses who had previously worked in COVID-19 units and were currently working in a palliative care center across two care settings. The qualitative study included 12 nurses, and data were collected through semi-structured interviews. The data were coded using MAXQDA and analyzed by developing subthemes and themes. The findings showed that burnout-related experiences differed according to the care setting. During COVID-19, uncertainty, infection risk, and rapid clinical changes were prominent, whereas prolonged care, repeated losses, and relationships with patients and their families became more prominent in palliative care. The meaning attributed to professional accomplishment also differed between the two care settings. Moreover, work load, working hours, shortage of staff and organizational factors were linked to burnout among healthcare professionals in both care settings. The findings indicate that burnout-related experiences should be considered together with the clinical and organizational characteristics of the care setting.

title: Molecular Epidemiological Dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 Variants Identified During the COVID-19 Pandemic (April 2021–January 2022) in Santander
abstract: La evolución y aparición de nuevas variantes del SARS-CoV-2 han generado cambios en la dinámica epidemiológica y evolutiva de la COVID-19, lo que ha puesto de manifiesto la necesidad de fortalecer la vigilancia genómica y el estudio de la dinámica viral a escala regional. El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar la dinámica evolutiva y epidemiológica de las variantes del SARS-CoV-2 circulantes en el departamento de Santander, Colombia, durante el periodo comprendido entre abril de 2021 y enero de 2022. Para ello, se analizó la evolución temporal de los casos y la letalidad por COVID-19, así como la variabilidad genética de la proteína de la espiga, el tamaño efectivo de la población (Ne) y el número reproductivo efectivo (Re) de las principales variantes identificadas. Durante el periodo estudiado se identificaron dos picos epidémicos de COVID-19 y la circulación sucesiva de las variantes Mu, Delta y Ómicron. La variante Mu predominó durante la tercera ola epidémica, mientras que Delta y, posteriormente, Ómicron se establecieron como variantes dominantes. El análisis del tamaño efectivo de la población (Ne) mostró una expansión asociada a los periodos de predominio de las distintas variantes, con diferencias en su velocidad y magnitud. Por su parte, Ómicron presentó la mayor variabilidad genética en la proteína de la espiga y los valores más elevados del número reproductivo efectivo (Re). En conjunto, los resultados evidencian que la dinámica epidemiológica de la COVID-19 en Santander estuvo influenciada por la sustitución de variantes con diferentes características evolutivas y capacidades de transmisión, en concordancia con las tendencias observadas a escala nacional.

title: SARS-CoV-2 infection, myelin, and cognition in middle-aged and older adults: The CLSA COVID-19 Brain Health Study
abstract: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2), the cause of COVID-19, has been hypothesized to contribute to cognitive decline through effects on myelin. We investigated SARS-CoV-2 infection effects on myelin and cognition in middle-aged and older adults. We analyzed cross-sectional MRI and cognitive data from the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging COVID-19 Brain Health Study. We quantified cerebral white matter myelin using myelin water imaging. Cognition included modified Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test, Mental Alternation Test, and verbal fluency via animal fluency. Analysis of covariance were perfomed to determine differences between SARS-CoV-2 cases and controls adjusting for relevant confounding factors. Exploratory moderation analyses assessed the influence of biological sex, APOE ε4 status, and COVID-19-related symptom incidence and severity. We included 352 community-dwelling individuals with infection status determined at time of MRI scanning (SARS-CoV-2 cases, n = 64; controls, n = 288). Participant mean (SD) age was 65.3 (8.4) years, and 50.3% were female. There were no differences between SARS-CoV-2 cases and controls in myelin content or objective measures of cognition. There were no moderating effects of sex or APOE ε4 status. Cases showed greater incidence (P<0.001) and severity (P<0.001) of COVID-19-related symptoms. Moderation analysis of myelin content revealed significant interactions between symptom incidence and severity with diagnosis group after correcting for multiple comparisons (P corrected < 0.05). Post hoc analysis showed that symptom incidence and severity were inversely associated with myelin content in SARS-CoV-2 cases but not in controls across multiple regions-of-interest. SARS-CoV-2 cases and controls did not differ in myelin content or cognition. Among cases, greater self-reported symptom incidence and severity were associated with lower myelin content, an exploratory finding that requires longitudinal confirmation before it can be interpreted as infection-related myelin loss.

title: Purinergic Imbalance and Adenosinergic Modulation of Antibacterial Activity in Severe COVID-19 and Sepsis
abstract: Sepsis and immunosuppression are major contributors to mortality in the intensive care unit. This study investigated dysregulated purinergic signaling, particularly systemic adenosine alterations, in relation to biomarkers and impaired antibacterial activity in severe COVID-19 and sepsis. Peripheral blood samples from COVID-19 patients at different disease stages were analyzed. Plasma purine levels were quantified by LC-MS/MS. To assess the functional effects of patient plasma, PBMCs from healthy donors were incubated with plasma from severe COVID-19 patients, resulting in increased CD39, PD-1, and KLRG1 and reduced CD73, CD28, and CD127 expression on T cells. Antibacterial activity was assessed in vitro using healthy-donor monocytes and RAW 264.7 macrophages exposed to patient plasma and challenged with GFP-expressing Escherichia coli (OP50-GFP). At hospital admission, ATP was lower, and AMP was higher in SARS-CoV-2-negative pneumonia and non-ICU and ICU COVID-19 patients than in healthy controls, whereas adenosine was lower in both COVID-19 groups. Longitudinally, nonsurvivors showed decreased ATP and increased adenosine from T1 to T2, with higher Δadenosine and lower ΔATP than survivors. Among septic patients, adenosine was higher in nonsurvivors. In vitro, cells exposed to plasma from septic ICU patients exhibited lower antibacterial activity. Adenosine and the A1/A2A antagonists DPCPX and ZM 241385 further supported a role for adenosinergic signaling: adenosine alone or combined with DPCPX reduced antibacterial activity, whereas DPCPX alone increased it. Overall, dysregulated purinergic signaling, particularly altered adenosine dynamics, may contribute to impaired antibacterial defense and immune dysfunction in severe COVID-19, with circulating plasma factors potentially increasing susceptibility to secondary infections.

title: Differential placental innate immune regulation in response to Hepatitis E virus and COVID-19 infected pregnant women
abstract: Background Pregnancy presents a unique immunological challenge, and requires a delicate balance between fetal tolerance and maternal antiviral defense. Placental estrogen receptors have been shown to modulate innate immune responses critical for antiviral defense, yet their role in viral infections such as Hepatitis E virus (HEV) and COVID-19 remains undefined.Material and methods Placental samples were collected at the time of delivery from COVID-19 +ve women, HEV-infected women, and healthy controls. mRNA expression of estrogen receptors alpha and beta (ESR-1, ESR-2), G-protein coupled receptor 30 (GPER-1), CD55, IL-10, and IFN-αR was assessed using qRT-PCR. Correlation analyses were performed to study the relationship between estrogen receptors and immune modulators.Results mRNA expression analysis revealed increased expression of ESR-1 and GPER-1, and decreased ESR-2 expression in both COVID-19 and HEV infected placentas compared to controls. Notably, alterations in ER expression were accompanied by increased complement decay accelerating factor (CD55) and decreased interleukin-10 (IL-10) and interferon-alpha receptor (IFN-αR) in both infection groups. ESR-2 revealed a positive correlation with IFN-αR, while ESR-1 displayed a negative correlation with CD55. Despite increased GPER-1, reduced IL-10 was observed in both infection groups.Conclusion Our findings highlight alteration in the innate immune responses modulated by estrogen receptors in HEV and COVID-19 infected pregnancies.

title: YONDOSH KASALLIKLARI BOR BOLALARDA OʻTKIR COVID-19 OGʻIRLIGINI BAHOLASHDA BIOMARKERLAR: MAVJUD DALILLAR VA BILIM BOʻSHLIQLARI BIOMARKERS FOR ASSESSING ACUTE COVID-19 SEVERITY IN CHILDREN WITH COMORBIDITIES: CURRENT EVIDENCE AND KNOWLEDGE GAPS
abstract: Maqsad: yondosh kasalligi bor bolalarda qaysi biomarker, qachon oʻlchanganda va qaysi keyingi klinik oqibat bilan bogʻliq ekanini baholash. Material va usullar: narrativ sharh. Dastlabki qoʻlyozmaning 39 bibliografik yozuvi 2026-yil 19-noyabrda PubMed va CyberLeninka’da bajarilgan, takrorlash mumkin boʻlgan qidiruv bilan toʻldirildi: PubMed’da 825 noyob yozuvdan 670 tasi sarlavha, 54 tasi annotatsiya boʻyicha koʻrib chiqildi va 22 tasi kiritildi. Dalillar A (yondosh kasallik kohortasi), B (umumiy pediatrik kohorta) va C (bilvosita dalil) guruhlariga ajratildi. Natijalar: yakuniy 52 manbadan 12 tasi yondosh kasalligi bor bolalarda biomarkerni klinik oqibat bilan bogʻlagan A guruhi tadqiqoti boʻldi: 11 tasi onkologik, onkogematologik kasalliklar va transplantatsiyadan keyingi holatlarga, 1 tasi 1-tip qandli diabetga tegishli. 8 ta tadqiqotda tashxis paytidagi limfopeniya yoki neytropeniya ogʻirroq kechish, intensiv terapiya yoki kasalxonaga yotqizish bilan bogʻliq boʻlgan; bitta registrda laborator markerlar oqibat bilan bogʻlanmagan. 1-tip diabetda yuqori HbA1c kasalxonaga yotqizish bilan bogʻliq boʻlgan, biroq yotqizishlarning 72% i diabetik ketoatsidoz sababli boʻlgan. Umumiy pediatrik kohortalarda prokalsitonin, ferritin, D-dimer, limfopeniya va trombotsitopeniya ogʻir oqibatlar bilan bogʻliq boʻlgan, ammo bu chegaralar prognostik vosita sifatida validatsiyadan oʻtmagan. Tugʻma yurak kasalligi, surunkali buyrak kasalligi, nevrologik kasalliklar va semizlikda, shuningdek leptin, adiponektin va VEGF-A boʻyicha A guruhidagi biomarker–oqibat tadqiqoti ushbu sharhga kiritilgan manbalarda aniqlanmadi. Xulosa: mavjud dalillar asosan immunosupressiyali bolalardagi limfotsit va neytrofil sonlariga taalluqli. Bitta marker yoki universal panel asosida klinik qaror qabul qilish uchun dalil yetarli emas; kasallik turi boʻyicha stratifikatsiyalangan, oʻlchash vaqti standartlashtirilgan va tashqi validatsiyaga ega prospektiv tadqiqotlar zarur.

title: COVID-19 and the rise of digital talent platforms amongst skilled professionals in Lebanon
abstract: The global growth of digital talent platforms is well-documented, yet adoption in fragile emerging markets remains underexplored. This study examines the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the attractiveness and adoption of these platforms among skilled professionals in Lebanon between 2018 and 2024. The research is grounded in a quantitative methodology, combining Google Trends of online interest with survey data to identify temporal trends. The study, conducted in the Middle East, offers a social and cultural layer. It encompasses HR professionals, recruiters and hiring managers. It establishes the foundation for understanding the relationship between the COVID-19 pandemic and the adoption of digital talent platforms among skilled professionals in Lebanon within the context of a multifaceted local crisis. Findings revealed a 76% increase in platform-related search interest and higher adoption rates during the COVID-19 pandemic, a crisis that normalized remote work and enabled Lebanese professionals to participate in global labor markets without physical relocation. Conversely, domestic shocks, such as political unrest and the Beirut port explosion, were associated with heightened emigration interest rather than platform engagement. This distinction challenges the assumption that all shocks uniformly drive platform adoption. It underscores that while digital talent platforms offer a mechanism for resilience during systemic disruptions, their success is contingent upon the infrastructure, stability and trust that local crises erode. By differentiating between crises through the Event System theory and the Resource-based View theory, this research contributes to the literature on digital talent markets and offers insights for talent-exporting countries with prolonged instability.

title: Dynamic flow promotes airway MPS maturation and host response to viral infection
abstract: Background High attrition rates in infectious disease drug and vaccine development are partly attributed to preclinical models that inadequately recapitulate the human airway microenvironment. Although dynamic flow microphysiological systems (MPS) have been proposed as more physiologically relevant alternatives to static culture, direct benchmarking in respiratory infection models remains limited. Methods We directly compared primary human airway MPS established under static conditions or continuous basolateral perfusion. Tissue organisation, epithelial differentiation, barrier integrity, spatial infection phenotypes, and host transcriptional responses were assessed following infection with SARS-CoV-2 variants (Pre-alpha, Delta, and Omicron BA.5). Results Dynamic flow promoted improved epithelial organisation without major alterations in baseline gene expression, consistent with accelerated differentiation kinetics rather than shifts in cell composition. Both static and dynamic systems supported productive SARS-CoV-2 infection; however, dynamic flow cultures demonstrated reduced inter-replicate variability and improved robustness of quantitative readouts. Spatial imaging revealed reproducible higher-order phenotypes, including variant-dependent syncytia formation. Transcriptomic analyses showed increased effect sizes and reduced variance under dynamic flow, resulting in improved discrimination between infected and mock tissues and greater confidence in pathway-level interpretation. Interferon-driven host responses aligned with published patient-derived datasets, supporting biological relevance. Conclusions While static airway models are sufficient for basic infection kinetics, incorporation of dynamic flow enhances reproducibility, sensitivity, and mechanistic interpretability between replicates. Dynamic flow airway MPS therefore provide a more reliable platform for comparative studies and may provide sufficient resolution to support intervention assessment, providing improved translational confidence in preclinical respiratory infection research. As continuous perfusion is required for integration into interconnected multi-organ pharmacokinetic systems, these findings also support the use of dynamic flow airway MPS within multi-organ chips.

title: LINKING SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE TO STOCK RESILIENCE DURING AND AFTER COVID-19 CRISIS: EVIDENCE FROM SOUTHEAST ASIA
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic severely disrupted markets. While sustainability performance measured by ESG scores theoretically buffers against shocks, its efficacy in emerging markets with nascent sustainability frameworks remains underexplored. Method: We analyze a balanced panel of 1,395 observations from 279 non-financial Southeast Asian firms (2020–2024). Using OLS, lagged, and fixed effects models, we compare the impact of sustainability performance on stock resilience during the 2020–2022 and post-pandemic (2023–2024) periods. Findings: Sustainability performance (ESG scores) significantly enhanced stock resilience during the pandemic. However, this protective effect dissipated post-pandemic. Results confirm a statistically significant improvement in overall resilience following the crisis, as investors redirected their focus toward traditional financial fundamentals such as profitability and leverage. Conclusion: Sustainability performance acts as situational crisis insurance. Its risk-mitigation value is highly salient during systemic uncertainty but diminishes under stable market conditions. Novelty/Originality of this article: Unlike prior single-phase studies in developed economies, this research provides longitudinal evidence on the dynamic, state-dependent nature of sustainability performance across crisis and recovery phases within Southeast Asia’s early-stage ESG landscape.

title: Public mourning under biosocial trauma: A comparative study of the institutionalization of COVID-19 commemoration
abstract: This study offers a comparative framework for understanding how states recognize, institutionalize, or omit public mourning under conditions of globally shared suffering conceptualized as biosocial trauma during the COVID-19 pandemic. The study comparatively analyzes state-level commemorative practices for COVID-19-related deaths across 12 countries in East Asia, Europe, and North America. The study examines how political and public actors shape the institutionalization of memory. The study develops a typological framework based on two dimensions: the degree of institutionalization of public mourning rituals (recurrent, sporadic, or absent) and the mode of governance (top-down vs collaborative). The findings demonstrate that the institutionalization of public mourning unfolds through diverse and uneven trajectories of collective memory construction shaped by differing configurations of political and institutional governance. In sum, the institutionalization of collective memory under conditions of biosocial trauma is shaped through complex layers of political, social, and cultural responsibility by which states and societies respond to collective suffering.

source_records.title: Public mourning under biosocial trauma: A comparative study of the institutionalization of COVID-19 commemoration

The study comparatively analyzes state-level commemorative practices for COVID-19-related deaths across 12 countries in East Asia, Europe, and North America. The study examines how political and public actors shape the institutionalization of memory. The study develops a typological framework based on two dimensions: the degree of institutionalization of public mourning rituals (recurrent, sporadic, or absent) and the mode of governance (top-down vs collaborative). The findings demonstrate that the institutionalization of public mourning unfolds through diverse and uneven trajectories of collective memory construction shaped by differing configurations of political and institutional governance. In sum, the institutionalization of collective memory under conditions of biosocial trauma is shaped through complex layers of political, social, and cultural responsibility by which states and societies respond to collective suffering.

title: Impactos comportamentais e funcionais da pandemia da COVID-19 em crianças e adolescentes com autismo na Amazônia brasileira
abstract: Objective: To analyze functional, behavioral, and psychosocial changes documented in children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder followed in specialized services in the Brazilian Amazon during the COVID-19 pandemic and after the easing of public health restrictions. Methods: Observational, retrospective, documentary study with quantitative and qualitative approaches, including 85 participants aged 3 to 15 years followed in Altamira, Pará, from 2019 to 2022. Clinical, behavioral, and care-related variables were analyzed, together with progress notes submitted to thematic content analysis. Results: Changes in communication and socialization occurred in 68.2%, agitation, aggression, or restlessness in 55.3%, feeding, sleep, or sensory changes in 42.4%, and stereotypies or learning difficulties in 25.9%. Documentary analysis identified five themes: behavioral dysregulation, functional and adaptive changes, social isolation and technology use, psychological distress, and therapeutic response. Loss to follow-up or treatment dropout was recorded in 41.2%. Conclusion: The findings indicate multidimensional changes in daily functioning and behavior in a context marked by challenges in continuity of care. The retrospective design and heterogeneity of clinical records limit causal inference and the characterization of functional regression.

title: Serological evidence of strongyloidiasis in COVID-19 hospitalized patients in northern Iran during the pandemic: prevalence and risk factors
abstract: Strongyloidiasis, a parasitic infection caused by the intestinal nematode Strongyloides stercoralis , remains a significant public health concern in tropical and subtropical regions. This helminthic infection poses particular risks for immunocompromised individuals, potentially progressing to life-threatening hyperinfection syndrome and disseminated disease. In Iran, endemic foci of S. stercoralis have been well-documented in both northern and southern coastal provinces. The current COVID-19 pandemic has introduced new clinical challenges, as immunosuppressive therapies commonly employed in COVID-19 management may predispose patients to severe parasitic complications. This descriptive cross-sectional study aimed to determine both the seroprevalence of S. stercoralis infection and associated risk factors among COVID-19 patients of Guilan province in northern Iran during 2022. A total of 208 serum samples were collected from patients with COVID-19 referred to Razi Hospital in Rasht City, Guilan province. Demographic data, such as sex, age, job, residential area, and educational level, were recorded through interviews. The presence of the anti- S. stercoralis IgG antibody was detected by S. stercoralis IgG ELISA kit. The seropositive rate of strongyloidiasis was 19.7% of all the studied subjects. The seropositivity rate for strongyloidiasis was 19.7% among the studied subjects. A significant difference ( P = 0.039) was observed between genders, with 25.2% of males and 13.9% of females testing seropositive. The prevalence was significantly higher ( P = 0.014) among farmers and workers compared to other occupational groups. Additionally, illiterate individuals had a significantly higher infection rate ( P = 0.007) than those with formal education. This study highlights a high prevalence of strongyloidiasis among COVID-19 patients in northern Iran. Therefore, screening for Strongyloides infection using serologic methods, particularly in endemic regions should be considered before initiating immunosuppressive therapy in COVID-19 patients. Future epidemiological research should systematically evaluate individual risk factors to facilitate targeted intervention strategies.

title: Impact of COVID-19 on the Mental Health of Essential Healthcare Workers in Pakistan: Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background: Covid-19 affected whole patterns of life. Healthcare workers (HWs) are the one who faced the pandemic primarily and most severely. There is a need to understand the effects of covid-19 on mental health of HWs. Objective: To measure the burden of Post-traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) or psychological symptoms resulting from the Covid-19 pandemic among the healthcare workers. Methodology: The study design was an ongoing cross sectional study conducted at Private Sector Medical University in Karachi (as part of a longitudinal cohort study), taking a universal sampling (All HWs) strategy after seeking Institutional approval. Data gathered through trained data collectors using Validated mental health scales i-e; Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), General Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Impact of Event Scale – Revised (IES-R), Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale (CD-RISC) & Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) besides demographic variables. Written consent was taken. Data analyzed through SPSS. Results: Female gender predominated (57.52%), 55.74% were of very younger age (20-30 years), 52.41% were married while 45.74% were single. High level of depression among 30.57% (n = 431), high anxiety among 35.25% (n = 497); Top quartile of stress scores among 29.08% (n = 410) were noted. Among all participants, 60.28% (n = 850) had experienced a stressful or traumatic event related to covid-19 and 371 (26.31%) were above the cut-off for high PTSD symptoms. Conclusion: HWs suffered mental health issues during pandemic situation with a common occurrence of anxiety, stress, depression and PTSD. Female gender, doctor, nurse and those living alone are affected more.

title: Divergent trends in attempted suicide and suicide deaths after the COVID-19 shock in Macao SAR, China: an interrupted time-series analysis
abstract: The impact of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic on suicidal behavior has diverged between fatal and non-fatal outcomes, yet parallel dual-outcome observation within a single population and long-window evidence are limited. Macao SAR, China—a micro-economy dependent on gaming—experienced the closure of casinos, cross-border travel restrictions, and a sharp decline in gross gaming revenue (GGR) in February 2020, an a priori composite breakpoint. Its police-recorded monthly suicide data have been published by age group and sex since 2015. We examined changes in attempted suicide and suicide death around this breakpoint and their coupling with income fluctuations. Using monthly counts (January 2015–June 2025; 126 months) verified cell-by-cell against official data, we estimated breakpoint associations with an interrupted time-series analysis (segmented Poisson regression) and calculated net excess under dual counterfactuals (trend extrapolation; pre-pandemic seasonal level). Fourteen subgroup models underwent Benjamini–Hochberg correction; age heterogeneity was tested with an age-by-breakpoint interaction model; and coupling with GGR fluctuations was examined using distributed-lag models and cross-correlation functions. Attempted suicide rose immediately after the breakpoint [level rate ratio (RR) 1.47, q = 0.022], with a period-mean RR of 1.93 (95% CI 1.25–3.07) and net excess of approximately 556 cases (95% CI 240–784), persisting 5.4 years without decline. The increase concentrated among people under 25 (level RR 2.31 for ages 15–24, q = 0.003; joint age-interaction χ 2 = 78.0, 6 df, p < 0.00001). Suicide death showed no corresponding increase (level RR 0.80, q = 0.176; net excess CI crossing zero); those aged 65 + showed a marginal increase concentrated in the early pandemic period (RR = 1.81, q = 0.021), sensitive to the covariance specification and partly reflecting pre-existing drift. The rise did not track monthly GGR fluctuations, a level-shift pattern that cannot exclude effects of the structural income decline collinear with the breakpoint. After the COVID-19 shock, Macao experienced a sustained non-fatal suicide crisis while suicide death showed no detectable net increase, with young people bearing most of the increase. Expanding youth mental health services and maintaining high-frequency, stratified surveillance are public health priorities.

title: Impact of COVID-19 on the Emotional and Cognitive Processes of Young Children: An Integrative Review
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly affected young children, particularly those attending kindergarten, a stage characterized by rapid emotional and cognitive development. This article analyzes the impact of COVID-19 on the emotional and cognitive processes of young children, emphasizing the effects of prolonged confinement, reduced social interaction, and changes in early educational environments. Evidence shows that disruptions in daily routines and limited peer interaction negatively influenced emotional regulation, social skills, motivation, attention, language development, and learning readiness. Young children were especially vulnerable due to their dependence on stable environments and consistent emotional support. Additionally, family dynamics and the availability of supportive educational contexts played a crucial role in mitigating negative effects. The findings highlight the importance of strengthening emotional support strategies, early childhood education practices, and family–school collaboration to promote healthy emotional and cognitive development in kindergarten-aged children in post-pandemic contexts.

title: Representaciones sociales de los padres sobre Aprende en Casa en primaria durante el COVID-19 Parents’ Social Representations of Aprende en Casa in Primary Education During COVID-19
abstract: The research sought to analyze the social representations of parents about the educational strategy Aprende en Casa, implemented during COVID-19 in Mexico, to understand their perceptions, experiences and challenges in accompanying their children’s learning in primary education. The study had a quantitative approach, with descriptive scope. Stratified random sampling was applied, with a sample of 497 parents, with children enrolled in public and private primary schools, from Xalapa. The data collection technique was the survey and the questionnaire instrument. The results showed tensions between the goals of Learn at Home and the circumstances of families, which had an impact on students' learning experiences. It is concluded that the social representations of parents shaped differentiated school practices and suggest the need for relevant educational strategies, to ensure greater equity and effectiveness in future educational initiatives.

title: MEASURING SHADOW BANKING ACTIVITIES IN INDONESIA DURING COVID 19 PANDEMIC
abstract: This study defines and measures shadow banking activities in Indonesia—locally categorized as Non-Bank Financial Institutions (NBFIs) or Industri Keuangan Non-Bank (IKNB)—during the COVID-19 pandemic (2018–2020). Although shadow banking assets account for only 0.25% of Indonesia's national GDP, the sector's rapid growth and lack of uniform regulation pose significant systemic and social risks. Utilizing the Financial Stability Board (FSB) framework and descriptive statistical methods, this research analyzes secondary data from national financial authorities to map macro-level assets and sector-specific interconnections. The macro-mapping reveals that insurance institutions dominate the sector with 55% of total shadow banking assets, followed by pension funds and various financing entities. Notably, while traditional financing institutions faced asset declines during the 2020 pandemic crisis, Fintech peer-to-peer lending and microfinance demonstrated remarkable resilience and growth. Additionally, risk-focused analysis indicates that pension funds exhibit higher systemic risk profiles than insurance funds due to their heavier reliance on capital and money market instruments. The study concludes by recommending the implementation of a robust regulatory framework, similar to China's phased approach, to license, monitor, and mitigate risks associated with Fintech and broader shadow banking activities in the post-pandemic era.Keywords: COVID-19 pandemic, Financial Stability Board, Fintech, Non-Bank Financial Institutions, Shadow Banking

title: Lecciones de las pandemias de influenza y de COVID-19 para la odontología: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar las lecciones de los brotes históricos de influenza y de la pandemia de COVID-19 aplicables a la atención odontológica. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones sistemáticas y narrativas, ensayos clínicos y documentos de análisis histórico. Resultados: la pandemia de 1918 mostró el valor de proteger al personal sanitario y la de 2009, el de los diagnósticos moleculares y del uso planificado de los antivirales. En odontología, la COVID-19 obligó a controlar los aerosoles, reforzar la bioseguridad, priorizar la atención urgente, evaluar colutorios antisépticos y atender el agotamiento profesional. Conclusión: la preparación odontológica exige protocolos permanentes de bioseguridad y planes de continuidad asistencial.

title: Diagnoosista immuniteettiin: COVID-19:n diagnostisen testin herkkyys ja vasta-ainevälitteisen immuunivasteen dynamiikka
abstract: COVID-19 is a viral disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which erupted in a pandemic between 2020-2023 and is still circulating in the population. At the beginning of the pandemic, there was a lack of reliable knowledge on the course of the disease, its diagnostics, and its possible long-term consequences. As lymphopenia is a common manifestation in COVID-19, there was speculation that it could cause transient or permanent immune dysregulation. This thesis aims to provide information on the reliability of the main diagnostic test for COVID-19 and on the state of the humoral immune system during and after COVID-19. COVID-19 is most often diagnosed through a nucleic acid amplification test called RT-PCR. We collected a cohort of 3008 patients tested for SARS-CoV-2 in Helsinki, Finland using the RT-PCR test during spring 2020 and estimated the clinical sensitivity of the test in inpatients and outpatients using two different approaches. We found the sensitivity to be between 85.7% and 67.5% in inpatients and between 95.5% and 34.9% in outpatients, with the real-life sensitivity likely falling between these figures. Based on these results, we recommend that patients with high clinical suspicion of COVID-19 be retested if their initial RT-PCR test is negative. To assess the condition of the humoral immune system in COVID-19 patients, we took blood samples from a cohort of 120 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients during and after the disease, with a follow-up of up to a year post-infection. We analyzed the proportions of circulating B cell and follicular T cell subpopulations, the concentrations of total IgG and SARS-CoV-2 and EBV specific antibodies, the concentrations of unrelated toxoid vaccine antibodies (tetanus, pertussis, and diphtheria), the concentration of free light chains, and the presence of herpesvirus DNA. Based on these analyses, we determined that during acute COVID-19, the humoral immune system undergoes several transient changes, including leukocytosis and lymphopenia; increased proportions of circulating plasmablasts, plasma cells, and transitional B cells; decreased proportions of class switched memory cells and T follicular helper cells; and increased free light chains in blood. Additionally, in inpatients, we saw decreased total IgG in blood and common EBV (47%) and HHV-6B (19%) reactivation. All the previously mentioned changes resolved in follow-up. The unrelated vaccine antibodies stayed stable throughout the follow-up period, reassuring concerns of immune amnesia (a loss of previously gained immune memory). Taken together, these results paint a picture of a normal, transient response to viral infection with stronger responses in hospitalized patients, including opportunistic herpesvirus reactivation.

source_records.title: Diagnoosista immuniteettiin: COVID-19:n diagnostisen testin herkkyys ja vasta-ainevälitteisen immuunivasteen dynamiikka
source_records.abstract: COVID-19 is a viral disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which erupted in a pandemic between 2020-2023 and is still circulating in the population. At the beginning of the pandemic, there was a lack of reliable knowledge on the course of the disease, its diagnostics, and its possible long-term consequences. As lymphopenia is a common manifestation in COVID-19, there was speculation that it could cause transient or permanent immune dysregulation. This thesis aims to provide information on the reliability of the main diagnostic test for COVID-19 and on the state of the humoral immune system during and after COVID-19. COVID-19 is most often diagnosed through a nucleic acid amplification test called RT-PCR. We collected a cohort of 3008 patients tested for SARS-CoV-2 in Helsinki, Finland using the RT-PCR test during spring 2020 and estimated the clinical sensitivity of the test in inpatients and outpatients using two different approaches. We found the sensitivity to be between 85.7% and 67.5% in inpatients and between 95.5% and 34.9% in outpatients, with the real-life sensitivity likely falling between these figures. Based on these results, we recommend that patients with high clinical suspicion of COVID-19 be retested if their initial RT-PCR test is negative. To assess the condition of the humoral immune system in COVID-19 patients, we took blood samples from a cohort of 120 SARS-CoV-2 positive patients during and after the disease, with a follow-up of up to a year post-infection. We analyzed the proportions of circulating B cell and follicular T cell subpopulations, the concentrations of total IgG and SARS-CoV-2 and EBV specific antibodies, the concentrations of unrelated toxoid vaccine antibodies (tetanus, pertussis, and diphtheria), the concentration of free light chains, and the presence of herpesvirus DNA. Based on these analyses, we determined that during acute COVID-19, the humoral immune system undergoes several transient changes, including leukocytosis and lymphopenia; increased proportions of circulating plasmablasts, plasma cells, and transitional B cells; decreased proportions of class switched memory cells and T follicular helper cells; and increased free light chains in blood. Additionally, in inpatients, we saw decreased total IgG in blood and common EBV (47%) and HHV-6B (19%) reactivation. All the previously mentioned changes resolved in follow-up. The unrelated vaccine antibodies stayed stable throughout the follow-up period, reassuring concerns of immune amnesia (a loss of previously gained immune memory). Taken together, these results paint a picture of a normal, transient response to viral infection with stronger responses in hospitalized patients, including opportunistic herpesvirus reactivation.

title: The somatic symptom burden of patients with medically unexplained oral symptoms across the COVID-19 pandemic: a retrospective cross-sectional study
abstract: To determine whether COVID-19 pandemic periods were associated with the general somatic symptom burden of patients with medically unexplained oral symptoms (MUOS) and to identify patient-level and diagnostic correlates. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 3,542 adults presenting for initial consultation at a psychosomatic dentistry clinic from April 2017 through September 2025. Somatic burden was assessed using the Somatic Symptom Scale-8 (SSS-8), and depressive symptoms using the Zung Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS). World Health Organization declarations defined three periods: before the pandemic, during the pandemic, and after the end of the Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC). Group differences and adjusted associations with SSS-8 scores were examined using analysis of variance, multiplicity-adjusted pairwise tests, and multivariable linear regression with categorical period indicators, without and with SDS adjustment. The mean SSS-8 scores were 9.04 (95% CI, 8.73–9.35) in the pre-pandemic period, 9.45 (9.11–9.79) during the pandemic, and 9.63 (9.23–10.04) in the post-PHEIC period. The overall ANOVA was statistically significant ( p = 0.047), but no pairwise comparison remained significant after false-discovery-rate correction. Without SDS adjustment, post-PHEIC scores were higher than pre-pandemic scores (b = 0.66; 95% CI, 0.17–1.15; p = 0.009; joint period p = 0.028). Period estimates were smaller after adding SDS (joint period p = 0.450). In this model, SDS was the strongest correlate (standardized β = 0.542, p < 0.001); psychiatric history, burning mouth syndrome, persistent idiopathic facial pain, and longer illness duration were associated with higher burden, whereas oral cenesthopathy was associated with lower burden. The adjusted R2 was 0.329. In this sample of patients with MUOS, observed differences in somatic symptom burden across calendar-period samples were small and depended on SDS adjustment. These comparisons cannot establish causal pandemic effects, absence of such effects, or mediation by depressive symptoms. Longitudinal studies incorporating individual pandemic-related exposures are needed.

title: Adolescents’ COVID-19 history is associated with their cognitive performance
abstract: Research has shown that SARS-CoV-2 infection can impact cognition in adulthood. Less is known about its cognitive impact in adolescence, a critical neurodevelopmental period. Based on data from N = 3,860 adolescents in Lower Austria ( M age = 13.5 years), we used multivariate regression and machine learning analyses to examine how self-reported COVID-19 history (infection occurrence, symptom severity) was related to performance on cognitive and (psycho)motor performance tests. While infection occurrence was not linked to performance, more severe COVID-19 symptom courses were significantly associated with lower logical reasoning and numerical ability without significant gender differences, as well as lower verbal ability specifically among girls. The machine learning models corroborated the regression findings for reasoning and verbal ability and additionally identified fine finger dexterity and long-term memory as showing non-linear associations with symptom severity relative to their linear regression coefficients. The observed effect sizes are practically meaningful, corresponding to an estimated 3- to 7-point performance deficit on standardized cognitive scales for the least and most severe symptom courses. Our findings indicate that adolescents’ COVID-19 history is associated with their cognitive performance. The results underline the need to investigate whether and how COVID-19 affects adolescents’ neurocognitive development, which may be specific for gender.

title: Machine learning and molecular validation reveal the PI3K/AKT/mTOR inflammatory axis for therapeutic targeting in severe COVID-19
abstract: Dysregulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling axis contributes to COVID-19 severity by amplifying hyperinflammatory responses. This pilot study integrates molecular biology and explainable machine learning to characterize this pathway, emphasizing its negative regulator PTEN , in stratifying disease severity. RT-qPCR gene expression profiles from 83 laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 patients were merged with clinical data of lung involvement in three severity classes (mild: n = 40, moderate: n = 24, severe: n = 19). Molecular analysis revealed significant upregulation of IL-6 , PI3K , mTOR , and AKT1 in severe and fatal cases, alongside progressive downregulation of PTEN ( P < 0.001) and Cyclin D1 , suggesting impaired pathway inhibition and disrupted cell-cycle regulation. MMP-2 levels correlated with lung involvement. Eight machine learning classifiers were evaluated using Stratified 5-Fold Cross-Validation for multiclass severity stratification. Crucially, SHAP-based explainable AI independently validated the molecular findings by identifying PI3K (mean |SHAP| = 0.0984) as the most discriminative feature, followed by AKT1 (0.0838), IL-6 (0.0537), Cyclin D1 (0.0327), and PTEN (0.0287), confirming the canonical PI3K → Akt → mTOR signaling hierarchy. These findings demonstrate that integrating explainable AI with molecular validation can identify biologically coherent prognostic biomarkers, offering a transparent, hypothesis-generating framework for future targeted immunomodulatory research in severe SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: COVID-19 as a Compound Hazard: Emergency Managers Experiences in Compound Disaster Management
abstract: The health impacts of the coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19) have been widely documented; however, less is known about the impacts of the COVID-19 response on emergency managers who were part of the COVID-19 response while continuing with their everyday disaster job, too. Interviews were conducted in late 2021 with state emergency management planners from 21 states to discuss their experience handling COVID-19 and other disasters concurrently. The 158 disasters declared during the COVID-19 pandemic give us a unique view of compound hazard events that include a long-duration hazard with a large geographic footprint. Experiences from emergency managers serving during COVID-19 were able to shine a light on activities and policies that helped and hindered their efforts to serve their communities most effectively. Common issues encountered were related to coordination, lack of training in roles, a need for more resources in rural areas, more planning for long duration events, and mental health resources.

title: Trends in myocarditis hospitalisations among children in the United States and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic: a kids’ inpatient database analysis
abstract: Population-based estimates of myocarditis hospitalisation rates in children in the post-COVID era are lacking. Our study objective was to evaluate paediatric myocarditis rates, outcomes, and complications over the last 15 years, including the post-pandemic period in United States. We analysed the 2009–2022 Kids Inpatient Database data and used a weighted sample to estimate national hospitalisation rates. We included children <18 years with diagnoses of myocarditis using Health Care Cost and Utilization Project codes. Weighted national myocarditis hospitalisations for the respective years were 716 (2009), 747 (2012), 833 (2016), 846 (2019), and 1416 (2022), which corresponded to an incidence per 100,000 children of 0.96, 1.01, 1.13, 1.16, and 1.93, respectively. The incidence in 2022 after excluding COVID-19-related admissions was 1.3/100,000 ( n = 951). Myocarditis showed a bimodal distribution with age categories of 0–4 and 15–17, comprising of 66% hospitalisations. Mortality rate was 7.4% (335/4558) with a significant decreasing trend over the years (10.2% in 2009 and 5.9% in 2022). Length of stay also decreased from a median of 8 days in 2009 to 6 days in 2022. Arrhythmia was the most common complication (18.6%). Extra-corporeal membrane oxygenation was utilised in 9.2% and ventricular assist device in 3%, with a decreasing trend from 2009 to 2022. Overall hospitalisation rates for myocarditis have increased over the last 15 years, with a significant increase in the post-pandemic era. There has been improvement in the mortality rate and a decrease in length of stay. Almost 1/3 of 2022 admissions were related to COVID-19.

title: Perceived effects of COVID-19 on health systems in Malawi: a qualitative stud​y
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted essential public health services, raising concerns about the risks associated with interruptions to these services. How these disruptions were perceived remains understudied, particularly in Malawi. This study aimed to understand key health stakeholders’ perceptions of COVID-19’s effects on Malawi’s health systems. This qualitative descriptive study was conducted in Lilongwe, Malawi, from 11 April to 11 May 2023. We purposively selected 15 technical personnel representing 13 essential Ministry of Health programs. Key informant interviews were conducted using a semi-structured guide and audio-recorded. The recordings were transcribed verbatim, cleaned, and analysed thematically using NVivo version 13. During the pandemic, routine health services, immunisations, and chronic disease management were disrupted as health facilities redirected resources to COVID-19 response efforts, reducing the availability of other essential services. Myths and fears about drug shortages led COVID-19 patients to delay seeking medical care. Health workers faced stigma and burnout from increased workloads, alongside severe shortages of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and medical supplies. Positively, COVID-19 also spurred innovations in screening, including the use of mobile diagnostic units. The COVID-19 pandemic has had a profound impact on Malawi’s health systems, exposing both vulnerabilities and strengths. Despite significant challenges, the health system showed resilience and adaptability. This study underscores the importance of investing in stronger health systems and preparedness to better manage future health crises

title: The effect of place of residence and social capital on depression prevalence in Poland before and after the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Introduction and Objective. The aim of the study is to verify changes in the association between place of residence and depression prevalence before and after the onset of COVID-19 pandemic, and to identify indicators of social capital as determinants of the prevalence of depression among people aged 50 years or older living in rural and urban areas in Poland. Materials and Method. The study used pooled data from two cross-sectional studies conducted in Poland: the COURAGE in Europe (2011–2012) and COURAGE-CAD (2024) including 2917 and 1802 participants, respectively, who were randomly selected from the general population aged 50 or older. Both studies applied the same methodology. The structured questionnaire included, among others, a scale measuring social network (COURAGE-SNI), social support (OSLO-3 SSS), formal and informal participation as well as social trust. It also incorporated an assessment of depression prevalence based on the DSM-IV algorithm for Major Depressive Disorder. The results showed that before the pandemic, there were no significant differences in depression prevalence between urban and rural areas. However, after the pandemic, urban residents had higher odds of experiencing depression than rural residents. Social networks emerged as one of the most consistent protective factors, particularly among urban residents, while other dimensions of social capital showed heterogeneous associations across time and place of residence. Trust was found as an important factor in protecting rural residents from depression. The findings underscore the necessity to incorporate social capital into the design of public health strategies or interventions targeting the mental well-being of older adults, who are especially vulnerable to the negative effects of the disease.

title: Telehealth for Older People During the COVID-19 Pandemic in Latin America and the Caribbean: A Cross-Sectional Study of Healthcare Providers’ Experiences and Implications for Disaster Preparedness
abstract: Pandemics are considered a type of disaster, sharing the common characteristic of abruptly disrupting in-person healthcare delivery and generating public health emergencies worldwide. However, the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the implementation of telehealth globally, across various groups, and within them, among older people, providing a wide range of implementation experiences that may be extrapolated to other disaster contexts. Background/Objectives: This paper describes the implementation of telehealth for older people during the COVID-19 pandemic in Latin America and the Caribbean from the perspective of healthcare providers. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted using non-probability sampling. Physicians and other healthcare professionals were included and completed a self-administered online questionnaire comprising 35 questions grouped into five sections. The questionnaire underwent content validity assessment (CVR ≥ 0.37; overall CVI = 0.80). Results: A total of 268 healthcare providers implemented telehealth for older people; the majority were women (69.0%), with a mean age of 44.2 years. The main country where telehealth was implemented was Chile (16.0%); the profession was geriatricians (19.0%); and the most frequently reported age group of older people was 70–79 years (identified by 77.6% of healthcare providers). Functional status showed mild dependence in 71.6%; cognitive status was normal in 82.8%; and mild cognitive impairment in 71.3%. The education level was primary education in 75.4%; the main type of center was private (29.5%); and the level of service was prevention (55.6%). The synchronous platform used was WhatsApp video calls (70.7%); the asynchronous platform was WhatsApp for sending materials (86.6%). The main facilitators were having help from family or caregivers (91.4%), while barriers were not having help from other people to perform telehealth (82.8%). The perceived positive effect was that it improves mood (affective sphere) for 67.2%. Conclusions: These findings provide insights into healthcare providers’ experiences with telehealth during the COVID-19 pandemic and may inform the planning and implementation of telehealth services in future emergencies and disasters.

title: Supply Chain Resilience Among Firms Operating in Lithuania: Adaptation to the COVID-19 Pandemic and the Russia–Ukraine War
abstract: This study examines how firms operating in Lithuania adapted their supply chains to two consecutive disruptions: the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent Russia–Ukraine war with its associated European Union sanctions. The study adopts a retrospective, qualitative cross-case interview design, drawing on semi-structured interviews conducted in 2026 with supply chain, logistics, procurement, and operations professionals in six firms spanning maritime logistics, e-grocery, customs brokerage, agri-trade, manufacturing, and construction. The data were analysed thematically and interpreted through the combined lens of dynamic capabilities and supply chain resilience. Across these cases, firm size appeared to operate as a double-edged capability, conferring agility on smaller firms while restricting their access to institutional support. In the cases examined, logistics and service firms were unable to access war-relief and digitalisation funding, and in the case of digitalisation support the barrier is traceable to an eligibility rule that conditions funding on revenue from the applicant’s own manufactured output, a condition service firms cannot meet by construction. title: Changes in Rectal Swab Surveillance Activity and Multidrug-Resistant Organism Colonisation Positivity Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic in a Tertiary-Care Hospital
abstract: Background/Objectives: The COVID-19 pandemic may have disrupted hospital surveillance for multidrug-resistant organism (MDRO) colonisation. We assessed changes in rectal swab screening density and MDRO positivity in a tertiary-care hospital. Methods: We conducted a retrospective interrupted time-series study of adult hospital admissions and surveillance rectal swab requests in Barcelona, Spain, from January 2018 to December 2021, with March 2020 as the interruption point. Screening density was assessed using all eligible requests per 1000 patient-days, whereas positivity was analysed using patient-level deduplicated requests. Segmented regression models estimated immediate changes and changes in monthly trends. Results: Among 101,655 adult hospitalisation episodes, 19,931 requests were eligible for the screening-density analysis. The positivity analysis included 16,863 deduplicated requests, of which 3007 were positive. Although observed screening density increased from 20.02 to 28.29 requests per 1000 patient-days between periods, its estimated level at pandemic onset was lower than projected from the pre-pandemic trend (rate ratio [RR] 0.756, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.595–0.961). This model-relative change was greater among patients aged ≥65 years than among those aged 18–64 years (ratio of RRs 0.721, 95% CI 0.583–0.890). MDRO positivity decreased (RR 0.512, 95% CI 0.412–0.637), followed by an upward change in the monthly trend (slope-change RR 1.026, 95% CI 1.010–1.042). Conclusions: Pandemic onset was associated with screening density below the level projected from the pre-pandemic trend and with reduced detected MDRO positivity. Changes in screening activity and patient selection may have influenced observed positivity, highlighting the importance of maintaining surveillance coverage during healthcare disruptions.

title: Long Covid: from viral persistence to invisible disability — A critical review of the 4th International Conference in Nice 2026
abstract: La 4e Conférence internationale sur le Covid long, tenue à Nice les 12 et 13 novembre 2026, a réuni 176 communications scientifiques, dont 32 présentations orales et 144 posters. Cette revue critique examine les principaux apports du congrès selon cinq dimensions : sciences biologiques, sciences cliniques, épistémologie, éthique et partenariat avec les patients. Les travaux présentés renforcent les hypothèses de persistance virale, de dysrégulation immunitaire, d'altérations neurovasculaires et de dysfonctionnement métabolique. Les avancées en multiomique et en neuroimagerie contrastent toutefois avec l'absence de biomarqueurs diagnostiques individuels validés et de traitements curatifs démontrés. Les recherches cliniques soulignent l'hétérogénéité des trajectoires, le malaise post-effort et l'importance du handicap fonctionnel, encore insuffisamment reconnu. Les contributions des patients et les nouvelles méthodes de phénotypage ouvrent des perspectives pour une recherche mieux ancrée dans l'expérience de la maladie. Le congrès témoigne ainsi d'un progrès scientifique considérable, mais aussi d'un décalage persistant entre production des connaissances, reconnaissance de la maladie et organisation des soins.

title: FORMATIVE PROCESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS IN NURSING IN THE CONTEXT OF COVID-19
abstract: Objective: to report the experience of remote teaching in an academic master’s degree course during the covid-19 pandemic. Methods: this is a descriptive study, experience report type, experienced from October to December 2020 in a mandatory subject of the Postgraduate Program in Nursing of a Public University in the state of Pará. Results: The educational activities took place synchronously and asynchronous, from virtual classes and texts for reading, all of that was possible by the use of educational technological strategies in the experienced pandemic scenario. Remote teaching required students and teachers to adapt to the new classroom routine in their homes, adapting the study environment and appropriate equipment for this context. Even with the challenges faced, the establishment of the remote learning process added skills among those involved, improvement of tools and digital transformation of the conventional classroom. Conclusion: remote teaching was efficient and provided opportunities for pedagogical mediations, promoting collaborative learning among students. It also revealed the need for training for those involved in the process.
authors: Marília de Fátima Vieira de Oliveira

title: Trajectories of self-reported dyspnoea, physical fatigue, and cognitive symptoms after hospitalization for COVID-19 - a nationwide registry study from Norway
abstract: The purpose of this study is to assess trajectories and prognostic factors for self-reported symptoms consistent with long COVID at 3 and 12 months after hospitalization for COVID-19. In a prospective, nationwide registry study in Norwegian patients hospitalized for COVID-19 from March to December 2020, we analysed patient-reported outcomes using the modified Medical Research Council dyspnoea scale (mMRC) and the 11-item Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (CFQ) completed online by participants three ( n = 657) and twelve months ( n = 647) after hospital discharge. We used generalized estimating equations to assess trajectories of, and prognostic factors for self-reported dyspnoea, fatigue, and specific cognitive symptoms including problems with concentration (CFQ8), verbal control (CFQ9), word retrieval (CFQ10), and memory (CFQ11). Participants’ mean age was 58.9 years (standard deviation SD 14.2), and 40.9% (275/673) were female. The prevalence of self-reported dyspnoea (mMRC ≥ 2) was 24.6% (151/615) at three and 22.0% (134/609) at twelve months, with no significant change in mMRC score (estimate −0.023, 95% confidence interval [CI] −0.099 to 0.054). Prevalence of self-reported physical fatigue (≥10 on 21-point scale of CFQ item 1–7) decreased from 62.3% (369/592) at three months to 60.4% (349/578) at twelve months (estimate −0.346, 95% CI −0.637 to −0.054, prevalence 62.3% to 60.4%). Self-reported specific cognitive symptoms, including problems with concentration (CFQ8), verbal control (CFQ9), word retrieval (CFQ10), and memory (CFQ11), assessed as a combined score of ≥ 6 on 12-point scale of CFQ items 8–11, increased significantly from 35.2% (211/599) to 46.6% (247/578, estimate 0.856, CI 0.663 to 1.050). Prognostic factors for self-reported dyspnoea were smoking (estimate 0.57, 95% 0.12 to 1.03), asthma/lung disease (estimate 0.34, 95% CI 0.18 to 0.50), neurological disease (estimate 0.56, 95% CI 0.01 to 1.10), liver disease (estimate 0.93, 95% CI 0.00 to 1.87), and prolonged hospital stay (estimate 0.02, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.03). Prognostic factors for self-reported physical fatigue were immunodeficiency (estimate 1.80, 95% CI 0.30 to 3.30), liver disease (estimate 4.08, 95% CI 2.68 to 5.49) and prolonged hospital stay (estimate 0.05, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.08). Smoking (estimate 1.00, 95% CI 0.00 to 1.99) was a prognostic factor for self-reported cognitive symptoms. Older age was associated with lower risk of self-reported physical fatigue (estimate −0.05, 95% CI −0.08 to −0.02) and cognitive symptoms (estimate −0.03, 95% CI −0.04 to −0.01). While self-reported physical fatigue improves, it is worrying that self-reported problems with concentration and memory significantly worsen from three to twelve months.

title: Tromboembolia Pulmonar y Covid 19
abstract: El coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, afecta preferentemente al tracto respiratorio debido a inflamación excesiva, activación plaquetaria, disfunción endotelial y estasis, así como un aumento de pacientes con predisposición a padecer complicaciones trombóticas venosas y arteriales. Los estudios demuestran que los pacientes graves con COVID-19, tienen una prevalencia aumentada de tromboembolismo pulmonar (26%) y la mayoría (78,7%) presenta una extensión moderada o grave de afectación pulmonar, por lo tanto, el TEP emerge como la complicación grave más frecuente, dando lugar al incremento de la morbimortalidad por Covid-19.Objetivo: Realizar una revisión teórica descriptiva de tipo documental sobre el Tromboembolismo Pulmonar y Covid-19.Material y métodos: Una investigación descriptiva de tipo documental, inicia con búsqueda, organización y análisis de artículos sobre Tromboembolismo Pulmonar y Covid-19. Se efectuó en publicaciones encontradas en bases de datos de PubMed, MedLine y revistas médicas NEJM, JAMA, LANCET, Science, Oxford, Wiley, MedRxiv, desde 2015 hasta 2021. Se rastreó con palabras clave que se combinaron para ampliar los criterios de búsqueda, de estos se revisaron 60 artículos y seleccionaron 26.Resultados: La infección por covid-19 genera respuesta inflamatoria sistémica y daño endotelial que activarían la coagulación y aumento de trombina y disminución de los anticoagulantes del organismo, activación plaquetaria, disfunción endotelial y estasis, incidiendo en la aparición del tromboembolismo pulmonar (TEP) como la complicación Conclusión: La infección por Covid-19(SARS-CoV-2) produce una respuesta inflamatoria sistémica y daño endotelial que genera un estado de hipercoagulabilidad predisponiendo a fenómenos trombóticos de localización venosa y arterial, siendo el Tromboembolismo Pulmonar la complicación más frecuente en estos pacientes.

title: Food Security, Migration and the COVID-19 Pandemic: An Introduction
abstract: The introductory chapter outlines the context and rationale for the book. It examines how the COVID-19 pandemic led to profound food security and socioeconomic challenges for migrants and refugees while exacerbating longstanding structural inequalities. These groups were often disproportionately affected by the pandemic and excluded from, or marginalised within, relief measures. The chapter articulates the book’s overarching goal and introduces five key themes addressed across the chapters, including the ways in which the pandemic reconfigured the migration-food security nexus, the food security implications of COVID-19 policy responses, the compounded vulnerabilities of marginalised migrant groups in the informal sector, gendered differences in these impacts and vulnerabilities, and policy lessons for strengthening food security and health in future crises. For each theme, we begin with a brief review of the existing scholarship and then introduce the chapters that engage with it through their empirical analyses. The chapter concludes by outlining the book’s structure and highlighting its relevance for researchers, policymakers, and practitioners working at the intersection of migration and food security.

title: Unshattered subject: traumatic memory and scriptotherapy in Remi Raji’s COVID-19 poetry
abstract: In the years following 2019, the COVID-19 pandemic reached its peak, becoming the very epitome of chaos. While medical personnel strove to contain the crisis, writers sought to make sense of the catastrophe. Critically re-engaging dominant trauma theorists’ presentation of trauma as unrepresentable, belated, and unspeakable, I draw insights from Richard McNally, Joshua Pederson and Suzette Henke, to argue that scriptotherapy offers traumatised individuals the opportunity to narrativise their experience of illness, thereby restoring meaning, coherence, and a sense of agency in the aftermath of a traumatic disruption, as evidenced by Remi Raji’s COVID-19 poetry. Closely read as a survivor’s ‘narrative’, the fifteen poems in ‘Corona Cantos and Monologues’, a section in Wanderer Cantos, depict the poetic persona’s experiences of infection, hospitalisation, and recovery and offer a therapeutic memorialization of the pandemic. For Raji, trauma is neither unclaimed nor unspeakable; rather, it can be recalled and meaningfully represented through language. Each poem presents not a textual lacuna, but a recreation of the sights and scenes in the isolation centre. Each poem invites the reader to bear witness to the persona’s experiences, giving those experiences an audience through the scriptotherapeutic act of narration. Raji’s work contributes to COVID-19 literary discourse and advances a postcolonial rethinking of trauma as both representable and therapeutically negotiable.

title: ICT, the Real Exchange Rate and Structural Change: Testing for Dutch Disease Effects in Developing Countries in the Post-Covid-19 Era
abstract: Purpose: This paper examined whether the rapid expansion of information and communication technology (ICT) generates Dutch disease effects in developing countries. Methodology: Using an annual panel of 37 low- and middle-income economies covering 2005-2021, the study tested the two channels of the Corden-Neary framework. The spending effect was assessed by estimating the effect of ICT on the real effective exchange rate, and the resource movement effect by estimating the effect of ICT on agricultural, manufacturing and services value added. Estimation moved from fixed effects with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors to system GMM to address endogeneity and persistence and allowed the effects to change after the Covid-19 pandemic through an ICT-Covid interaction. Findings: The results did not support a spending effect: ICT was not associated with real appreciation, and the negative coefficient implied a depreciation of about 2.0 per cent for a 10-percentage point rise in internet use, which was significant only with Driscoll-Kraay standard errors. Higher ICT use was associated with a lower manufacturing share of GDP, but this association was not robust in the dynamic specification and did not operate through the exchange rate. No clear effect was found for agriculture or services, and the effects did not strengthen after 2020. Unique Contribution to Theory, Practice and Policy: The findings suggest that policymakers need not adjust exchange rate policy in response to digital expansion but should support manufacturing competitiveness directly and monitor sectoral structure as digital adoption deepens.

title: Features of interleukin levels-1 and -6 in patients with obstructive sleep apnea and metabolic syndrome after COVID-19
abstract: When assessing the relationship between obstructive sleep apnea syndrome (OSA) and metabolic syndrome (MS) in patients with arterial hypertension (AH), it becomes clear that they demonstrate a mutual causal relationship with each other and that inflammation, including after COVID-19, affects this bidirectional interaction of organs and leads to subsequent organ damage. The aim of the study was to evaluate the levels of interleukins -1 and -6 in patients with obstructive sleep apnea and metabolic syndrome with arterial hypertension who had suffered from COVID-19. Materials and methods: 92 male patients were examined. The age of the subjects ranged from 30 to 75 years. Depending on the presence or absence of a history of coronavirus infection, patients were divided into 2 groups: the number of subjects in group 1 (n= 51), in the second group (n=41). All patients with grade 1-3 hypertension, with the achieved target blood pressure level. The age of the subjects was 30-75 years. All patients underwent: collection of complaints and anamnesis, assessment of body mass index (BMI); determination of the lipid spectrum, blood glucose, glomerular filtration rate. The ELISA method determined interleukins 1, 6. Instrumental studies were carried out: cardiorespiratory monitoring. In patients of group 1 who had COVID-19, the levels of IL-1 and IL-6 were significantly higher compared to group 2 (p=0.034 and p=0.041, respectively). An intragroup analysis in group 1 revealed statistically significant correlations between BMI and episodes of apnea over 40 seconds (r=0.89; p=0.012), no statistically significant differences were obtained between BMI and IL-1 and IL-6 levels (p>0.05). An intragroup analysis in group 2 revealed a direct relationship between IAG and IL-1 levels (r=0.88; p=0.017).

title: Assessment of the Challenges of donning and Doffing in the Management of Covid 19 Patients in Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital Bauchi, Northeast Nigeria
abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic has a major impact on the capacity of health systems to continue the delivery of essential health services. While health systems around the world are being challenged by increasing demand for care of COVID-19 patients, it is critical to maintain preventive and curative services, especially for the most vulnerable populations, such as children, older persons, people living with chronic conditions, minorities and people living with disabilities. Countries need to achieve the optimal balance between fighting the COVID-19 pandemic and maintenance of essential health services. WHO have been coordinating efforts across several regions and departments to support country implementation of targeted actions to reorganize and maintain access to safe and high-quality essential health services across the life course (WHO, 2020). This research had specifically appraised on Challenges of donning and Doffing in the Management of Covid 19 Patients in Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital Bauchi, Northeast Nigeria. The methodology employed were mixed method research designed was used to collect data from ten (10) nurses at the covid 19 isolation centre ATBU Teaching hospital, who were frontline using an in-depth interview who were purposively selected and quantitative data was analyzed using descriptive data statistics while the qualitative data transcribed and analyzed using content analysis. The respondents confirms that one of the significant challenges is wrong doffing by the health workers, which was observed to be mostly improper disposal of the cloths/items at initial stage, but it was later corrected. 75% of the respondents complained that strict adherence to the step by step donning and doffing processes was not adhered to initially, but there has been a significant improvement due to enlightenment and obvious dangers noticed. As a result of these, the researchers recommended that: Training and retraining of health workers with respect to donning and doffing should be prioritized, Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) should be adequately provided, and Enlightenment to patients on the dangers of diseases spread should be given serious attention.
