title: Association of Pulmonary Function, Dyspnea, Clinical Frailty, and Cognitive Function Among Adults Evaluated After COVID-19: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Background and Objectives: This study aimed to investigate the relationships among pulmonary function, dyspnea, clinical frailty, and cognitive performance during post-COVID follow-up and to examine their relationships within a hypothesized serial pathway. Materials and Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included 226 adults evaluated in a post-COVID follow-up program. Pulmonary function, modified Medical Research Council (mMRC) dyspnea scores, Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) scores, and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores were assessed. A path model (FEV1 → mMRC → CFS → MMSE), including an additional direct path from FEV1 to CFS and adjusted for age, sex, and BMI, was evaluated using robust maximum-likelihood (MLR) estimation. Indirect effects were assessed using 5000 bootstrap resamples. FVC- and PEF-based models were examined as sensitivity analyses. Results: The primary path analysis included 213 participants with complete data, and the hypothesized model showed acceptable fit (Yuan–Bentler χ2(2) = 5.57, p = 0.062; robust CFI = 0.990; robust RMSEA = 0.089; SRMR = 0.017). Lower FEV1 was associated with higher mMRC scores (β = −0.470), higher mMRC scores with higher CFS scores (β = 0.373), and higher CFS scores with lower MMSE scores (β = −0.538; all p < 0.001). The direct path from FEV1 to CFS was also significant (β = −0.310; p < 0.001). The serial indirect effect through mMRC and CFS was significant (β = 0.094; 95% CI: 0.043–0.149), as was the total indirect effect (β = 0.261; 95% CI: 0.124–0.411). The FVC-based sensitivity analysis showed a similar pattern, with a significant total indirect effect (β = 0.245; 95% CI: 0.118–0.387) and good model fit. Conclusions: The findings suggest that pulmonary function, dyspnea, clinical frailty, and cognitive performance are interrelated during post-COVID follow-up. These associations warrant further investigation to determine their potential clinical relevance. Given the cross-sectional design, the observed pathways should not be interpreted as evidence of causal mediation.

title: Psychosoziale Bedarfe bei Long COVID patientenzentriert behandeln
abstract: Der Begriff Long COVID beschreibt das Fortbestehen oder Neuauftreten von Symptomen im Zusammenhang mit einer SARS-CoV-2-Infektion. Diese reichen von leichten anhaltenden Beeinträchtigungen bis hin zu schwerwiegenden Symptomen in mehreren Körperbereichen und Organsystemen, und die Beschwerden führen zu relevanten Einschränkungen der Alltagsfunktion. Das vorliegende PsyLoCo-Therapiemanual („Psychosoziale Bedarfe bei Long COVID patientenzentriert behandeln“) bietet ein strukturiertes, integratives Konzept zur psychotherapeutischen Versorgung von Menschen mit Long COVID. Ziel ist es, die Betroffenen dabei zu unterstützen, einen konstruktiven Umgang mit den anhaltenden Symptomen und deren Auswirkungen auf Alltag, Beruf und soziales Leben zu finden. Das Manual kombiniert Elemente aus verschiedenen psychotherapeutischen Verfahren und ist als 12 Sitzungen umfassende Kurzzeitpsychotherapie im Einzelsetting konzipiert. Die Inhalte gliedern sich in vier aufeinander aufbauende Module: Coping und Distressmanagement, Körperbeschwerden und Schmerzen, chronische Erschöpfung und affektive Symptome sowie Sozial- und Arbeitsleben. Für jedes Modul finden sich klar strukturierte Interventionen, Arbeitsblätter und Übungen, die flexibel an die individuellen Bedürfnisse der Patientinnen und Patienten angepasst werden können. Umfangreiche Arbeitsmaterialien ergänzen das Manual und können nach erfolgter Registrierung von der Hogrefe Webseite heruntergeladen werden.

title: Teleworkability and labour market resilience during COVID-19: gender differences in South Korea
abstract: By focusing on gender differences, this study examines the impact of teleworkability on labour market outcomes amid the COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea. Using a Difference-in-Differences (DiD) framework, we ascertain that teleworkability mitigated employment shocks during the pandemic, primarily by reducing transitions into furlough or unemployment, which consequently mitigated declines in wages and working hours. Moreover, teleworkability’s protective effect was more pronounced for women, who experienced greater labour market shocks. These gender differences stem from a stronger protective effect in the social and non-essential sectors, where women are more heavily represented. In contrast to previous studies, we find no significant differences in teleworkability’s impact based on childcare responsibilities. Our findings highlight teleworkability’s role in enhancing labour market resilience and provide policy insights for pandemic preparedness and gender-sensitive labour market policies.

title: Trajectories of COVID-19 impact and associations with alcohol use in the aftermath of the pandemic: observational investigation of two German cohorts
abstract: Governmental restrictions to curb COVID-19 have been associated with heightened psychological distress, with substantial inter- and intrapersonal variation. Alcohol use as a coping strategy may increase under psychosocial stress, but its persistence over time remains unclear. This study identified trajectories of perceived COVID-19-related impact over 3 years, related them to individual characteristics, and examined differences in post-pandemic alcohol consumption. K -means-based longitudinal clustering of retrospectively recalled perceived COVID-19-related impact (January 2020–March 2023) was conducted in 188 participants from two cohorts (IMAGEN: n = 95, 60% female, age = 27.7 (SD = 0.94) years; ROLS: n = 93, 54% female, age = 52.4 (SD = 0.78) years). Analysis of covariance tested differences in drinking frequency and quantity across clusters, controlling for age and sex. Hierarchical multinomial logistic regression characterized cluster membership. Three impact-related clusters emerged across cohorts (high, moderate, low impact of COVID-19). Quantity [ F (2, 165) = 0.22, p = 0.803, η 2 part = 0.003] or frequency [ F (2, 165) = 1.02, p = 0.362, η 2 part = 0.01] of alcohol consumption did not differ significantly among the clusters. Female sex predicted higher odds of moderate-impact, while greater satisfaction with governmental measures predicted lower odds of high-impact. Distinct trajectories of perceived COVID-19 impact emerged across age-diverse cohorts. Women were more likely to experience moderate impact, whereas greater satisfaction with governmental measures was linked to lower long-term impact. Post-pandemic alcohol consumption was primarily related to demographic factors, with higher consumption among men and more frequent drinking among older individuals.

title: Intellectual capital efficiency and firm performance: A bibliometric analysis across COVID 19 periods
abstract: This study maps research relevant to intellectual capital efficiency (ICE) and firm performance using 846 Scopus-indexed journal publications from 2015 to 2025. Publication and citation analysis, author and institutional productivity rankings, and a pooled keyword co-occurrence map describe the literature. Three operational periods are distinguished: pre-COVID-19 (2015 to 2019), COVID-19 onset (2020), and post-COVID-19 (2021 to 2025), with the final label referring to a publication window rather than the end of the pandemic. The periods contain 247, 98, and 501 publications, respectively; annual output increased from 36 in 2015 to 110 in 2025. The corpus accumulated 26,877 citations at extraction. Xu Jian recorded the highest reported author output, while Qingdao Agricultural University recorded the highest reported institutional output. Intellectual capital, knowledge management, and financial performance were prominent keywords. Highly cited studies illustrate financial, innovation, and organizational performance perspectives, including research on SME hotels. These patterns identify connections between efficiency measurement and knowledge deployment, but do not establish a causal effect of COVID-19 or validate ICE as a dynamic capability. The study develops a research agenda for contextual comparisons, longitudinal analysis, and sustainability measurement while acknowledging database, citation-age and network-reproducibility limitations.

title: Relationship between marital adjustment, maternal role perception, social support, and perceived mental health among pregnant women during the COVID-19 pandemic: A cross-sectional study.
abstract: This study examined associations among marital adjustment, maternal role perception, social support, and perceived mental health in pregnant women during the COVID-19 pandemic. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 452 pregnant women at ≥ 20 weeks of gestation at a state hospital in Türkiye between November 2020 and July 2021. Data were collected using the Descriptive Information Form, the Marital Adjustment Scale (MAS), and the Myself as a Mother Scale (MMS). Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, and logistic regression analyses were performed. Overall, 70.4% of pregnant women had good marital adjustment, while 29.6% had poor marital adjustment. Marital adjustment was weakly but positively associated with maternal role perception (r = 0.28, P < .001). In the regression model examining the factors associated with marital adjustment among pregnant women, age, perceived mental health, perceived social support from the spouse and spouse's first-degree relatives, and the number of pregnancies were significantly associated with marital adjustment (Model χ2 (19) = 164.072, P < .001; Nagelkerke R2 = 0.433). Increasing age was significantly associated with higher odds of good marital adjustment (OR = 1.072, 95% CI: 1.004-1.146, P = .039). Pregnant women who perceived their mental health as moderate (OR = 0.355, P < .001) or below moderate/not good (OR = 0.314, P = .028) had lower odds of good marital adjustment than those who perceived their mental health as good. Women who perceived the support they received from their spouse as inadequate had lower odds of good marital adjustment than those who perceived it as adequate (OR = 0.289, 95% CI: 0.128-0.653, P = .003). Similarly, women who perceived the support they received from their spouse's first-degree relatives as inadequate had lower odds of good marital adjustment than those who perceived it as adequate (OR = 0.278, 95% CI: 0.162-0.478, P < .001). This study suggests that marital adjustment among pregnant women during the COVID-19 pandemic may be associated with maternal role perception, perceived social support, and mental health status. Routine antenatal assessment of marital adjustment and perceived social support may help healthcare professionals identify potential risks early.

title: Impacto de la COVID-19 en los servicios y las políticas de salud de América Latina
abstract: Objetivo: analizar el impacto de la COVID-19 en los servicios de salud pública de América Latina y las políticas adoptadas. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios. Resultados: la pandemia interrumpió los servicios esenciales de rutina, incluidas la atención materna y odontológica, y amplió vulnerabilidades previas de sistemas fragmentados y desiguales. Las respuestas incluyeron la reorganización de servicios, la telesalud, la protección de las cadenas de suministro, medidas no farmacológicas y planes de vacunación con prioridades distintas. La recuperación fue parcial. Conclusión: la pandemia evidenció la fragilidad de los sistemas de salud latinoamericanos y la necesidad de políticas que garanticen la continuidad de la atención esencial.

title: DEVELOPMENT STABILITY OF CHINESE PROVINCES BEFORE AND AFTER THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC: AN I-DISTANCE APPROACH
abstract: Regional inequality among China’s thirty-one provinces is a central concern for economic policy, yet how the COVID-19 shock reshaped their development remains unclear. This study applies the Ivanovic I-distance method to rank the provinces on nine per-capita socio-economic indicators spanning income, consumption, living standards and innovation, comparing the pre-pandemic year 2019 with the post-pandemic year 2022. The I-distance, which weights variables through their partial correlations, suits this small-sample, strongly correlated setting and yields an interpretable composite. The results reveal a pronounced stability: the development hierarchy is almost perfectly preserved across the shock, with a Spearman rank correlation of 0.95 and a Kendall coefficient of 0.85, while Ward clustering reassigns only three of the thirty-one provinces. Behind this stability lie localized asymmetries: several inland provinces rise by up to six places, while economic prosperity diverges from per-capita public provision. Disposable income and consumption dominate the ranking, with a leading contribution of 0.92, whereas educational capacity contributes least. The correlation of the 2022 ordering with independently sourced 2023 income data is 0.85. The pandemic thus perturbed but did not restructure China’s regional development order.

title: Rethinking “Learning Loss”: BIPOC Mothers’ Insights on Loss and Learning During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: The experiences and perspectives of Black Indigenous and People of Color (BIPOC) families have been largely missing from the research and policy discourse on post-pandemic schooling. Through in-depth interviews and using an intersectionality lens, we examine BIPOC mothers’ perspectives on loss and learning during the COVID-19 pandemic. Mothers identified a holistic set of concerns that center engagement in learning, support and connection, student autonomy, sustaining cultural knowledges and practices, and addressing racism. Their experiences were shaped by gender, work, class, and race. These findings illustrate the flaws of “learning loss” and productivity culture in schools and suggest an alternative vision for schooling.

title: A COVID-19 COMO FATOR DE MUDANÇA NA PERSPECTIVA DE COMPRAS ONLINE NA VIDA DO CONSUMIDOR CAPIXABA
abstract: O comércio eletrônico desempenhou um papel fundamental como canal de abastecimento emergencial durante as restrições sanitárias impostas pela pandemia da Covid-19, impulsionando transformações profundas na dinâmica do varejo. O presente estudo teve como objetivo geral analisar as mudanças no comportamento do consumidor no mercado de e-commerce após o período pandêmico, mapeando os novos hábitos de consumo, os critérios de tomada de decisão e os fatores determinantes para a construção da confiança no ambiente digital. Para tanto, realizou-se uma pesquisa descritiva de natureza quantitativa, operacionalizada por meio da aplicação de um questionário estruturado que obteve a participação de 141 respondentes residentes na região da Grande Vitória e adjacências. Os resultados revelaram uma consolidação definitiva do canal virtual na rotina dos indivíduos, evidenciada pela manutenção de uma alta frequência de compras no cenário pós-pandemia. Os principais resultados apontam que o e-commerce regional atingiu um patamar de maturidade onde a transparência operacional e os canais de feedback público constituem os principais ativos de conversão e sobrevivência estratégica para as empresas no mercado contemporâneo.

title: Estatus epiléptico refractario recurrente como posible secuela neurológica pos-COVID-19 reporte de caso
abstract: Introducción: Las secuelas neurológicas pos-COVID-19 son heterogéneas y su relación causal con epilepsia de novo continúa en investigación. El estatus epiléptico exige tratamiento inmediato y búsqueda sistemática de precipitantes reversibles. Objetivo: Describir un caso de epilepsia focal farmacorresistente con episodios recurrentes de estatus epiléptico convulsivo, temporalmente posterior a una neumonía grave compatible con COVID-19. Presentación del caso: Varón de 31 años, trabajador de salud, con antecedente de neumonía atípica grave en 2020 que requirió ventilación mecánica. En 2021 inició crisis focales con generalización bilateral. El 21 de octubre de 2025 presentó más de diez crisis tonicoclónicas sin recuperación del estado basal, por lo que fue intubado y tratado con midazolam, propofol y múltiples fármacos antiseizure. La tomografía no mostró lesión intracraneal aguda; el expediente informó una hipodensidad crónica en ganglios basales izquierdos. El electroencefalograma no documentó actividad ictal generalizada, aunque registró descargas agudas frontotemporales. Tras una evolución complicada por recurrencia convulsiva, delirium e infección respiratoria probable, fue extubado y egresó sin nuevas crisis. Presentó recurrencias en 2026 asociadas con hiponatremia, fiebre, alteraciones electrolíticas y ajustes farmacológicos. Conclusión: El cuadro es compatible con estatus epiléptico refractario recurrente sobre epilepsia focal farmacorresistente. La secuela neurológica pos-COVID-19 constituye una hipótesis clínicamente plausible por la temporalidad, pero no puede establecerse como causa definitiva sin resonancia magnética, estudio etiológico ampliado y seguimiento electroencefalográfico continuo.
authors: Luis Leonardo De la Cruz Martínez

title: Emissões veiculares de CO2 em Curitiba-PR: análise espaço-temporal e impacto da pandemia de COVID-19 em março de 2019 e 2020
abstract: Este estudo analisa a distribuição espaço-temporal das emissões veiculares de dióxido de carbono (CO2) na cidade de Curitiba (PR), com ênfase na comparação entre março de 2019 e março de 2020, período marcado pelo início das restrições de mobilidade associadas à pandemia de COVID-19. A estimativa das emissões foi realizada por meio de uma abordagem bottom-up integrada ao aprendizado de máquina. Um modelo Random Forest foi treinado com dados horários de contagem de tráfego provenientes de 201 estações de monitoramento, combinados a atributos da infraestrutura viária extraídos do OpenStreetMap, permitindo estimar o fluxo e a velocidade média em segmentos não monitorados. As emissões foram calculadas com base em fatores dependentes da velocidade utilizando o pacote VEIN. O modelo apresentou elevado desempenho em março de 2019 (R2 = 0,92 para volume; R2 = 0,86 para velocidade), com redução em março de 2020 (R2 = 0,78), refletindo a instabilidade dos padrões de mobilidade durante o período pandêmico. Os resultados indicam reduções horárias de CO2 entre 50% e 65% nos horários de pico em 2020, bem como diminuição expressiva das emissões totais (−52,5%). A análise espacial evidencia que as maiores reduções se concentraram nos principais eixos estruturais da cidade, associados ao tráfego pendular.

title: Analisis Kinerja Keuangan PT Sampoerna Agro Tbk Sebelum dan Selama Masa Pandemi Covid-19
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dampak pandemi Covid-19 terhadap kinerja keuangan PT Sampoerna Agro Tbk sebelum dan selama pandemi Covid-19 berlangsung. Penelitian ini dilakukan untuk mengidentifikasi perubahan kondisi keuangan perusahaan, baik berupa peningkatan maupun penurunan, berdasarkan perbandingan kinerja keuangan pada periode sebelum dan selama pandemi. Populasi dalam penelitian ini adalah laporan keuangan PT Sampoerna Agro Tbk, sedangkan sampel penelitian berupa laporan keuangan triwulan periode 2018–2020 yang telah dipublikasikan melalui Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI). Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan metode dokumentasi dengan memanfaatkan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan keuangan perusahaan. Metode analisis data yang digunakan adalah analisis rasio keuangan, yang meliputi rasio likuiditas, rasio aktivitas, dan rasio profitabilitas. Selanjutnya, pengujian hipotesis dilakukan dengan menggunakan metode paired sample t-test untuk mengetahui apakah terdapat perbedaan kinerja keuangan yang signifikan antara periode sebelum dan selama pandemi Covid-19. Hasil penelitian secara empiris menunjukkan bahwa rasio likuiditas mengalami perbedaan yang signifikan sebelum dan selama pandemi Covid-19. Sementara itu, rasio aktivitas dan rasio profitabilitas tidak menunjukkan adanya perbedaan yang signifikan pada kedua periode tersebut. Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa pandemi Covid-19 memberikan dampak terhadap aspek likuiditas perusahaan, tetapi tidak secara signifikan memengaruhi aktivitas operasional dan kemampuan perusahaan dalam menghasilkan laba. Dengan demikian, kinerja keuangan PT Sampoerna Agro Tbk menunjukkan kondisi yang relatif stabil pada aspek aktivitas dan profitabilitas selama pandemi berlangsung.

title: AVALIAÇÃO DO PAPEL DA IL-6 E HEPCIDINA NA ANEMIA CRÔNICA EM PACIENTES COM COVID-19
abstract: Na COVID-19, a anemia crônica tem sido frequentemente identificada e relacionada à intensa resposta inflamatória provocada pelo coronavírus, onde sintomas inflamatórios persistem por períodos prolongados. Nesse cenário, o presente estudo tem como objetivo analisar o papel do eixo Interleucina-6/hepcidina no desenvolvimento da anemia da inflamação em pacientes com COVID-19, considerando seus impactos sobre marcadores inflamatórios e metabolismo do ferro. Trata-se, de uma revisão de literatura com procedimento descritivo-qualitativo baseada em artigos publicados entre os anos de 2021 e 2026, nos idiomas português e inglês, abordando temas como anemia da inflamação, coronavírus e tempestade de citocinas. Foram excluídos artigos fora do período estipulado, exceto aqueles para contextualização da COVID-19 ou dados desatualizados. As obras analisadas evidenciam que o aumento da Interleucina-6 estimula produção de hepcidina, promovendo a internalização da ferroportina, que reduz absorção intestinal e a liberação de ferro pelos macrófagos, ocorrendo menor disponibilidade desse mineral para síntese de hemoglobina e formação de eritrócitos. Além disso, hepcidina e ferritina elevadas, associadas à redução do ferro sérico, podem auxiliar na avaliação das alterações do metabolismo do ferro durante a infecção, sendo então, biomarcadores da inflamação associada ao COVID-19. Entretanto, a escassez de estudos recentes que relacionam esses mecanismos ao coronavírus, especialmente no Brasil, e a dificuldade de encontrar publicações sobre a via JAK/STAT limitaram o aprofundamento da discussão. Assim, pesquisas futuras poderão investigar a interação entre IL-6 e hepcidina, ampliando a compreensão da anemia da inflamação e avaliando a possível utilidade desses marcadores no acompanhamento clínico e prognóstico dos pacientes.

title: El discurso en redes sociales en español como expresión de racismo cultural hacia la población china en el contexto del COVID-19
abstract: This article examines how social media contribute to the reproduction of racist discourses toward the Chinese population in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, from the perspective of Critical Discourse Analysis. The analyzed corpus consists of 118 texts taken from Twitter posts and Facebook comments, produced between January 2020 and December 2021, within the Spanish-speaking discursive space. The methodological approach is qualitative and interpretive, and the analysis was conducted based on four semantic categories. The results show that the identified discursive racism falls within the so-called ‘new racism’ or ‘cultural racism’ (Balibar y Wallerstein, 1991; De la Cadena, 1998, 2004; Van Dijk, 2005), that is, a subtle and naturalized form of racism that is no longer grounded in biological criteria, such as skin color, but rather in cultural practices, social behaviors, customs, and values.

title: Association of mRNA COVID-19 vaccination with overall survival in patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors: a retrospective cohort analysis.
abstract: Background: A retrospective study in Nature recently reported improved overall survival (OS) when COVID-19 mRNA vaccination was administered around initiation of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Whether this association depends on vaccination timing relative to ICI treatment remains unclear. Methods: We conducted a single-centre retrospective cohort study of patients receiving palliative-intent ICI therapy at a UK tertiary cancer centre between October 2014 and December 2025. Two vaccination exposure definitions were evaluated: (1) vaccination from 100 days before to 100 days after the first ICI cycle (initial window); and (2) vaccination from 100 days before the first ICI cycle to 100 days after the final ICI cycle (extended window). Multivariable Cox models adjusted for age, sex, treatment line and year of ICI initiation, with the baseline hazard stratified by tumour group. Landmark, time-varying, pre-ICI, active vaccinated comparator and calendar-restricted analyses were performed. Results: Among 2,054 patients, 493 (24.0%) received [≥]1 COVID-19 vaccination. In the initial fixed-window analysis, mRNA vaccination was not significantly associated with OS (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.60-1.06; p=0.123). No significant association was observed in day-100 landmark, initial time-varying or pre-ICI analyses. The active vaccinated comparator analysis was also non-significant. In the extended fixed-window analysis, longer OS was associated with mRNA (HR 0.59; 95% CI 0.46-0.76; p<0.001) and adenoviral-vector vaccination (HR 0.65; 95% CI 0.51-0.83; p<0.001). The mRNA association was attenuated in calendar-restricted analyses and was non-significant in the supportive time-varying analysis (HR 0.82; 95% CI 0.66-1.04; p=0.099). Conclusions: Survival associations with COVID-19 mRNA vaccination varied according to exposure definition and analytic handling of vaccination timing. The strong association observed in the extended fixed-window analysis was attenuated in calendar-restricted and supportive time-varying analyses. Prospective studies are required to determine whether COVID-19 mRNA vaccination at specific time points during ICI therapy influences clinical outcomes.

title: Beyond Metastatic Lymphadenopathy in Breast Cancer: Approach to Axillary Masses.
abstract: The axilla is a pyramid-shaped space containing tissues of various origins including adipose, neural, vascular, cutaneous, myogenic, and lymphatic structures. Axillary masses are typically identified when patients present with palpable areas of concern or during imaging for breast cancer screening or staging. Breast imagers frequently encounter axillary masses while evaluating the axillary region at mammography and US. While reactive lymphadenopathy represents the most common cause of axillary lymph node enlargement, lymph node metastasis from breast cancer is a common cause of axillary masses requiring clinical evaluation. Recent immunization, particularly COVID-19 vaccination, is an important cause of unilateral axillary lymphadenopathy. Additional causes beyond metastatic lymphadenopathy must be considered in the differential diagnosis, including benign and malignant entities arising from accessory breast tissue, adipocytic, neurogenic, vascular, infectious, traumatic, and cutaneous origins. Understanding axillary anatomy is essential for developing a comprehensive differential diagnosis and determining appropriate management strategies. Systematic assessment of characteristic imaging and clinical findings, combined with thorough correlation with patient history and symptoms, enables accurate diagnosis. US serves as the primary imaging modality for mass assessment and biopsy guidance. Depending on the differential diagnosis, mammography, CT, and MRI provide supplementary information to better define mass origin and extent. Definitive diagnosis often requires histopathologic analysis. A systematic approach ensures accurate diagnosis and optimal management of axillary masses. © The Author(s), 2026. title: Infectious Disease Diagnostic Capacity Across Hospital Tiers in China: National Cross-Sectional Survey.
abstract: BACKGROUND China's notifiable infectious disease surveillance relies on clinical recognition and diagnostic testing, but uneven hospital capacity may affect case ascertainment and interpretation of reported burden. OBJECTIVE This study aims to assess infectious disease diagnostic capacity across hospital tiers in China, including alignment with notified disease burden, regional variation, diagnostic modalities, and implementation barriers. METHODS We conducted a national cross-sectional web-based survey of hospitals in China in 2023. After centralized quality control and eligibility screening, 2689 hospitals were included: 124 (4.6%) primary, 1478 (55%) secondary, and 1087 (40.4%) tertiary hospitals. We assessed in-house and send-out testing availability; compared diagnostic availability with national notified incidence and mortality; and examined regional variation, selected diagnostic modalities, and reported barriers. RESULTS Median in-house diagnostic coverage increased from 11.6% (IQR 9.3%-18.6%) in primary hospitals to 27.9% (IQR 18.6%-37.2%) in secondary hospitals and 39.5% (IQR 27.9%-48.8%) in tertiary hospitals; corresponding overall coverage, including send-out testing, was 14% (IQR 9.3%-23.3%), 32.6% (IQR 23.3%-44.2%), and 44.2% (IQR 30.2%-55.8%), respectively. Tier differences persisted in sensitivity analyses. Diagnostic availability was not consistently aligned with notified disease burden. In-house hepatitis B testing was available in 82.3% (102/124), 98% (1449/1478), and 99.3% (1079/1087) of primary, secondary, and tertiary hospitals, respectively. Pulmonary tuberculosis showed a pronounced tier gradient (26/124, 21% in primary vs 910/1087, 83.7% in tertiary hospitals). Hand, foot, and mouth disease and other infectious diarrheal diseases had limited availability even in tertiary hospitals (380/1087, 35% and 456/1087, 42%, respectively) despite high incidence. Some lower-incidence but high-consequence infections also had limited local capacity, including hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (151/1087, 13.9%) and rabies (43/1087, 4%) in tertiary hospitals. Geographic variation was partly consistent with known disease endemicity, with higher testing availability for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome in northeastern hospitals, although only 35.9% (55/153) of tertiary hospitals in this region offered in-house testing. Diagnostic depth also varied across tiers: hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA testing increased from 8.1% (10/124) in primary hospitals to 61.1% (664/1087) in tertiary hospitals. For COVID-19, primary hospitals more frequently reported antigen than nucleic acid testing (57/124, 46% vs 27/124, 21.8%). Lower-tier hospitals more often reported workforce and infrastructure constraints, whereas tertiary hospitals more frequently cited reagent-licensing and fee-schedule barriers. CONCLUSIONS Among surveyed hospitals, infectious disease diagnostic capacity differed substantially across hospital tiers, varied geographically, and was not consistently aligned with notified disease burden. These disparities extended beyond disease coverage to specific testing modalities and barriers to capacity expansion. These findings support tiered, regionally responsive diagnostic networks that provide essential testing closer to first-contact care while ensuring timely access to specialized diagnostics through reliable, quality-assured referral pathways.

title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 1 Transmission Risk During Commercial Air Travel, 2000-2025
abstract: Objectives: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 1 (SARS-CoV-1) have the potential for global translocation and transmission through infected travelers. This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed transmission of these viruses during commercial air travel. Methods: We searched 8 databases for studies published during 2000-2025 of MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-1 transmission during air travel. We included studies describing contact investigation(s) and outcome(s) of MERS-CoV or SARS-CoV-1 exposures on aircraft. We completed title and abstract screening, full-text review, and data extraction in Covidence. We assessed risk of bias using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. We classified contacts of index cases as close contacts according to study-defined contact definitions. We calculated attack rates for close contacts, non-close contacts, and passengers (and/or crew) on the whole plane. We used a random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled attack rates (PARs) and pooled risk differences (PRDs). A leave-one-out sensitivity analysis assessed the robustness of pooled estimates. Results: Nineteen studies met inclusion criteria. No secondary cases were identified from 11 MERS-CoV studies. Among 5 SARS-CoV-1 studies reporting whole-plane data, the PAR was 1.2% (95% CI, 0.3%-4.3%). Sensitivity analyses indicated that this estimate was robust. Among 4 studies reporting outcomes for close contacts, the PAR was 3.4% (95% CI, 1.0%-11.1%), while 2 studies of non-close contacts yielded a PAR of 0.3% (95% CI, 0.1%-1.3%). The PRD comparing close and non-close contacts was 0.8% (95% CI, −5.5% to 7.1%). Conclusions: Although both viruses are capable of person-to-person transmission, evidence of transmission during air travel was identified only for SARS-CoV-1. The findings support an evidence- and risk-based, pathogen-specific approach to aircraft contact investigations rather than a uniform strategy for all emerging respiratory viruses.

title: Developing a syndromic case definition for timely surveillance of severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) based on financial claim codes in the Netherlands
abstract: INTRODUCTION: To improve pandemic preparedness, a sustainable and timely surveillance system for severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) is crucial. We developed and evaluated a proxy for syndromic SARI-surveillance using financial claim codes (DTC-codes). METHODS: With data from 2016-2020 we compared DTC-codes with primary discharge diagnosis classified by ICD-10 codes (J0-J22, U07) as comparative benchmark for SARI, distinguishing between paediatric and adult populations, and pre- and during COVID-19-pandemic periods. To establish DTC-based proxies for SARI, accuracy metrics of individual and combinations of DTC-codes, and temporal trends were assessed. We retrospectively assessed its ability to detect COVID-19 epidemic patterns and its relationship with outcomes of existing respiratory surveillance systems. RESULTS: For adults, DTC-codes for pneumonia and unspecified respiratory and viral infections served as proxy for SARI. In the paediatric population, codes for laryngitis subglottica, RSV bronchiolitis and respiratory tract infection were used. While trends in DTC-based SARI proxies correlate with trends in ICD-10-coded SARI, the accuracy relative to this benchmark was moderate. The adult DTC-based SARI proxy reflected peaks in COVID-19 hospitalisations during the pandemic and aligned with influenza and RSV laboratory detections in the pre-pandemic period. The paediatric DTC-based SARI proxy aligned with RSV laboratory detections. CONCLUSION: We established DTC-based proxies for syndromic SARI-surveillance that appeared suitable to monitor SARI-trends. However, on the patient level the accuracy for ICD-10-coded SARI appeared moderate. Accuracy of the DTC-based SARI proxy and its ability to detect relevant epidemic signals, should be assessed prospectively with real-time data.

title: EXPRESS: A Meta-analysis Reporting the Most Common Infectious Complications in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma Patients Treated with FDA Approved Bispecific Antibodies.
abstract: Bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) are used for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM), but infectious complications remain an important concern. We estimated the reported proportion of all-grade and grade ≥3 infections during teclistamab, talquetamab, and elranatamab treatment.A systematic literature review was conducted with Pubmed to extract data which, included the number of patients, grade ≥ 3 infectious adverse events, and non-grade ≥ 3 infectious adverse events. Analyses were conducted using R software and the meta package. A random effect model was utilized.Eight studies (6 RCTs, 2 retrospective studies) involving 946 patients (teclistamab: 394, talquetamab: 374, elranatamab: 178) were analyzed. Pooled proportion (PP) for teclistamab was 0.517 [95% CI, 0.183-0.837], and grade ≥ 3 was 0.233 [95% CI, 0.058-0.598]. The talquetamab group had a PP of 0.636 [95% CI, 0.305-0.874], and grade ≥ 3 were 0.201 [95% CI, 0.110-0.339], with COVID-19 & pneumonia most reported. For elranatamab, the PP was 0.714 [95% CI, 0.397-0.904], with grade ≥ 3 infections at 0.344 [95% CI, 0.015-0.948]. Common infections were adenovirus, CMV, COVID-19, and pneumocystis jirovecii. Table 2 shows consistently reported AEs amongst the three bispecific antibodies for comparability.Infections were frequently reported, but substantial heterogeneity limits the precision and generalizability of a single pooled estimate. Consistent outcome definitions and follow-up are needed.

title: Targeting T follicular helper (Tfh) Cells for Improved Vaccine Efficacy: Lessons from Diverse Disease Models.
abstract: Despite remarkable progress in vaccinology, many vaccines fail to generate durable and broadly protective immunity against rapidly evolving and deadly pathogens. Conventional vaccine strategies often rely on quantifying antibody titers or neutralizing antibodies, but accumulating evidence suggests that humoral responses alone may not ensure long-term protection. An effective vaccine must engage multiple components of the immune system, harnessing intricate cellular interactions to generate durable immunological memory. Among these, CD4 + T follicular helper (Tfh) cells have emerged as central players in orchestrating germinal center (GC) dynamics, where they provide essential signals to B cells for affinity maturation, class switching, and differentiation into memory B cells and long-lived plasma cells. Tfh cells thus directly shape the magnitude and quality of vaccine-induced antibody responses. Clinical and experimental studies across infections such as influenza, HIV, HBV, and SARS-CoV-2 highlight that robust Tfh responses correlate with effective immunity and reduced disease severity. However, most licensed vaccines elicit suboptimal or short-lived Tfh activation, underscoring a critical limitation in current vaccine design. This review provides a comprehensive overview of vaccines targeting Tfh cells across various diseases, elucidating their mechanistic contributions to vaccine-induced immunity, and how their modulation could improve next-generation vaccine strategies. By harnessing Tfh biology, future vaccines could achieve durable, high-quality antibody responses, offering improved protection against emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases.

title: [Gender and age characteristics of cases of disability during the pandemic of coronavirus infection in Moscow].
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has been a global stress factor for population health in most countries, including Russia. The high prevalence and economic burden of diseases make it important to study the regional characteristics of population morbidity among different population groups. The aim of this study was to identify the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on temporary disability cases among residents of Moscow by gender and age, based on data from a primary healthcare organization. The assessment was based on data from 2019 to 2024. The dynamics of the total number of disability cases from 2019 to 2024, as well as their distribution by gender and age categories, were analyzed. The «disability coefficient» was calculated for the entire attached population and for specific gender and age groups. The average duration of days of disability due to respiratory diseases during the study period was also evaluated. It can be stated that the female part of the working population was more likely to apply for disability leaves, and the 35-49 age group had the highest number of temporary disability cases. There were no significant differences in the duration of temporary disability cases between men and women.
journal: Problemy sotsial'noi gigieny, zdravookhraneniia i istorii meditsiny

The aim of this study was to identify the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on temporary disability cases among residents of Moscow by gender and age, based on data from a primary healthcare organization. The assessment was based on data from 2019 to 2024. The dynamics of the total number of disability cases from 2019 to 2024, as well as their distribution by gender and age categories, were analyzed. The «disability coefficient» was calculated for the entire attached population and for specific gender and age groups. The average duration of days of disability due to respiratory diseases during the study period was also evaluated. It can be stated that the female part of the working population was more likely to apply for disability leaves, and the 35-49 age group had the highest number of temporary disability cases. There were no significant differences in the duration of temporary disability cases between men and women.

title: Two Axes of Sleep, One Heart: Dissociating Objective Sleep-Disordered Breathing From Subjective Sleep Duration in Cardiac Risk
abstract: Background: Cardiovascular epidemiology has long treated "sleep" as a single exposure, although it denotes both an objective physiological state and a subjective behaviour. We tested whether these domains carry separable information about cardiac risk. Methods and Results: We derived an objective axis from 8,444 polysomnograms (Sleep Heart Health Study) and a subjective axis of self-reported duration from 407,303 adults in the 2020 and 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System. Multivariable regression (n=213,489), quadratic dose-response modelling, sleep-stratified comorbidity networks, and era-stratified tests were combined. Objective sleep-disordered breathing was continuous and right-skewed (median apnea-hypopnea index, 31.8 events/h; median sleep efficiency, 69%) in a risk-enriched cohort. Both short ( 9 h) sleep were associated with disease after full adjustment: adjusted odds ratios for heart attack were 1.24 (95% CI, 1.19-1.30) and 1.30 (1.19-1.42), and for stroke 1.12 (1.06-1.17) and 1.42 (1.29-1.57). A positive quadratic term confirmed a U shape for all 4 outcomes formally tested (P[≤]6.3x102), with fitted nadirs of 7.26 to 7.85 hours. Suboptimal sleep also raised comorbidity-network density from 0.089 to 0.112 (short sleep; +26%) and 0.108 (long sleep; +22%), with non-overlapping bootstrap CIs and concordant effects across demographic strata. A survey-weighted replication in official CDC microdata (n=344,010; median design effect, 4.43) preserved the principal cardiac, U-shaped, and network findings; an exploratory COVID-19 interaction (P=0.020) did not survive design-based correction. Conclusions: Objective breathing pathology and subjective duration are separately prognostic, and suboptimal sleep amplifies the cardiometabolic comorbidity network. Duration alone cannot exclude asymptomatic sleep-disordered breathing; cardiovascular prevention should assess both axes.

title: Patterns of influenza in Iraq: Sentinel surveillance 2021–2025
abstract: Seasonal influenza affects individuals of all age groups and represents a significant global public health concern. In Iraq, influenza surveillance is a part of the national surveillance framework for influenza-like illness (ILI) and severe acute respiratory infection (SARI). This cross-sectional study described the epidemiological characteristics of ILI/SARI cases and circulating influenza viruses using data from six sentinel surveillance sites across Iraq between November 2021 and December 2025. Demographic and clinical data were collected and respiratory specimens were tested using RT-PCR. A total of 7,131 cases were reported, of which 3,571 (50.1%) were classified as SARI and 3,560 (49.9%) as ILI. Individuals aged 16–50 years constituted the majority (55.9%), and sex distribution was nearly equal. Logistic regression identified increasing age and the presence of diabetes mellitus, heart disease, chronic respiratory diseases, and chronic hematological diseases as independent predictors of SARI (p < 0.001). Out of 7,131 collected specimens, 7,037 (98.7%) were successfully tested. Among these, 1,552 (22.1%) tested positive. Influenza accounted for 812 cases (52.3%) and SARS-CoV-2 for 740 (47.7%). Influenza positivity was highest among individuals aged 6–15 years and among patients with comorbidities. Increasing age was independently associated with lower odds of influenza positivity, whereas diabetes mellitus, heart disease, chronic respiratory diseases, chronic hematological diseases, and chronic kidney diseases were associated with higher odds. Influenza A predominated throughout most of the study period, with subtype dominance alternating between A/H1N1pdm09 and A/H3N2. All typed Influenza B cases belonged to the Victoria lineage with no evidence of Yamagata circulation. Influenza activity demonstrated a consistent winter seasonal pattern, which emphasize the importance of implementing vaccination campaigns prior to winter before peak season. Overall, these findings highlight the importance of enhancing sentinel surveillance systems and laboratory capacity to improve detection, guide vaccination strategies, and support public health preparedness.

title: Establishment and characterization of a recombinant VSV-based pseudotyping platform for studying RSV F-mediated entry and antibody-mediated neutralization
abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of severe lower respiratory tract disease, underscoring the need for safe, scalable platforms to evaluate neutralizing antibodies, and entry-targeting antivirals. Here, we established and characterized a vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV)-based pseudovirus neutralization assay for RSV that uses fusion (F) proteins from RSV A and RSV B strains as functional entry glycoproteins. Key assay parameters were systematically evaluated, including target cell type, F-expression plasmid input, packaging multiplicity of infection, pseudovirus inoculum, detection time point, and cell seeding density. Western blotting confirmed F expression and incorporation into pseudovirus particles, and a GFP reporter-based syncytium assay verified fusion activity. Under the selected assay conditions, the assay showed strong signal linearity, low background, and reproducible reporter readouts in HEK293T cells at 24 h post-infection. Neutralization by monoclonal antibodies targeting six major antigenic sites on RSV F (sites Ø and I–V) supported the functional preservation and accessibility of multiple neutralization-relevant epitopes on the pseudovirus surface. RSV-specific fusion inhibitors selectively blocked both pseudovirus entry and F-mediated cell-cell fusion in a dose-dependent manner, whereas SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitors had no effect, consistent with the expected virus-specific inhibition profiles. Importantly, pseudovirus neutralization titers showed positive correlations with live-virus neutralization results in both human and mouse sera. Together, these findings establish the VSV-RSV pseudovirus neutralization assay as a robust and scalable platform for measuring F-directed neutralizing activity and for supporting vaccine evaluation, serological surveillance, monoclonal antibody characterization, and antiviral discovery. IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial disease in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals, underscoring the need for robust assays to evaluate vaccines, antibodies, and antivirals. Authentic-virus assays remain essential because they measure neutralization in the context of intact RSV, but the involvement of multiple viral components can complicate attribution of neutralization differences specifically to F. The vesicular stomatitis virus-based pseudovirus system developed here uses F as the sole RSV envelope glycoprotein and restricts infection to a single reporter-expressing round, enabling controlled comparisons of F variants, F-directed antibodies, and entry inhibitors. Its positive correlation with authentic-virus neutralization further supports its utility as a complementary platform for mechanistic and comparative studies of RSV F-directed entry and neutralization.

title: A prospective, comparative cohort analysis of influenza antibody waning in Michigan and Hong Kong during periods of low influenza circulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND Reduced influenza transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic prompted concern about waning of population immunity that could lead to subsequent surges in circulation. We compared longitudinal influenza antibody titers in Michigan and Hong Kong, two regions with reduced influenza transmission during the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS In two prospective cohort studies (HIVE, Michigan; EPI-HK, Hong Kong), we analyzed longitudinal serum samples collected from 2020 through 2023 from participants without influenza infection or vaccination. Sera were tested using hemagglutination inhibition assays (HAI) and microneutralization (MN) against vaccine strains. Two-year fold changes in titers were estimated using multivariable power-law models adjusted for age and baseline titer. RESULTS We analyzed 173 sera from 57 HIVE participants and 259 sera from 60 EPI-HK participants. Initial HAI geometric mean titers ranged from 12.3-123.4 in HIVE and 6.3-40.9 in EPI-HK. Among those with >1:40 baseline titers in HIVE, fold-change estimates indicated waning for H1N1 strains, including A/Brisbane (0.70 [95% CI: 0.56,0.86]), A/Idaho (0.40 [0.32,0.50]), and A/Michigan (0.43 [0.34,0.52]), while H3N2 and influenza B showed minimal or no waning. In EPI-HK, fold-change estimates demonstrated heterogeneous patterns by strain for H1N1, and waning for selected H3N2 strains, including A/Cambodia (0.44 [0.29,0.65]) and A/Singapore (0.48 [0.33,0.69]). title: Localizing Unsampled Regions in Partially Sampled Pathogen Phylogenies Using Machine Learning
abstract: Motivation: Pathogen phylogenies are useful for monitoring the evolution of pathogens and for detecting new variants, as it provides information that can aid public health decisions and outbreak response. Since not all infections are sequenced, certain pathogen lineages may be missing or only poorly represented in reconstructed phylogenies. Identifying these gaps could help to determine where additional data collection is required. Results: We developed a computational method to locate regions of missing samples from the observed tree alone, without sequences from those samples. A machine learning model predicts which branches lead toward the missing region. Beam search then identifies three representative paths and estimates a candidate most recent common ancestor (MRCA) of the missing region for each path. We tested this framework on 5,000 simulated phylogenies where we controlled which tips were deleted. On an independent test set, the best candidate recovered an average of 89.9% of deleted tips, increasing to 90.7% when all three candidates were combined. Predicted and true MRCAs lay on the same ancestral-descendant lineage in 91.3% of cases. We further evaluated the approach on an empirical SARS-CoV-2 phylogeny with introduced missingness. By identifying potentially underrepresented lineages, this framework could help real-time identification of missing infections and improve outbreak response.

title: Precannulation Risk Factors Associated With Hemorrhagic Events During Respiratory Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation in Children: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: Hemorrhagic complications are frequent and clinically significant during pediatric extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), yet associated precannulation factors remain poorly defined. We evaluated these factors in a multicenter retrospective cohort of children receiving respiratory ECMO at four Colombian centers during 2018-2022. A total of 106 children were included; 53 (50.0%) developed at least one hemorrhagic complication during ECMO support, and 83% of events occurred within the first 7 days after cannulation. Cannulation-site bleeding was most frequent (41.5%), followed by intracranial hemorrhage (22.6%) and pulmonary hemorrhage (17.0%). In bias-reduced adjusted analyses, higher precannulation lactate concentrations, lower bicarbonate levels, previous severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection, adenovirus infection at admission, and longer mechanical ventilation and vasoactive support before ECMO remained associated with bleeding. Patients who developed hemorrhagic complications had higher 28 day mortality than those without bleeding (39.6% vs. When bleeding was modeled as a time-dependent exposure, hemorrhagic events were associated with a higher subsequent hazard of 28 day mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 4.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.09-11.64). Hemorrhagic complications affected half of children receiving respiratory ECMO, occurred predominantly during the first week, and were associated with increased mortality. Several precannulation characteristics remained associated with bleeding in bias-reduced adjusted analyses. These hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation.

title: Serial vaccination establishes and refines the human CD4+ T cell memory repertoire.
abstract: CD4+ T cells coordinate protective immunity against pathogens. However, how human CD4+ T cell memory is established and evolves following primary and repeated vaccinations remain incompletely understood. Using COVID-19 mRNA vaccination as a model, we tracked 50 distinct antigen-specific populations directly ex vivo with peptide-MHC class II tetramers in eight SARS-CoV-2-naïve individuals from pre-exposure baseline through memory time points after three mRNA doses. We showed that primary vaccination established the architecture of antigen-specific memory. Initial vaccination leveraged pre-existing memory while preferentially recruiting high-avidity T cells, establishing an immunodominance hierarchy dominated by a small subset of precursors. Booster vaccination refined both the magnitude and quality of T cell memory. It increased select populations and enhanced differentiation of subdominant CD4+ T cells. Populations that did not become more abundant after boosting retained their polyfunctional potential. Beyond establishing memory to the ancestral spike, vaccinations recruited cross-reactive T cells and increased the breadth of CD4+ T cell memory. Collectively, these findings reveal how human T cell memory evolves through sequential immunizations to generate a functionally diverse and broadly responsive memory repertoire against future viral challenges.

title: Mortality and prognostic factors in invasive aspergillosis: a systematic review and individual patient data meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Invasive aspergillosis remains a life-threatening infection, but robust real-world mortality estimates are scarce. We aimed to generate contemporary overall and subgroup-specific mortality estimates for invasive aspergillosis using individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis. Methods In this systematic review and IPD meta-analysis, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science for articles published between Jan 1, 2015, and Dec 31, 2024, that reported mortality of at least ten patients with invasive aspergillosis diagnosed using established criteria, with clearly defined and analysed follow-up periods. Corresponding authors were contacted to obtain IPD on demographics, underlying conditions, site of invasive aspergillosis, diagnostic certainty, and mortality. The primary outcome was overall all-cause mortality at 4, 6, 12, and 24 weeks, 1 year, and 2 years after invasive aspergillosis diagnosis. Secondary outcomes were intensive care unit (ICU) mortality and in-hospital mortality. One-stage IPD meta-analysis was performed to estimate pooled mortality. This study was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42025621772). Findings 16 020 articles were identified, of which 9686 articles were screened after removal of duplicates. Of the articles screened, 209 studies including 15 357 patients were eligible. IPD were obtained from 46 studies, comprising 3880 patients. Across IPD cohorts, patients were predominantly middle-aged and had pulmonary involvement, and probable invasive aspergillosis was the most common diagnostic certainty; classic immunocompromised host factors were common in the mortality-after-invasive aspergillosis-diagnosis cohort, whereas COVID-19 predominated in the ICU mortality cohort. Estimated overall mortality was 26·7% (95% CI 21·0-38·2) at 4 weeks, 32·0% (26·9-42·6) at 6 weeks, 41·7% (34·9-55·1) at 12 weeks, 48·5% (41·4-61·4) at 24 weeks, 53·8% (46·8-64·0) at 1 year, and 57·2% (49·7-68·3) at 2 years. ICU mortality was 57·1% (47·5-66·5) and in-hospital mortality was 46·7% (39·4-54·1). By underlying condition, estimated 4-week mortality was highest among patients with ICU admission (42·9%, 30·4-53·2). By site, estimated 4-week mortality was 27·2% (21·3-40·0) for pulmonary, 21·1% (15·1-28·9) for sinus, and 40·4% (35·0-54·5) for brain invasive aspergillosis. The overall pooled estimates yielded I 2 values of 93·2% (92·0-94·3) for 4-week mortality, 89·5% (87·6-91·2) for in-hospital mortality, and 92·3% (90·8-93·5) for ICU mortality. Interpretation Mortality among patients with invasive aspergillosis remains high despite modern diagnostic and therapeutic advances. Greater vigilance, earlier diagnosis, and timely antifungal treatment are needed, particularly for patients with newly recognised host factors, including ICU admission and COVID-19. Funding Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

title: Viral detection and clinical heterogeneity among severe community-acquired pneumonia patients stratified by respiratory virus status: a secondary analysis of combined retrospective and prospective multicenter cohorts.
abstract: Purpose To describe the prevalence, viral subtypes, and clinical outcomes of viral-positive severe community-acquired pneumonia (sCAP) patients, and the heterogeneities among different respiratory viruses. Method This secondary analysis enrolled sCAP patients from a retrospective 17-center cohort (2019-2023) and a prospective 26-center cohort (Sep 2023-Apr 2025) receiving clinical metagenomic sequencing. Patients were stratified into virus-positive/negative groups, and positive cases were subdivided into SARS-CoV-2, influenza virus (IFV), other respiratory viruses and mixed viruses. However, the mixed-virus group exhibited a significantly shorter ICU and hospital length of stay. When using IFV as the reference, the viral subgroups did not differ significantly in 28-day mortality, whereas the mixed-virus group again showed significantly shorter ICU length of stay. title: Frontotemporal Slow-Frequency Dominance in Quantitative EEG as a Potential Biomarker of Post-COVID Cognitive Dysfunction.
abstract: ObjectiveTo characterize quantitative electroencephalographic alterations associated with persistent cognitive complaints following mild COVID-19 and to explore their relationship with cognitive performance and their discriminative potential.MethodsIn this exploratory case-control study, qEEG recordings from 21 patients with persistent cognitive complaints following mild COVID-19 infection and 21 age- and sex-matched healthy controls were analyzed. Subject-level spectral power and slow-to-fast frequency ratios were quantified using a harmonized 14-electrode common-average reference. Associations with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) performance were explored within the post-COVID group using univariate Random Forest regression. Exploratory classification was performed using 112 spectral qEEG features with leakage-controlled repeated cross-validation and training-fold-specific feature selection.ResultsPost-COVID patients showed a spatially heterogeneous shift toward slower spectral activity, with the most consistent differences involving frontal electrodes and the right temporal region. Cognitive associations were modest and domain-specific, with the clearest out-of-sample performance observed for identification/naming (best mean cross-validated R 2 = 0.328 ± 0.319). Leakage-controlled classification showed substantial exploratory discriminative performance between patients and controls: logistic regression achieved a weighted F1-score of 0.877 ± 0.109 (ROC-AUC = 0.947), and Random Forest achieved 0.898 ± 0.123 (ROC-AUC = 0.949).ConclusionsThese findings suggest spectral qEEG alterations in patients with persistent cognitive complaints following mild COVID-19, predominantly involving frontal and right-temporal slow-frequency activity. Cognitive and classification findings remain exploratory and require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

title: When One Case Feels Riskier Than One Hundred Cases: A New Framing Effect in Risk Communication
abstract: Time‐based rates are widely used in risk communication, yet little is known about how their framing shapes perception and behavior. This article distinguishes between two common frames of rate—the average‐time frame (e.g., “one death every 30 seconds”) and the average‐outcome frame (e.g., “two deaths every minute”). Four studies were conducted to examine the rate framing effects on perceived risk and behavioral intention. A pilot text analysis of Weibo posts showed that the average‐time frame was relatively more prevalent in COVID‐19 risk communication and generated higher user engagement. Across three studies ( N = 979), we found that the average‐time frame elicited higher perceived risk than the average‐outcome frame, and such a rate framing effect weakened as the objective risk level increased. Moreover, framing information in an average‐time format effectively promoted intentions to limit sedentary behavior. These findings identify a new framing effect in risk communication and offer practical implications for designing persuasive public health messages.

title: MetaEntropy: quantifying protein variability in complex viral mixtures via entropy
abstract: High-density sequence data has become commonplace in the study of complex viral mixtures from wastewater. Established algorithms are available for lineage deconvolution and labelling of clinically-elusive mutations. However, less attention has been paid to the quantification of translated amino acid diversity. We present MetaEntropy, a modular R package for assessing protein sequence variability and identifying sites under potential selection via Shannon entropy. MetaEntropy integrates utility functions for visualizing genome-wide and protein-specific variability, extracting nucleotide and amino acid mutation profiles, and identifying entropy hotspots. Despite being designed for wastewater surveillance, the package can also profile protein diversity from cross-sectional intra-patient data. However, it does not analyze population structure or quasispecies, for which several tools are available. By focusing on positional entropy, MetaEntropy bypasses the sequence constraints, computational overhead, and consensus-based variant loss typical of traditional haplotype reconstruction and multiple sequence alignment strategies. To balance sensitivity against neutral variation, the package evaluates entropy using a standard 20-class canonical amino acid scheme and a 7-class model based on traditional physicochemical properties. Calculated entropy values are normalized to a 0-1 scale, enabling direct comparisons of protein diversity across loci and sample strata. As proofs of concept, we employ MetaEntropy to detect well-known SARS-CoV-2 functional changes from wastewater data, and to explore tissue-specific heterogeneity in systemic infections. MetaEntropy is available from the Comprehensive R Archive Network (CRAN) at https://CRAN.R-project.org/.

title: Improving respiratory virus forecasts by capturing the effects of school holidays, public holidays and seasonal changes in transmission
abstract: Respiratory viruses impose a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality globally, and models that forecast this burden are widely used to support public health decision-making. However, the public health utility of these forecasts can be limited by poor predictive accuracy. In this work, we show how capturing the effects of school holidays, public holidays and seasonal changes in transmission can improve respiratory virus forecasting performance. We construct a Bayesian renewal model where the effective reproduction number R ( t ) is composed of log-additive components including school and public holiday effects and an annually-periodic Gaussian process. The model also allows for the relative rate of reporting to vary with school and public holidays. We use this model to forecast respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza and SARS-CoV-2 case incidence across a 28-day horizon over five jurisdictions in Australia. Applied to the 2025 winter season, our forecasts outperform a random-walk baseline forecast across all settings. We find that the inclusion of holiday and seasonal transmission effects improved forecasting performance across the three pathogens. We show that the school holidays are associated with population-wide reductions in R ( t ) on the order of 5–15% but are generally not associated with changes in reporting. Collectively, our results provide support for the inclusion of holiday and seasonal effects in future respiratory virus forecasting models.

title: Validation of Centers for Disease Control and Prevention National Wastewater Surveillance System’s Wastewater Viral Activity Level for Respiratory Viruses, 2025 –2026 Respiratory Season
abstract: Abstract Background The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) developed the Wastewater Viral Activity Level metric (WVAL) for SARS-CoV-2 in 2023 to meet the need for a public metric that aggregates wastewater viral RNA concentration data to provide jurisdictional, regional, and national surveillance system estimates for the United States. The WVAL was expanded in August 2024 to include virus-specific metrics for influenza A and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). This paper describes results the 2025 validation of the updated WVAL methodology. Methods During validation conducted from March through July 2025, candidate WVAL methods were evaluated using wastewater surveillance data collected through March 22, 2025, from SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, and RSV sampling sites. Evaluated components included the baseline calculation and stabilization period, the frequency of baseline and standard deviation updates, the sample look-back period used to calculate the baseline, and the cut points used to assign WVAL categories. Results Data included 4,447 SARS-CoV-2, 1,592 influenza A, and 1,454 RSV data submitter level sampling sites. A z-score threshold of 4 was selected for outlier removal, and non-normalized wastewater concentrations with a 24-month look-back period were selected for baseline and standard deviation calculations across pathogens. title: [THE STRUCTURAL AND DYNAMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF THE DISEASES OF BLOOD CIRCULATION ORGANS IN THE KYRGYZ REPUBLIC].
abstract: The diseases of circulatory system continue to occupy leading positions in structure of morbidity and mortality of population, remaining one of key public health problems. The purpose of the study is to investigate dynamics of primary morbidity and prevalence of diseases of circulatory system by main nosological forms among adult and adolescent population of the Kyrgyz Republic in 2018-2024. The study used official data from the Center for E-Health Care that was analyzed using retrospective, statistical and comparative analytical methods. It was found that indicators of primary morbidity and prevalence were characterized by pronounced variability with greatest increase in 2022, against the background of decrease in 2020-2021, that may be due to changes in availability of medical care in period of COVID-19 pandemic. The highest levels of morbidity and prevalence were found for hypertension, coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular diseases. Some nosologies, including myocardial infarction and other peripheral vascular diseases, demonstrated sharp increase in indicators, suggesting changes in disease detection and health care seeking behavior of population. The obtained results confirm necessity to improve system of monitoring, prevention and early detection of cardiovascular diseases, especially among high-risk groups.

title: Infections and Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Narrative Review of Acute Triggers, Chronic Risk, and Coronary Outcomes
abstract: This narrative review evaluates associations between bacterial and viral infections and myocardial infarction (MI) or acute coronary syndrome (ACS), with attention to event timing, coronary outcome definitions, and MI subtype. PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase were searched on October 6, 2026. The non-exhaustive narrative inventory comprises 44 selected original studies, including 41 primary association studies and three complementary studies of broader outcomes, prognosis, or classification. Findings were synthesized qualitatively according to infection, study design, comparator, and risk window. The MI-specific outcomes were considered separately from ACS and broader cardiovascular composites, and study limitations informed the interpretation of individual findings. No pooled effect was calculated. Across the selected evidence, the clearest short-term pattern was an increase in coronary events during the first days after respiratory infection and laboratory-confirmed influenza. Early associations were also reported after COVID-19, bloodstream infection, and urinary tract infection (UTI). Estimates varied with infection severity, comparator selection, and the handling of events diagnosed on the same day as infection. Post-acute COVID-19, HIV, and tuberculosis studies described associations over longer follow-up, whereas the limited MI-specific hepatitis C evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant association. These longer-term findings addressed a different question from acute triggering and could not establish a shared mechanism. Residual confounding, overlapping populations, outcome misclassification, and incomplete MI subtype information limited interpretation. Most studies did not establish whether coronary events reflected type 1 MI, type 2 MI, or another process, and myocardial injury during infection could not be assumed to represent ischemic MI. Overall, the review supports considering recent infection when evaluating new ischemic symptoms while interpreting the evidence in relation to the population, endpoint, and time window studied. The observational associations do not establish causation or support routine cardiac testing or antithrombotic treatment based on infection alone. Further studies should distinguish MI subtypes and report absolute as well as relative risks.

title: Trends of delayed healthcare access in ocular injuries: a multicenter study in community hospitals, Central Thailand.
abstract: AIM To determine the annual trends and risk factors for delayed access to care in community hospitals across Central Thailand-an area with high occupational injury risk. METHODS This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed data from four community hospitals in Central Thailand over six years (October 1, 2018-September 17, 2024). Patients aged ≥20y with ocular injuries, identified via International Classification of Diseases-10 (ICD-10) codes, were included. Demographics, injury characteristics, and care-seeking behaviors were recorded. Delayed access was defined as presentation >24h post-injury. Linear and logistic regression models were used to identify associated risk factors. Annual fiscal trends were analyzed to assess year-to-year patterns in delayed healthcare access. RESULTS Among 6571 ocular injury cases, 4034 (61.4%) were male, with median age 43y [interquartile range (IQR) 31-57y], and 3983 (79.3%) were manual laborers. Delayed healthcare access was observed in 2426 cases (36.9%). Significant risk factors included age ≥60y [aOR: 1.55; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.32-1.82], visits to F2-level hospitals [adjusted odds ratio (aOR): 2.03; 95%CI: 1.73-2.38], and outpatient visits (aOR: 14.01; 95%CI: 12.18-16.12). In F2 hospitals, subgroup analysis revealed a U-shaped reduction in delayed healthcare access for ocular injuries during the COVID-19 pandemic (2019-2021), adjusted for age and gender. CONCLUSION This first in-depth study of ocular injuries in Central Thailand's community hospitals found persistently high delayed presentations, with older age, F2 hospital visits, and outpatient department (OPD) attendance as key contributing factors. The trend during the COVID-19 pandemic highlights the important role of lower-tier community hospitals in providing prompt and accessible care for patients. Strengthening healthcare infrastructure and public awareness is essential to ensure timely care and reduce preventable vision-related complications.

title: Crystal Structure of Equine Coronavirus Main Protease in Complex with the inhibitor GC376-Considerations for Pan-Coronaviral Inhibitor Design.
abstract: Coronaviruses are highly transmissible pathogens that infect a broad range of hosts, with some causing severe illness in both humans and animals. Considerable research effort for the treatment of acute infection has been directed towards human coronaviral targets, including SARS-CoV-1/-2, MERS-CoV and other human coronaviruses. However, comparable study of related animal coronaviruses that may cross-over to humans is less prominent. Here we describe the cloning, isolation and purification of the genomically proposed equine coronavirus main protease (EqCoV-M pro ) and its C59S and C225S mutants to facilitate drug development. FDA-approved and investigational SARS-CoV-2 M pro inhibitors, including GC376, inhibit EqCoV-M pro with nanomolar potency. A surface-cysteine C59S mutation enabled the first X-ray co-crystal structure of EqCoV M pro with GC376 at 2.0 Å. It reveals a deeper, more hydrophobic active site than related human and animal CoV M pro s, favoring compact inhibitors and informing future pan-coronaviral inhibitor design.

title: Atomic layer deposition of antigen-decorated phage-like particles as a platform for thermally stable, single-injection antiviral vaccines.
abstract: Overcoming barriers to the distribution, availability, and effectiveness of vaccines, are major public health challenges. For example, thermal instabilities of vaccines result in the need for strict cold-chain conditions during storage and shipping. In addition, many vaccines require the administration of multiple vaccine doses per individual for protective and durable immunity. In this study, we describe the combination of a SARS-CoV-2 receptor binding domain (RBD) lambda phage-like particle (PLP) vaccine platform with our spray-drying and atomic layer deposition (ALD) formulation to generate highly thermostable single-dose immunogens. We show that ALD formulated SARS-CoV-2 RBD PLP vaccines retain potent immunogenicity in mice following incubation for one month at temperatures up to 50°C. In addition, mice immunized with a single dose of ALD formulated SARS-CoV-2 RBD PLP vaccines developed SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody responses similar to those induced by standard prime-boost regimens and were strongly protected against SARS-CoV-2 infection and disease. These data suggest that ALD-coated PLP-based vaccine formulations can address two critical barriers to effective deployment of antiviral vaccines-thermal stability and single-shot dosing.

title: Duration of Methotrexate Interruption and Vaccine Immunogenicity in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Systematic Review of Hold Intervals Stratified by Vaccine Platform
abstract: Methotrexate (MTX) blunts humoral responses to several vaccines in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and temporary interruption, hereafter termed a hold, is widely recommended, yet the optimal hold interval and whether it differs by vaccine platform remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed original peer-reviewed studies that compared an MTX hold of defined duration, or an MTX-free post-vaccination window, with continued MTX, or that compared hold durations, in adults with RA alone or as the predominant group within a mixed inflammatory arthritis cohort. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to September 30, 2026, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines. Risk of bias was assessed with Risk-of-Bias Tool 2 for randomized trials and Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies - of Interventions for non-randomized studies, and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation. Eleven studies (nine randomized, two observational cohorts) including 2,099 analyzed MTX-treated participants met the eligibility criteria, covering inactivated influenza vaccines, inactivated whole-virion, adenoviral-vector and mRNA SARS-CoV-2 vaccines, and pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. Across platforms, holding MTX for about two weeks after vaccination consistently improved humoral responses: an absolute gain in satisfactory influenza response of 21.0 percentage points (95% confidence interval (CI): 10.6-31.7), a 2.08-fold higher anti-spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) titer after mRNA-predominant boosters (95% CI: 1.59-2.70) that persisted to 26 weeks, and 2.2- to 2.6-fold higher median anti-RBD titers after ChAdOx1. In the one trial that tested it, holding MTX only before vaccination conferred no benefit, whereas holds spanning the post-vaccination window did, and observational data suggested a useful duration of about 10 days. A one-week hold was noninferior to two weeks for influenza (difference = -6.1 percentage points, 95% CI: -19.3 to 7.1; margin = -20) and carried fewer flares, but one-week data for other platforms are sparse. Repeating the hold after each dose of a two-dose series increased flares, whereas a single hold after the final dose preserved the immunologic gain without a significant excess of flares. Deferring MTX initiation by one month after pneumococcal conjugate vaccination improved responses in early RA without compromising one-year disease control. Certainty was moderate for influenza, mRNA, and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines; low for the adenoviral-vector vaccine; and very low for the inactivated whole-virion vaccine. A post-vaccination MTX hold of one to two weeks is supported with moderate certainty for influenza and mRNA vaccines, but with low or very low certainty for vector and whole-virion vaccines, with one week a reasonable option for influenza; trials testing one-week holds for other platforms and linking titers to clinical protection are needed.
