In the one trial that tested it, holding MTX only before vaccination conferred no benefit, whereas holds spanning the post-vaccination window did, and observational data suggested a useful duration of about 10 days. A one-week hold was noninferior to two weeks for influenza (difference = -6.1 percentage points, 95% CI: -19.3 to 7.1; margin = -20) and carried fewer flares, but one-week data for other platforms are sparse. Repeating the hold after each dose of a two-dose series increased flares, whereas a single hold after the final dose preserved the immunologic gain without a significant excess of flares. Deferring MTX initiation by one month after pneumococcal conjugate vaccination improved responses in early RA without compromising one-year disease control. Certainty was moderate for influenza, mRNA, and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines; low for the adenoviral-vector vaccine; and very low for the inactivated whole-virion vaccine. title: Lipid nanoparticles and their successors: Design principles for dense tissue penetration and clinical translation.
abstract: Nucleic acid therapeutics have transformed modern medicine, enabling targeted treatments that address a wide range of diseases at their genetic roots. From RNAi-mediated gene silencing to mRNA vaccines and CRISPR-based editing, these advances offer precision strategies for previously intractable conditions. The success of these modalities hinges entirely on delivery technologies which have evolved lockstep with nucleic acid research, facilitating transport from administration site to intracellular target(s). Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as the leading delivery platform for nucleic acid therapeutics which is partially due to extensive research and development of lipid-based vehicle derivatives previously developed for small molecule-based drugs. While LNPs themselves have a relatively brief clinical history, the COVID-19 pandemic propelled nucleic acid technologies into the global spotlight, accelerating public, industrial, and regulatory engagement. This surge in attention catalyzed the maturation of clinical, manufacturing, and regulatory frameworks for therapies that rely on delivery technologies like LNPs for success. While this progress has enabled a new wave of therapies, it has also underscored the limitations of LNPs, including poor penetration into dense extracellular matrix (ECM) tissues and dose-limiting toxicities driven by immunogenicity. As optimization of LNP formulations continues, a new generation of nanoparticle platforms is emerging, aiming to address these shortcomings in morphology, chemistry, and tissue specificity. These platforms are well-positioned to leverage the translational groundwork laid by LNPs, potentially accelerating their own path to clinical relevance. In this review, we examine the evolution and clinical impact of LNPs, analyze their key limitations, and explore emerging delivery platforms, such as biomimetic nanoparticles and polymeric systems that seek to overcome the physicochemical limitations of LNPs while building on the lessons and regulatory frameworks they established.

title: Senescence and Genotoxicity Signatures Across Clinical and Laboratory Outcomes in Patients at High Cardiovascular Risk: An Automated Machine Learning Study
abstract: Abstract Background. Cellular senescence, chromosomal instability, endothelial injury, and altered immune composition may jointly reflect biological aging and cardiometabolic dysfunction. We evaluated whether a fixed 12-biomarker panel provided reproducible feature-level clues for 11 pre-selected clinical and laboratory outcomes in a three-group cohort at high cardiovascular risk. The dataset included 90 patients suffered from acute coronary syndrome (ACS), divided equally into three groups (n = 30 each): pre-pandemic ACS (Group 1), ACS with concomitant laboratory-confirmed acute COVID-19 during the pandemic (Group 2), and ACS without concomitant acute COVID-19 during the COVID-19 pandemic period (Group 3). Four model families were evaluated separately using 5-fold cross-fitting repeated five times. All imputation, scaling, and model fitting were restricted to training folds. Feature evidence integrated held-out permutation importance, cross-fitted SHAP values, linear coefficient stability, Group+SEX-adjusted partial rank associations, within-group sensitivity analyses, and leave-one-group-out transportability. The largest median improvements over Group+SEX baselines occurred for history of acute myocardial infarction with coronary revascularization procedures (Δ=0.161), glucose level (Δ=0.118), heart rate (Δ=0.096), and glycated hemoglobin percentage (Δ=0.091). Recurrent feature themes included senescence-associated heterochromatin foci and CD34 + progenitor cells for glycemic outcomes, micronuclei for heart rate and prior COVID-19, nucleoplasmic bridges for cardiac-history and inflammatory/immune outcomes, and CD31 hi circulating endothelial cells for leukocyte and granulocyte counts. Absolute performance remained weak for several outcomes despite stable feature rankings. Rather than predicting any single outcome with strong absolute accuracy, the same senescence and genotoxicity markers recurred as leading clues across metabolically, cardiac, and immunologically distinct outcomes, and did so consistently across three pathogenetic different cohorts. This cross-outcome stability suggests these markers may index a shared, stressor-independent dimension of cellular burden in ACS patients rather than outcome-specific biology, a hypothesis that warrants mechanistic follow-up.

title: A Machine Learning-Based Early Warning System for Renal Replacement Therapy in the Intensive Care Unit.
abstract: BACKGROUND Renal replacement therapy (RRT) is a life-saving intervention for acute kidney injury in the intensive care unit (ICU). The decision to initiate RRT remains highly complex and subjective. Accurate and timely predictions for the need of RRT initiation are crucial components of personalized care. Using time series patient data (vital signs, laboratory findings, medications, ventilator settings, intake/output, risk scores), we aimed to develop machine learning (ML) models for predicting future initiation of RRT. METHODS Using data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC)-III, MIMIC-IV, and Electronic ICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU), we trained and internally validated models using dataset-specific training, validation, and test splits. We externally validated model performance using held-out eICU hospitals excluded from model development and a temporally distinct cohort of ICU patients admitted during the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic period (2020-2022). Models were developed for: (1) screening patients for prediction of the need for RRT after their first 12 hours in the ICU; and (2) real-time dynamic prediction of the likelihood of documented RRT initiation within the next 24 hours. RESULTS Here, we summarize the results of the ML model aimed at screening patients for early prediction of RRT. In internal validation, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.90 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.886-0.906) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) was 0.53 (95% CI, 0.496-0.564) in MIMIC-III. Results were similar in MIMIC-IV and eICU. External validation on ICU patients admitted during the coronavirus disease (COVID) period yielded an AUROC of 0.90 (95% CI, 0.894-0.913) and an AUPRC of 0.57 (95% CI, 0.534-0.602). Additional hospital-level external validation across eight individual eICU hospitals showed AUROCs ranging from 0.86 to 0.91 and AUPRCs ranging from 0.35 to 0.52. Accuracy ranged from 0.78 to 0.84 across validation experiments. CONCLUSION By accurately identifying patients at high risk for RRT initiation, the early prediction ML model could serve as a triage tool to prompt closer nephrology evaluation or optimization of fluid and hemodynamic management before overt renal failure develops.

title: Rapid Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance Informed Precautionary Public Health Action Following the 2024 Kiteezi Landfill Disaster in Uganda
abstract: Abstract Background Wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) has been used to detect pathogen signals during pandemics and mass gatherings, yet its role in sudden-onset environmental disasters remains poorly understood. Following the catastrophic August 9, 2024, Kiteezi landfill collapse in Kampala, Uganda, which caused fatalities, displaced communities, destroyed sanitation infrastructure, and contaminated the surrounding environment with leachate and sewage, the Ministry of Health rapidly deployed WES to assess infectious disease risks and guide emergency public health action. Methods Between 10 and 12 August 2024, with sampling initiated within 72 hours of the collapse, we conducted a purposive cross-sectional assessment at five high-risk sites: a leachate-floodwater interface, a flowing leachate stream, two stagnant wastewater pools, and a community borehole. Moore swabs were collected at Sites A-D, and a 500 mL grab sample was collected at Site E. Concentrated extracts were qualitatively tested using commercial qPCR or RT-qPCR assays for selected enteric, respiratory, and zoonotic pathogens. The borehole sample was also cultured for Escherichia coli as an indicator of fecal contamination, and field observations documented potential exposure pathways. Results Nucleic acids from Shigella spp., Salmonella spp., non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae, enteric adenovirus 40/41, selected enteroviruses, SARS-CoV-2, and rotaviruses A-C were detected in one or more leachate or wastewater samples. We did not detect influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, or mpox virus. In the single borehole sample, Escherichia coli and all molecular targets were not detected; this single grab-sample result does not establish that the water source was safe. Field observations identified potential exposure pathways, including unprotected contact with contaminated water, children's proximity to polluted pools, livestock access to leachate, and inadequate protection of a community borehole. The response team reported implementing precautionary measures, including water-source restrictions, household water treatment, access controls, WASH activities, animal-control measures, and enhanced clinical surveillance. These measures were implemented within the broader disaster response, with environmental surveillance findings informing risk assessment and decision-making alongside field observations and other operational information. Conclusions Rapid deployment of WES after the Kiteezi landfill disaster was operationally feasible and produced site-specific evidence of environmental microbial hazards. When combined with field observations and routine disaster-response information, these findings informed precautionary public health decision-making, including drinking-water protection and exposure-reduction measures. Although the assessment did not establish the effectiveness of these interventions in preventing infections, it demonstrated the potential value of integrating environmental surveillance into early disaster-response frameworks. Future applications should incorporate repeated environmental sampling, linked clinical surveillance, and systematic documentation of public health actions and outcomes.

title: Assessing adenovirus structural integrity and stability through analytical ultracentrifugation and supporting biophysical methods.
abstract: Adenoviruses (AdV) are used as vectors for gene therapy and for vaccination, such as the COVID-19 vaccines AD26.COV2.S (AdV1) and ChAdOx1-S (AdV2). To develop a platform of methods for AdV characterization, we used untreated and thermally stressed samples. During heating ramps, nanoDSF/DLS detects first structural changes accompanied by aggregation for AdV1 and AdV2 at 50°C. SYBR green-enhanced DSF reveals an increased dye-accessibility of viral DNA within this temperature range, suggesting a loss of structural integrity of the capsid. By introducing the relative ratio of initial fluorescence to maximum fluorescence intensity at the transition point, we derive a numerical value reflecting the extent of heat-induced change. In heat-stressed samples also negative-staining transmission electron microscopy visualizes a loss of structural features. Sedimentation-velocity AUC confirms the changes of AdV quaternary structure upon heat-treatment with formation of high molecular weight species (HMWS). Density gradient equilibrium AUC shows the formation of lower density species and fluorescence detection during SV-AUC with SYBR green further indicates the presence of cargo and capsid within these HMWS. During a storage stability study, the combination of nanoDSF/DLS, DSF and SV-AUC provided a beneficial methods set to assess changes in AdVs with optimized sample consumption.

title: Alginate-DNA Core-Shell Hydrogel Microspheres Program Antigen Release Kinetics for Potent Single-Dose Subunit Vaccination.
abstract: Conventional vaccine sustained release strategies exhibit monophasic antigen kinetics that fail to align with the temporal order of T and B cell activation, limiting single-dose efficacy. Using a protein-carrier peptide vaccine model, we designed an alginate-DNA core-shell hydrogel microsphere that programmed differential antigen release kinetics through orthogonal loading mechanisms. Physical encapsulation enabled carrier protein release within 3 days to prime T cells, while DNA cross-linking sustained epitope-carrier protein conjugate release over 11 days to drive B cell responses, achieving a release interval exceeding 8 days that orchestrates sequential T and B cell activation. In a single immunization, this strategy induces significantly higher epitope-specific IgG titers compared to formulations with either co-rapid or co-sustained release. A SARS-CoV-2 peptide vaccine based on our strategy elicits substantially stronger humoral immunity than traditional aluminum-adjuvanted vaccines. This work establishes orthogonal loading-mediated kinetic programming as a versatile platform for next-generation single-injection subunit vaccines.

title: Predicting county-level opioid overdose mortality in Ohio through multimodal data: A spatiotemporal study using toxicology and EMS indicators, 2020-2024
abstract: Background: The opioid crisis is the leading driver of overdose mortality in the United States. While overdose deaths have decreased in recent years, the reporting lag in official overdose deaths presents a hurdle in implementing public health interventions to combat the crisis. Objective To address these data-reporting delays and improve prediction during highly volatile periods, we developed a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model using real-time drug overdose data sources to predict quarterly overdose deaths across Ohio counties from 2020 to 2024. Methods We implemented a Bayesian spatiotemporal model using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA). Rapid-reporting surveillance metrics, specifically urine drug test (UDT) positivity rates and Emergency Medical Services (EMS) naloxone administration events, were incorporated as fixed covariates. Models were constructed stepwise by first optimizing the spatiotemporal random effect structure and then sequentially adding fixed effects to minimize prediction error. A rolling training window was implemented and evaluated across different training window sizes. Results were assessed overall and stratified by county population size. Results We found that the optimal predictive model structure consists of a two-year training window, a random walk temporal effect, a structured spatial effect, and fentanyl UDT positivity and EMS naloxone events. Incorporating these UDT and EMS data significantly enhanced predictive performance, with the most pronounced accuracy gains occurring during the unprecedented overdose increase associated with the COVID-19 pandemic in the second quarter of 2020. While predictive performance was highly robust in large, urban counties, predictive capability in smaller counties was limited by low data availability. Conclusion Our spatiotemporal prediction model successfully bridges the administrative reporting lags and offers near-real-time quarterly overdose prediction. The study also showed that integration of real-time data sources is especially beneficial for capturing sudden, volatile spikes in overdose deaths.

title: Multiple simultaneous acute infarcts in CADASIL: a retrospective cohort study and systematic review
abstract: Background Cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL) is the most common monogenic cause of stroke and typically presents with single lacunar infarcts. However, multiple simultaneous acute infarcts have increasingly been reported.Methods We retrospectively reviewed a prospectively recruited CADASIL registry from a British National Referral Clinic to identify cases with multiple simultaneous acute infarcts. We combined this with data from a systematic review on MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science and Cochrane Library from inception to 16 February 2026. Multiple simultaneous infarcts were defined as multiple diffusion-restricted lesions on brain MRI.Results Eight cases (five male) were identified from 612 symptomatic CADASIL patients, corresponding to 1.3% of the cohort (95% CI 0.6 to 2.6%). Mean (SD) age 49.6±13.1 compared with 49.5±9.8 for 291 stroke patients with single lacunar infarct. All had a recent infection (COVID-19 3, unspecified respiratory tract infections 4 and Campylobacter infection 1), occurring 2–14 days before symptom onset. The systematic review identified an additional 36 cases (total n=44). Mean age was 48.3±10.2 years and 26 were male. Preceding events were identified in 31 cases, most commonly infection (n=25), followed by surgery (n=4), trauma (n=1) and severe anaemia (n=1). Most patients had infarcts involving bilateral internal watershed regions (90.9%).Conclusions Multiple simultaneous acute infarcts are a rare but important CADASIL presentation, typically involving bilateral watershed regions and frequently preceded by acute systemic stressors, most commonly infection but also surgery and hypotension. This pattern may reflect increased cerebral microvascular vulnerability in CADASIL patients and warrants further investigation.PROSPERO registration number CRD420251053590.

title: Deletion of Furin Facilitates Efficient and Versatile Coronavirus Pseudotyped Particle Generation
abstract: Coronaviruses bring threats to both humans and animals. To initiate successful infections, coronaviruses must first navigate entry into a host cell. Coronavirus spike-bearing pseudotyped particle systems are indispensable tools for studying coronavirus entry and evaluating neutralizing antibodies and entry inhibitors. However, pseudotyped particle titers can be low when packaged particles bear coronavirus spikes that contain the furin cleavage site, and this has been a limitation for pseudotyped particle production and applications. Here, we demonstrate that CRISPR/Cas9-mediated knockout of furin protease in HEK293T cells significantly enhances the production of functional pseudotyped particles bearing spikes containing the furin cleavage site, including those from SARS-CoV-2, MERS-CoV, and MHV-JHM. Moreover, deletion of endogenous furin in producer cells yields an effect equivalent to deletion of the furin cleavage site, but with broader application across different spike proteins, and without virus manipulation. This work establishes a simple and effective platform to improve coronavirus pseudotyped particle systems by eliminating furin-mediated pre-activation, enabling more efficient and reliable production for downstream applications.

title: mRNA-Lipid Nanoparticle Vaccines for Infectious Diseases: Mechanisms of Action and Translational Progress
abstract: Six years after the first emergency use authorizations, mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines have gone from a platform without a licensed product to one that supplies a large share of the world's COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine doses and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. Their performance depends on mechanisms that are being resolved with unusual speed at the level of individual cell types, receptors and molecular interactions, and several textbook assumptions have had to be revised in the process. This review follows the vaccine from the formulation vial to the germinal centre. We first describe how the RNA is engineered for efficient translation and for partial escape from cytosolic and endosomal RNA sensors, and why N1-methylpseudouridine is neither immunologically silent nor translationally neutral. We then examine how the ionizable lipid, the helper phospholipid, cholesterol and the PEG-lipid determine particle behaviour, cell uptake and endosomal release, and how the lipid and RNA components act as separable adjuvant signals. Evidence from mouse models and from human lymph node sampling is compared, with attention to the substantial species differences in innate cytokine control that limit extrapolation from mice to people. The clinical section summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for COVID-19, RSV and influenza vaccines, and the preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against cytomegalovirus, mpox, HIV, malaria, Nipah virus and Clostridioides difficile. Safety data are discussed in absolute terms rather than as signals alone. We close with the questions that currently block rational improvement: the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the design of antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.

title: Molecular basis of behavioral and cognitive changes induced by neurotropic viruses.
abstract: Neurotropic viruses induce behavioral and cognitive alterations through diverse molecular and cellular mechanisms that extend beyond simple neuronal damage. Comparative analysis of rabies virus (RABV), pseudorabies virus (PRV), Borna disease virus (BoDV-1), SARS-CoV-2, Nipah virus (NiV), West Nile virus (WNV) and Herpes Simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) reveals distinct pathogenic strategies targeting specific neural circuits. While neuroinflammation characterized by microglial activation, astrocytic responses, and pro-inflammatory cytokine production contributes significantly to synaptic and network dysfunction in WNV and NiV infections, other mechanisms predominate in different pathogens. RABV selectively disrupts cholinergic, serotonergic, and glutamate/GABAergic pathways while preserving neuronal integrity to facilitate transmission, whereas BoDV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 induce dopaminergic and serotonergic dysfunctions through persistent immune activation and endothelial damage. Additionally, systemic factors such as the gut-brain axis and microbiome alterations, particularly evident in SARS-CoV-2 infection, modulate neurotransmitter metabolism and neuroimmune responses. Considering the lack of even diffuse neuronal loss observed during infection, behavioral changes may arise more from selective, circuit-dependent vulnerabilities, involving specific disruptions to emotion, cognition, and motor control networks. To provide a clear review of the knowledge regarding how targeted neuronal population alterations translate into behavioral phenotypes, we here integrate molecular, cellular, and systems-level insights across these seven neurotropic viruses used as models, with the aim of identifying common pathways linking infection to behavioral changes and cognitive dysfunction. Understanding these discrete mechanisms ranging from acute synaptic manipulation to long-lasting neuroimmune dysregulation is essential for developing therapeutic strategies that address both the infectious agent and the specific neural networks mediating acute disturbances and long-term neurological sequelae.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Lung Diseases: Screening, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Prognosis.
abstract: Pulmonary diseases currently pose significant threats to global health, spanning common chronic conditions including lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and asthma, as well as infectious and inflammatory diseases like tuberculosis, interstitial lung disease (ILD), and COVID-19. Therefore, accurate diagnosis, effective therapeutic strategies, and reliable assessment of prognosis for pulmonary diseases are essential for improving patient outcomes and safeguarding public health. Despite the increasing availability of medical imaging and pathological data owing to improvements in detection technologies, what is becoming increasingly evident are the limitations of conventional diagnosis, which relies solely on clinicians' subjective judgment based on imaging, pulmonary function, pathology, and clinical experience. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) technology, especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has made significant progress in areas such as image recognition and model construction. Numerous studies have demonstrated the widespread application of AI in the screening and diagnosis of lung diseases, the optimization of treatment strategies, and prognosis assessment, revealing its remarkable ability to process and interpret complex clinical data. Although concerns persist regarding data quality, the "black box" nature of algorithms, clinical practice, and the regulatory landscape, the application of AI in lung disease research and clinical care is more and more promising. In this review, we summarize the latest advances of AI in the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary diseases, analyze the challenges and limitations of current AI technologies ranging from data and algorithms to clinical translation, and highlight directions for future research.

title: GUT MICROBIOTA PATTERNS IN PEDIATRIC RESPIRATORY INFECTIONS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF MICROBIAL SIGNATURES
abstract: Early-life gut microbiota plays a crucial role in immune maturation and has been increasingly associated with host responses to infectious diseases. Emerging evidence highlights the gut–lung axis as an important component of pediatric respiratory health, yet child-focused syntheses remain limited. This systematic review with qualitative analysis summarizes recent original studies evaluating gut microbiota profiles in children with acute respiratory infections, providing a child-specific perspective distinct from reviews that combine age groups or focus on single pathogens. PubMed and the Virtual Health Library were systematically searched and the data were extracted using a structured matrix to identify patterns in microbial composition and methodological strengths and gaps. Twelve studies (2019–2025) including participants aged 0–18 years with conditions such as COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus infection, bronchiolitis, and recurrent respiratory tract infections met predefined inclusion criteria. Across studies, children with respiratory infections consistently exhibited gut dysbiosis, characterized by depletion of beneficial taxa and enrichment of pro-inflammatory genera. While methodological differences, including study design, sampling timing, and handling of confounders, limited direct quantitative comparisons, patterns of microbial alterations were identifiable. Overall, this review highlights a consistent association between gut microbiota alterations and pediatric respiratory infections, supporting the relevance of the gut–lung axis in early life. Nevertheless, methodological heterogeneity prevents inference about cause-and-effect relationships, highlighting the need for well-designed longitudinal and interventional studies to better understand the directionality of these associations.

title: Increasing Adenovirus Upstream Process Productivity Using a High Cell Density Perfusion Strategy.
abstract: Adenovirus vectors are a major vaccine platform and have potential roles as oncolytics and gene therapies. Large-scale production of adenovirus-vectored COVID-19 vaccines demonstrated the value of platform manufacturing processes for such products but vaccine scarcity remained problematic in 2021. There is a need for widely-accessible and higher-yielding platform processes for adenovirus production. This highly productive process could be valuable both in large-scale production and in maximizing the output of smaller facilities making products for niche indications or stockpiles.

title: Respiratory Virus Activity — United States, July 2025–June 2026
abstract: Respiratory viral illnesses are common and can lead to severe outcomes, including hospitalization and death. trends in respiratory virus activity during July 2025-June 2026 were analyzed using data from six complementary public health surveillance systems. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) activity occurred unusually late in most U.S. SARS-CoV-2 circulated nationally with typical bimodal peaks that occurred in August 2025 and January 2026. Annual RSV-associated hospitalization rates (number of hospitalizations per 100,000 persons) were highest among infants aged <12 months (790.2; 95% CI = 757.9-825.3), followed by children aged 12-23 months (611.9; 95% CI = 586.3-639.8) and adults aged ≥75 years (352.1; 95% CI = 309.9-407.7). Annual RSV rates overall and by age group did not exceed those observed during 2022-2025. COVID-19-associated hospitalization rates were highest among adults aged ≥75 years (361.2), infants aged <6 months (173.3), and adults aged 65-74 years (111.4). Newly established 2025-2026 national pediatric mortality surveillance provisionally identified 34 RSV-associated pediatric deaths from 35 reporting jurisdictions and 31 COVID-19-associated pediatric deaths from 43 reporting jurisdictions. RSV sequencing did not identify variant substitutions associated with reduced susceptibility to the available RSV monoclonal antibodies for infants. Most SARS-CoV-2 lineages were JN.1 descendants, but detections of BA.3.2, a highly divergent SARS-CoV-2 variant, increased. Circulation of other respiratory viruses followed usual historical patterns. Staying current with recommended RSV and COVID-19 vaccinations reduces the risk for severe illness and disease caused by these viruses.

title: Comprehensive review of notifiable conditions in Vanuatu: 2024 update
abstract: The 1994 Vanuatu Public Health Act lists 38 conditions and syndromes that must be notified to public health officers. Despite occasional amendments, including adding influenza A(H1N1) in 2019 and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 in 2021, the list of notifiable conditions is inconsistent with current and emerging infectious disease threats in Vanuatu. In 2024, a review was undertaken to amend the list of notifiable conditions using a simplified review process based on Australian and Canadian criteria. A total of 54 conditions were included in the prioritization exercise, which incorporated additional conditions identified for this review based on current global, regional and national health security threats. Each condition was scored on six criteria (communicability, severity, requirement for or likelihood of initiating a public health response, emergence, vaccine preventability and importance), with scores ranging from 0 to 4 for each criterion, for a maximum score of 24. The scores were then summed, and the conditions were ranked. A cutoff score of 8 was used to determine inclusion in the proposed update to the list. The rankings were subsequently reviewed by a local advisory committee. Among the existing 38 conditions and syndromes, it was recommended that 19 should be retained, 10 be excluded, seven be renamed, one be consolidated into another, and one be separated into three distinct conditions. Twelve additional conditions were recommended for inclusion. The final list comprises 41 notifiable conditions. The methods used here are relevant to other Pacific island countries.

title: The impact of the coronavirus pandemic on the dynamics of cases of disability related to respiratory diseases in the provision of primary health care in Moscow
abstract: The high contagiousness and prevalence of diseases during the COVID-19 pandemic necessitated the creation of electronic and digital disability certificates, as well as the introduction and active use of telemedicine technologies in medical institutions. However, the contribution of COVID-19 to the structure of temporary disability rates in different regions and its comparison with similar rates in other territories has not been fully studied. The article provides a comparative analysis of cases, days, and the sex-age structure of temporary disability and their distribution by respiratory diseases in the period 2019—2024, as recorded in a medical organization providing primary healthcare in Moscow. The analysis of the presented data reveals a complex dynamic of disability cases, demonstrating significant variability throughout the period under review.

title: Dendrimers in cytomegalovirus therapy: mechanistic insights and translational prospects.
abstract: Introduction Dendrimers are highly branched, nanoscale molecules with precise architectures that enable controlled interactions with biological systems. Their tunable size, charge, and composition make them promising carriers for antiviral therapeutics. While dendrimer-based formulations have demonstrated efficacy against HIV, HSV, HPV, and SARS-CoV-2, applications in cytomegalovirus (CMV) therapy remain underexplored. Given CMV's clinical burden, particularly in immunocompromised patients and transplant recipients, there is a pressing need to optimize drug delivery strategies. Areas covered This review systematically evaluates dendrimer synthesis approaches, drug-loading techniques, and preclinical/clinical outcomes of dendrimer-based antiviral formulations. Relevant literature was identified through searches of PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis Online, MDPI, and SpringerLink covering publications from January 2010 to August 2026. Special emphasis is placed on existing CMV therapeutics such as ganciclovir derivatives incorporated into dendrimer scaffolds. Evidence indicates that dendrimer conjugation enhances drug solubility, stability, and cellular uptake. Preliminary studies with ganciclovir-loaded dendrimers show improved antiviral activity and reduced systemic toxicity. However, no dendrimer-based formulations have yet advanced to late-stage CMV clinical trials. Expert opinion Expanding dendrimer applications to major anti-CMV drugs, including letermovir, maribavir, valganciclovir, foscarnet, and cidofovir, could enable targeted, sustained, and safer delivery. This review underscores dendrimers as structurally precise nanocarriers with transformative potential in CMV therapy, warranting further translational research.

title: Lipid Nanoparticle–mRNA Vaccines for Infectious Diseases: Making a Potent Platform Predictable
abstract: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)–mRNA vaccines compressed the path from pathogen sequence to licensed product into less than a year and are now approved for three viral diseases (COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus and seasonal influenza), with more than twenty indications in clinical development. The platform’s potency is no longer in doubt; its predictability is. We argue that progress is now limited by three interfaces that are engineered largely independently: the lipid–RNA interface, which sets encapsulation, internal structure and storage stability; the particle–cell interface, which sets tropism and the efficiency of endosomal escape; and the particle–immune interface, which sets the balance between adjuvanticity and reactogenicity. Quantitative design rules exist for the first interface, remain empirical for the second, and are almost absent for the third, which is why formulation development still proceeds by screening rather than by calculation. We review the molecular design of the mRNA payload and structural antigen selection; the chemistry, manufacture and intracellular trafficking of LNPs; the immunological chain that links innate activation and dendritic-cell cross-presentation to germinal-centre output; and the clinical evidence across COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, cytomegalovirus, HIV, personalised cancer vaccines and other targets. We conclude by identifying the measurements, pharmacopoeial quality attributes and design rules that would make the next generation of LNP–mRNA vaccines predictable rather than empirical.

title: A universal molecular bridge unifying viral persistence and chronological tissue aging
abstract: Abstract Chronological aging and acute/post-acute viral infections (such as SARS-CoV-2 Orf7b, Epstein-Barr Virus, Hepatitis C Virus, and Long COVID extracellular vesicles [LC-EVs]) have traditionally been investigated as distinct pathological entities. Here, we establish a unifying mechanistic framework demonstrating that aging and chronic viral persistence converge on a common master regulatory network. Specifically, aging-induced fidelity loss of p53 and SIRT6, combined with viral upregulation of c-Myc and RUNX2, dismantles protective non-coding RNA brakes (miR-145) and longevity deacetylase pathways. We uncover a key feed-forward mechanism wherein hyperactivated RUNX2 directly activates and stabilizes c-Myc [14, 15]. Elevated c-Myc subsequently represses miR-145 while upregulating Tissue Factor (TF) and thrombin via lncRNA MEG3 induction [16], accelerating arterial thrombosis and microvascular occlusion. This dual transcriptional and epigenetic assault disinhibits tissue-destructive proteases like Granzyme K (GzmK), paralyzes the NRF2-Parkin-PGC-1α mitochondrial/peroxisomal axis, and drives structural remodeling and functional decline across multiple organs. Using stiff ordinary differential equation (ODE) modeling, we demonstrate that targeted host-directed restoration via p53/NRF2 co-activation and SIRT6-dependent pathways successfully re-establishes homeostatic control, clearing pathological effectors and rejuvenating tissue function.

title: Lipoplex Nanoparticle-Based RNA Delivery to 3D Melanoma Spheroids.
abstract: Lipoplex nanoparticle-based vaccination technologies have shown tremendous efficiency for in vivo transfection during the COVID-19 pandemic and also hold promise for treating melanoma. While pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics need careful in vivo and clinical testing, other parameters of drug performance can be assessed with in vitro systems as well. Spheroids composed of more than one cell type can serve to assess drug penetration, cell-type specificity, and transfection efficiency at an early stage of drug development.

title: C-terminal engineered human H-chain ferritin for peptide loading within the protein nanocage.
abstract: Self-assembling proteins are widely used in bionanotechnology due to their biocompatibility, non-toxicity, structural stability, and easy functionalization. Ferritins (Fts) are particularly attractive systems, as they assemble into highly ordered nanocages with a hollow internal cavity. Their assembly and disassembly can be modulated by various protocols, such as changes in pH or the use of denaturing agents, enabling their application in molecular encapsulation and drug delivery. However, the efficiency of encapsulation remains challenging, often resulting in low or heterogeneous loading and incomplete protein recovery. Here, we load peptides into the core of the human H-chain ferritin (hHFt) by genetically fusing them to the C-terminus of the Ft subunit, a region facing the inner cavity. As model peptides, we used fragments derived from the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein sharing similar physicochemical properties but different charges. The structure of the functionalized nanocages was assessed using techniques like transmission electron microscopy, native gel electrophoresis, and X-ray crystallography. High-resolution structural analysis revealed interesting conformational changes in the hHFt BC-loop associated with C-terminal functionalization, while the overall nanocage architecture is preserved. Additionally, NMR measurements of the transverse relaxation (T 2 ) of a target peptide demonstrated that the nanocages do not expose the fused peptides under native conditions, but upon disassembly, can efficiently expose them, demonstrating that C-terminal genetic functionalization of ferritin nanocages is a robust and effective approach for nanobiotechnological applications.

Ferritins (Fts) are particularly attractive systems, as they assemble into highly ordered nanocages with a hollow internal cavity. Their assembly and disassembly can be modulated by various protocols, such as changes in pH or the use of denaturing agents, enabling their application in molecular encapsulation and drug delivery. However, the efficiency of encapsulation remains challenging, often resulting in low or heterogeneous loading and incomplete protein recovery. Here, we load peptides into the core of the human H-chain ferritin (hHFt) by genetically fusing them to the C-terminus of the Ft subunit, a region facing the inner cavity. As model peptides, we used fragments derived from the SARS-CoV-2 Spike protein sharing similar physicochemical properties but different charges. The structure of the functionalized nanocages was assessed using techniques like transmission electron microscopy, native gel electrophoresis, and X-ray crystallography. High-resolution structural analysis revealed interesting conformational changes in the hHFt BC-loop associated with C-terminal functionalization, while the overall nanocage architecture is preserved. Additionally, NMR measurements of the transverse relaxation (T2) of a target peptide demonstrated that the nanocages do not expose the fused peptides under native conditions, but upon disassembly, can efficiently expose them, demonstrating that C-terminal genetic functionalization of ferritin nanocages is a robust and effective approach for nanobiotechnological applications.

title: Molecular basis of ACE2 inhibition by the peptide DX600 revealed by computational and biophysical analysis.
abstract: This study investigates the molecular mechanism of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 (ACE2) inhibition by the peptide DX600 using an integrated computational and biophysical approach. Small molecules and peptides have been explored as ACE2 antagonists, including MLN-4760 and the peptide DX600, but the molecular determinants underlying their inhibitory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. MLN-4760 is known to interact within the catalytic cleft of ACE2 thereby inducing structural changes in ACE2 causing the receptor to undergo a transition from opened to closed conformation. On the contrary, our molecular dynamics simulations reveal that DX600 binding stabilizes the receptor, dampening fluctuations of key residues such as to lock the receptor in an open conformation. This stabilization produces a more rigid ACE2 structure, consistent with steric hindrance that may impede viral protein, for example, the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, engagement. RMSF analysis, which quantifies local structural fluctuations at the residue level, confirms that DX600 reduces local residue mobility, highlighting a distinct mechanism from small-molecule inhibitors. These results provide a detailed molecular picture of peptide-mediated ACE2 inhibition and offer insights for the rational design of ACE2-targeted small molecule therapeutics.

title: Modeling and simulation methods used in the maritime industry: evolution, applications and future perspectives
abstract: Modeling and simulation (M&S) techniques have evolved from optional engineering tools to indispensable pillars of modern maritime practice. This article presents a comprehensive systematic review of the most important modeling and simulation methodologies applied to maritime industry processes, including workflows for ship design, shipyard fabrication and construction, port and terminal operations, vessel traffic management, maintenance scheduling, supply chain logistics, and risk management procedures. The study demonstrates that M&S techniques enable safer, more efficient, and more environmentally sustainable operations, validated by scientific standards. The COVID-19 pandemic served as a critical catalyst, consolidating the strategic value of M&S as a central component of maritime resilience and innovation. This research traces the evolution of M&S adoption from 2010 to 2025, identifying four dominant research directions: maritime simulators, computational fluid dynamics (CFD)/finite element analysis (FEA), digital twins, and artificial intelligence-based methods. The analysis reveals that while traditional approaches dominated the 2010-2020 period, emerging technologies—particularly digital twins and AI-based methods—have accelerated exponentially since 2020, reflecting the maritime industry's accelerated digitalization. Forward projections through 2035 indicate that AI-based methodologies will experience the highest growth rate at approximately 329%, followed by digital twins at 147%, underscoring the fundamental transformation of maritime research and practice. The integration of these advanced modeling approaches offers optimal equilibrium between physical precision and computational efficiency for addressing complex maritime challenges.

title: A novel secretome rewrites the immune response in viral acute respiratory distress syndrome
abstract: Background Hyperinflammatory syndromes such as viral acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) demand immunotherapies that are safe and effective at suppressing cytokine storm. Cell-free secretomes such as PRS CK STORM, derived from cocultures of M2 macrophages and mesenchymal stromal cells, may represent a novel treatment strategy for ARDS. Methods A preclinical animal study was performed to test the effects of PRS CK STORM in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice infected intranasally with 10 5 PFU of SARS-CoV-2 BE.1.1. This was complemented by an in vitro mechanistic analysis of this secretome using transcriptomic, cytokine secretion, and COX2 enzymatic activity studies, as well as a compositional analysis of its proteomic and miRNA profile. Results In a lethal SARS-CoV-2 ARDS mouse model, PRS CK STORM significantly improved lung histopathology to a degree on par with corticosteroids, while stimulating angiogenesis in damaged lung tissue. Early and late cytokine profiling showed marked reductions in IFN-γ. In response to PRS CK STORM treatment, transcriptomic analyses in inflamed macrophages revealed robust downregulation of key proinflammatory drivers (MyD88, TRAF6, IKK2, NF-κB, COX2). In vitro enzymatic assays confirmed potent, dose-dependent inhibition of COX2, with high inter-batch reproducibility. A compositional analysis revealed this secretome to be rich in anti-inflammatory miRNAs, immune-modulating proteins, and regenerative factors. Conclusions PRS CK STORM operates as a multi-target immune recalibrator, enabling broad downregulation of pathological inflammation while promoting tissue repair in the context of ARDS.

title: Behind the Breathlessness: Defining Pulmonary Phenotypes in Post-COVID Syndrome.
abstract: Background Persistent respiratory symptoms after COVID-19 may conceal distinct pulmonary disorders despite normal routine lung function. We characterized clinical phenotypes and three-month physiological outcomes. Methods This retrospective single-center study included all 122 eligible patients. Multimodal evaluation informed phenotype-directed management. Available paired measurements were compared with two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment across 10 parameters; a separate sensitivity analysis carried baseline values forward when follow-up was missing. Results Alveolitis/ILD-dominant, bronchiolitis-dominant, and asthma-dominant presentations accounted for 61 (50.0%), 47 (38.5%), and 11 (9.0%) patients; 3 (2.5%) remained unclassified. Baseline routine lung function was categorized as normal in 98 (80.3%). Median paired changes were +2 percentage points for FEV1 (adjusted p=0.0032), +1 for FVC (p=0.0036), +2 for DLCO (p=0.0032), and -7 for RV/TLC expressed as percent predicted (p=0.0432). Paired sample sizes differed by parameter. Carrying baseline forward did not alter the signed-rank p-values. Conclusion Multimodal assessment identified pulmonary phenotypes alongside modest physiological changes after treatment. These uncontrolled observations do not establish treatment efficacy or a measured quality-of-life benefit and require prospective controlled validation.

title: Mode of T-cell priming durably shapes the TCR repertoire, effector function, and α4β1 integrin expression of human virus-specific CD4+ T cells
abstract: The generation of an effective T-cell response against an antigen depends on the recognition of the antigen by the T-cell receptor (TCR), followed by T-cell priming, initiating coordinated biophysical, biochemical and proliferative changes that drive differentiation into effector and memory clones. The immunological environments in which priming occurs, such as natural infection or vaccination, influence the quality and persistence of memory T cells, but the long-term impacts remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigate how the mode of priming shapes durable antigen-specific CD4 + T-cell memory, utilising two cohorts 3–4 years after initial antigen encounter: individuals recovered from SARS-CoV-2 infection and infection-naive individuals who received a SARS-CoV-2 vaccination. Using ex vivo single-cell RNA sequencing, paired TCR sequencing and in vitro functional analyses, we characterise the transcriptional, clonal and functional profile of spike-specific CD4 + T cells. Across both cohorts, CD4 + T-cell responses against spike epitopes S 166–180 , S 751–765 and S 866–880 were immunodominant, with shared public TCR clonotypes indicating conserved antigen-recognition regardless of mode of priming. Despite this shared specificity, infection-primed individuals exhibited greater diversity of the TCR repertoire and lower convergence of CDR3αβ sequences. Transcriptionally, infection-primed cells exhibited a more cytotoxic and effector phenotype, while vaccine-primed cells preferentially adopted T follicular helper (Tfh)- and Th1-associated phenotypes. Infection-primed individuals also displayed enrichment of cell adhesion and integrin signalling pathways, with a greater proportion of spike-specific CD4 + T cells expressing α4β1 integrin subunits, consistent with enhanced migratory and effector potential. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the mode of antigen priming may influence long-term CD4 + T-cell memory states, influencing TCR repertoire diversity, functional differentiation and tissue-homing potential, years after the initial immune response.

title: The RdRp Thumb-1 Pocket Is a Conserved Target for Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Development
abstract: RNA viruses cause human diseases ranging from mild colds to deadly pandemics. Direct-acting, broad-spectrum, non-nucleoside antivirals have been characterized as impossible to develop because allosteric binding sites are poorly conserved. The HCV NS5B RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) Thumb-1 allosteric site and its interaction with the HCV NS5B Λ1-loop governs an essential conformational change required for polymerase initiation. The only approved NS5B Thumb-1 inhibitor, beclabuvir, has been shown to be inactive against a broad panel of non-HCV viruses, including poliovirus, rhinovirus, coronavirus, coxsackievirus, influenzavirus, and HIV. A conserved, homologous allosteric site on RdRp that spans multiple viral families has not been reported. Here, we report GALILEO’s discovery that the Thumb-1 pocket, its associated Λ1-loop and their interaction are conserved between RNA viral families for the first time. The discovery is structurally validated through comparative analysis of Protein Data Bank (PDB)-deposited viral polymerases utilizing a method that allows independent, public validation. We further demonstrate that beclabuvir’s dependence on its indole C6 carbonyl to interact with the HCV-specific residue R503 restricts its activity to HCV. The discovery is biochemically validated with MDL-001, which does not contain a C6 carbonyl substituent. MDL-001 directly blocks viral RNA synthesis in isolated HCV and SARS-CoV-2 replication complexes and selects for the canonical Thumb-1 resistance mutation P495S in HCV NS5B. The discovery is validated at the cellular level through demonstration of MDL-001’s broad-spectrum, in vitro inhibition of both HCV and SARS-CoV-2. Preclinical proof of concept and development of MDL-001 in HCV, HBV, HDV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and RSV have been previously reported. These findings establish RdRp Thumb-1 as a conserved allosteric pocket and a druggable target for broad-spectrum direct-acting antiviral development.

title: Feline intestinal organoids reveal cell type-specific tropism and antiviral responses to type II feline infectious peritonitis virus
abstract: Feline infectious peritonitis virus (FIPV), a highly pathogenic feline coronavirus (FCoV), causes a nearly uniformly fatal disease in cats, yet its infection dynamics within the intestinal epithelium-the primary site of viral entry and replication-remain largely unresolved. Here, we report the first establishment of long-term, passageable three-dimensional (3D) feline intestinal organoids, including feline ileal organoids (fILOs) and feline colonic organoids (fCOs), which faithfully recapitulate the cellular diversity and architecture of the feline intestine and support infection by type II FIPV. Using this physiologically relevant platform, we demonstrate that FIPV infection induces profound epithelial remodeling in fCOs, characterized by a marked expansion of proliferative cell populations and depletion of differentiated epithelial lineages. High-resolution single-cell RNA sequencing of fCOs revealed pronounced cell type-specific viral tropism, with preferential infection of differentiated epithelial cells, particularly goblet and tuft cells, while stem and transit-amplifying cells exhibited relative resistance. This differential susceptibility was strongly associated with cell type-specific expression of host entry and trafficking factors, including aminopeptidase N (APN), TMPRSS2, and Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Importantly, our organoid-based infection model recapitulated in vivo-relevant antiviral responses, enabling robust evaluation of therapeutic candidates and accurately reflecting the potent antiviral efficacy of GS-441524 and the neutralizing antibody 1AF10. Collectively, this study establishes a novel, scalable, and physiologically faithful feline intestinal organoid platform that provides unprecedented insight into type II FIPV epithelial tropism and pathogenesis, and represents a powerful preclinical tool for accelerating the development of effective antiviral and preventive strategies against feline infectious peritonitis.

title: The molecular interactions of viruses with apolipoproteins: Evidence, Mechanisms, and Therapeutic Implications.
abstract: Host lipid metabolism is extensively hijacked by viruses to support their replication cycle. Apolipoproteins, the core protein components of lipoprotein particles, mediate lipid transport, receptor recognition, and immune regulation, making them key host targets for diverse viruses. This review systematically examines the molecular mechanisms underlying virus-apolipoprotein interactions and establishes a classification framework distinguishing direct from indirect modes of action. Direct interactions involve physical binding between viral components and apolipoproteins or their receptors, exemplified by hepatitis C virus (HCV) ApoE-dependent lipoviroparticle assembly, hepatitis B virus (HBV) ApoE-mediated entry, Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) spike protein binding to high-density lipoprotein (HDL)-associated apolipoproteins, and rabies virus ApoD-glycoprotein interaction. Indirect mechanisms include viral regulation of apolipoprotein expression through epigenetic modifications, cytokines, and oxidative stress. We also compare the differential effects of ApoE2, ApoE3, and ApoE4 subtypes on infection susceptibility and disease severity across HCV, human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1), and SARS-CoV-2. The clinical-pathological consequences, including hepatic steatosis, atherosclerosis (AS), dyslipidemia, and thrombotic complications, are discussed, and therapeutic strategies targeting lipid metabolism are critically evaluated. We close by outlining unresolved questions and suggesting future research directions leveraging single-cell multi-omics, spatial biology, and organoid models.

title: Monolith, porous bead, membrane or fibre? A comparative characterisation of four oligo-dT affinity chromatography matrices for mRNA capture
abstract: Oligo-deoxythymidine (oligo dT) affinity chromatography is the most widely used capture step for in vitro transcribed mRNA and is now offered in four stationary-phase architectures, yet, to our knowledge, no published study has compared all four. We characterised a monolith, perfusive porous beads, a membrane adsorber and an electrospun cellulose fibre adsorber with a short (eGFP, 930 nt) and a long (SARS CoV 2 spike, S 2P, 4284 nt) mRNA. After screening the loading salt (NaCl or guanidine hydrochloride, Gu HCl), we mapped load flow rate, load concentration and Gu HCl concentration with response surface designs and compared the formats at near-optimal conditions. Gu HCl gave a higher peak recovery than NaCl in seven of the eight matrix construct combinations. At the near-optimal runs, the fibre adsorber recovered 17.9 mg eGFP and 13.3 mg S 2P per mL of bed, 2.3 to 2.6 fold the membrane and 3.5- to 4.8-fold the monolith and beads (p membrane > monolith > beads (0.314 to 0.035 mg/mL/min for eGFP). The membrane and fibre adsorber lost yield sharply above 0.4 to 0.6 M Gu HCl, whereas the monolith and beads declined gradually. In an amortised cost model at baseline cost inputs, the fibre adsorber was the least expensive format per milligram of purified mRNA at every number of device cycles (USD 114 to 140/mg for single use and 78 to 92/mg at 20 cycles), and the membrane the most expensive. A one at a time sensitivity analysis over wide ranges of the mRNA feed cost, the labour and facility rate, the device price and the number of cycles per device left the fibre adsorber the least expensive format in almost every combination examined, with the mRNA feed cost the dominant input. Only the monolith and beads are currently marketed as GMP grade, process scale materials, so the choice of format depends on whether capacity, productivity, cost or manufacturing readiness takes priority.

title: Environmental stochasticity can account for patterns of within-host respiratory virus evolution.
abstract: The ecological and evolutionary dynamics of populations, including viral populations, are known to be jointly shaped by deterministic and stochastic processes. While the impact of stochastic processes has been rigorously explored for viral dynamics at the level of the host population, most dynamic models for acutely infecting respiratory viral pathogens at the within-host scale remain deterministic in their formulation. Although deterministic formulations may be reasonable for identifying key processes shaping within-host viral population dynamics, recent studies indicate that stochastic processes need to be invoked for understanding patterns of within-host viral evolution. Specifically, several studies have shown that viral allele frequencies can change dramatically over the time course of days in acute infections. Here, we use stochastic dynamic models to explore the role of environmental noise in shaping observed patterns of virus evolution in acute respiratory virus infections. We summarize ways in which environmental stochasticity can be biologically realized in these acute viral infections and describe within-host models that can be implemented to jointly yield viral population dynamics and evolutionary dynamics. We further develop a statistical approach to estimate the extent of environmental noise from observed within-host allele frequency changes, both in the absence and in the presence of additional measurement noise. We test this approach on simulated data and apply it to existing influenza A virus and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 within-host data. With these applications, we show that environmental stochasticity can parsimoniously reproduce key features of empirically observed allele frequency changes. We additionally show that these features differ from those derived under a Wright-Fisher model formulation with a constant effective population size and that the model incorporating environmental stochasticity performs better than the Wright-Fisher model when interfaced with empirical data. Finally, we show that both purifying selection and positive selection can still contribute to within-host viral evolution in the context of environmental noise, providing theoretical support for studies that have found evidence of purifying and positive selection in acutely infecting within-host respiratory virus populations.

title: Inferring Locations and Correcting Bias in Infectious Disease Data Using Human Mobility
abstract: Understanding and reconstructing infectious disease transmission remains challenging due to sparsely sampled and biased epidemiological case data: only a small fraction of infectious disease cases are reported to health authorities, and an even smaller fraction are sent to labs for genomic sequencing. In this work, we study the problem of inferring unobserved transmission events by integrating pathogen genomic data with human mobility information. Intuitively, even if we do not have case data for a certain region, such as a census block group, we can use massive-scale individual mobility data to understand where people may be exposed and infer where unobserved cases may be located. Assuming only a subset of cases are reported and sequenced, we reconstruct a phylogenetic tree from observed cases and transform it into a partial transmission tree using the outbreaker2 tool. This tree contains inferred transmissions based on the genetic distance of the observed cases. As these inferred nodes have unknown locations, we propose a mobility-aware belief propagation approach to estimate their locations using human mobility data. Experiments on simulated and real-world genomic surveillance data with biased sampling show that incorporating mobility data improves the reconstruction of inferred transmission trees, reducing cross-entropy relative to the observed distribution by 39.4% and 16.1%, respectively. Results on real-world COVID-19 sequence data show the promise of combining genomic and mobility data for more reliable location inference, with potential implications for outbreak analysis and public health decision-making.

title: Risk of respiratory infections in closed communities: multi-dimensional risk assessment and integrated surveillance in a nursing home and a prison (Stell-ARI project)
abstract: Viral Acute Respiratory Infections (ARIs) are particularly relevant for people living in closed and vulnerable communities. The Stell-ARI Project aimed to design and apply a multi-dimensional framework integrating environmental risk assessment (based on building structure and management, resident population characteristics, indoor air quality (IAQ), and microbiological contamination of air and surfaces) with wastewater-based and clinical surveillance for SARS-CoV-2, Human Adenovirus (HAdV), Influenza Virus A (IVA) and B (IVB), Respiratory Syncytial Virus A (RSVA) and B (RSVB). This system was applied in two pilot institutional communities: a nursing home and a prison. The study design included questionnaire surveys of facility managers, residents and workers alongside environmental monitoring of chemical and microbial contaminants. Domain-specific and global risk scores were calculated. title: Focal Neurological Involvement in Adult-Onset Still Disease-Associated Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis: A Diagnostic Challenge
abstract: A woman in her late 40s with adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD), previously independent in mobility, personal care, and cognition, presented with fever, sore throat, and a diffuse erythematous eruption involving the palms, soles, and lower limbs. Her medical history was also significant for established hepatitis B infection, for which she had been receiving long-term entecavir therapy. Her regular immunomodulatory medications included anakinra 100 mg subcutaneously once daily and methotrexate 20 mg subcutaneously weekly, alongside folic acid; prednisolone had recently been discontinued. Anakinra and methotrexate were temporarily withheld for one week on rheumatology advice due to concerns regarding COVID-19 infection. Investigations revealed marked hyperferritinemia, with ferritin peaking at 23,321 μg/L, hypertriglyceridaemia, hypofibrinogenaemia, liver dysfunction and a peak HScore of 214, a diagnostic scoring system for reactive haemophagocytic syndrome supporting a diagnosis of haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), also termed macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) in the context of rheumatological disease. A SARS-CoV-2 reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) was positive; severe COVID-19 pneumonitis was considered a potential infectious trigger. The patient subsequently developed type 1 respiratory failure requiring admission to the intensive care unit (ICU). Despite treatment with corticosteroids and escalation of anakinra, her clinical course was complicated by profound encephalopathy, aphasia and focal neurological deficits. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated left temporoparietal restricted diffusion and superficial pial enhancement, while ophthalmological assessment identified a right homonymous hemianopia. Electroencephalography (EEG) demonstrated persistent left hemispheric dysfunction. Despite extensive infectious investigations identifying potential contributing pathogens, no single definitive trigger for HLH/MAS could be established. National multidisciplinary review considered a broad differential diagnosis for the neurological abnormalities, including central nervous system involvement secondary to HLH, peri-ictal changes, cerebral ischaemia, viral infection and occult intravascular lymphoma. This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of HLH/MAS, in which multiple potential triggers and overlapping neurological manifestations may prevent identification of a single underlying aetiology despite extensive investigation. New-onset encephalopathy, aphasia, seizures or focal neurological deficits in patients with HLH/MAS should prompt early neurological assessment, appropriate MRI, EEG and cerebrospinal fluid investigations, and multidisciplinary specialist input. Neuroimaging findings should be interpreted alongside clinical, laboratory and other investigative findings, maintaining a broad differential diagnosis rather than prematurely attributing abnormalities to a single cause.

title: Vaccine Injury: Recognition, Research and Re-establishing Trust
abstract: Background : Patients who report serious health changes following vaccination frequently face barriers to recognition, coordinated evaluation, and treatment. The October 5, 2026, Health and Human Services (HHS) Vaccine Injury Roundtable at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) brought patient, family, physician, and federal leadership perspectives into direct dialogue and highlighted an urgent need for compassionate care and rigorous inquiry. Clinical Perspectives : Three physicians described distinct but overlapping concerns. A pediatrician with extensive experience caring for children with autism and complex chronic illness called for research into biologic susceptibility, post-vaccination regression, and treatment strategies for affected children. A second pediatrician raised questions about chronic inflammation, neurodevelopmental conditions, vaccine components, and the need for research into individual vulnerability and long-term outcomes. A neurologist described complex, multi-system presentations among patients with suspected post-acute coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination syndrome, including neurologic, autonomic, cognitive, cardiopulmonary, and immune-related symptoms. Call to Action : The authors commend HHS and NIH for establishing a clinic to study patients reporting vaccine-related injuries. However, the national need is for urgent clinical care and educating clinicians on how to deliver it. Priority actions include prospective longitudinal studies; standardized clinical phenotyping; transparent case definitions; improved adverse-event surveillance; research into genetic, metabolic, mitochondrial, immunologic, and inflammatory susceptibility factors; and a national network of multidisciplinary referral and treatment centers. Conclusions : Patient testimony should be treated as a starting point for clinical care and scientific inquiry. Restoring trust requires institutions to listen without prejudice, investigate uncertainty openly, report adverse events effectively, and ensure that no patient reporting vaccine-related injury is left without care, recognition, or hope.

title: Timing of de novo vaccination during pregnancy impacts maternal and newborn immunity
abstract: Maternal immunity is essential for protecting both the pregnant individual and fetus, balancing immune tolerance with defense against infection. While maternal vaccination enhances protection, the impact of gestational timing on antibody responses and transplacental antibody transfer remains unclear. The COVID-19 pandemic provided a unique opportunity to study primary SARS-CoV-2 vaccine-induced humoral responses in individuals without documented prior SARS-CoV-2 infection or vaccination. To investigate how vaccination timing shapes maternal and fetal immunity, we performed comprehensive serological profiling in 263 individuals, including 96 maternal–neonatal dyads, sampled across pregnancy and at delivery. Leveraging natural variation in SARS-CoV-2 vaccine timing, we assessed antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 and 13 additional pathogens using Systems Serology, analyzing isotypes, subclasses, FcγR binding, glycosylation, neutralization, and Fc-mediated functions. Pregnant individuals maintained stable immunity to previously encountered antigens (from past infections or vaccinations) and mounted expected responses to pertussis and tetanus boosters. Initial responses to COVID-19 mRNA vaccination were attenuated in third-trimester vaccinees but reached comparable levels after the second dose. Enhanced responses to unrelated antigens, such as poliovirus and measles, were observed, particularly in later gestation, potentially due to cross-reactivity. Antibody transfer was most efficient following late second to early third trimester vaccination, with decreased transfer in the late third trimester. Fetal sex also influenced antibody transfer efficiency, favoring male fetuses in the third trimester. These findings underscore the importance of vaccine timing to optimize maternal and neonatal immunity.

title: From APT to APBT: a taxonomy and large-scale metadata exposure audit of genomic surveillance infrastructure
abstract: Introduction Open genomic repositories are critical infrastructure for pathogen surveillance, variant tracking, outbreak reconstruction, and public health decision making, yet many were designed primarily for rapid scientific data sharing rather than adversarial verification. In cybersecurity, Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) describe long duration, strategically coordinated campaigns against digital systems. This paper extends that logic to genomic surveillance by introducing Advanced Persistent Biological Threats (APBTs): persistent cyber biological campaigns in which malicious actors target sequence data, metadata, reference datasets, and analytical models to degrade surveillance reliability over time. We present, to our knowledge, the first integrated multilayer taxonomy of APBTs, structured around a four phase lifecycle, and examine whether metadata conditions relevant to this threat model are present in an operational genomic repository ecosystem. Methods We audited 100,000 SARS-CoV-2 NCBI BioSample records using 23 checks across five metadata layers: temporal, geographic, host and specimen, provenance and administrative, and technical and analytical. Where selected provenance or technical information was unavailable in BioSample, linked BioProject, SRA, and Nucleotide/GenBank resources were examined before an exposure indicator was assigned. Results Every record triggered at least one APBT relevant metadata exposure indicator. The mean composite exposure score was 5.22 (SD = 2.37), and 51.5% of records were classified as High or Critical. Exposure affected 3.8% of records in the temporal layer, 0.5% in the geographic layer, 52.0% in host and specimen metadata, 74.2% in provenance and administrative metadata, and 100.0% in technical and analytical metadata. Cross repository retrieval recovered substantial information not visible in BioSample alone, particularly for BioProject association, sequence linkage, sequencing platform, and assembly method. Information on who collected the sample was absent from 51.3% of records, while BioProject association remained unavailable for 28.8% after linked NCBI resources were examined. Discussion The findings do not demonstrate deliberate metadata poisoning. However, the structural incompleteness of BioSample metadata creates vulnerabilities that an adversary can exploit to introduce poisoned, misleading, or weakly traceable metadata into genomic repositories. As a result, maliciously altered metadata can appear plausible, remain undetected, and influence downstream genomic analysis and surveillance.

title: Period-specific differences in clinical characteristics of hospitalized children with Epstein–Barr virus infection: a single-center retrospective study
abstract: Objective This study aimed to compare the demographic characteristics, laboratory parameters, major clinical complications, and comorbidities of hospitalized children with Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) infection across three calendar periods—2018–2019, 2020–2022, and 2023–2025—and to describe temporal changes in the characteristics of hospitalized cases during periods broadly overlapping with different phases of the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods The study period was divided into three calendar periods: 2018–2019, 2020–2022, and 2023–2025, which broadly overlapped with different phases of the COVID-19 pandemic. This temporal classification was used solely to describe period-specific differences in the clinical and laboratory characteristics of hospitalized children with EBV infection and was not intended to infer causal effects of the COVID-19 pandemic or related public health measures on EBV infection. The numbers of hospitalized children included in the three periods were 39, 96, and 307, respectively, resulting in marked imbalance in group sizes. Annual case numbers also varied substantially, with 4 cases in 2018, 35 in 2019, 2 in 2020, 21 in 2021, 73 in 2022, and 117, 119, and 71 cases in 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively. Results The age distribution differed across periods (χ2 = 20.07, P < 0.001), with older children accounting for a larger proportion in 2023–2025. EBV nuclear antigen antibody and viral capsid antigen IgG levels were higher in 2020–2022 than in the other periods, whereas plasma EBV-DNA levels were lower. Infection-status classification was available for 267 children, with substantial differences in data completeness across periods. Non-severe pneumonia showed a nominal period difference (P = 0.046); no statistically significant differences were detected for the other evaluated clinical outcomes. Documented coinfection occurred in 206 children (46.61%) and was associated with higher odds of non-severe pneumonia (OR = 2.63, 95% CI: 1.79–3.87) and severe pneumonia (OR = 5.23, 95% CI: 1.47–18.62), but lower odds of liver function impairment (OR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.15–0.68). Hospitalization costs were higher in 2023–2025. Conclusion Across the three calendar periods broadly overlapping with different phases of the COVID-19 pandemic, hospitalized children with EBV infection showed temporal differences in age distribution, selected laboratory parameters, and the distribution of EBV infection status. Infection-status analysis indicated a lower proportion of acute primary infection in 2020–2022 than in 2023–2025; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because of differences in the completeness of infection-status classification across periods. These findings reflect period-specific characteristics of hospitalized children and should not be interpreted as evidence of changes in EBV epidemiology in the general pediatric population.

Results The age distribution differed across periods (χ2 = 20.07, P < 0.001), with older children accounting for a larger proportion in 2023–2025. EBV nuclear antigen antibody and viral capsid antigen IgG levels were higher in 2020–2022 than in the other periods, whereas plasma EBV-DNA levels were lower. Infection-status classification was available for 267 children, with substantial differences in data completeness across periods. Non-severe pneumonia showed a nominal period difference (P = 0.046); no statistically significant differences were detected for the other evaluated clinical outcomes. Documented coinfection occurred in 206 children (46.61%) and was associated with higher odds of non-severe pneumonia (OR = 2.63, 95% CI: 1.79–3.87) and severe pneumonia (OR = 5.23, 95% CI: 1.47–18.62), but lower odds of liver function impairment (OR = 0.31, 95% CI: 0.15–0.68). Hospitalization costs were higher in 2023–2025. Conclusion Across the three calendar periods broadly overlapping with different phases of the COVID-19 pandemic, hospitalized children with EBV infection showed temporal differences in age distribution, selected laboratory parameters, and the distribution of EBV infection status. Infection-status analysis indicated a lower proportion of acute primary infection in 2020–2022 than in 2023–2025; however, this finding should be interpreted cautiously because of differences in the completeness of infection-status classification across periods. These findings reflect period-specific characteristics of hospitalized children and should not be interpreted as evidence of changes in EBV epidemiology in the general pediatric population.
