title: From Bench to Bedside: Clinical Translation of Electrochemical Biosensors for Viral Diagnostics
abstract: Electrochemical biosensors have emerged as promising platforms for rapid viral diagnostics, offering high analytical sensitivity, portability, short detection times, and potential compatibility with point-of-care testing. Advances in electrode nanostructuring, biorecognition strategies, signal amplification, and miniaturized instrumentation have enabled remarkably low limits of detection, reaching femtomolar and attomolar concentrations for synthetic viral targets under optimized experimental conditions. However, exceptional analytical performance under controlled conditions does not necessarily translate into clinical diagnostic utility. This review examines the progression of electrochemical biosensors from analytical proof-of-concept toward clinical application, emphasizing the evidence required for successful translation. Following a brief overview of viral targets, recognition strategies, and electrochemical detection approaches, particular attention is given to studies evaluating authentic clinical specimens, including those targeting SARS-CoV-2, dengue virus, human papillomavirus, and hepatitis C virus. Despite encouraging findings, clinical validation remains limited by small sample sizes, incomplete reporting of diagnostic sensitivity and specificity, and insufficient multicentre evaluation, while many platforms have been assessed only using artificial or spiked matrices. Additional challenges include matrix interference, biofouling, reproducibility, sample preparation, manufacturing consistency, stability, workflow integration, and regulatory requirements. Importantly, analytical limits of detection must be interpreted in relation to viral biology, specimen characteristics, clinically relevant thresholds, and intended clinical use. Future research should prioritize reproducible sample-to-answer performance over increasingly extreme analytical sensitivity. Accordingly, this review proposes a staged translational framework encompassing native-matrix analytical validation, adequately powered clinical studies, multicentre reproducibility, manufacturing and usability assessments, and regulatory evaluation. Ultimately, the clinical adoption of electrochemical biosensors will depend on robust evidence demonstrating reliable diagnostic performance in real-world healthcare settings.

title: Standardized Annotation of Quantitative Proteomics Datasets Using SDRF-Proteomics.
abstract: Proteomics datasets require detailed and standardized metadata annotation to ensure reproducibility, reusability, and alignment with FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) principles. This chapter presents a practical, hands-on workflow for annotating a label-free proteomics dataset using the Sample and Data Relationship Format for Proteomics (SDRF-Proteomics), a HUPO-PSI and EuBIC-MS standard that has been adopted by major proteomics data repositories. We demonstrate the process on a COVID-19 nasal-swab dataset (PXD020394), showing how to derive sample and assay metadata from the study files, encode them in SDRF with the lesSDRF web application, and validate the result. Although the worked example is label-free, the approach can be generalized to other quantification strategies.

title: LmPro-Nano: a method for nanobody optimization using pretrained language and energy prediction models
abstract: Nanobodies are an important therapeutic scaffold for multiple diseases and have been shown to neutralize severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). However, optimizing affinity for a chosen antigen remains slow and expensive. Here, we present LmPro-Nano, a sequence-driven workflow coupling a pretrained nanobody language model with a structure-based binding-energy predictor and molecular dynamics. We demonstrate LmPro-Nano on 3-2A2-4 and VHH72, two nanobodies against the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain. We find that LmPro-Nano improves antigen-binding-loop recovery by 4.37 points over a frequency reference, and for VHH72, sequence-only localization of the binding region raised the top-ten hit rate from two to seven tighter binders.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics revealed immunological and molecular profiling of pangolin viruses at the viral interface.
abstract: Pangolins have been identified as potential intermediate hosts for various viruses, including coronaviruses related to SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-CoV, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying their viral susceptibility remain poorly understood. Here, we establish the first comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas for two pangolin species Manis pentadactyla and Manis javanica, generated through single-cell RNA sequencing of 246,813 high-quality cells from 12 major tissues, combined with bulk transcriptome profiling of 123 samples across multiple tissues. This resource is integrated with cross-species data from humans (Homo sapiens), the big brown bat (Eptesicus fuscus), domestic pigs (Sus scrofa), mice (Mus musculus), and tigers (Panthera tigris). Our analysis reveals a myeloid-biased hematopoiesis in pangolin bone marrow, dominated by monocyte and T cell, which contrasts sharply with the lymphoid-skewed composition observed in Homo sapiens and Mus musculus. We also identify species-specific features, including thyroid-specific expression of FKBP5 in Manis pentadactyla validated by qRT-PCR and western blot, suggestive of a role in immune-endocrine crosstalk, and MIF-signaling-mediated cellular interactions in intestinal lymphoid tissue. Furthermore, key viral entry factors (AXL, NRP1, DPP4, ACE2, SCARB1, UVRAG) are broadly expressed in immune cell (e.g., B cell, T cell, macrophage), fibroblast, and endothelial cell across tissues, as confirmed by both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses. Cross-species comparisons uncover fundamental differences in splenic immune architecture, hematopoietic lineage distribution, and viral receptor expression. Together, these findings, reinforced by transcriptomic and molecular experimental validation, establish a molecular and cellular framework for understanding pangolins as potential mixing vessels for viruses and provide a foundation for targeted surveillance of emerging zoonotic pathogens.

title: ARE-Wochenbericht des RKI KW46
abstract: Die ARE-Aktivität auf Bevölkerungsebene und im ambulanten Bereich befindet sich aktuell auf einem moderaten Niveau; im stationären Bereich befindet sie sich auf einem niedrigen Niveau. Das AREGeschehen wird weiterhin hauptsächlich durch Rhino-/Enteroviren bestimmt. Jedoch zeigt sich seit Saisonbeginn ein Anstieg der SARS-CoV-2- und Influenzavirus-Zirkulation in den verschiedenen Systemen. Zudem ist ein Anstieg in der Erkrankungsaktivität von Influenza und COVID-19 zu beobachten. In den Proben der virologischen ARE-Surveillance wurden seit Saisonbeginn in jeder Woche Influenzaviren detektiert, vorwiegend Influenza A(H1N1)pdm09-Viren.

title: Seamless household epidemiological modelling with housepi
abstract: Mathematical modelling has proven to be a valuable tool for estimating key epidemiological parameters from household transmission studies. The relative ease of sampling household data makes it a readily available source of information during the early phases of an epidemic. In addition, retrospective serological household data can provide critical insights into the history of transmission within a population. Given the well-defined contact structures and natural exposure to infection, households provide an ideal setting for evaluating the efficacy of pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical interventions. Despite its importance, epidemiological modelling of household transmission remains technically demanding, and accessible, well-documented inference tools are sparse. To address this gap, we introduce housepi, an open source R package for the statistical analysis and modelling of household transmission studies. The unified framework enables both simulations and Bayesian inference, with individual data augmentation to handle unobserved variables. This allows estimating infection risk factors for both final-size designs and case-ascertained longitudinal follow-ups with temporal records (such as test and onset dates). The package provides a streamlined workflow that allows users, with minimal configuration, to move from raw household data to posterior estimates of key epidemiological quantities, including secondary attack rates, and the effects of interventions and transmission risk factors, such as vaccine effectiveness. We demonstrate some capabilities of the package on publicly available datasets, covering the cases of influenza and SARS-CoV-2. Using the package routines, we validate our estimates on simulated data, and we show that fitted models can reproduce the target observations. The results are coherent with the original studies associated with the data. The modular design of housepi further facilitates extension to user-defined features, making it a versatile tool for future epidemiological investigations.

title: Physical-Measure Merton Jump-Diffusion Calibration Surrogates and Direct Realized Volatility Forecasting: An Empirical and Numerical Audit on S&P 500 ETF (SPY) Returns
abstract: Abstract Continuous-time Geometric Brownian Motion (GBM) fails to capture the leptokurtic tails and sudden price discontinuities observed in equity index returns. While Merton’s (1976) Jump-Diffusion (MJD) model accounts for sudden shocks by superimposing a compound Poisson jump process onto Brownian diffusion, rolling physical-measure (\(\:P\)) Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) suffers from severe finite-sample weak identification, Kiefer (1978) mixture singularities, and iterative computational overhead. In this study, we design, audit, and evaluate a rigorous, leakage-free dual-task quantitative pipeline on daily S&P 500 ETF (SPY) returns (\(\:N=\text{1,237}\) validated sessions, 2019–2023). We explicitly separate two research questions that are frequently conflated in student and practitioner implementations: (Task 1) whether Ridge regression and hybrid sequence-summary Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks can serve as fast calibration surrogates for rolling 126-session multistart compound-Poisson MLE, and (Task 2) whether direct supervised volatility models or calibrated total-volatility proxies can forecast forward 21-session realized volatility better than classical historical persistence and RiskMetrics EWMA (\(\:{\lambda\:}_{ewma}=0.94\)) baselines. Across 211 chronological calibration windows (\(\:134\) Fit, \(\:31\) Validation, \(\:46\) Test) separated by an explicit \(\:H=21\)-session forward-label purge, raw five-parameter MJD fits hit box boundaries in \(\:165/211\) windows (\(\:78.2\%\)), while a conservative Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) parsimony rule against an exact nested two-parameter Gaussian submodel (\(\:\lambda\:=0\)) selects jumps in \(\:69/211\) windows (\(\:32.7\%\), concentrated entirely around the 2020 COVID-19 crash). Online surrogate inference achieves a \(\:63.9\times\:\) wall-clock speedup (\(\:0.359\:ms\) for Mean, Ridge, and LSTM combined versus \(\:22.939\:ms\) median multistart MLE), but 5-session parameter persistence (\(\:{\widehat{\theta\:}}_{t}={\widehat{\theta\:}}_{t-5}\)) outperforms ML surrogates on rolling 126-session labels (validation standardized MSE \(\:0.0268\) vs. \(\:1.8052\) for Ridge and \(\:2.2362\) for LSTM) due to \(\:96\%\) window overlap. On the held-out 2023 test split (\(\:n=46\)), the direct hybrid LSTM achieves the lowest future 21-session realized volatility RMSE (\(\:0.026553\), MAE \(\:0.023191\), Campbell–Thompson \(\:{R}_{oos}^{2}=+16.95\%\), \(\:r=0.5049\)), followed by direct Ridge (\(\:RMSE=0.028088\), \(\:{R}_{oos}^{2}=+7.07\%\)) and EWMA (\(\:RMSE=0.028179\), \(\:{R}_{oos}^{2}=+6.46\%\)), outperforming 21-session historical volatility (\(\:RMSE=0.029137\)). However, because chronological validation during the high-volatility 2022 bear market selected the 126-session calibrated total-volatility proxy (mle_total_vol, validation \(\:RMSE=0.056528\)), which subsequently lagged the 2023 volatility decline (\(\:test\:RMSE=0.050488\), \(\:{R}_{oos}^{2}=-200.26\%\)), freezing model selection prior to test evaluation prevents claiming consistent out-of-sample forecasting superiority without a fresh post-2023 holdout.

title: Metabolic reprogramming and immune-metabolic interactions in Respiratory viral infections
abstract: Respiratory viruses, including influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2, hijack host metabolic machinery to facilitate their replication and evade immune surveillance. This review synthesizes current evidence on the bidirectional interplay between viral-induced metabolic reprogramming – specifically the upregulation of glycolysis, lipogenesis, and glutaminolysis, and the disruption of mitochondrial homeostasis – and the host immune response. We highlight how this metabolic rewiring not only provides biosynthetic precursors for viral proliferation but also modulates immune cell differentiation and inflammatory outcomes. Furthermore, we discuss how preexisting host metabolic conditions (e.g. obesity, diabetes, aging) exacerbate disease severity through this metabolic-immune axis, and how persistent metabolic alterations may underlie post-acute sequelae such as Long COVID. Finally, we evaluate the therapeutic potential and challenges of targeting metabolic checkpoints, such as mTOR and SREBP, to balance antiviral efficacy with immune homeostasis. PubMed was searched for articles from database inception to July 2026.

title: Should the Lung Ultrasound Score Be Used to Evaluate Interstitial Syndrome Severity in Intensive Care Units? A Prospective Observational Study
abstract: Background: The correlation between the lung ultrasound score (LUSS), a quantitative point of care ultrasound (POCUS) method used to evaluate pulmonary interstitial syndrome (IS), and the arterial oxygen pressure-to-fraction of inspired oxygen (P/F) ratio, a severity marker for IS, has been demonstrated in small cohorts of COVID-19 patients, supporting the utility of LUSS as a reliable severity indicator for IS. This post-pandemic study investigated the same correlation in a larger cohort of intensive care unit (ICU) patients with IS of any etiology, potentially supporting the broader application of the LUSS as a severity indicator across all types of IS. Methods: This was a prospective multicentre observational study. A sample of adult patients who were admitted to the ICU with acute respiratory failure (ARF) and required arterial blood gas analysis (ABG) was used. The primary endpoint was to assess whether the correlation between the LUSS and P/F ratio in ICU patients with IS reached a prespecified magnitude (r = −0.70), defined a priori based on previous findings for sample size estimation. Results: In total, 86 patients were included. The results showed a weak negative linear correlation between LUSS and P/F ratio with a correlation of r = -0.2945 (95% CI: -0.4767 to -0.0881). Conclusion: In this heterogeneous ICU cohort, LUSS showed a weak correlation with P/F ratio. This suggests that although LUSS is a useful tool for assessing disease severity in COVID-19 pneumonia, it may not be appropriate as a standalone severity marker of IS.

title: Longitudinal Analysis of Candida Antifungal Susceptibility and Epidemiological Shifts at a Jordanian Tertiary Hospital (2019–2024)
abstract: Background: Fungal infections from Candida species pose a clinical threat due to changing distributions and emerging resistance. Shifts in species, antifungal susceptibility and factors associated with length of hospital stay were studied at a tertiary hospital in Jordan from 2019 to 2024. Methods: A retrospective study analyzed microbiology records at Jordan University Hospital. Isolates were identified with CHROMagar Candida and automated Vitek 2 Compact System. Antifungal susceptibility testing (AST) was CLSI M60-based. Mucosal colonization in non-blood specimens was excluded from clinical criteria. Amphotericin B activity was assessed against Epidemiological Cutoff Values (ECVs) of CLSI M60 and azole Susceptible-Dose-Dependent (S-DD) categories were examined explicitly. Trends before the COVID-19 pandemic and after the pandemic were analyzed using denominator-adjusted species proportions. Results: A total of 182 clinical isolates were analyzed. albicans (53.8%) dominated, followed by non-albicans Candida (NAC) species (especially C. Voriconazole was the most susceptible (92.9%), while fluconazole showed the lowest susceptibility (63.7%), influenced by resistance in C. krusei (100% resistant) and low susceptibility in C. glabrata (2.4% S-DD). Amphotericin B Wild-Type (WT) profile rate is 91.2% (166/182 isolates; MIC ≤ 2.0 ug/mL per CLSI M60 ECVs), whereas C. glabrata showed an automated resistance signal to caspofungin, with 76.2% having an MIC ≥ 0.5 μg/mL, representing an automated screening signal requiring confirmatory reference broth microdilution testing. Species proportions changed significantly across COVID-19 periods (p < 0.001): C. albicans predominated during the pandemic (70.9%), whereas NAC species extended post-pandemic. Multivariable logistic regression identified patient’s age to be a predictor of hospital length of stay (LOS) ≥ 21 days (OR = 0.982, 95% CI: 0.971–0.993, p = 0.001). glabrata showed significant resistance to conventional azoles in Jordan. Automated echinocandin resistance signals need confirmatory reference testing before updating clinical guidelines. Standardized clinical infection criteria, routine AST, and institutional antifungal stewardship programs are robust in tertiary hospitals in Jordan.

title: Kynurenine Pathway Activation and Host-Response Heterogeneity in Acute Hypoxemic Respiratory Failure
abstract: Background/Objectives: Host-response phenotyping has emerged as a promising strategy for precision medicine in critical illness, but whether tryptophan catabolism through the kynurenine pathway is associated with organ dysfunction across data-derived inflammatory profiles remains unclear. Methods: We investigated associations between the kynurenine-to-tryptophan ratio (Kyn/Trp), a surrogate marker of tryptophan catabolism; neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR); and organ dysfunction in patients with COVID-19-associated acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF). Baseline data-derived inflammatory phenotypes, descriptively designated hyperinflammatory-like and hypoinflammatory-like, were identified using a locally fitted Gaussian mixture model based on routinely available clinical and laboratory variables adapted from a previously published ARDS phenotyping framework. Associations between day-3 Kyn/Trp and organ dysfunction were evaluated using multivariable restricted cubic spline regression adjusted for baseline SOFA score, baseline Kyn/Trp, age, and sex. Longitudinal mixed-effects models examined associations between Kyn/Trp and clinical outcomes, while exploratory interaction analyses assessed whether the relationship between Kyn/Trp and NLR differed according to baseline phenotype. Results: Eighty-nine patients were included, of whom 38 (42.7%) were classified as hyperinflammatory-like. Higher day-3 Kyn/Trp was nonlinearly associated with greater predicted SOFA score (nonlinear p = 0.03). Longitudinal analyses showed higher Kyn/Trp levels among patients who met ARDS diagnostic criteria at day 3 and among those requiring invasive mechanical ventilation or ICU admission. The association between Kyn/Trp and NLR differed according to baseline phenotype (interaction β = 0.24, 95% CI 0.06–0.41; p = 0.008), with a positive association observed only in hyperinflammatory-like patients. Findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Conclusions: Higher Kyn/Trp was associated with greater organ dysfunction, while its relationship with NLR differed across locally derived inflammatory-like profiles. These exploratory findings suggest that Kyn/Trp may provide metabolic information complementary to NLR, without establishing IFN-specific activation or distinct biological endotypes. Validation in larger, independent cohorts, including non-COVID-19 populations, is warranted.

abstract: В настоящей работе проведено исследование по изучению реакции камбиальных (стволовых) клеток при инфицировании вирусом папилломы человека (ВПЧ) и вирусом SARS-CoV-2 [1, 2, 3]. Проведён анализ литературы, подтверждающий связь между персистенцией вирусов, дисрегуляцией стволовых клеток и развитием фиброза This acticle presents a comparative analysis of two independent studies devoted to examining the response of stem (cambial) cells to infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV) and the SARS‐CoV‐2 virus [1, 2, 3]. An analysis of the literature has been carried out, confirming the link between viral persistence, dysregulation of stem cells, and the development of fibrosis

title: Evaluation of Alpha-1 Antitrypsin as a Prognostic Biomarker in Severe Influenza: A Prospective Study
abstract: Background: Influenza is a global health issue involving inflammatory mediators, the imbalances of which contribute to pulmonary and extrapulmonary damage. Objectives: To evaluate whether AAT1 levels are elevated in patients with severe influenza and assess its potential as a prognostic biomarker. Materials and methods: A prospective, analytical, non-interventional study was conducted on 72 patients admitted for severe influenza to the Internal Medicine Department at “Lozano Blesa” University Hospital (Zaragoza, Spain). Blood AAT1 concentrations at admission were analyzed alongside clinical and biochemical variables. Results: The mean patient age was 80.31 years (54.2% female). Overall mortality was 4.17%, one patient required ICU admission, and five had SARS-CoV-2 coinfection. Mean AAT1 concentration was 164.1 mg/dL (normal range: 100–200 mg/dL). AAT1 levels correlated significantly with leukocyte counts and C-reactive protein (r = 0.582, p < 0.001). Leukocyte counts were significantly higher in the patient requiring intensive care. Notably, AAT1 concentrations were significantly higher in patients with SARS-CoV-2 coinfection compared to non-coinfected influenza cases (p < 0.05). Conclusions: Admission AAT1 concentration does not serve as a useful prognostic biomarker in severe influenza. However, elevated AAT1 levels at diagnosis in hospitalized patients should prompt consideration of SARS-CoV-2 coinfection. Further research is warranted to clarify AAT1 involvement in influenza pathophysiology.

title: Epidemiologic Analysis of Mortality Predictors and Readmissions in Patients with Transverse Myelitis and/or Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis: A Nationwide Readmissions Database Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Transverse myelitis (TM) and acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) are debilitating neurological conditions. We aimed to examine in-hospital mortality and readmissions in patients hospitalized with TM and/or ADEM. Methods: In this retrospective study, we analyzed the Nationwide Readmissions Database from 2010 to 2020, excluding 2015, to identify index hospitalizations for TM and/or ADEM. Patients were stratified according to in-hospital mortality status. We used the Pearson chi-square test and Wilcoxon rank-sum test to compare baseline characteristics, while multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to identify predictors of in-hospital mortality. Results: Of 50,357 patients hospitalized with TM and/or ADEM, 1236 (2.5%) did not survive index hospitalization. Nonsurvivors were older with longer lengths of stay and a higher comorbidity burden. Among those ≥45 years, there was a trend towards increased odds of in-hospital mortality. Infection-related factors were associated with increased odds of in-hospital mortality, including streptococcal infection (odds ratio [OR]: 5.45 [1.07–27.68], p = 0.04) and coronavirus disease 2019 (OR: 4.54 [2.51–8.19], p < 0.001). Stroke (OR 2.71 [2.11–3.48], p < 0.001) and congestive heart failure (OR 2.17 [1.66–2.85], p < 0.001) emerged as the strongest predictors amongst chronic comorbidities. Over the study period, 5301 (11.8%) patients were readmitted to the hospital within 30 days. Conclusions: In patients with TM and/or ADEM, in-hospital mortality was associated with older age, greater comorbidity burden, and concurrent infections, particularly COVID-19 and streptococcal infections. These findings highlight opportunities for prevention, early detection, and management strategies to improve outcomes for patients with TM and/or ADEM.

source_records.abstract: Background/Objectives: Transverse myelitis (TM) and acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) are debilitating neurological conditions. We aimed to examine in-hospital mortality and readmissions in patients hospitalized with TM and/or ADEM. Methods: In this retrospective study, we analyzed the Nationwide Readmissions Database from 2010 to 2020, excluding 2015, to identify index hospitalizations for TM and/or ADEM. Patients were stratified according to in-hospital mortality status. We used the Pearson chi-square test and Wilcoxon rank-sum test to compare baseline characteristics, while multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to identify predictors of in-hospital mortality. Results: Of 50,357 patients hospitalized with TM and/or ADEM, 1236 (2.5%) did not survive index hospitalization. Nonsurvivors were older with longer lengths of stay and a higher comorbidity burden. Among those ≥45 years, there was a trend towards increased odds of in-hospital mortality. Infection-related factors were associated with increased odds of in-hospital mortality, including streptococcal infection (odds ratio [OR]: 5.45 [1.07–27.68], p = 0.04) and coronavirus disease 2019 (OR: 4.54 [2.51–8.19], p < 0.001). Stroke (OR 2.71 [2.11–3.48], p < 0.001) and congestive heart failure (OR 2.17 [1.66–2.85], p < 0.001) emerged as the strongest predictors amongst chronic comorbidities. Over the study period, 5301 (11.8%) patients were readmitted to the hospital within 30 days. Conclusions: In patients with TM and/or ADEM, in-hospital mortality was associated with older age, greater comorbidity burden, and concurrent infections, particularly COVID-19 and streptococcal infections. These findings highlight opportunities for prevention, early detection, and management strategies to improve outcomes for patients with TM and/or ADEM.

title: Enrolling and retaining a representative population in the NIH Researching COVID to Enhance Recovery (RECOVER)-Adult Cohort
abstract: Vulnerable populations are underrepresented in clinical studies. The design of the national RECOVER-Adult cohort study aimed to enroll a population that reflected the demographics of people infected with SARS-CoV-2 in the US. We quantify and assess follow-up visit completion among a representative population in the RECOVER-Adult cohort. Between October 2021 and October 2023, we enrolled adult participants across 16 hub-sites in the US. Follow-up visits continued until October 2025. Community outreach was used to gather and incorporate feedback prior to and during study implementation. Recruitment methods included electronic and in-person outreach by individuals trained in diversity, equity, and inclusion at health centers, health departments, and community-based organizations, as well as snowball sampling. Study staff maintained regular contact with participants between study visits via phone, email, and text, and arranged free transportation to support attendance. The primary outcome was follow-up visit completion, assessed via the completion of an in-person visit or symptom and social determinants of health survey. Follow-up visit completion of the first four visits and the last scheduled visit were assessed. Socio-demographic characteristics were self-reported at baseline. A logistic mixed effects model, clustered by hub-site, explored the longitudinal relationship between visit completion and each socio-demographic characteristic. Of the 14,880 adult participants who were enrolled in the RECOVER-Adult Cohort Study, 14,522 participants (mean[SD] age: 47.1[15.5] years, 57.0% Non-Hispanic White, 27.7% Male) completed a baseline visit. Over 85% of participants completed the first four follow-up visits, while over 90% completed a last visit. Across follow-up visits, participants who identified as minoritized groups, younger, had less education, lower income, were uninsured, lived in a rural area, and reported a disability were less likely to complete their visits, while older, retired, and female participants were more likely to complete them. Our findings indicate that enrolling and retaining a socio-demographically representative study population over time is feasible. However, vulnerable population may still face barriers to long-term study engagement, highlighting a need for innovative approaches to sustain ongoing study participation in the post-pandemic era.

title: A Koopman-PINN Framework for Epidemic Models: Parameter Inference and Forecasting
abstract: We propose a Koopman-enhanced physics-informed neural network (K-PINN) framework for parameter inference and forecasting in nonlinear epidemic models. This method combines Koopman operator theory and physics-informed learning. It maps epidemic states into a latent observable space where the dynamics evolve approximately linearly while satisfying the governing epidemic equations through automatic differentiation. This integration improves interpretability, parameter identifiability, and long-term predictive stability. We apply the proposed framework to a normalized SEIRSD epidemic model and evaluate it using synthetic monkeypox (Mpox) data and real-world datasets from Germany, Morocco, and Sweden for the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Synthetic trajectories are generated using a structure-preserving, nonstandard finite difference scheme to ensure reliable training data. Numerical results demonstrate that K-PINN achieves more accurate parameter estimation, trajectory reconstruction, and long-term forecasting than classical PINNs and Koopman-EDMD approaches. These results suggest that K-PINN is an effective machine learning framework for epidemic modeling that can be extended to more complex systems.
journal: Numerical Mathematics Theory Methods and Applications

title: Development of a Miniaturized Airborne Virus Detector Combining Gas Collection and Electrochemical Chip Platform
abstract: In the post-COVID-19 era, the need for real-time monitoring of airborne viruses in public spaces has become increasingly critical. Current detection methods largely rely on centralized laboratory testing, which limits their applicability for continuous monitoring in daily environments. Here we report the development of a miniaturized air-virus detection system that integrates a gas collection module with an electrochemical chip platform. The core sensing element is based on aptamer-functionalized gold magnetic nanoparticles, enabling specific viral recognition, while a negative-pressure collection unit was designed to enhance sampling efficiency. The system features a modular architecture that allows rapid assembly, disassembly, and cleaning, and can be powered by portable power banks for flexible deployment in diverse public settings. In addition, the device incorporates Bluetooth connectivity and a custom smartphone application for wireless data transmission, real-time visualization, and remote monitoring. The prototype was fabricated using 3D printing, offering cost-effectiveness and rapid prototyping advantages. Taken together, this integrated platform demonstrates substantial potential for on-site viral surveillance, public health protection, and the advancement of portable biosensing technologies.

title: The Role of Forkhead Box O1 Transcription Factors in Airway Epithelial Cells
abstract: Abstract The airway epithelium serves as a critical barrier against inhaled environmental stimuli, including viral and bacterial pathogens as well as non-infectious particles, and plays an active role in coordinating early innate immune responses Transcriptional regulators that integrate epithelial barrier maintenance with antiviral signaling remain incompletely defined. This thesis investigates the role of the Forkhead box O1 (FOXO1) transcription factor in airway epithelial homeostasis and responses to viral stimulation. Using FOXO1-deficient BEAS-2B airway epithelial cells and complementary pharmacologic and overexpression approaches, we first examined FOXO1 regulation of Toll-like receptor 3 (TLR3)–mediated responses. FOXO1 knockdown significantly reduced TLR3 mRNA expression, while constitutively active FOXO1 increased TLR3 transcription. Inhibition of FOXO1 activity attenuated Poly(I:C)-induced TLR3 mRNA expression in both BEAS-2B and primary normal human bronchial epithelial (NHBE) cells. Functionally, FOXO1 deficiency enhanced epithelial barrier recovery following injury and selectively reduced Poly(I:C)-induced IL6 and CCL2 release. FOXO1 nuclear localization increased transiently following Poly(I:C) stimulation, supporting activation downstream of viral mimic exposure. In primary NHBE cells infected with SARS-CoV-2, FOXO1 inhibition reduced viral spike mRNA levels, indicating that FOXO1 activity influences epithelial infection dynamics during active viral challenge. To define FOXO1-dependent transcriptional programs more broadly, RNA sequencing was performed in FOXO1-deficient and control cells under resting conditions and after Poly(I:C) stimulation. At baseline, FOXO1 deficiency altered expression of genes involved in adhesion, extracellular matrix organization, cytoskeletal structure, and epithelial migration. Poly(I:C) stimulation induced a interferon-dominated antiviral transcriptional response that was largely preserved in FOXO1-deficient cells; however, FOXO1 loss selectively altered expression of genes associated with extracellular matrix remodeling, receptor–ligand signaling, and MAPK-associated pathways during stimulation. Comparative analyses demonstrated that while core interferon programs were FOXO1-independent, structural and remodeling gene networks were sensitive to FOXO1 status. Collectively, these findings establish FOXO1 as a regulator of epithelial structural gene expression and a modulator of selected inflammatory and remodeling pathways during viral mimic stimulation. This work provides insight into how airway epithelial transcriptional networks integrate barrier integrity with antiviral and inflammatory responses.
journal: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)

title: CNATM SiReVir: Chemisch modifizierte komplexe siRNA Pools gegen respiratorische RNA-Viren
abstract: Im Teilvorhaben SiReVir untersuchte siTOOLs Biotech, wie komplexe Mischungen von siRNAs für den Einsatz gegen respiratorische RNA-Viren weiterentwickelt werden können. siPOOLs sind definierte Mischungen von 30 ausgewählten siRNAs. Durch die sehr niedrige Konzentration jeder einzelnen siRNA in der komplexen Mischung werden die von der Seed-Region der siRNAs verursachten off-Target Effekte minimiert. Gleichzeitig ist die Zielgen-Stilllegung durch die kooperative Wirkung vieler siRNAs extrem effizient. siRNAs Pools eignen sich auf ideale Weise zur Bekämpfung von RNA-Viren da deren RNA-Genom ein direktes Ziel für siRNAs darstellt. Die komplexe Mischung vieler unterschiedlicher siRNAs verhindert zuverlässig jede Resistenzbildung. Für einen therapeutischen Einsatz müssen die RNA-Moleküle vor Nukleasespaltung geschützt werden und in die Zielzellen eingeschleust werden. siTOOLs verfügte zu Projektbeginn über ein proprietäres, patentiertes Verfahren zur enzymatischen Herstellung komplexer siRNA-Mischungen. In Vorarbeiten wurden hocheffiziente siPOOLs gegen SARS-CoV-2 entwickelt. Chemische Modifikationen können die Stabilität von siRNAs erhöhen, sind jedoch nicht ohne Weiteres mit den enzymatischen Herstellungsschritten vereinbar. Das Projekt sollte geeignete RNA-Modifikationen identifizieren, ein lungenähnliches Zellkulturmodell aufbauen und die Prüfung antiviraler siPOOLs mit einem mRNA-Reportersystem ermöglichen.

title: Temporal Trends in Recorded Mental Disorder Prevalence and Healthcare Utilisation Across the Pre-Pandemic, Pandemic, and Post-Pandemic Periods: A Nine-Year Single-Centre Study Using Administrative Health Records
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare delivery and may have altered the detection and management of mental disorders in primary care. This study examined temporal changes in outpatient healthcare utilisation and recorded mental disorder prevalence before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. A nine-year longitudinal observational study was conducted using routinely collected administrative health records from a single primary care clinic in Mexico City between 2017 and 2025. Of 609,469 initial outpatient records, 234,596 were retained following the identification and selection procedures. Annual healthcare-based recorded prevalence was estimated using healthcare users as the denominator and examined overall and according to sex, age, ICD-10 diagnostic group, and individual diagnosis. Interrupted time-series analysis assessed changes in recorded outpatient healthcare utilisation following the onset of the pandemic. Both overall outpatient consultations and consultations with recorded mental disorder diagnoses showed substantial immediate reductions, followed by significant positive post-interruption trends. The recorded prevalence of mental disorders among primary healthcare users declined during the pandemic period but subsequently increased, reaching its highest observed level in 2025. The post-pandemic period was also characterised by changes in the distribution of recorded diagnoses across sex and age groups. These findings suggest that disruptions in healthcare utilisation may influence observed patterns of recorded mental disorders in primary care. Future pandemic preparedness should integrate longitudinal surveillance of recorded mental health diagnoses with healthcare utilisation data, support continuity of essential mental healthcare, and extend monitoring beyond the acute emergency to identify changes in recorded mental healthcare needs during recovery.

title: Analyzing the Sensitivity of Coronavirus Disparities in Nigeria Using a Mathematical Model
abstract: In this paper, we analyzed the sensitivity of coronavirus disparities in Nigeria using a dynamical mathematical model. Due to the government implementing strict measures such as banning public gatherings, closing places of worship and businesses and encouraging social distancing, we looked closely at the statistics and developed a mathematical model that showed the possible control of this virus and thereby preventing an individual getting infected with the virus. The method of solution involves the first and second sensitivities with a fixed population size that is no further births or migration and the only deaths infections are taken due to baby infections with indication on the initial infected population. The first sensitivity is solved using method separation of variables whose COVID-19 profiles were sketched using ODE45. Obtaining the second sensitivity gives a non-linear ordinary differential equation which is used to determine the behavior of the fixed population size. If the second sensitivity greater than zero then the COVID19 patients steadily decreases to zero while if the second sensitivity less than zero then the COVID19 patients steadily increases and reach maximum. After this maximum point the number of COVID-19 patients decreases and tends to zero. In either case, the COVID-19 patients tends to extinction. The mathematical model showed that the control of this virus is possible

title: Adaptive confidence-aware ensemble machine learning for viral disease detection and severity
abstract: The rapid emergence and overlapping clinical presentations of viral infectious diseases such as COVID-19 and dengue pose significant challenges for timely diagnosis and risk stratification in resource-limited settings. Conventional single-model approaches often suffer from limited generalizability, class imbalance, and suboptimal feature utilization, resulting in delayed interventions and inefficient resource allocation. This study introduces a weighted adaptive confidence-aware ensemble machine learning framework (WACAM) for accurate early detection and subsequent severity prediction of viral infections using routine hematological and demographic data. A merged dataset comprising 1,369 patient records was preprocessed with median imputation, Z-score outlier handling, Winsorization, and standard scaler normalization. Boruta feature selection identified key clinical markers, followed by synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) for class balancing. Seven diverse base learners were integrated through a novel confidence-weighted soft-voting scheme. Model weights were adaptively assigned via exponential softmax of out-of-fold (OOF) area under the curve (AUC) scores, with an optimized probability threshold maximizing Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC). The proposed WACAM achieved superior performance with 86.5% accuracy, 0.8795 F1-score, 0.9156 ROC-AUC, and 0.726 MCC on the test set, outperforming individual models.
journal: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics

title: Analysis of diagnostic yield and duplicative testing reduction using a customizable and reflexive syndromic panel
abstract: Syndromic molecular panels offer a rapid approach to assessing a broad collection of pathogens; however, they come with a significant cost to both patients and healthcare systems. Customizable and reflexive syndromic panels offer an opportunity to harness the diagnostic capabilities of syndromic panels, with the potential to reduce cost or increase diagnostic yield. A total of 300 samples from patients with symptoms of an upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) that received inpatient standard of care testing (BioFire ® RP2.1) were tested with the LIAISON PLEX ® Respiratory Flex Assay. To assess seasonal differences, samples were collected in two cohorts covering a period of low influenza-like illness (ILI) (April 2024-June 2024) and elevated ILI (January 2025-March 2025). Following testing, pathogen prevalence was used to retrospectively design panels to maximize diagnostic yield and clinical utility. A 7-target base panel had a diagnostic yield of 80.4% during the low ILI period and 82.5% during the elevated ILI period, as compared to the standard of care syndromic panel. Customizable and reflexive panel design has the potential to increase diagnostic yield while reducing duplicative testing and associated costs.

title: Traditional Chinese medicine as a multi-target therapeutic strategy for mitigating severe human coronavirus infections
abstract: This study aims to narratively synthesize the multi-target mechanisms and clinical efficacy of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas against human coronavirus infections, with particular emphasis on their therapeutic value in inhibiting viral replication and preventing the progression from mild to severe disease. Relevant scientific literature was searched and analyzed, focusing on the representative TCM formulations recommended in the National Diagnosis and Treatment Protocol for COVID-19 (Trial Versions), such as the “Three Medicines and Three Formulations.” Evidence from pharmacological investigations, molecular docking analyses, network pharmacology predictions, and clinical trials was integrated to elucidate the multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms by which TCM formulations mitigate severe coronavirus disease. TCM formulations exert antiviral effects through multiple targets and pathways. They directly inhibit the enzymatic activities of the coronavirus 3CLpro, PLpro, and RdRp; among these, quercetin and baicalin exhibit strong binding affinities. Moreover, TCM formulations modulate the NF-κB and MAPK signaling pathways to suppress the release of proinflammatory cytokines such as IL-6 and TNF-α, thereby attenuating cytokine storm responses. They also improve microcirculatory and coagulation functions, reduce D-dimer levels, and downregulate vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) expression. In addition, TCM interventions enhance host immune homeostasis and restore intestinal and respiratory microbial balance, thereby reducing the risk of secondary bacterial or fungal infections. Clinical studies have reported improvements in selected symptom-resolution and imaging outcomes, although the evidence remains heterogeneous and does not establish a consistent reduction in severe disease progression across populations. Through the synergistic actions of “multi-components–multi-targets–multi-pathways,” TCM formulations exhibit remarkable antiviral and immunomodulatory effects. These integrated mechanisms provide an effective strategy for preventing and treating coronavirus infections and their severe progression, highlighting the substantial clinical value and developmental potential of TCM in this field.
journal: Beni-Suef University Journal of Basic and Applied Sciences

title: Quantum Chemical Study of the Complexation of Favipiravir Anion and of Its 6-Halogenated Homologues
abstract: Favipiravir is fluoropyrazine carboxamide (C5H3N3OOHF). It has two main tautomeric forms: oxo and hydroxy forms. Favipiravir is an antiviral substance used against RNA viruses and is therefore used to treat various types of influenza, including COVID-19. Since coordination of a given drug molecule is known to enhance the therapeutic activities of both the metal and the drug molecule, this research is devoted to a theoretical study of the reactivity of favipiravir and its 5-halogenated analogues as potential ligands. The aim of this research is to identify the most favourable coordination site within each potential ligand while also establishing the thermodynamic conditions for the coordination reactions. In each case, the methodology consisted of bringing zinc(II) chloride into proximity with a 6-halo-3-oxido-pyrazine-2-carboxamide ion. Versions 09 and 16 of the Gaussian software and the GaussView 6.0.16 interface were the main tools used in this investigation. The coordination indicators were bond lengths, APT atomic charges, atomic electrostatic potentials, HOMO–LUMO gaps, hardness, softness, electronegativity, electrophilicity index, electron affinity, ionisation energy, electrofugacity, nucleofugacity and donor power. Considering these coordination indicators as a whole made it possible to draw conclusions regarding the most favourable coordination sites. The calculations were carried out at the DFT/B3LYP level using the 6-311G++(d,p), Lanl2dz and Aug-cc-pvdz orbital basis sets. Analysis of the calculation results revealed that the two oxygen atoms are the preferred coordination sites. The complexation reactions were simulated. The complexes formed were tetrahedral zinc(II) chelates. The bioavailability test based on Lipinski's Rule of Five demonstrated that the modelled coordination compounds can be considered drug candidates.
journal: International Research Journal of Pure and Applied Chemistry

title: Explainable spatiotemporal graph learning for early identification of localized infectious disease risk
abstract: Localized infectious disease forecasting is important for targeted public health interventions, but remains challenging because of complex spatiotemporal dynamics and limited model interpretability. We propose an explainable spatiotemporal graph learning framework for region-level infectious disease forecasting, using COVID-19 in Sweden as a case study. The framework integrates demographic, socioeconomic, syndromic surveillance, and epidemiological data within a nationwide graph of fine-grained geographic areas. We introduce an adaptive gating mechanism that modulates graph-derived spatial representations using temporal context while the geographic adjacency graph remains fixed. To improve interpretability, we combine analysis of gating behavior with post hoc explainable AI analyses of temporal, structural, and spatial feature sensitivities. The framework is evaluated across 3-, 7-, 14-, and 21-day forecasting horizons under both offline (held-out temporal split) and online (prequential predict-before-update) learning settings and compared with LSTM, tree-based machine-learning models, and standard and advanced spatiotemporal graph models. In the offline setting, the spatiotemporal graph convolutional network with adaptive gating (STGCN-AG) generally performed better than LSTM, tree-based, and standard spatiotemporal graph baselines, with the clearest gains at shorter horizons. Among the advanced graph forecasting models evaluated, STGCN-AG performed best at the 3-day horizon and remained broadly competitive at longer horizons. Nevertheless, in the offline evaluation, all models showed limited absolute predictive performance, which further deteriorated as the forecasting horizon increased, highlighting the difficulty of longer-term localized forecasting. In the online setting, the models continued to track evolving incidence under sequential updating, although predictions at longer horizons showed greater temporal lag and weaker responsiveness to rapid changes in observed incidence. The adaptive gate indicates when, where, and across which latent dimensions the model more strongly modulates graph-derived representations. These findings highlight both the potential and the remaining challenges of explainable spatiotemporal graph learning for localized infectious disease forecasting.

title: Pivot or persevere? IntiGo’s entrepreneurial journey through resistance and reinvention
abstract: By engaging with this case, students will be able to: This case study investigates the entrepreneurial path and strategic challenges of IntiGo, a Tunisian startup founded in late 2019 by entrepreneur Bassem Bouguerra, initially launched as a scooter-based ride-hailing service that was introduced to disrupt Tunisia’s challenged transportation system. IntiGo immediately gained public interest but encountered significant taxi union resistance and legal ambiguity that threatened its survival from the outset. The COVID-19 pandemic in early 2020 forced IntiGo to halt operations entirely. Caught at a strategic crossroads, IntiGo had to act fast by pivoting from urban mobility to last-mile delivery to survive. By 2023, after repurposing its scooter fleet, combining hundreds of delivery drivers and pickup locations and partnering with Jumia, Africa’s largest e-commerce platform, IntiGo emerged as the top last-mile logistics company in Tunisia. Jumia, however, abruptly decided to exit Tunisia’s market in late 2024, endangering IntiGo’s business model and financial stability. Bouguerra was once more faced with a strategic decision: should IntiGo focus on becoming a logistics-led platform by building more direct relationships with merchants and e-commerce partners, or should it preserve a link with its original mobility model through a hybrid approach combining delivery and urban mobility? Set between 2019 and 2025, this case is intended to instruct students in making strategic decisions in the face of uncertainty and legal constraints by using core strategic frameworks such as institutional theory and stakeholder analysis, dynamic capabilities framework and SAF criteria and resource-based view (RBV) and TOWS matrix. It is well suited to courses in entrepreneurship, emerging markets, non-market strategy and innovation management. This case is designed for final-year undergraduate students, master’s students and Master of Business Administration students enrolled in programmes such as management, business, entrepreneurship, strategic management and innovation management. It is particularly suited for modules in entrepreneurship, strategic management, startup strategy, emerging markets, non-market strategy and business model innovation. Students are expected to have a foundational understanding of core concepts in business strategy, including stakeholder analysis, competitive positioning, business models and strategic decision-making under uncertainty. Prior exposure to institutional theory, dynamic capabilities, RBV/VRIO, SAF criteria, the TOWS matrix and emerging market contexts is beneficial but not required, as instructors may introduce selected frameworks during the session.

abstract: Dynamic systems described by differential equations often involve feedback among system components.When there are time delays for components to sense and respond to feedback, delay differential equation (DDE) models are commonly used.This paper considers the problem of inferring unknown system parameters, including the time delays, from noisy and sparse experimental data observed from the system.We propose an extension of manifold-constrained Gaussian processes to conduct parameter inference for DDEs, whereas the time delay parameters have posed a challenge for existing methods that bypass numerical solvers.Our method uses a Bayesian framework to impose a Gaussian process model over the system trajectory, conditioned on the manifold constraint that satisfies the DDEs.For efficient computation, a linear interpolation scheme is developed to approximate the values of the time-delayed system outputs, along with corresponding theoretical error bounds on the approximated derivatives.Two simulation examples, based on Hutchinson's equation and the lac operon system, together with a real-world application using Ontario COVID-19 data,

title: Whole-body vibration training in addition to muscle-strengthening exercises alone in improving muscle function in children with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 - a preliminary randomised interventional trial.
abstract: Identify whether whole-body vibration additionally to muscle-strengthening exercises improved muscle function in children with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 and muscle weakness, compared to muscle-strengthening exercises alone. No difference was noted in outcomes between the two groups. The interventions did not improve muscle function, albeit with low adherence. Children with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) can have impaired muscle function. This preliminary randomised interventional trial investigated whether whole-body vibration (WBV) therapy in combination with muscle-strengthening exercises would improve muscle function compared to muscle-strengthening exercises alone, and their feasibility, in this cohort. Children with NF1 aged 6-16 years with muscle weakness were randomised to daily muscle-strengthening exercises for 6 months, or these daily exercises plus a WBV therapy programme for 6 months. The primary outcome was jumping power standard deviation score (SDS). Secondary and pre-determined exploratory outcomes included other measures of muscle function, balance, physical activity, fatigue and quality of life. Qualitative data regarding safety, feasibility and adherence were collected. Forty-four children were recruited into the trial, with equal allocation to both groups. There was no effect on jumping power SDS between the two groups at the end of the trial (absolute effect size = -0.1, 95% confidence interval -0.5 to +0.3, P = 0.53). Similarly, no difference was detected with regard to secondary and exploratory outcomes. No significant changes in muscle function SDS were noted from baseline. The regimes within both groups were reported to be feasible. Adherence was low, affected by the COVID-19 pandemic and decreased enthusiasm over time. No adverse events were reported. Six months of daily muscle-strengthening exercises alone or in combination with a WBV therapy programme is safe, although adherence was low. No difference in muscle function, balance, physical activity, fatigue or quality of life was detected when WBV therapy was added to daily muscle-strengthening exercises.

title: A nationwide health claims data analysis of peri-pandemic changes in invasive and non-invasive paediatric group A streptococcal (GAS) infections.
abstract: Purpose Group A streptococcal (GAS) infections are common in childhood. In the late phase of the COVID-19 pandemic, increases in GAS-tonsillopharyngitis, scarlet fever and invasive GAS (iGAS) infections were reported in several countries. We aimed to identify peri-pandemic changes of paediatric invasive and non-invasive GAS infections, and to compare their temporal patterns with those of non-bacterial acute respiratory infections (ARI). Methods We analysed nationwide Statutory Health Insurance claims data from 800,000 children and adolescents aged 0-17 years insured by DAK-Gesundheit. Quarterly administrative prevalence of GAS-tonsillopharyngitis, scarlet fever, invasive GAS infections and selected ARIs was assessed, alongside temporal diagnostic patterns across consecutive quarters. Results In 2019, quarterly prevalence of GAS-tonsillopharyngitis and scarlet fever ranged from 43 to 83 per 10,000 and 20 to 59 per 10,000 respectively. Both declined during 2020-2021, reaching a minimum of 9 per 10,000 for GAS-tonsillopharyngitis and 4 per 10,000 for scarlet fever. From 2022, prevalence rose peaking in Q1 2023 at 154 and 130 per 10,000, respectively. iGAS infections remained rare ( Conclusion This first comprehensive analysis charaterises peri-pandemic changes in paediatric invasive and non-invasive GAS infections and non-bacterial ARI in Germany. Invasive and non-invasive GAS infections follow the same pattern suggesting epidemiological reasons rather than changes in bacterial virulence. title: Joint Degrees, Shared Goals
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted discussions on the future of international and transnational education. Many higher education institutions are forming international partnerships and implementing joint-degree programs to enhance their internationalisation efforts and curriculum, improve global rankings and advancing quality education for all, in line with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG4). Joint Degrees, Shared Goals explores the localisation of internationalised curricula within joint-degree programs, focusing on their role in supporting quality education and enhancing graduate employability. Examining the implementation of these programs in Vietnam, chapters draw on perspectives from various stakeholders and showcase how localising internationalised curriculum (LIC) strategies can transform education. Case studies demonstrate how these programs equip students with the skills needed for success in both local and international contexts, thereby improving their employability. Serving as a vital resource for educators, policymakers, and administrators aiming to internationalise curricula in non-Western settings, Joint Degrees, Shared Goals underscores that localising internationalised curricula is not just a means to enhance educational quality, but also a potent tool for boosting employability, fostering innovation, and preparing graduates for a globalised world. With its blend of theoretical insights and practical recommendations, this is a comprehensive guide to advancing internationalisation while aligning with local educational and cultural contexts.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence Uncovers Non-Bank Financial Industry Contagion and Safeguards Central Bank Institutional Governance
abstract: Introduction/Main Objectives: This paper examines systemic risk interconnections within Indonesia's Non-Bank Financial Industry (NBFI), which displays intricate systemic risk interconnections that alter traditional macroprudential dynamics. As financial ecosystems digitalize, understanding cross-sectoral risk transmission beyond banking is crucial for stability. The study further aims to develop a transparent artificial intelligence framework capable of supporting timely macroprudential policy interventions and institutional decision-making. Background Problems: Systemic risk from NBFI interconnections insurance, pension funds, finance companies, guarantee institutions, and P2P lending remains insufficiently mapped, and linear models fail to capture nonlinear contagion, raising the question of how risks transmit across NBFI sectors and what their primary drivers are. Novelty: This paper pioneers integrating econometrics with Explainable AI (SHAP-Random Forest) to construct an NBFI systemic risk framework, offering transparent, actionable insights for regulators to strengthen macroprudential governance and safeguard financial stability. Research Methods: The study employs correlation analysis, Granger causality, OLS regression, and Random Forest with SHAP decomposition using Indonesian NBFI sectoral data (2016–2024). Finding/Results: Results reveal strong cross-sectoral risk linkages and nonlinear transmission, identifying pension fund asset size and foreign funding exposures as dominating cross-sectoral systemic risk, contributing mean SHAP values of 0.576 and 0.326, respectively. During COVID-19, NBFI sectors acted as shock absorbers rather than amplifiers. Conclusion: The findings underscore the need for Algorithmic Macroprudential Governance, where explainable AI enhances evidence-based supervision, strengthens institutional autonomy, improves systemic risk monitoring in emerging financial architectures, and provides actionable insights for regulators in safeguarding long-term financial stability.

title: Sociocultural Health Code as an Instrument of Social Policy
abstract: Despite the government’s significant interest in sustainable development of the population and maintaining public health, its health policies do not always achieve the desired results, either in containing the spread of infectious diseases during outbreaks (e.g., COVID-19) or in preventing noncommunicable diseases. This discrepancy can be explained by the fact that population health behavior is shaped not so much by targeted policy measures as by ingrained cultural traditions of specific social communities. The Sociocultural Health Code (SHC) framework methodology developed at the National Medical Research Center for Therapy and Preventive Medicine (Moscow, Russia) is designed to identify vulnerabilities in citizens’ health attitudes, their capacity for self-organization in maintaining health, their level of health literacy, and the degree of trust in information sources, interpersonal networks, and the public organizations, the activities of which influence health outcomes. This study offers a theoretical analysis of the value of the findings obtained using the SHC methodology for policymaking at both the central and regional levels of government. The study also provides a comparative assessment of the analytical potential offered by alternative methodological frameworks that consider the sociocultural dimension of health. The study assesses the potential of employing the SHC methodology to obtain and interpret data essential for developing technologies contributing to understanding the semantic context in which individuals make health-related decisions, as well as for addressing, where necessary, issues associated with personal attitudes of people toward their health. The SHC framework is designed to capture behavioral vulnerabilities and the population’s level of trust in government health initiatives; like several mixed-methods frameworks, it combines qualitative and quantitative techniques. At its current stage of development, however, the findings should be read as an assessment of analytical potential rather than as evidence of predictive accuracy or policy effectiveness. Given these limitations, the approach may help identify population groups based on an appropriate set of parameters and the implementation of targeted legal and informational measures in response to specific challenges and policy goals.

title: Infectious Agents as Drivers of Lung Cancer
abstract: Globally, lung cancer is the most diagnosed cancer and the leading cause of cancer deaths. While tobacco smoke remains the predominant etiological factor for lung cancer, a growing body of evidence implicates chronic infection by specific pathogens as significant co-factors or independent contributors to lung carcinogenesis. This chapter examines the role of infectious agents (Bacteria: Mycobacterium tuberculosis , Chlamydophila pneumoniae , and Helicobacter pylori ; Virus: human immunodeficiency virus, human papillomavirus, Epstein–Barr virus (EBV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2; and Parasite: Toxoplasma gondii ) in lung cancer development. It reviews molecular mechanisms by which these infections may promote carcinogenesis through chronic inflammation, immune modulation, and direct oncogenic effects. The chapter also addresses co-infections and their interaction with environmental carcinogens, underscoring the importance of studying infectious risks in regions with high burdens of these diseases, including Africa. Finally, the chapter also discusses prospects for prevention strategies (e.g., antimicrobial therapy and vaccination) and the development of novel diagnostic or therapeutic approaches targeting infection-related pathways. Understanding the role of infectious agents provides crucial insights into the multifactorial origins of lung cancer and opens new avenues for risk reduction and intervention.

title: From surveillance data to public health action: the usability gap in WHO digital influenza surveillance
abstract: Interpretable surveillance evidence connects reported influenza activity with a defined analytical task. Under what conditions can influenza surveillance records shared through the World Health Organization (WHO) FluNet and FluID provide interpretable evidence for local forecasting and alert assessment? We assessed valid-rate availability and continuity in WHO FluNet and FluID for 2015–2025 and compared seasonal-naive, domestic, and target-excluded international models in rolling held-out evaluations for 2022–2025, with alert trade-offs expressed as scenario costs. Sensitivity analyses examined zero coding, model specification, and the COVID-19 period, whereas official-document mapping and exploratory analyses assessed recording context and background conditions. Valid-rate construction was possible for 162 FluNet, 61 ILI (influenza-like illness), and 97 severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) reporting codes. Median FluNet coverage increased from 50.0% in the primary snapshot to 76.9% in the zero-restored later snapshot, making zero coding consequential for interpreting coverage. Domestic models outperformed seasonal repetition in the primary comparison, while the tested international aggregate yielded negative mean increments across all robustness specifications. SARI sensitivity gains entailed more false alerts, and the ILI alert pattern was not robust. Restoring zero-positive partner weeks improved the 1-week SARI contrast by 13.1 per 10,000 admissions (95% interval, 0.8–33.4). The findings identify conditions for constructing and evaluating interpretable shared evidence: valid local baselines, explicit recording context, and assessment for a specified outcome, horizon, threshold, and loss preference. Continuous domestic surveillance provides the comparator for judging candidate external inputs. Metadata and feedback reforms offer an agenda for testing these conditions in local practice.

title: Tail risk spillover effects of the technology market on Chinese new energy vehicle firms: A perspective of time-varying technological cycles
abstract: This study investigates the dynamic tail-risk connectedness and spillover effects from the global technology market to the Chinese New Energy Vehicle (NEV) industry. Amidst the global energy transition and heightened financial volatility, we employ a Conditional Autoregressive Value at Risk (CAViaR) model to quantify marginal tail risks, coupled with a Time-Varying Parameter Vector Autoregression (TVP-VAR) framework to construct dynamic risk spillover networks. Using daily data from January 2015 to March 2025, our analysis captures structural shifts in connectedness driven by critical technological cycles (e.g., the battery revolution and the emergence of disruptive AI models like DeepSeek) as well as exogenous shocks (e.g., the COVID-19 pandemic). Empirical findings reveal that tail-risk spillovers are highly asymmetric and time-varying. Notably, global technology markets serve as consistent net sources of tail-risk spillovers to the NEV sector, with network connectedness intensifying sharply during technological breakthroughs and macro-crises. Frequency-domain decomposition further demonstrates that while short-term spillovers dominate during tranquil periods, long-term tail-risk connectedness escalates significantly during crises. Additionally, leading NEV firms act as pivotal hubs in shaping intra-industry network dynamics. These findings elucidate the evolutionary patterns of tail-risk connectedness across distinct technological phases, providing actionable insights for dynamic portfolio allocation and risk management in the green economy.

title: Beyond access: the evolution of Portugal’s pharmacy-based vaccination strategy and the future role of AI-driven outreach
abstract: Vaccination programmes increasingly face a paradox: expanding access does not necessarily translate into coverage at policy targets. Portugal provides an instructive example. The integration of community pharmacies into seasonal influenza and COVID-19 vaccination created more than 3,500 vaccination points and approximately 70% of influenza doses were administered in pharmacies in 2023–2024. The pharmacy share then fell to under 46% by 2025–2026, while total influenza doses remained broadly stable (2.41 to 2.56 million per season). This indicates a redistribution of doses across settings rather than a loss of vaccination activity; changes in age eligibility, high-dose vaccination for adults aged ≥85 years in SNS units, and invitation and recall activity may all have contributed. Influenza coverage among adults aged ≥65 years remained below the World Health Organization target of 75%, at 70.5% in 2024–2025 and 73.0% in 2025–2026. This suggests that, residual under-vaccination reflects barriers beyond physical access. The authors use “activation gap” descriptively for potentially addressable interruptions between eligibility and vaccination. Portugal already uses registry-based invitations and reminders, the open question is what a conversational layer, scripted or based on generative AI, could add. Evidence is relatively strong for reminders, growing for scripted conversational interventions and preliminary for generative AI. The authors therefore propose a registry-based randomised comparison of existing recall, existing recall plus a scripted conversational intervention, and existing recall plus a generative-AI conversational intervention, with incremental vaccination, safety, equity, trust and cost per additional vaccinated person as outcomes.

title: SPATIAL DISPARITIES IN CULTURAL TOURISM: A MULTIDIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS OF MUSEUM ATTENDANCE DYNAMICS IN BULGARIA
abstract: This study aims to identify and analyse spatial disparities and structural stratification of regional museum activity in Bulgaria over a 13-year period (2012-2024). The primary objective is to evaluate the stability, growth trajectory, and resilience of regional cultural supply models in response to external and macroeconomic shifts, specifically the COVID-19 pandemic. A multidimensional statistical analysis was applied to panel data from the National Statistical Institute and the Institute for Market Economics, encompassing all 28 administrative districts in Bulgaria. Quartile grouping (based on visits per 1000 inhabitants) was utilized to differentiate clusters, while long-term dynamics and crisis resilience were assessed through specific indicators: Coefficient of Variation (CV), Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR), Sensitivity Index (SI), and Recovery Index (RI). Through this approach, the districts were categorized into three distinct performance tiers: Highlevel (Leaders), Mid-level, and Low-level. The analysis reveals significant structural imbalances and high systemic volatility across all clusters, indicating a critical dependence on incidental tourist flows. A “scale paradox” was identified, whereby districts with moderate attendance volumes and a developed local product demonstrate considerably higher post-crisis adaptability compared to traditional leaders. Although all groups exhibit coefficients of variation exceeding 40%, the Mid-level segment achieves the highest annual growth (4.95%) and positive recovery (17.15%), outperforming the top-tier districts, which record slower growth (1.62%) and negative post-pandemic recovery (-12.08%). Empirical profiles highlight stable cores (Veliko Tarnovo, Gabrovo), strategic event legacies (Plovdiv), and nature-integrated recovery (Smolyan), contrasting with transitdependent declines (Vidin). The high structural volatility underscores an urgent need for a conceptual shift in regional cultural policies. Strategic management should pivot towards active audience development and integrated regional tourism products, linking public subsidies to institutional flexibility and proven post-crisis resilience rather than merely static volumes.
journal: Geo Journal of Tourism and Geosites

title: Le calque et l'emprunt dans la langue française durant la crise sanitaire : enjeux et répercussions
abstract: Résumé : Bien que le calque reste l’un des procédés d’emprunt à une langue étrangère, il permet, à la fois, la création de nouvelles unités lexicales autochtones et l’extension du sens d’unités existantes. Ce transfert linguistique du signifié, entre deux systèmes différents (anglais/français), contribue au dynamisme permanent de la langue d’accueil ; mais, il a, aussi, des retombées notables sur sa morphologie, sa syntaxe et sa sémantique. Le présent article vise à décrire, analyser et illustrer la fonction du calque de l’anglais dans l’évolution de la langue française durant la pandémie de Covid-19, et à montrer son impact sur les composantes de la langue d’accueil. Il s’attache ensuite à comparer l’apport de ce procédé à celui de l’emprunt. Afin de mener un travail rigoureux, nous nous sommes appuyés sur un corpus élaboré à partir de dictionnaires, de plateformes terminologiques et d’articles datant de la période de la crise sanitaire. L’analyse quantitative révèle une nette prédominance du calque morphologique (80 %), suivi du calque sémantique (12,3%) et du calque phraséologique (6,7 %). Les emprunts bruts non adaptés représentent 67,8 % des emprunts relevés, contre 32,2 % d’emprunts adaptés. Mots-clés : calque, emprunt, enrichissement lexical, politique linguistique, Covid-19

title: Improving the Efficiency of Distance Learning with a Minimum Network Load
abstract: The rapid onset of the COVID-19 crisis compelled immediate responses to mitigate infection risks, particularly in education. A swift transition to e-learning became a necessity, posing myriad challenges for students and institutions. Issues ranged from technical considerations to educators' preparedness and students' readiness, necessitating a reevaluation of the role of information technology in education. The didactic potential of e-learning tools is considered, and methodological recommendations are formulated for their integration into pedagogical practice, adaptation to both distance and traditional conditions. An analysis of relevant international studies informs the development ofa teaching method that optimizes distance-learning efficiency and minimizes network load. This method strategically balances synchronous and asynchronous learning, considering network traffic reduction, fostering equal educational opportunities regardless of location, health, or financial status. This study affirms the method's effectiveness through a com-parative analysis of the results with those of previous traditional semesters. This research contributes valuable insights for navigating the challenges posed by the pandemic in the education sector. This study aims to explore the pedagogical possibilities of e-learning tools and offer methodological recommendations for their incorporation into teaching practices, adaptable to both remote and conventional environments. Additionally, it seeks to develop and validate a teaching approach that enhances the efficiency of distance learning, reduces network load, and promotes equitable educational access, addressing the challenges associated with the rapid development and widespread adoption of e-learning technologies.

title: The crisis of meaning in the digital age: analysis of the degeneration of the sign from Industry 4.0 to 6.0
abstract: This study aims to analyze the discursive evolution of the meaning of Industries 4.0, 5.0 and 6.0 in scientific production and discuss their consequences for health management, using Peirce’s Triadic Categorical Model. A hybrid approach with methodological triangulation was adopted across two publication periods (2018–2026; 2020–2026). Advanced bibliometric techniques – cooccurrence networks and principal component analysis – allowed mapping the evolution of the meaning of Industries 4.0, 5.0, 6.0 and 7.0, interpreted according to the categories of firstness, secondness and thirdness. The study identifies a decisive transition – driven by semiosis in the post-COVID-19 era – from philosophical discourse to pragmatic applications. Industry 4.0 has rapidly evolved into practice, giving rise to Industry 5.0 indicators and speculative icons of Industry 6.0. This evolution entails potential ethical risks and technological failures that necessitate global standards, whereas the absence of references to Industry 7.0 points to a prespeculative stag. This research pioneers the systematic application of Peircean semiotics to the bibliometric and scientometric analysis of signs within Industries 4.0 through 7.0. It identifies the crisis of meaning as digital vulnerability and interprets disruptive “deep news” as an ethical-informational challenge. The study concludes that critical literacy is not merely desirable but a semiotic and ethical imperative for emerging industrial revolutions, ensuring information veracity, strengthening digital security and safeguarding the centrality of human health knowledge within technological paradigms.
