title: The Path from Open Innovation to Innovation Performance: The Roles of Employee Perseverance of Effort and Thriving at Work
abstract: This study examines the roles played by employees’ perseverance of effort and thriving at work levels in the transformation process of open innovation, an organizational dynamic capability, into firm innovation performance. To test the structural stability of the research model from the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic to the changing work practices in the post-pandemic era and changing work practices on the research model, two independent datasets collected in 2020 (n1 = 579) and 2026 (n2 = 157) were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and Multi-Group Analysis (MGA). The PLS-SEM findings demonstrate that perceived open innovation climate positively influences employees’ perceptions of firm innovation performance and thriving at work; additionally, it has a significant impact on employees’ perseverance of effort as a psychological capital component. The findings indicate that perseverance of effort is a strong individual capacity that supports thriving at work and the perception of firm innovation performance. The MGA results indicate that the structural path relationships exhibit broad contextual consistency across both periods (2020 vs. 2026), with no statistically significant path differences identified between the groups (p > 0.05). Rather than reflecting absolute insensitivity to macro-environmental shocks, this consistency suggests that the psychological transmission mechanisms linking open innovation climate, perseverance of effort, and thriving at work retain their general relational pattern in the post-pandemic context. Nevertheless, because the smaller sample size in the 2026 cohort (n2 = 157) resulted in wider confidence intervals, these temporal comparisons should be interpreted cautiously as evidence of structural robustness rather than invariance across all environmental conditions.

title: Innovation Trends In Multirepresentational Digital Worksheets Research For Physics Education
abstract: General Background Digital technologies provide unprecedented opportunities to integrate abstract, visual, verbal, and mathematical elements into physics education materials. Specific Background Although product-specific case studies demonstrate the feasibility of digital media, a comprehensive systematic visualization linking thematic shifts, research saturation, and institutional collaboration patterns regarding multirepresentational tools has not been firmly established. Knowledge Gap Existing bibliometric mapping either focuses broadly on digital tools or isolates representation theories without examining the intersection and thematic evolution specifically within digital worksheets. Aims This study maps the publication trends, dominant research topics, structural collaboration networks, and thematic evolution surrounding multirepresentational digital worksheets in physics education from 2016 through mid-2026. Results Bibliometric analysis of 35 documents reveals a fluctuating but generally upward publication trend peaking in 2026. Network visualization identified five dominant clusters revolving around product development, validity testing, cognitive assessment using N-Gain, and student engagement strategies. Thematic shifts indicate a transition from COVID-19 emergency tools to sophisticated R&D product testing focused predominantly on mechanics and thermodynamics. However, collaboration structures remain isolated within narrow, localized institutional networks. Novelty This mapping highlights the saturation of classical mechanics topics and quantitatively pinpoints low-density research areas requiring urgent investigation. Implications Consequently, future studies must expand institutional partnerships, address abstract modern physics concepts, and integrate adaptive learning algorithms or augmented reality to advance multimodal physics education. Highlights • Multirepresentational digital worksheet research experienced significant upward momentum, peaking in 2026. • Current literature demonstrates heavy saturation within classical mechanics and localized collaboration. • Augmented reality and modern physics applications represent high-value opportunities for future studies. Keywords Bibliometric Analysis; Digital Worksheet; Multirepresentational; Physics Education; Thematic Evolution

title: Belonging through a web of connections in a first-year online course
abstract: University learning, teaching and assessment is experiencing significant digital and pedagogical disruption. Accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, university teachers have experienced the shift to Emergency Remote Teaching, the increase of hybrid and online learning, followed by the rise of GenAI. These disruptions, combined with ramifications of neoliberalism and managerialism, have led to the erosion of connections and trust between students and teachers that have always been at the centre of learning and teaching. As such, knowing how to build and re-build connections with students is critical. Renewed research interest in the concept of belonging shows promise for re-building human connection in learning and teaching, however few studies have specifically focussed on belonging in post-pandemic online learning environments, especially within the first-year cohort. This qualitative case study examines one course including interviews with two teachers and three students, analysis of the course site, and observations of synchronous classes. Findings evidence that the teaching team humanised the online environment and directed academic belonging through place and social belonging by emphasising the learner-instructor relationship to facilitate student belonging.

title: HbA1c Testing Before, During and After a Health System Crisis: A Public Sector Laboratory Analysis in the Western Cape, South Africa
abstract: Abstract Objective Diabetes imposes a significant public health burden in South Africa, yet public sector glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) testing patterns remain poorly characterized. This study examined HbA1c testing adherence and glycemic control in the Western Cape across the COVID-19 pandemic. Methods A retrospective observational study used National Health Laboratory Service data for adults in the Western Cape (January 2017-December 2022) across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods. A linear mixed-effects model, restricted to patients with a baseline HbA1c ≥7%, assessed associations between study period, facility location, testing interval, and HbA1c. Results After exclusions, 1,191,486 HbA1c measurements from 546,466 patients were included. Testing adherence was poor throughout, with 89.4% of pandemic-period tests and 88.7% of post-pandemic tests performed later than recommended. In patients with a baseline HbA1c ≥7% and at least two measurements, adjusted mean HbA1c increased from 9.6% pre-pandemic to 9.9% during the pandemic, then decreased to 9.7% post-pandemic (eight-month period), without returning to pre-pandemic levels. Non-metropolitan location was associated with higher HbA1c; testing interval length showed no meaningful association. Conclusions These findings suggest that the pandemic compounded pre-existing weaknesses in HbA1c monitoring rather than creating an entirely new problem. Continuous structural investments, including decentralized HbA1c testing and community-based monitoring, are needed to strengthen chronic disease care during future health-system disruptions.
journal: Disaster Medicine and Public Health Preparedness

title: Pandemic crisis and the race for supply chain resilience through organizational learning and agility
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed deep structural vulnerabilities in global supply chains (SC) and demonstrated the importance of resilience as a capability for adaptive continuity under prolonged disruption. This study examines how organizational learning (OL) and organizational agility (OA) were associated with resilience-related SC responses during large-scale disruption, with particular attention to digitally enabled coordination. Drawing on a multiple case study of seven European firms and 17 semi-structured interviews, the study provides qualitative evidence on how firms developed crisis preparedness, adaptive response, and recovery capabilities during the pandemic. The case findings associated structured training, crisis reflection, cross-functional learning, employee empowerment, and the knowledge-sharing routines with preparedness and adaptive SC responses. Accounts of agility emphasized rapid decision-making, responsive communication, process reconfiguration, and technology-enabled coordination under conditions of supply shortages, logistics disruptions, and demand volatility. Across the cases, digital coordination, timely information sharing, and technology-enabled communication were described as supporting resilience-related SC responses across interconnected supply networks. Theoretically, the paper advances the SCR literature by explaining how OL and OA operate as interrelated organizational mechanisms that support resilience-related supply chain responses during prolonged disruption. Managerially, the findings suggest that firms should institutionalize learning routines, deepen collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, and invest in digital capabilities that support agile communication, visibility, and coordination during future crises.

title: From Pandemic Disruption to Service Recovery: Changes in Healthcare Utilization and Access to Surgery in a Tertiary Hand Surgery Clinic
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare utilization and continuity of surgical care. This study evaluated changes in utilization, case mix, and in-hospital surgery completion in a tertiary hand surgery clinic across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and 2022 comparison periods. Methods: This retrospective study included 1453 presentations with a new upper-extremity complaint between 1 October and 31 December in 2019, 2020, and 2022. Demographics, traumatic origin, diagnosis, surgical indication, in-hospital surgery completion within 180 days of the surgical decision, and time to surgery among operated presentations were compared across periods. Multivariable logistic regression examined non-completion. Results: Presentation volume declined from 618 in 2019 to 232 in 2020 (−62.5%) and was 603 in 2022. The proportion of traumatic presentations increased from 50.8% to 69.8%. Fractures and dislocations became proportionally more frequent, whereas the proportions of osteoarthritis/chondral disorders and ganglion/mass/tumor diagnoses decreased. Surgical indication rates did not differ significantly (p = 0.519), but completion among indicated presentations decreased from 95.5% to 56.9% and was 95.7% in 2022 (p < 0.001). The pandemic period was associated with higher adjusted odds of non-completion versus 2019 (adjusted OR, 12.26; 95% CI, 4.64–32.41). Median decision-to-surgery time among operated presentations was 6, 12, and 7 days in 2019, 2020 and 2022 respectively. Conclusions: The pandemic period was associated with altered utilization and case mix and lower in-hospital surgery completion. In 2022, presentation volume and completion were close to 2019 values, although case mix remained different.

title: Fertility, skilled birth attendance, and maternal mortality in BRICS: long-run evidence from heterogeneous panels with cross-sectional dependence, 2000–2023
abstract: Maternal mortality is a sensitive marker of health-system performance in BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa). This study examines the long-run associations of fertility, female education, and skilled birth attendance with the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), controlling for health expenditure, income, and urbanization. Using data for 2000–2023, we evaluate standard and break-adjusted unit-root and cointegration tests against simulated finite-sample critical values. Long-run associations are estimated with pooled and fixed-effects regressions with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and with mean group, common correlated effects mean group, and augmented mean group (AMG) estimators, all with country-specific COVID-19 dummies. The heterogeneous estimates are summarized with medians, trimmed means, and precision weights and re-estimated in a parsimonious specification, complemented by sensitivity, missing-data, leave-one-country-out, and Dumitrescu–Hurlin analyses. Fertility is the most consistent correlate: the AMG elasticity is 0.64 ( p = 0.003), positive in all five countries and in every summary of the country estimates, although it is smaller and imprecise in the parsimonious specification. Skilled birth attendance is negatively associated with MMR in all fixed-effects specifications and missing-data checks. GDP per capita is negative in almost all specifications but significant mainly in the two-way models; health expenditure, female schooling, urbanization, and governance show no association that is stable across estimators. Short-run predictive relationships are absent once common shocks are removed. The findings support sustained investment in family planning and in skilled, facility-based childbirth care. Because the MMR series is a modeled estimate that uses fertility, income, and skilled attendance as covariates, the estimates are long-run associations, not causal effects.

title: Manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles: revisión sistemática
abstract: Objetivo: sintetizar la evidencia sobre el manejo odontológico de pacientes con enfermedades transmisibles. Método: revisión sistemática con síntesis narrativa en PubMed y SciELO (2012-2025); se incluyeron 15 estudios: revisiones, estudios transversales y retrospectivos. Resultados: la exposición ocupacional a la sangre, sobre todo por objetos punzocortantes, fue el principal riesgo para el personal. La vacunación contra la hepatitis B y la profilaxis posexposición fueron las medidas más eficaces frente a las infecciones sanguíneas. Frente al SARS-CoV-2 se recomendaron el triaje, el control de aerosoles y el equipo de protección. Conclusión: el manejo se basa en precauciones estándar aplicadas a todos los pacientes, que permiten una atención segura y sin discriminación.

Frente al SARS-CoV-2 se recomendaron el triaje, el control de aerosoles y el equipo de protección. Conclusión: el manejo se basa en precauciones estándar aplicadas a todos los pacientes, que permiten una atención segura y sin discriminación.

title: MORE MONUMENTS, MORE TOURISTS? EXAMINING HERITAGE-TOURISM RELATIONSHIPS ACROSS ROMANIAN COUNTIES
abstract: Cultural heritage is an important territorial resource for tourism development, yet the relationship between the distribution of listed heritage assets and tourism activity remains insufficiently understood. This study examines the geographical relationships between listed cultural heritage and tourism in Romania, focusing on territorial disparities and long-term changes. The analysis covers all 41 Romanian counties and the Municipality of Bucharest, combining 30,147 entries from the 2015 List of Historic Monuments with tourism statistics for 2001-2025. The methodological framework integrates correlation analysis, measures of territorial concentration, a heritage-tourism mismatch indicator, principal component analysis, k-means clustering, and cross-sectional and panel regression models. The results reveal a positive association between the listed heritage stock and tourist arrivals (r = 0.616) and overnight stays (r = 0.489). However, the association with tourist arrivals weakens substantially after accounting for heritage composition and accommodation capacity, the latter retaining a significant positive relationship with arrivals. Tourist arrivals are geographically more concentrated than listed heritage assets, revealing considerable territorial mismatches. Four exploratory county profiles demonstrate differences in heritage resources, accommodation provision, occupancy and length of stay. Between 2001 and 2025, tourist arrivals increased considerably, while average length of stay declined markedly. No statistically significant association was identified between the size of the heritage stock and the initial COVID-19 tourism decline or subsequent annual recovery levels. The findings demonstrate that the distribution of listed cultural heritage alone cannot adequately explain tourism patterns and highlight the importance of wider territorial conditions in understanding tourism development.
journal: Geo Journal of Tourism and Geosites

title: ANALYTICAL INSIGHT AT THE ECONOMIC BENEFITS, TOURISM IMPACTS AND FUTURE DEVELOPMENT AT THE EXAMPLE OF THE SZIGET MUSIC FESTIVAL IN HUNGARY
abstract: The economic impact of tourism and its types and forms on the economy of individual destinations is an undeniable topic. Its importance is demonstrated not only in standard types of holiday stays, but also in alternatives such as the organization of various events, which at the same time help to increase the attractiveness of the destination. The goal of the paper was to look analytically at the positive economic impact of the Sziget festival, organized for many years in the Hungarian metropolis of Budapest. Its functioning was also affected during the long pandemic years, which caused damage to its overall performance. However, the suspension of activity did not cause the total demise of the event. After the pandemic and its restrictions subsided, the festival's activity resumed. The interest shown confirmed its strength and popularity and, therefore, its economic importance. Based on the use of secondary data resulting from scientific abstraction such as event attendance, average entrance fees, etc., direct and indirect impacts were subsequently described in more detail using descriptive statistics, with links to the economic essence of the festival. In addition, time series of expected future developments were also created, taking into account the previous significant impact of the season during the Covid-19 pandemic. From an economic perspective, the festival represents approximately 0.05% of GDP, and is therefore a significant short-term boost to the tourism sector concentrated within one week. Three scenarios of the economic impact of the festival were developed, where in the conservative scenario (multiplier 1.30) the total effect reaches a value of 97.5, which represents the lowest estimated benefit and reflects a cautious view of the economic impacts. The medium scenario (1.50) increases the total effect to 112.5, indicating a more realistic and balanced estimate of the benefits, and the optimistic scenario (1.60) brings the highest value of 120, which indicates a situation with maximum use of the economic potential of the event, higher visitor spending and stronger secondary effects in the economy.

title: The Effect Of ROA, EPS, And PBV On Stock Prices In The Financial Sector Listed On The Indonesia Stock Exchange 2021–2025
abstract: The financial sector capital market has experienced considerable dynamics and fluctuations in the post-COVID-19 period that have not always moved in line with companies’ financial fundamentals. An empirical anomaly occurred in 2023, when improvements in financial ratios were followed by a weakening of the sectoral stock price index. Objective This study examines the effects of Return On Assets (ROA), Earning Per Share (EPS), and Price to Book Value (PBV) on stock prices of financial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2021–2025. Method: A quantitative explanatory approach was employed. Using purposive sampling, 13 companies were selected, resulting in 65 observations. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression. Results: ROA has no significant effect on stock prices (Sig. 0.053 > 0.05), while EPS and PBV have positive and significant effects (Sig. Simultaneously, ROA, EPS, and PBV significantly affect stock prices, with a coefficient of determination of 52.2%. Conclusion EPS and PBV are stronger determinants of investor decisions than ROA. The findings confirm the applicability of signaling theory in the Indonesian capital market.
journal: Jurnal Ekonomi Bisnis, Manajemen dan Akuntansi

title: Reações editoriais à desinformação em saúde: uma análise comparativa entre Brasil e Espanha
abstract: Analisamos editoriais dos jornais mais lidos no Brasil e na Espanha sobre desinformação em saúde durante a pandemia de Covid-19. Combinando enquadramento e estudos sobre desinformação, verificamos que na Espanha o sistema comunicacional sustentou consenso institucional nas evidências científicas; no Brasil, a desinformação veio do topo do Executivo, tornando o editorial uma “barreira sanitária” contra o discurso da extrema-direita.

title: Influence Without Authority: Bottom-Up Normalization of Organizational Corruption
abstract: Research on organizational corruption has largely portrayed normalization as a top-down, management-driven process. We know less about how employees with limited formal authority can escalate wrongdoing beyond isolated acts and drive its normalization. Drawing on a qualitative study of a German recruitment firm’s practices during the COVID-19 pandemic, we develop a three-phase model of bottom-up normalization of organizational wrongdoing. Less powerful actors first engage in tolerated rule-bending to demonstrate competence and indispensability and build influence through informal networks. When disruption threatens this influence and legitimate alternatives are unavailable, they may escalate to more serious wrongdoing to safeguard their standing by framing new opportunities as extensions of familiar rule-bending. Normalization then depends on their ability to sustain a cohesive coalition, secure support from actors with formal authority, and contain resistance. We make three contributions. First, we advance a relational view of corruption by showing how central positions in informal networks enable actors lacking formal authority to mobilize support across hierarchical levels and normalize wrongdoing. Second, we show how organizational corruption can become a means of building and preserving social influence, fostering a sense of accomplishment rather than guilt or shame. Third, we identify a disruption-driven pathway to normalization in which threats to less powerful actors’ social influence precipitate abrupt escalation from tolerated rule-bending to more serious wrongdoing.

title: Uneven recovery: spatial and temporal patterns in owner-driven housing reconstruction after the 2015 Nepal Earthquake
abstract: This study aims to examine whether urban disadvantage in post-earthquake housing reconstruction in Nepal is a general urban pattern or is concentrated within the Kathmandu Valley, and whether spatial disparities persisted over time. Quarterly panel data from 131 municipalities across the 14 districts most severely affected by the 2015 Gorkha earthquake, covering November 2018 to November 2020, are analyzed. Pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) regression with municipality-clustered robust standard errors and period fixed effects models quarterly reconstruction flow rates using municipality type, lagged cumulative reconstruction progress, housing characteristics, poverty and other municipal characteristics. Additional robustness analyses assess the sensitivity of the findings to alternative model specifications. Urban disadvantage is not uniform. Urban municipalities within the Kathmandu Valley had significantly lower quarterly reconstruction flow rates than rural municipalities, whereas urban municipalities outside the Valley showed no statistically significant difference. Lagged cumulative reconstruction progress was negatively associated with reconstruction flow, while the share of stone/mud-masonry housing showed a positive association. Reconstruction activity varied across periods, including a decline coinciding with the COVID-19 pandemic. The observed spatial disparities highlight the importance of considering local reconstruction conditions when designing and delivering financial and technical assistance, particularly in dense and historically complex urban settings such as the Kathmandu Valley. This municipality-level longitudinal analysis highlights important heterogeneity within urban areas, showing that reconstruction patterns vary not only between urban and rural municipalities but also across different urban contexts.
journal: International Journal of Disaster Resilience in the Built Environment

title: Resilience and Adaptation of Myanmar’s Hospitality Industry Before and After the 2021 Coup
abstract: Myanmar’s hospitality industry grew between 2011 and 2019 due to political and economic reforms, reduced travel restrictions, and increased foreign direct investment. However, the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021 military coup, political instability, and natural disasters, including the earthquake, severely disrupted the industry. These challenges affected hospitality businesses’ operations, employment, investment, and overall recovery. This article examines the challenges Myanmar’s hospitality industry faced before and after the 2021 coup, considering the current economic situation and other influencing factors. It also suggests strategies to support business survival and recovery. Key recommendations include providing financial and administrative assistance to hospitality SMEs, addressing electricity shortages and poor internet connectivity, retaining employees, diversifying markets, and strengthening domestic tourism. Above all, ensuring peace, safety, and security for visitors and customers is essential. The industry needs a coordinated approach among the government, businesses, and other stakeholders to survive and recover.

title: Navigating the NAPDS presidency during COVID
abstract: The article highlights the experience of National Association for Professional Development Schools’ (NAPDS's) 2020–21 president, Dr Lorri Sapp. The article is written in an epistolary, narrative style. Due to the nature of the piece, there are no research findings. However, the article features the insights of NAPDS President, Dr Lorri Sapp. Dr Sapp discusses her involvement in the local professional development schools (PDS) context through her unofficial PDS role, navigating the NAPDS presidency during the Covid-19 pandemic, and suggestions for National Association for School-University Partnerships (NASUP) in order to strengthen the future of the organization. The article draws additional attention to the exemplary leadership of the organization's second decade and may inspire others to seek leadership within NASUP.
journal: PDS Partners: Bridging Research to Practice

title: Descomposición de la inflación en el área del euro y España entre perturbaciones de oferta y de demanda
abstract: En este documento se analiza la evolución de la inflación núcleo (inflación general excluidos la energía y los alimentos) en el área del euro y en España, descomponiéndola en factores asociados a las dinámicas de oferta o de demanda. Para ello, se sigue la metodología propuesta por Shapiro (2026), que permite clasificar las perturbaciones observadas en los precios de consumo y en las cantidades —aproximadas por los indicadores de producción de bienes y servicios— a partir de una desagregación por clases del índice armonizado de precios al consumo. Los resultados sugieren que la inflación experimentada, tanto en el área del euro como en España, durante los años posteriores a la crisis del COVID-19, se debe principalmente a los factores de oferta, si bien los factores de demanda también habrían sido relevantes.

title: Digital Tourism Research: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global Publication Trends (2020-2025)
abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping tourism into a platform-based and data-driven ecosystem, resulting in rapid growth of scholarly publications and increasing complexity in identifying dominant themes and emerging research frontiers. This study aims to map the global intellectual structure of digital tourism research from 2020 to 2026 using bibliometric science mapping. Bibliographic data were collected from Google Scholar via Publish or Perish (PoP) using the keyword “digital tourism,” followed by relevance screening, duplicate removal, and metadata verification, resulting in 200 documents for analysis. The study applied VOSviewer with binary counting and term co-occurrence analysis to visualize research networks and thematic clusters. The findings reveal four major research streams. The first cluster highlights tourism development and destination competitiveness as central themes in digital transformation. The second emphasizes technology adoption, acceptance factors, and the role of COVID-19 as a catalyst for contactless innovation and digitalization. The third focuses on smart tourism, innovation, travel experience, and digital infrastructure. The fourth reflects emerging studies on digital nomadism and workation, indicating a shift toward hybrid mobility patterns. Additionally, emerging concepts such as metaverse tourism represent promising but underexplored research areas. This study provides a comprehensive research roadmap and identifies future opportunities for mechanism-based investigations into digital tourism innovation.

title: Co-creating pedagogy through an institution wide Community of Practice on learning and teaching technologies
abstract: The Australian higher education sector is operating in a period of rapid technological and social change. As a result, educators are navigating increasing complexities in their teaching, including complexities related to assuring learning, providing quality learning experiences and responding with appropriate pedagogical practices. As a way of navigating some of this complexity, RMIT University has developed an institution-wide Community of Practice (CoP) focused on learning and teaching technologies (L&T Tech). The CoP brings together academic and professional staff from across vocational and higher education sectors, to collaboratively drive continuous improvement in high-quality, technology enhanced learning and teaching. Established to support teaching continuity during the COVID-19 pandemic, the CoP has evolved into a collaborative space where participants collectively explore, critique and influence technology related pedagogical practices. This practice report describes the design, implementation and early outcomes of the CoP, highlighting how a pedagogy-first approach, that is informed by social learning, has enabled the co-creation of institutional teaching practices. Through peer-led showcases, collaborative problem-solving, themed discussions, hackathons, and cross-functional engagement, the CoP fosters reflective practice. Early anecdotal outcomes indicate strengthened cross-institutional networks, increased confidence in technology-enhanced and pedagogically informed teaching, and the emergence of collaborative initiatives that extend beyond individual CoP sessions. The paper concludes by reflecting on the role of institution-wide communities of practice as career communities that enable collective capability development and educational innovation.

title: “O mundo é um trem desgovernado”: bricolagens epistêmicas, trajetórias biográficas e Covid-19da Coorte de Nascimentos de Pelotas (1982–2025)
abstract: Este artigo analisa as práticas de cuidado emergentes durante a pandemia de Covid-19 sob a lente da bricolagem epistêmica. Fundamentada em uma etnografia de longa duração vinculada à Coorte de Nascimentos de Pelotas (1982), a investigação explora como indivíduos na casa dos 40 anos ressignificaram saberes e protocolos de saúde diante de um cenário de falência institucional e instabilidade informacional. Através das trajetórias de interlocutores como Daniele, Felícia, Theo, Antônia, Julia, Jailson e Tamires, observamos que as respostas à situação-limite sanitária não se reduzem a uma dicotomia entre ciência e negacionismo, mas compõem um espectro reflexivo que abrange desde a crítica política e o ceticismo institucional até a formulação de uma eu-pistemologia. Argumentamos que a costura de fragmentos de discursos especializados, memórias familiares e experiências incorporadas permitiu a esses sujeitos fabricar "abrigos de sentido" e estratégias pragmáticas de sobrevivência em um mundo percebido como um "trem desgovernado".

Através das trajetórias de interlocutores como Daniele, Felícia, Theo, Antônia, Julia, Jailson e Tamires, observamos que as respostas à situação-limite sanitária não se reduzem a uma dicotomia entre ciência e negacionismo, mas compõem um espectro reflexivo que abrange desde a crítica política e o ceticismo institucional até a formulação de uma eu-pistemologia. Argumentamos que a costura de fragmentos de discursos especializados, memórias familiares e experiências incorporadas permitiu a esses sujeitos fabricar "abrigos de sentido" e estratégias pragmáticas de sobrevivência em um mundo percebido como um "trem desgovernado".

title: Overhead Cost Share, Material Cost Share, and Profitability: Evidence From Indonesian Listed Textile Firms, 2018–2024
abstract: Background: Listed Indonesian textile producers lost money in most years between 2018 and 2024, a period of fibre and energy price shocks, the COVID-19 pandemic, weak demand, and import competition. Studies that link production costs to profit mostly use pooled cross-firm variation and report conflicting signs.Purpose: The study asks whether the composition of production costs (the shares of factory overhead and direct materials, with direct labour as the reference category) is associated with return on assets (ROA), and whether that association differs between firms and within firms over time.Design/methodology/approach: An unbalanced panel of 11 textile and textile-product firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (76 firm-years) combines hand-collected cost shares from audited annual reports with balance-sheet and income data from LSEG Workspace. Two-way fixed-effect models are estimated with firm-clustered standard errors and wild cluster bootstrap p-values, and a within–between (Mundlak) random-effects model separates the two sources of variation.Findings/Result: Within firms, the overhead share is negatively associated with ROA at the 10% significance level in every fixed-effects specification: moving one percentage point of the cost base from direct labour to overhead is associated with an ROA about 1.8 percentage points lower. The association loses significance when size and leverage are lagged and disappears once Sri Rejeki Isman, which collapsed in 2021–2022, is excluded. The material share shows no within-firm association. Between-firm and within-firm coefficients differ significantly at the 1% level (joint Mundlak test): firms with structurally higher overhead or material shares are not less profitable on average. All estimates are associations.Conclusion: In this sample, a rising overhead share goes with lower profitability within firms, but mainly as a signal of severe volume collapse rather than as a general driver of profitability, and pooled estimates of cost composition and profitability mix two different relationships.Originality/value (State of the art): The study applies the within–between distinction to cost composition in an energy- and asset-intensive industry over the 2018–2024 shock period and shows how sensitive firm-level cost–profit evidence can be to a single distress episode in small listed-firm panels. Keywords:cost composition, operating leverage, within–between estimation, profitability, textile industry
journal: AI, Big Data and Quantitative Methods in Finance

title: Optimal free energy requirements for managing disruptive and unexpected organizational change
abstract: This study aims to develop a systems-theoretic framework to understand how organizations maintain adaptive functioning amid disruptive, unexpected environmental change. Drawing on the free energy (FE) principle, the paper conceptualizes organizational FE as an adaptive reserve capacity that enables organizations to absorb, interpret and respond to environmental uncertainty. Using archival data from Canadian manufacturing sectors during the COVID-19 disruption period, the study explores whether pre-pandemic levels of FE, operationalized through manufacturing capacity utilization, were associated with post-pandemic organizational resilience and GDP growth between 2019 and 2023. The analyses also examine the potential roles of automation, government stimulus and supply-chain disruption within a moderated mediation framework. The analysis provides no evidence that FE directly predicts post-pandemic GDP growth. However, FE consistently predicts sector-level organizational resilience measured through absorptive, adaptive and recovery capacities. These findings suggest that adaptive reserve capacity may operate more meaningfully at organizational and sectoral levels than as a direct driver of macroeconomic performance. The study contributes to resilience and systems research by reframing FE as a resilience-oriented systems construct associated with adaptive capacity amid uncertainty. The findings further suggest that systems optimized exclusively for short-term efficiency may become more vulnerable to brittleness during large-scale disruption. This paper integrates systems theory, organizational resilience research and adaptive systems perspectives into a novel interdisciplinary framework for understanding how reserve capacity, environmental uncertainty and resilience interact during periods of disruptive change.

title: Finanse i bezpieczeństwo ekonomiczne
abstract: W niniejszej monografii Finanse i bezpieczeństwo ekonomiczne poruszono tematykę finansów, zarządzania finansami, predykcji upadłości przedsiębiorstw, bezpieczeństwa finansowego oraz wpływu czynników zewnętrznych, takich jak COVID-19 i konflikt zbrojny na Ukrainie, na sytuację finansową przedsiębiorstw. Monografia składa się z dziewięciu rozdziałów napisanych przez autorów reprezentujących różne ośrodki akademickie. Należy również podkreślić duży wkład studentów z Uniwersytetu Rzeszowskiego, którzy samodzielnie lub pod opieką naukową przygotowali artykuły. Dziękuję wszystkim autorom za dostarczone teksty oraz patronom II Ogólnopolskiej Konferencji Naukowej „Finanse i bezpieczeństwo ekonomiczne Polski” i III Ogólnopolskiej Konferencji Naukowej „Finanse, innowacyjny rozwój i bezpieczeństwo ekonomiczne”, zorganizowanych w latach 2023–2024, na których większość opublikowanych prac została zaprezentowana i szeroko dyskutowana. Szczególne podziękowania składam prof. Jerzemu Kitowskiemu za wsparcie i pomoc merytoryczną przy organizacji ww. konferencji naukowych. Wyrażam nadzieję, że w związku z dużym przekrojem artykułów monografia zainteresuje liczne grono osób nie tylko ze świata nauki, lecz również praktyków z zakresu finansów, a także studentów, którzy będą mogli poszerzyć swoją wiedzę i wykorzystać zawarte w nich informacje podczas pisania prac dyplomowych. Ponadto publikacja monografii wyłącznie w wersji on-line pozwoli każdemu odbiorcy na szybki dostęp do jej treści.

title: Analysis of Nitrogen Oxide (NOx) and Sulfur Oxide (SOx) Concentration Trends in Ambient Air in Malang City: Secondary Data Approach (2019–2023)
abstract: Malang City is an educational and tourism hub experiencing a significant increase in motor vehicle volume, which potentially degrades ambient air quality. This study aims to analyze the trend of Nitrogen Oxide (NOx) and Sulfur Oxide (SOx) pollutant concentrations in Malang City over a five-year period (2019–2023). This study uses a descriptive quantitative method using secondary data from the ambient air quality monitoring reports of the Environmental Agency (DLH). Data analysis was conducted by comparing annual average values ​​against the National Ambient Air Quality Standards based on Government Regulation No. The analysis results show that NOx concentrations fluctuated with a significant decrease in 2020 due to COVID-19 mobility restrictions, but increased again in 2022-2023 along with the recovery of urban activities. On the other hand, SOx concentrations tend to be stable and well below the quality standard threshold, considering the lack of heavy industrial activity in Malang City. In conclusion, air pollution in Malang City is dominated by mobile sources (transportation) which contribute to NOx emissions, while SOx parameters are still in a very safe category. Stricter traffic management policies are needed to control the upward trend of NOx emissions in the future.
journal: Ambidextrous Journal of Innovation Efficiency and Technology in Organization

title: ANÁLISE EPIDEMIOLÓGICA DAS INTERNAÇÕES POR BRONQUIOLITE AGUDA EM CRIANÇAS NO ESTADO DO PARANÁ ENTRE 2015 E 2025
abstract: Este estudo descritivo, ecológico e retrospectivo analisou o perfil epidemiológico das internações hospitalares por bronquite e bronquiolite agudas (CID-10 J20/J21) em crianças de 0 a 4 anos no estado do Paraná, entre janeiro de 2015 e dezembro de 2025, com base em dados públicos do Sistema de Informações Hospitalares do SUS (SIH/SUS). No período, foram registradas 30.072 internações e 27 óbitos. Observou-se estabilidade no volume de internações entre 2015 e 2019 (média de ~2.250 casos/ano), seguida de queda abrupta em 2020 (79,2%) associada às medidas não farmacológicas de controle da COVID-19, recuperação parcial em 2021 e aumento progressivo a partir de 2022, atingindo o maior número da série em 2025 (4.630 internações), padrão compatível com o fenômeno de "dívida imunológica". A sazonalidade das internações mostrou-se bem definida, concentrada entre abril e julho (outono/início do inverno), enquanto a taxa de mortalidade hospitalar manteve-se baixa (média de 0,09% ao ano) ao longo de toda a série. Os resultados evidenciam o impacto da pandemia sobre a dinâmica epidemiológica da doença e reforçam a importância do monitoramento contínuo para subsidiar o planejamento de estratégias de vigilância e assistência pediátrica.
journal: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

title: ANÁLISE DO PERFIL EPIDEMIOLÓGICO E DAS CONDIÇÕES DE SAÚDE DA COMUNIDADE QUILOMBOLA DO CEDRO EM MINEIROS, GOIÁS
abstract: As comunidades quilombolas brasileiras apresentam importantes vulnerabilidades sociais e sanitárias, especialmente em áreas rurais, onde o acesso aos serviços de saúde pode ser limitado. Trata-se de um estudo observacional, transversal, descritivo e de abordagem quantitativa, realizado com 71 moradores adultos da comunidade. Os dados foram coletados por meio de questionário estruturado aplicado presencialmente e analisados por estatística descritiva. Observou-se predominância do sexo feminino (70,4%), baixa escolaridade e dependência de benefícios sociais como principal fonte de renda. Entre as condições de saúde autorreferidas, destacaram-se hipertensão arterial sistêmica (52,1%), diabetes mellitus (31,0%) e sintomas relacionados à ansiedade e depressão (28,2%). Embora a maioria dos participantes tenha relatado acesso regular a profissionais de saúde, persistiram dificuldades relacionadas à realização de exames, consultas e atendimento especializado. Em relação aos impactos da pandemia, verificaram-se relatos de infecção por COVID-19, perdas familiares, dificuldades de acesso aos serviços de saúde, comprometimento da renda e alterações nas tradições culturais comunitárias. Conclui-se que a comunidade quilombola Cedro ainda enfrenta desafios relacionados às condições de saúde e ao acesso aos serviços assistenciais, ao mesmo tempo em que mantém forte vínculo com práticas tradicionais de cuidado, evidenciando a importância da valorização dos saberes populares e do fortalecimento de políticas públicas voltadas à saúde das populações quilombolas.

title: Managing occupational dermatitis during pandemics using virucidal emollient Dermol 500.
abstract: Abstract Background: Work-related contact dermatitis is a significant problem for healthcare workers. Repeated exposure to water, soap and alcohol-based gels can cause dry skin, irritation and contact dermatitis. Soap substitutes such as Dermol 500 are commonly prescribed to prevent and treat dermatitis. However, hand hygiene recommendations during the COVID-19 pandemic advised against using soap substitutes in clinical settings as their virucidal capacity had not been established. Aims: To investigate whether Dermol 500 lotion exhibits virucidal activity and is a suitable soap substitute for use during viral disease outbreaks. This study aims to inform best practice in occupational medicine and help combat the increased incidence of work-related contact dermatitis in clinical settings. Methods: The virucidal activity of Dermol 500 lotion and its antimicrobial constituents benzalkonium chloride (BAK) and chlorhexidine dihydrochloride (CD) was assessed against influenza A virus (IAV), SARS-CoV-2 and pseudotyped viruses expressing glycoproteins from 2026 outbreak strains of Ebolavirus and Hantavirus. Viruses or pseudoviruses were incubated with treatment prior to quenching serial dilution and infectivity measurement by plaque assay, tissue culture infectious dose 50 (TCID50) or bioluminescent reporter activity. Results: Dermol 500 exhibits comparable virucidal activity to alcohol-based hand sanitisers against IAV and SARS-CoV-2. Furthermore, the Dermol 500 components BAK and CD exhibit independent and synergistic virucidal activity against IAV, SARS-CoV-2 and pseudoviruses. Conclusions: The virucidal activity of Dermol 500 lotion and its active antimicrobials BAK and CD indicates its suitability as a soap substitute to treat and prevent contact dermatitis in front line workers during viral disease outbreaks.

title: ENCOMENDA TECNOLÓGICA COMO ESTRATÉGIA DE INOVAÇÃO EM SAÚDE PÚBLICA
abstract: O artigo analisa a encomenda tecnológica (ETEC) como instrumento jurídico e estratégico de inovação em saúde pública, a partir do contrato celebrado entre a AstraZeneca e o Instituto de Tecnologia em Imunobiológicos (Bio-Manguinhos), unidade produtora da Fundação Oswaldo Cruz (Fiocruz), para a produção da vacina contra a Covid-19. A pesquisa combinou revisão de literatura, análise documental e estudo de caso detalhado. O estudo se baseou no contrato de ETEC, em documentos institucionais correlatos e em onze entrevistas semiestruturadas com profissionais diretamente envolvidos na negociação, na gestão e na execução da parceria. Os resultados, sistematizados por meio da técnica de análise de conteúdo, demonstraram o potencial da encomenda tecnológica como instrumento de inovação, ao possibilitar a transferência de tecnologia e a produção nacional de imunizantes em curto prazo. Apesar de desafios jurídicos e contratuais, a iniciativa fortaleceu a capacidade nacional de resposta a crises, na medida em que viabilizou o acesso rápido ao imunizante, promoveu autonomia tecnológica nacional e fortaleceu as capacidades institucionais de inovação em saúde.
journal: Revista de Estudos Empíricos em Direito

Os resultados, sistematizados por meio da técnica de análise de conteúdo, demonstraram o potencial da encomenda tecnológica como instrumento de inovação, ao possibilitar a transferência de tecnologia e a produção nacional de imunizantes em curto prazo. Apesar de desafios jurídicos e contratuais, a iniciativa fortaleceu a capacidade nacional de resposta a crises, na medida em que viabilizou o acesso rápido ao imunizante, promoveu autonomia tecnológica nacional e fortaleceu as capacidades institucionais de inovação em saúde.

title: Developing a Subdistrict-Level Economic Progress Index Using Geospatial Data
abstract: This paper develops an Economic Progress Index (EPI), a composite measure built from Earth Observation (EO) and open geospatial data with unsupervised Principal Component Analysis (PCA) weighting. The index captures the observable productive and enabling capacity of local economies and the intensity with which economic space is used. Sub-national monitoring in developing economies is held back by sparse data: district GDP estimates arrive with multi-year lags, rely on price deflators and top-down allocation, and do not exist at the subdistrict (taluka/tehsil) scale where place-based policy is targeted. The EPI fuses multi-sensor satellite data, gridded population and OpenStreetMap road and amenity networks across 357 subdistricts of Maharashtra, India, over 46 quarters (2015 Q1 - 2026 Q2). Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS (STL) separates long-run trends from monsoon and crop-cycle seasonality. A non-negative PCA gives sign-consistent, interpretable weights and rankings nearly identical to standard PCA ($\rho$ = 0.998). Across districts, the index explains 74% of the variation in the NFHS-5 wealth index, 52% in household consumption (HCES 2023-24) and about 78% in real district GDP levels (65% in logs), but does not track short-run output growth. Because it measures structural capacity rather than annual output, the index kept rising through the FY2020-21 COVID-19 contraction. Across Maharashtra's six revenue divisions, relative inequality fell by 44% even as the absolute gap between leading and lagging divisions widened by 32%; district-level $\beta$-convergence implies a half-life of about 14 years. The framework offers a scalable, deflator-free basis for structural monitoring in data-sparse economies.

title: Population-scale machine learning models estimate individual-level risk for acute respiratory infection
abstract: Summary / Abstract BackgroundModels based on administrative population health records can help improve understanding of disease and hospitalisation risk. This understanding can support evidence-based population health policy and processes. Influenza and other acute respiratory diseases place a large, inequitable burden on the New Zealand population and health care resources. We have developed and evaluated such models using retrospective New Zealand hospitalisation records linked to other administrative data to estimate individual-level risk of hospitalisation due to acute respiratory infection. MethodsWe analysed linked annual records for approximately 4{middle dot}85-5{middle dot}36 million people in 2017-2024. Six machine learning algorithms and eight variable sets were assessed using five-fold cross-validation grouped by demographic profile. Variables comprised demographics, continuous hospital-based (M3) and pharmaceutical-based (P3) morbidity indices, and influenza vaccination status. Models trained on one year were also evaluated on data from the following year. Performance measures were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the average precision score (APS). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) described model contributions, including paired vaccination-input changes in 2024. FindingsAnnual national hospitalisation prevalence ranged from 1{middle dot}01% to 1{middle dot}60%. With all variables, mean cross-validation AUROC and APS were 0{middle dot}8430 and 0{middle dot}1283 for LightGBM (LGB), and 0{middle dot}8415 and 0{middle dot}1285 for XGBoost (XGB). Adding both morbidity indices to the demographics increased LGB APS from 0{middle dot}0720 to 0{middle dot}1158; adding vaccination further increased it to 0{middle dot}1283. Next-year AUROC and APS averaged 0{middle dot}8429 and 0{middle dot}1267 for LGB and 0{middle dot}8423 and 0{middle dot}1277 for XGB. Age and morbidity were the most influential variables. Among vaccinated individuals, SHAP analysis indicated that vaccination contributed most strongly towards lower model-estimated hospitalisation risk in the oldest age group. InterpretationCombining historical morbidity and vaccination information in gradient boosting models improved the ability to distinguish between people who experienced respiratory hospitalisation and those who did not in annual New Zealand population data. Similar next-year performance and interpretable variation across age and morbidity profiles support further development toward practical risk assessment, including calibration and evaluation across population groups. Research in contextO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSOur focused narrative review considered population-based respiratory hospitalisation models, respiratory disease burden in New Zealand, and the development of the M3 and P3 morbidity indices. Existing studies include population models for COVID-19 and infant respiratory syncytial virus, risk-factor analyses of broad respiratory admissions, and evidence that hospital and pharmaceutical morbidity measures provide complementary information. Added value of this studyThis is the first evaluation of national hospitalisation data linked to other national administrative data to model the risk of acute respiratory infection admission across eight annual datasets, comparing six algorithms and eight variable sets. Together with the benchmark results, these findings illustrate how gradient boosting applied to population-scale records can represent and explain combinations of routinely recorded health information. Implications of all the available evidenceQuantifying historical morbidity and including vaccination information improved respiratory hospitalisation classification, with gradient boosting providing the strongest overall performance. The explanatory analyses further showed that vaccination-related contributions depended on the individuals age and morbidity profile. Representing these clinically plausible patterns supports the use of flexible, non-linear models, such as tree-based algorithms, and rich population-scale records for developing interpretable respiratory risk assessments. The study establishes a basis for a New Zealand respiratory risk model by identifying effective algorithms and useful combinations of variables.
